project_text:
Protracted Relief and Recovery Operations (PRRO) - Ukraine 200953: “Assistance for food insecure and vulnerable populations affected by conflict and loss of livelihoods in eastern Ukraine”. After two years of conflict, the security situation in eastern Ukraine remains fragile. The consequences of conflict and political stalemate are felt by individuals and communities throughout Ukraine. An estimated 1.1 million people are in need of food assistance, with many resorting to negative coping mechanisms. The Government continues to face massive challenges, including a deepening economic crisis and the urgent need for social and fiscal reform. Without medium- to long-term interventions, more people will require humanitarian assistance in the months and years to come.

The proposed protracted relief and recovery operation (PRRO) builds on the activities and lessons learned from emergency operation 200765. It is informed by assessments, evaluations and participatory consultations, which have led to a refinement of the program strategy and the choice of transfer modalities. WFP will address the food needs of the most vulnerable people in eastern Ukraine while gradually supporting early recovery. 

The operation is aligned with WFP’s Strategic Plan (2017–2021) and gender and protection policies and guidelines. It is guided by Sustainable Development Goals 2 and 17, fostering partnerships and national plans and strategies to achieve zero hunger.
The operation is in line with the United Nations Development Assistance Framework; contributes to the Government’s Single and Comprehensive Strategy and Action Plan for Agriculture and Rural Development in Ukraine for 2015–2020 by enhancing food security and monitoring systems; and is aligned with national social protection schemes. It also builds on the priorities of the humanitarian response plan and national recovery plans.

Under planned PRRO, over the period January-December 2017, WFP will provide food assistance to 220,000 food insecure people in conflict-affected eastern Ukraine through a combination of food in kind and cash based transfers.

destinationObjects_Project.name: Provision of community based protection to displaced and affected communities in Ukraine
reportDetails_organization: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
project_text:
Provision of community based protection to displaced and affected communities in Ukraine The overall aim of the protect is to improve the protective environment for those affected, and to improve access to and quality of protection services. Delivery priority will be to populations at the line of contact and in non-Government controlled areas of Ukraine.  

Objectives include:   

1) Promote the Centrality of Protection in the on-going humanitarian response and support the transition to early recovery in the development response. 
2) Provision of quality protection services, including legal and other referral pathways
3) Increase capacity of government, and support community capacity to deliver quality protection services.
4) Enhance community capacity and networks to prevent gender-based violence. 
5) Engage in information sharing and solutions oriented rights based advocacy, with government, communities and other relevant stakeholders.
7) Increase protection mainstreaming to enhance the overall humanitarian response.
8) Continue protection by presence as well as systematic monitoring to support joint analysis and response.
9) Support Communty-based protection networks to empower communities and foster resilience

Specific protection activities will target the most vulnerable, predominantly in host communities: including older persons without caretakers, children, women at risk especially when head of household, persons with disabilities, and other groups at risk as a result of the conflict.  Tailored assistance will be provided, including through cash.  The community based approach will seek to strengthen referral networks, improve access to services, increase awareness on basic rights and reduce discrimination.  Priority delivery will be in non-Government controlled areas of Ukraine.

reportDetails_organization: European Commission's Humanitarian Aid and Civil Protection Department
project_text:
Programme de sécurité alimentaire et de renforcement de la résilience des ménages en insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle, affectées par les chocs agro climatiques et le conflit, dans 20 communes du nord du Mali (Gao, Tombouctou) Cette fiche de proposition se situe dans la droite ligne des axes stratégiques prioritaires du Cluster Sécurité Alimentaire, à savoir : 1) l’assistance coordonnée et intégrée aux personnes en situation d'urgence pour garantir leur survie, 2) le soutien des populations vulnérables à l'insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle pour mieux faire face aux chocs agro climatiques et sécuritaires en renforçant leurs moyens d'existence, 3) le renforcement de capacité des structures et acteurs nationaux pour mieux coordonner les réponses d'urgence et de résilience des populations affectées. Elle fait partie d’un projet multisectoriel plus global intégrant des activités de nutrition et de EHA.
   Résultat 1: Les besoins alimentaires et non alimentaires essentiels de 51 443 ménages en insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle sévère sont couverts à travers une intervention coordonnée et intégrée d’assistance alimentaire et de transferts monétaires multi-usages, dans 20 communes les plus vulnérables des cercles de Tombouctou, Goundam, Salam, Gao et Ansongo
   Résultat 2: Les capacités de préparation, d’adaptation et de renforcement des moyens d´existence face aux chocs agro climatiques et sécuritaires de 12 750 ménages très vulnérables à l’IAN dont 2 550 dirigés par des femmes veuves (20%) et/ou mères d’enfants < 5 ans sont développées
   Résultat 3: Les capacités des structures et acteurs nationaux de coordination des réponses d'urgence et de résilience des populations affectées sont renforcées, ainsi que les capacités techniques des 12 750 ménages bénéficiaires

project_text:
Programme de sécurité alimentaire et de renforcement de la résilience des ménages en insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle, affectées par les chocs agro climatiques et le conflit, dans 20 communes du nord du Mali (Gao, Tombouctou) Cette fiche de proposition se situe dans la droite ligne des axes stratégiques prioritaires du Cluster Sécurité Alimentaire, à savoir : 1) l’assistance coordonnée et intégrée aux personnes en situation d'urgence pour garantir leur survie, 2) le soutien des populations vulnérables à l'insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle pour mieux faire face aux chocs agro climatiques et sécuritaires en renforçant leurs moyens d'existence, 3) le renforcement de capacité des structures et acteurs nationaux pour mieux coordonner les réponses d'urgence et de résilience des populations affectées. Elle fait partie d’un projet multisectoriel plus global intégrant des activités de nutrition et de EHA.
   Résultat 1: Les besoins alimentaires et non alimentaires essentiels de 51 443 ménages en insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle sévère sont couverts à travers une intervention coordonnée et intégrée d’assistance alimentaire et de transferts monétaires multi-usages, dans 20 communes les plus vulnérables des cercles de Tombouctou, Goundam, Salam, Gao et Ansongo
   Résultat 2: Les capacités de préparation, d’adaptation et de renforcement des moyens d´existence face aux chocs agro climatiques et sécuritaires de 12 750 ménages très vulnérables à l’IAN dont 2 550 dirigés par des femmes veuves (20%) et/ou mères d’enfants < 5 ans sont développées
   Résultat 3: Les capacités des structures et acteurs nationaux de coordination des réponses d'urgence et de résilience des populations affectées sont renforcées, ainsi que les capacités techniques des 12 750 ménages bénéficiaires

sourceObjects_Location.name: France

destinationObjects_Project.name: From education in emergency to formal schooling for conflict-affected children in Iraq (integrated approach education and child protection)
project_text:
From education in emergency to formal schooling for conflict-affected children in Iraq (integrated approach education and child protection) This project aims at providing timely, culturally-appropriate and gender-sensitive access to education to conflict-affected children. 
The mobile strategy based on “Magic Bus” approach will be used to provide a timely, context-specific and need-based response to address emergency education needs and ensure transition to formal education. Cash assistance for transportation and school supplies for children out of school or at risk of dropping out will boost their enrolment and attendance to formal education. Teachers will also be supported through a cash transfer scheme, which is expected to increase the performance of the education services.

The project will contribute to the following objectives of the Education Cluster: 
Objective 1: Provide immediate safe, protected learning spaces for highly vulnerable girls and boys aged 4-18
Objective 2: Help improve the quality of learning for highly vulnerable girls and boys aged 4-18
Objective 3: Help to expand and upgrade education and learning opportunities for highly vulnerable girls and boys aged 4-18 


This project covers the first line response (30%), second line response (20%) and full cluster response (50%).

project_text:
Drought Emergency Social Protection Response (DEER) in Kenya: Cash transfer to the poorest households with children in six ASAL counties (Garissa, Isiolo, Kilifi, Samburu, Taita Taveta and Tana River).  Provide cash transfer (CT) support to vulnerable households with children: 
Regular cash transfer programmes in Kenya (CT-OVC, older person CT, disability CT) are targeting the most vulnerable households. Given the amount of cash provided to households only represents 40 per cent of their needs, there is a high risk with the drought that they fall again into extreme food insecurity and start using negative coping mechanisms by selling the assets they have already built in recent years. Providing cash transfer to top-up these most food-insecure families with children will help them meet basic food and non-food needs.

Improve the targeting of vulnerable households with children during emergencies: 
The government-funded regular cash programmes (CT-OVC, older person CT, disability CT) have been inert during this drought. The purpose of this intervention is to support the ongoing harmonized targeting system as well as the single registry to be flexible to support targeting during emergencies.

reportDetails_organization: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
project_text:
Provision of community based protection to displaced and affected communities in Ukraine The overall aim of the protect is to improve the protective environment for those affected, and to improve access to and quality of protection services. Delivery priority will be to populations at the line of contact and in non-Government controlled areas of Ukraine.  

Objectives include:   

1) Promote the Centrality of Protection in the on-going humanitarian response and support the transition to early recovery in the development response. 
2) Provision of quality protection services, including legal and other referral pathways
3) Increase capacity of government, and support community capacity to deliver quality protection services.
4) Enhance community capacity and networks to prevent gender-based violence. 
5) Engage in information sharing and solutions oriented rights based advocacy, with government, communities and other relevant stakeholders.
7) Increase protection mainstreaming to enhance the overall humanitarian response.
8) Continue protection by presence as well as systematic monitoring to support joint analysis and response.
9) Support Communty-based protection networks to empower communities and foster resilience

Specific protection activities will target the most vulnerable, predominantly in host communities: including older persons without caretakers, children, women at risk especially when head of household, persons with disabilities, and other groups at risk as a result of the conflict.  Tailored assistance will be provided, including through cash.  The community based approach will seek to strengthen referral networks, improve access to services, increase awareness on basic rights and reduce discrimination.  Priority delivery will be in non-Government controlled areas of Ukraine.

destinationObjects_Project.name: Protracted Relief and Recovery Operations (PRRO) - Ukraine 200953: “Assistance for food insecure and vulnerable populations affected by conflict and loss of livelihoods in eastern Ukraine”.
project_text:
Protracted Relief and Recovery Operations (PRRO) - Ukraine 200953: “Assistance for food insecure and vulnerable populations affected by conflict and loss of livelihoods in eastern Ukraine”. After two years of conflict, the security situation in eastern Ukraine remains fragile. The consequences of conflict and political stalemate are felt by individuals and communities throughout Ukraine. An estimated 1.1 million people are in need of food assistance, with many resorting to negative coping mechanisms. The Government continues to face massive challenges, including a deepening economic crisis and the urgent need for social and fiscal reform. Without medium- to long-term interventions, more people will require humanitarian assistance in the months and years to come.

The proposed protracted relief and recovery operation (PRRO) builds on the activities and lessons learned from emergency operation 200765. It is informed by assessments, evaluations and participatory consultations, which have led to a refinement of the program strategy and the choice of transfer modalities. WFP will address the food needs of the most vulnerable people in eastern Ukraine while gradually supporting early recovery. 

The operation is aligned with WFP’s Strategic Plan (2017–2021) and gender and protection policies and guidelines. It is guided by Sustainable Development Goals 2 and 17, fostering partnerships and national plans and strategies to achieve zero hunger.
The operation is in line with the United Nations Development Assistance Framework; contributes to the Government’s Single and Comprehensive Strategy and Action Plan for Agriculture and Rural Development in Ukraine for 2015–2020 by enhancing food security and monitoring systems; and is aligned with national social protection schemes. It also builds on the priorities of the humanitarian response plan and national recovery plans.

Under planned PRRO, over the period January-December 2017, WFP will provide food assistance to 220,000 food insecure people in conflict-affected eastern Ukraine through a combination of food in kind and cash based transfers.

project_text:
Improving the protection environment for highly vulnerable, displaced conflict-affected households in Iraq DRC aims to provide a comprehensive remedial protection program to support vulnerable groups across the displacement spectrum and increase community-led protection mechanisms in Iraq. DRC Protection services support a full-cluster approach that aligns with the following objectives of the protection cluster and HRP:
Objective 1) Provide protection assistance, including community-based support, for highly vulnerable displaced persons living in camp and non-camp settings, thereby enabling them to enjoy their rights
Objective 2) Provide protection assistance, including community-based support, for highly vulnerable persons, to facilitate voluntary, safe, non-discriminatory and sustainable returns
Objective 3) Deliver immediate support to newly displaced persons by facilitating access to safety and providing protection assistance
Objective 4) Provide assistance to vulnerable individuals living in mixed populations areas with support to access government social protection systems, and assist with the provision of other specialised protection services.
 
DRC protection services seek to align with the following Strategic Objectives of the Humanitarian Response Plan:
Strategic Objective 1: Support highly vulnerable displaced families living in camps and sub-standard accommodation by providing services and assistance packages
Strategic Objective 2: Support highly vulnerable displaced families who are willing to return to their homes, but are unable to do so without assistance by providing package at their place of displacement when they return home. 
Strategic Objective 4: Support highly vulnerable people inadequately covered under the social protection floor by providing assistance packages and facilitating access to services.

This will be achieved through promotion of self-reliance and livelihood enhancement projects including agricultural/livestock support, vocational training and cash based interventions. 

The proposed project objectives are in line with refugees response plan outcome  and outcome 2 (Displaced populations, refugees, returnees and host communities meet their basic needs and/or access basic services while increasing their self-reliance) women and children represents 84% of the total beneficiaries. The project will adopt a bottom up participatory approach to ensure community ownership towards promotion of community self reliance. This approach also guarantees the principles of accountability to the affected population. The project will give particular attention to strengthen household income to build resilience. Different gender and age groups needs will be integrated in the course of the project implementation. In addition, the project will consider the likelihoods of negative impact on environment and mitigation strategies. Monitoring, evaluation and learning system will be put in place to ensure that not only the project beneficiaries’ needs are fulfilled, but also are of relevance, cost effective and with an efficient service delivery mechanism. The project will coordinate, document and share the learning’s with RCF, TAGS and work within the strategic approach of RCF.

destinationObjects_Project.name: Providing food security in the most vulnerable, conflict affected and hard to reach areas of the Eastern Ukraine, through daily home delivery of high caloric ready hot food to isolated, home-bound, immobile seniors and provision of  ready meals to highly vulnerable mobile seniors at the Canteens.
project_text:
Providing food security in the most vulnerable, conflict affected and hard to reach areas of the Eastern Ukraine, through daily home delivery of high caloric ready hot food to isolated, home-bound, immobile seniors and provision of  ready meals to highly vulnerable mobile seniors at the Canteens. Supreme objective of the given proposal is ensuring access to high caloric, ready food intake to the exceptionally vulnerable, elderly men and women of the Eastern Ukraine, those who are unable to prepare food for themselves due to age and health related conditions.
Humanitarian agencies mostly distribute food baskets. What is vastly overlooked is the program ensuring proper food intake for persons who are unable to prepare their own meals especially home-bound (often bed-bound), single, isolated seniors residing in in the most vulnerable conflict affected and hard to reach areas of the Eastern Ukraine. 
The proposed project will ensure daily provision of the ready, high caloric food intake to the elderly beneficiaries:  1000 home-bound beneficiaries will be delivered  high caloric ready food once a day (7 times a week - via mobile groups) and 1000 canteen beneficiaries will be served hot food once a day (5 times a week) for the duration of at least 8 months. 
PAH is coordinating its humanitarian activities with the actors operating in the target locations.

destinationObjects_Project.name: Emergency upgrade and repair of vulnerable households’ substandard shelters in the Gaza Strip
project_text:
Emergency upgrade and repair of vulnerable households’ substandard shelters in the Gaza Strip The aim of this project is to assist acutely vulnerable households living in substandard shelter to access adequate and safe shelters in the Gaza Strip and strengthen their capacity to cope with future shocks through a community based approach

The project will establish a shelter self-repair / upgrade mechanism through provision of conditional cash. In addition, close engagement with communities through Community Protection and Preparedness Committees (CPPC) will enable beneficiaries to increase their Knowledge, Attitudes and Practices (KAP) in shelter reparation, protection and preparedness to future shocks.

The project has been designed to take into account the specific needs of men and women, as well of vulnerable groups such as children, the elderly, persons with disability (PWDs) and the chronically ill. Through fully fledged community engagement and accountability tools, they will be able to express their views and concerns from the project onset to ensure assistance is tailored to their needs, and will then receive increased support throughout project implementation. 

In order to maximize beneficiaries involvement, ACTED and MA’AN will capitalize on the expertise gained during former project by involving CPPCs throughout the project implementation, by giving them a crucial role in beneficiary selection, project monitoring, community outreach and project evaluation. Eventually, accountability to beneficiaries will be ensured by a fully-fledged Complaint Response Mechanism, in line with ACTED standard procedures across all its interventions.

This action is in line with the result 1 of the Shelter Cluster 2016 HRP  “Ensure access for women, girls, boys and elderly men to a basic level of adequate shelter” aiming at achieving the strategic objective 2 “Ensure acutely vulnerable Palestinians under occupation in Gaza and the West Bank have access to essential services”

reportDetails_organization: United States of America, Government of; United States of America, Government of
project_text:
Improving short-term and long-term food availability and livelihoods access in Western Equatoria, Western Bahr el Ghazal, Jonglei, Warrap, Upper Nile and Lakes states through investment in food production assets, and utilization and strengthening of local capacities. To provide immediate food assistance to insecure individuals in Greater Equatoria, Western Bahr el Ghazal, Jonglei, Warrap, Upper Nile and Lakes states, while working with communities to invest in long term food security interventions.
To provide immediate food assistance, ACTED plans to make unconditional cash transfers, conditional cash transfers , and restricted cash vouchers. Conditional cash transfers will not only improve purchasing power of beneficiaries, but will also contribute to creation, construction and rehabilitation of key livelihood assets such as water catchments and dykes to manage floods. Restricted cash will focus on purchase of livelihood inputs and assets such as seeds and tools to enable beneficiaries invest on their lands thereby increasing amount of land planted, and addressing the challenge of seeds scarcity. 
Long term investment on productive assets will also be achieved through resilience programming. ACTED will adopt the APFS model to encourage transfer of knowledge and skills in modern farming techniques, encourage community engagement through participatory risk assessments, toward participatory planning and joint ownership of resources. Such an investment will be pegged on utilization of local capacities and knowledge, which will then be reinforced through interactive sessions toward realizing improved livelihoods, reduced gender inequality, inclusive economic and social growth, and overall transformation of communities.

project_text:
Provision of nutrition sensitive, targeted seasonal food assistance to families with PLW and/or children aged 6-23 months WFP supports the Government, and in particular the Ministry of Health, in the implementation of the National Nutrition Policy and protocols to reduce chronic malnutrition to acceptable levels. In line with the Government strategic priorities, WFP will be exploring the possibilities to replace nutritious foods with targeted seasonal food assistance using cash-based transfers to prevent chronic malnutrition in the areas of the country where prevalence is the highest. WFP will base its intervention on the results of the evaluations of similar projects ongoing in the country.

WFP will also build on the lessons learnt in undertaking behavioural change communication sessions to accompany the targeted seasonal food assistance in order to maximize its impact. A strong collaboration with the Ministry of Health is planned in order to make the transition from food to CBT the most efficient and sustainable possible.

?	Focus Areas 
This strategic outcome will be supported by WFP’s engagement towards the Government to prevent chronic malnutrition through seasonal transfer programmes. The primary focus of this outcome is ‘Resilience Building’.

project_text:
Sustained full response WASH services in Mamilyan Camp with improvements in access to WASH facilities for disabled people and grey water drainage; Rehabilitation and construction of boreholes in Sinjar City 1 - JEN aims to continue to improve the personal hygiene and environmental
sanitation in Mamilyan Camp through the continued provision of a full WASH
package to all camp residents (partial funding likely); including bi-monthly
distribution of hygiene kits (consumable), annual distribution of WASH kit items
(durable) via a voucher to be used at a temporary shop in the camp, maintenance of
household level water and sewage systems, hygiene promotion activities with emphasis of engagement and targeting of women, solid waste removal and desludging of septic pits and quality/quantity monitoring of
water. During 2017 JEN would like to accomplish two additional projects in
Mamilyan Camp (unfunded): providing additional WASH support to families with
disabled members in order to improve access to toilets and shower facilities, this
will involve installing access ramps, pull bars and handicapped toilets on a case by
case basis and install fencing along the open grey water channel which often
becomes blocked leading to poor drainage of waste and storm waters from the
camp.

2 – JEN aims to restore sustainable water delivery in Sinjar City through the
rehabilitation and pipe extension of one existing but war-damaged borehole and the
construction of a new borehole. (unfunded)

destinationObjects_Project.name: Country Strategic Plan for food assistance to the poor and severely food insecure population in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip
project_text:
Country Strategic Plan for food assistance to the poor and severely food insecure population in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip WFP is committed to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and is guided by a strategic, programmatic and governance instrument to operationalize its plan and achieve its project objectives to: 
• End Hunger by protecting access to food and by improving dietary diversity;
• Support the implementation of the SDGs by enhancing the capacities of national institutions to implement food security strategies and operations;
This project directly contributes to strategic objectives two and three of the Humanitarian Response Plan 2018 2020, by meeting the basic food needs of severely vulnerable Palestinians and by improving their dietary diversity. 
WFP’s interventions focus on high food insecurity levels, including the malnutrition levels recorded by national surveys. By assisting the poor and severely food insecure Palestinian households in Gaza and Bedouin and herding communities in West Bank’s Area C, and by disseminating information on food and nutrition practices, WFP addresses the basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians and tackles one of the or root causes of some of the food insecurity levels recorded by the government institutions.
These interventions aim at improving the overall food security levels including nutrition and health status of the vulnerable Palestinians and therefore at increasing their coping abilities to sudden shocks in the market for access to food. 
The project also contributes to the Food Security Sector’s three objectives as well as to the National Policy Agenda 2017-2022 (policies on escaping poverty and strengthening social protection as well as meeting the basic needs of the communities) to ensure that the vulnerable Palestinians households basic food needs are met, by assisting households in enhancing their food security levels and by strengthening national institutions in implementing food security strategies and social security safety net programs to best identify and target food insecure and vulnerable Palestinians.

destinationObjects_Project.name: Humanitarian Support to Protect Palestinians in the West Bank (including East Jerusalem) from Forcible Transfer.
reportDetails_organization: European Commission's Humanitarian Aid and Civil Protection Department
project_text: Humanitarian Support to Protect Palestinians in the West Bank (including East Jerusalem) from Forcible Transfer. This Project contributes to the protection of Palestinians in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, from forcible transfer (FT) through a protection-centered approach to humanitarian responses incorporating: emergency support (cash/in-kind); provision of material assistance and essential services; legal aid; advocacy; and community empowerment.  188 communities will be specifically targeted each year for medium-term resilience-building support based on their vulnerability to FT, initially assessed using the OCHA VPP, supplemented with in-depth protection assessments taking into consideration the specific needs of women, men, children, elderly, and people with disability. Emergency and legal aid activities will be implemented across the whole West Bank, based on needs and referrals. Within the framework of the HCT, the Project supports the implementation of the Area C Policy Framework and coordinates with other actors meeting humanitarian needs of communities at risk of FT. The Project provides a mechanism to respond to OCHA triggers and ICCG coordination of response to demolitions. Shelter, WASH, Education, Health, FSS, legal responses, settler violence interventions and advocacy will be coordinated through the relevant Clusters/WGs. The Project is built on an integrated protection approach envisaged to contribute to all HRP objectives: S1:  The rights of Palestinians living under occupation are protected, respected and promoted; S2:   The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of essential services; S3:   The ability of vulnerable Palestinians to cope with the protracted crisis, including environmental threats, is supported, while solutions to violations and other root causes of threats and shocks are pursued. The Project further contributes to the three Shelter Cluster objectives (1. Support to the displaced; 2. Support to vulnerable households; 3. Increased response capacity).

WV Monitoring, Evaluation and Accountability team:
 WV will ensure its partners adhere to the do no harm principles and this will be monitored through WV’s internal M&E systems. Conflict sensitivity will be considered in beneficiary selection ensuring that there is equitable access to services by the different population and religious subgroups in Mosul city. WV will set up humanitarian accountability systems at project sites level, these will enable beneficiaries to receive information on the project and to give the feedback through a hotline, suggestion box and during focus group discussion. WV will monitor the project implementation regularly and train all staff and community groups on the WVI child Protection policy and the humanitarian imperatives. WV will also empower the community and will ensure that the community is aware of the WVI complaint response mechanism.

project_text:
Specialized GBV Prevention and Response Services for Conflict-affected Women and children in Iraq Overall Objectives:  To improve access to quality life-saving GBV prevention and response services for women and girls who are survivors or at risk of GBV, through age appropriate and survivor centered approaches. 

Pervasive GBV abuses against women and girls, in particular sexual violence, family violence, sexual exploitation, forced and child marriage persist.  Fears of harassment, reprisal and stigmatization, including honour killing, remain real barriers to seeking services, justice and protection for GBV survivors. The consequences of GBV require a sustained and multi-sector responses, including specialized case management services and prevention and risk mitigation strategies to ensure the safety and dignity of women and girls and reduce risks of GBV. 

This project aims to address the broad and critical needs of conflict-affected women and girls survivors or at risk of GBV and strengthen the protective environment through case management, psychosocial support and community-based prevention programmes and activities.

Specific Objectives:
1.	Provide GBV prevention and response services for highly vulnerable women and children, including community-based mitigation of GBV, in camps, non-camps settings and for those newly returning to their places of origin, to ensure their rights, safety and dignity.
2.	Provide specialized GBV case management and PSS services and protection assistance for survivors and women and girls who are at risk of GBV, including returnees, stayees, IDPs, host community and those living in mixed population areas of return.
3.	Provide emergency GBV response and protection assistance to newly displaced women and girls.
4.	Provide critical services and assistance to vulnerable women and children in areas of return to access government provided social assistance and support systems.

destinationObjects_Project.name: Provision of shelter assistance to internally displaced and conflicted affected communities in Ukraine
project_text:
Provision of shelter assistance to internally displaced and conflicted affected communities in Ukraine The overall aim of the project is to improve living conditions of the affected population, support returns of IDPs to the places of their previous residence and, to prevent further displacement of those who are the most affected with on going conflict. Delivery priority will be to populations at the line of contact and in non Government controlled areas of Ukraine.
In continuity with the 2017 plan, UNHCR objectives include:

-   Urgent assistance in repairing damaged houses and apartments on both sides of the line of contact.
-   Provision of emergency shelter kits.
-   Procurement and distribution of NFIs to address individuals’ urgent needs and reduce long term vulnerability.
-   Distribution of NFI kits as a part of the response in emergency situations.
-   Winterization support – provision of winter clothes, coal, firewood or, if applicable, cash assistance for winterization purposes (fuel for heating).
-   Logistics and operational support will be provided in storage and delivery of necessary shelter and NFI assistance.

As part of its exit strategy (outside the humanitarian scope and set at 0 budget), UNHCR will be engaged in two additional activities not included in the 2017 plan: 

-   Protection guidance to state and development actors involved in the development of pilot projects on social housing.
-   Advocacy interventions for IDPs’ access to social housing.

reportDetails_organization: France, Government of; World Food Programme
project_text:
Country Strategic Plan for food assistance to the poor and severely food insecure population in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip WFP is committed to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and is guided by a strategic, programmatic and governance instrument to operationalize its plan and achieve its project objectives to: 
• End Hunger by protecting access to food and by improving dietary diversity;
• Support the implementation of the SDGs by enhancing the capacities of national institutions to implement food security strategies and operations;
This project directly contributes to strategic objectives two and three of the Humanitarian Response Plan 2018 2020, by meeting the basic food needs of severely vulnerable Palestinians and by improving their dietary diversity. 
WFP’s interventions focus on high food insecurity levels, including the malnutrition levels recorded by national surveys. By assisting the poor and severely food insecure Palestinian households in Gaza and Bedouin and herding communities in West Bank’s Area C, and by disseminating information on food and nutrition practices, WFP addresses the basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians and tackles one of the or root causes of some of the food insecurity levels recorded by the government institutions.
These interventions aim at improving the overall food security levels including nutrition and health status of the vulnerable Palestinians and therefore at increasing their coping abilities to sudden shocks in the market for access to food. 
The project also contributes to the Food Security Sector’s three objectives as well as to the National Policy Agenda 2017-2022 (policies on escaping poverty and strengthening social protection as well as meeting the basic needs of the communities) to ensure that the vulnerable Palestinians households basic food needs are met, by assisting households in enhancing their food security levels and by strengthening national institutions in implementing food security strategies and social security safety net programs to best identify and target food insecure and vulnerable Palestinians.

reportDetails_organization: Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
project_text: Humanitarian Support to Protect Palestinians in the West Bank (including East Jerusalem) from Forcible Transfer. This Project contributes to the protection of Palestinians in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, from forcible transfer (FT) through a protection-centered approach to humanitarian responses incorporating: emergency support (cash/in-kind); provision of material assistance and essential services; legal aid; advocacy; and community empowerment.  188 communities will be specifically targeted each year for medium-term resilience-building support based on their vulnerability to FT, initially assessed using the OCHA VPP, supplemented with in-depth protection assessments taking into consideration the specific needs of women, men, children, elderly, and people with disability. Emergency and legal aid activities will be implemented across the whole West Bank, based on needs and referrals. Within the framework of the HCT, the Project supports the implementation of the Area C Policy Framework and coordinates with other actors meeting humanitarian needs of communities at risk of FT. The Project provides a mechanism to respond to OCHA triggers and ICCG coordination of response to demolitions. Shelter, WASH, Education, Health, FSS, legal responses, settler violence interventions and advocacy will be coordinated through the relevant Clusters/WGs. The Project is built on an integrated protection approach envisaged to contribute to all HRP objectives: S1:  The rights of Palestinians living under occupation are protected, respected and promoted; S2:   The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of essential services; S3:   The ability of vulnerable Palestinians to cope with the protracted crisis, including environmental threats, is supported, while solutions to violations and other root causes of threats and shocks are pursued. The Project further contributes to the three Shelter Cluster objectives (1. Support to the displaced; 2. Support to vulnerable households; 3. Increased response capacity).

project_text: Emergency assistance to vulnerable people affected by natural disasters To provide comprehensive shelter to IDPs and host communities affected by natural disasters, as well as Burundian returnees from Tanzania. Activities include: i) preposition shelter and Non-Food non-food item (NFI) kits  to repair affected houses in disaster-prone areas, respond to emergencies and support affected populations; ii) provision of rental and shelter repair cash grants through bank and/or phone transfers, reaching 1,000 of the most vulnerable of the 26,000 IDP households living in urban areas throughout the country; iii) seek durable shelter solutions for the 3,000 people (600 households) living in collective sites by improving traditional construction mechanisms; iv) provision of semi-permanent shelter, repair shelter kits, cash grants and NFI kits to 15% of the most vulnerable returnees from Tanzania, targeting the provinces of Makamba, Rutana, Ruyigi and Muyinga, where the biggest returnee population is concentrated in Burundi; v) train civil servants and host communities using a shelter risk reduction approach; and vi) conduct sensitization sessions to increase awareness of safe construction mechanisms aiming to prevent landslides and the destruction of houses due to poor construction techniques and usage of low-quality materials.

project_text:
Coordinated and multi-sectoral Responses to Address the Needs of  Vulnerable Women and Girls  in Gaza The objective of the project is to 

a) To Improve vulnerable women's and girls' access to income generation opportunities and quality multi-sectoral services in Gaza
b) To improve the quality of GBV services provided to vulnerable women and girls. 

In the second year of the project,  UN Women will capitalize on the achievements and lessons learnt of the first year, supporting partners to improve quality, accessibility and responsiveness of the services to the needs of those who are most vulnerable. The project will aim at reaching more vulnerable groups while at the same time provide deepened support to certain groups that benefited from the first year of implementation. UN Women will also work with partners in the second year to involve men who will participate in the HEforShe dialogues in becoming advocates for GBV prevention in their local communities.  The project second year will also benefit  from the development of the peer review system of professional and ethical standards in cooperation with PC, GBV sub cluster and MHPPSWG which will be piloted in the second year of implementation. UN Women will also assess the benefit of combining GBV services with cash for work programming and the impact this has over beneficiaries' lives and  design an expansion of the cash for work in the second year accordingly. 

The project responds to HRP Strategic Objective 2:   The basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians living under occupation are met through the provision of essential services, in accordance with the rights of protected persons under IHL.

It will directly target children, adolescents but also their parents, and to a larger extent their community. It will especially benefit to girls and women by taking into consideration gender specificities at all stages

Objective 1: Provide specialized protection support to highly vulnerable displaced persons living in camp and non-camp settings to access services and exercise their rights

Objective 3: Deliver immediate support to newly displaced persons by providing specialized and targeted protection assistance  

Objective 4: Provide assistance to vulnerable individuals living in mixed populations areas with support to access government social protection systems, and assist with the provision of other specialised protection services

project_text:
Niger Transitional Interim Country Strategic Plan This T-ICSP is in line with SDG 2 and 17 and aims to contribute to the following strategic outcomes: -	Crisis-affected populations, including refugees and IDPs, in targeted areas are able to meet their basic food and nutrition needs during and in the aftermath of crises. 
-	Food insecure school-age children, in targeted regions have access to adequate and nutritious food all year-round.
-	Vulnerable groups including children, pregnant women and adolescent girls in targeted areas have enhanced nutritional status all year-round.

project_text:
Country Strategic Plan for food assistance to the poor and severely food insecure population in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip WFP is committed to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and is guided by a strategic, programmatic and governance instrument to operationalize its plan and achieve its project objectives to: 
• End Hunger by protecting access to food and by improving dietary diversity;
• Support the implementation of the SDGs by enhancing the capacities of national institutions to implement food security strategies and operations;
This project directly contributes to strategic objectives two and three of the Humanitarian Response Plan 2018 2020, by meeting the basic food needs of severely vulnerable Palestinians and by improving their dietary diversity. 
WFP’s interventions focus on high food insecurity levels, including the malnutrition levels recorded by national surveys. By assisting the poor and severely food insecure Palestinian households in Gaza and Bedouin and herding communities in West Bank’s Area C, and by disseminating information on food and nutrition practices, WFP addresses the basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians and tackles one of the or root causes of some of the food insecurity levels recorded by the government institutions.
These interventions aim at improving the overall food security levels including nutrition and health status of the vulnerable Palestinians and therefore at increasing their coping abilities to sudden shocks in the market for access to food. 
The project also contributes to the Food Security Sector’s three objectives as well as to the National Policy Agenda 2017-2022 (policies on escaping poverty and strengthening social protection as well as meeting the basic needs of the communities) to ensure that the vulnerable Palestinians households basic food needs are met, by assisting households in enhancing their food security levels and by strengthening national institutions in implementing food security strategies and social security safety net programs to best identify and target food insecure and vulnerable Palestinians.

reportDetails_organization: European Commission's Humanitarian Aid and Civil Protection Department
project_text: Renforcement de la coordination et du plaidoyer humanitaire au Tchad Le projet vise à renforcer la mobilisation et la coordination  de la réponse humanitaire au Tchad afin de sauver des vies et protéger les personnes affectées par les crises, notamment celles affectées par la crise du lac Tchad. Une coordination humanitaire efficace et performante permet aux acteurs humanitaires de mieux identifier et répondre aux priorités humanitaires. OCHA jouera un rôle clé dans la création d'espaces d'échange et d'analyse d'informations, pour mieux guider les actions humanitaires, répondre aux besoins les plus aigus et être mieux préparé face aux urgences soudaines. Le projet permettra également d’assurer conjointement avec la communauté humanitaire le plaidoyer en faveur du respect des principes humanitaires, de la protection des civils, de l'accès humanitaire et pour la mobilisation et l'allocation efficace de ressources humanitaires. OCHA continuera de jouer  également un rôle moteur dans le renforcement du lien entre les acteurs humanitaires et de développement et la transformation de la réponse humanitaire, en lien avec les engagements pris au Sommet mondial de l'action humanitaire de 2016 et ceci à travers la nouvelle façon de travailler (NWOW).OCHA continue de mettre en oeuvre sa mission à travers ses fonctions clés (Coordination, Gestion de l' information et plaidoyer). Un accent a été mis sur l' opérationalisation de la nouvelle façon de travailler, la mise en oeuvre des plans d' action de la redevabilité envers les populations affectées (AAP) et la PSEA, la préparation aux urgences et le plaidoyer pour plus de visibilités et de mobilisation de ressources pour les différentes crises au Tchad (Bassin du Lac Tchad, insécurité alimentaire et malnutrition, épidémie sanitaires). De même, OCHA à travers sa participation dans le groupe de travail sur le CASH, continu de faire le plaidoyer pour renforcer l' utilisation du CASH pour la réponse humanitaire dans tous les secteurs et du Cash à usage multiple (Multipurpose CASH)

destinationObjects_Project.name: Strengthening women and girls' safety and recovery in BAY
project_text:
Strengthening women and girls' safety and recovery in BAY Gender based violence remains a serious challenge within northeast Nigeria, causing more psychological imbalance for armed conflict-affected IDPs as well as returnees, especially women and girls. Displacement and continued movement of IDPs creates major protection concerns women and girls which has increased gender-based violence and access services remain a serious gap especially in hard to reach Local Governmental Areas. According to Humanitarian Response Plan, 2018, an estimated 2.4 million people have been identified to be in need of gender-based violence prevention and response across Adamawa, Borno, and Yobe states. Women and girls are often targeted while performing basic tasks such as travelling to water points, collecting firewood to cook food and going to communal latrines. They are often exposed to SEA, forced into prostitution, early marriages, and survival sex in exchange for food, their movement is restricted and basic needs are deprived. Women and girls are abducted by armed groups, are often raped and forcibly married and may be used in person borne improvised explosive device (PBIED) attacks. These women and girls, along with their children born as a result of rape, are often feared by communities and ostracized from society because they are suspected to be sympathizers of armed opposition groups. Upon their return, they require access to a full range of services to meet multiple immediate and reintegration needs as well as those of their children. Despite the consequences, families are still forcibly marrying daughters as young as 12 years old to men or members of armed opposition groups, citing poverty as the main reason. Between August 2017 and April 2018, the IRC provided case management services for over 400 gender based violence survivors in Adamawa, Borno and Yobe, indicating the high need for continued support.
 An April 2018 assessment from OCHA shows that violence against women and girls is the most widely reported protection issue (24% of all key informants). From the October 2017 OCHA assessment in Yobe, child marriage was reported to affect over a third of households in each population group in eight LGAs throughout the state, including Gujba. Additionally, according to the Nigeria HRP 2018, sexual violence, including rape, is a defining characteristic of the ongoing conflict, with 6 out of 10 women in the northeast having experienced one or more forms of GBV. Women and girls are at particular risk within the current environment, with many reports of survival sex in exchange for food, money, and freedom of movement (into and out of IDP sites). This exposes the population to increasing incidences of sexually transmitted infections including HIV, unwanted pregnancies, and obstetric fistula caused by sexual violence, leading to overall poor sexual and reproductive health outcomes. The crisis has significantly affected the dignity of women and children. This further entrenches pre-existing gender disparities. In the Global Gender Gap Index, Nigeria ranks 118th out of 144 countries.

project_text:
Country Strategic Plan for food assistance to the poor and severely food insecure population in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip WFP is committed to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and is guided by a strategic, programmatic and governance instrument to operationalize its plan and achieve its project objectives to: 
• End Hunger by protecting access to food and by improving dietary diversity;
• Support the implementation of the SDGs by enhancing the capacities of national institutions to implement food security strategies and operations;
This project directly contributes to strategic objectives two and three of the Humanitarian Response Plan 2018 2020, by meeting the basic food needs of severely vulnerable Palestinians and by improving their dietary diversity. 
WFP’s interventions focus on high food insecurity levels, including the malnutrition levels recorded by national surveys. By assisting the poor and severely food insecure Palestinian households in Gaza and Bedouin and herding communities in West Bank’s Area C, and by disseminating information on food and nutrition practices, WFP addresses the basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians and tackles one of the or root causes of some of the food insecurity levels recorded by the government institutions.
These interventions aim at improving the overall food security levels including nutrition and health status of the vulnerable Palestinians and therefore at increasing their coping abilities to sudden shocks in the market for access to food. 
The project also contributes to the Food Security Sector’s three objectives as well as to the National Policy Agenda 2017-2022 (policies on escaping poverty and strengthening social protection as well as meeting the basic needs of the communities) to ensure that the vulnerable Palestinians households basic food needs are met, by assisting households in enhancing their food security levels and by strengthening national institutions in implementing food security strategies and social security safety net programs to best identify and target food insecure and vulnerable Palestinians.

description: Humanitarian Food Assistance to the the most food insecure people during the 2018/19 lean season, including urban population (ECHO/-SF/BUD/2019/91004)
sourceObjects_Organization.name: European Commission's Humanitarian Aid and Civil Protection Department
destinationObjects_GlobalCluster.name: Food Security

destinationObjects_Cluster.name: Food Security

destinationObjects_Project.name: Lean Season Food Assistance to the most food insecure people in rural areas
reportDetails_organization: European Commission's Humanitarian Aid and Civil Protection Department
project_text:
Lean Season Food Assistance to the most food insecure people in rural areas Under this Flash Appeal, Food Security sector partners plan to address the most urgent food security needs of people in rural areas across the country, who are adversely affected by multiple crises, including last year’s poor harvest for many small-holder farmers, economic shocks and recent cholera and typhoid outbreaks. Building on the funding already received to reach an estimated 900,000 people as of January 2019 and the Government’s Food Deficit Mitigation Strategy, partners aim to expand the geographic coverage of assistance to reach an additional 700,000 people in food insecure rural communities through primarily cash-based assistance. Focus will be on the low-lying areas relying on rainfed agriculture disproportionately affected by last year’s erratic rain. Market-based interventions are viable despite the current economic stress, as essential food commodities remain available on rural as well as urban markets, according to the national market assessment conducted by WFP and partners in November 2018. 

The IPC analysis conducted in January 2019 projects that nearly 3.8 million people in rural areas are in need of urgent humanitarian assistance, including 2.9 million who are severely food insecure (IPC phase 3 or 4) and a further 900,000 people who are currently receiving humanitarian assistance, without which they would be in IPC phase 3 or above.

In the face of the high prevalence of food insecurity (IPC phase 4 and 3), and the high probability of another El Niño phenomena in 2019 (90% likelihood according to the most recent SARCOF analysis), partners will provide a specialised food ration in the form of CSB++ specifically targeting children 6-59 months and pregnant and lactating women to increase the nutritional value of the food basket provided as part of the general household ration/cash. 

Based on the findings of the national market assessment conducted by partners in November, partners will select the most appropriate transfer modality for each district (cash or in-kind). According to the latest price information, partners aim to cover approximately 80% of the targeted individuals’ daily food energy needs (based on a 2100 kcal diet) to supplement other available food sources, thus enabling households to meet their basic food and nutrition needs. 
 
In view of the high probability of another El Nino, food assistance at this juncture can be considered as an early action to prevent further deterioration of food insecurity amongst particularly households already in IPC 3 (Crises) and 4 (Emergency).

reportDetails_organization: Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
project_text: Renforcement de la coordination et du plaidoyer humanitaire au Tchad Le projet vise à renforcer la mobilisation et la coordination  de la réponse humanitaire au Tchad afin de sauver des vies et protéger les personnes affectées par les crises, notamment celles affectées par la crise du lac Tchad. Une coordination humanitaire efficace et performante permet aux acteurs humanitaires de mieux identifier et répondre aux priorités humanitaires. OCHA jouera un rôle clé dans la création d'espaces d'échange et d'analyse d'informations, pour mieux guider les actions humanitaires, répondre aux besoins les plus aigus et être mieux préparé face aux urgences soudaines. Le projet permettra également d’assurer conjointement avec la communauté humanitaire le plaidoyer en faveur du respect des principes humanitaires, de la protection des civils, de l'accès humanitaire et pour la mobilisation et l'allocation efficace de ressources humanitaires. OCHA continuera de jouer  également un rôle moteur dans le renforcement du lien entre les acteurs humanitaires et de développement et la transformation de la réponse humanitaire, en lien avec les engagements pris au Sommet mondial de l'action humanitaire de 2016 et ceci à travers la nouvelle façon de travailler (NWOW).OCHA continue de mettre en oeuvre sa mission à travers ses fonctions clés (Coordination, Gestion de l' information et plaidoyer). Un accent a été mis sur l' opérationalisation de la nouvelle façon de travailler, la mise en oeuvre des plans d' action de la redevabilité envers les populations affectées (AAP) et la PSEA, la préparation aux urgences et le plaidoyer pour plus de visibilités et de mobilisation de ressources pour les différentes crises au Tchad (Bassin du Lac Tchad, insécurité alimentaire et malnutrition, épidémie sanitaires). De même, OCHA à travers sa participation dans le groupe de travail sur le CASH, continu de faire le plaidoyer pour renforcer l' utilisation du CASH pour la réponse humanitaire dans tous les secteurs et du Cash à usage multiple (Multipurpose CASH)

destinationObjects_Project.name: Mitigate identified protection risks, reduce vulnerabilities and enhance the protection of displaced persons, returnees and conflict affected host communities in Syria through integrated, community based protection activities to prevent and respond to rights violations.
destinationObjects_Emergency.name: Syrian Arab Republic - Civil Unrest (from 2012)
project_text:
Mitigate identified protection risks, reduce vulnerabilities and enhance the protection of displaced persons, returnees and conflict affected host communities in Syria through integrated, community based protection activities to prevent and respond to rights violations. The project aims to assist IDPs, returnees and crisis-affected communities by fostering an improved protection environment through the provision of community-based protection services. Protection interventions include 1) legal counselling and assistance 2) protection monitoring, referrals and information sharing on services 3)  social protection and support on PSS; GBV prevention and response programmes 4) child protection; 5) case management; 6) provision of in kind assistance covering basic needs and programmes of elderly and persons with disabilities; 7) non-formal education support for children at risk; 8) social protection through small-scale vocational skills training and socio-economic support specifically directed to the most vulnerable individuals, ; 9) campaigns and awareness  session including on mine risk education for communities targeting women, men, boys and girls and; 10) capacity building of first responders working in communities, volunteers, partners and government counterparts to provide better protection services. Legal aid interventions will facilitate access to civil/HLP documentation for IDPs and returnees and provide support in legal matters related to GBV, CP and other protection issues. Support to community initiatives will also be implemented engaging communities to address their own protection concerns. Intervention in the context of refugee returnees will focus on, legal aid, coordination with government counterparts and stakeholders, information management and return tracking systems and sub – district profiling to better inform return programming and interventions. In addition, the project will support coordinated protection interventions with UNHCR Syria continuing to lead Protection Sector.
Accountability to affected population in the project will be realized through participatory engagement of communities and outreach programmes conducted through community volunteers’ network. Over 2844 outreach volunteers and 112 CC were mobilized in 2018 and this project will build on this approach, to ensure a continuous link with communities, including to receive feedback on project programmes.

Through the project intervention approximately 3.35 million IDPs, returnees and crises affected individuals in host communities (70.5%, 15.5% and 14% respectively) will be reached in government and non-government controlled areas redressing their protection concerns. In addition 4,140 humanitarian workers and local authority staff will be trained and 624 communities assessed. 30% of the project beneficiaries are girls, 25% are boys, 26% are women, and 15% are men and 2% elderly women and 2% elderly men.

project_text:
Securing of basic needs in physical and mental health of people affected by conflict in Ukraine, 2019-2020 (funded by German Federal Foreign Office) Overall context of crises in Ukraine
The human toll of the armed conflict in eastern Ukraine is critical, with 4.4 million people affected by the crisis, of whom 3.4 million require humanitarian assistance and protection. The shelling of urban areas and civilian infrastructure means that 60 per cent of 200,000 people living along the 457-kilometre ‘contact line’ in the Government-controlled area (GCA) are affected by shelling regularly, and almost 40 per cent are affected every day. There is just under a million individual crossings of the ‘contact line’ each month, which is rapidly becoming one of the most mine contaminated stretches of land in the world. Food insecurity has doubled since 2016, with 1.2 million people food insecure, and there are escalating cases of multi-drug resistant TB, HIV and even polio. HIV prevalence among pregnant women in conflict-affected oblasts is significantly higher than the national average. These impacts are aggravated by Ukraine’s extremely harsh winter, severe restrictions on humanitarian access and limited livelihood opportunities for those affected by the crisis. As hopes of a political solution have waned, so have people’s savings and their ability to cope. Four years into the crisis, millions of people, including 1.6 million internally displaced persons (IDPs), half of whom are the elderly, are being forced to make impossible choices between food, medicine, shelter, heating or their children’s education. The unique demographics of the crisis in Ukraine is that the elderly make up almost 30 per cent of people in need. Those who are most vulnerable are increasingly resorting to risky means to cope, including survival sex, trafficking and alcoholism. Today, the dire humanitarian crisis in eastern Ukraine is protracted and complex, whilst the response is severely underfunded and largely forgotten by the international community.
(HNO2019)
Logic of project intervention is based on Theory of Change and aimed to contribute to resolve main problem of affected population by elimination of core causes according to following program concept:
Main problem 	
Basic needs of affected population in health are not secured
Resolved if:
basic needs of affected people  in  mental and physical health are secured
Core cause 1	
Lack of access of beneficiaries to needed goods and services
Eliminated if:
Access to necessary goods and services or to appropriate product/service providers is ensured. Beneficiaries have appropriate conditions to keep goods.
Core cause 2
Lack of purchasing ability of beneficiaries  to cover basic medical needs
Eliminated if:
Beneficiaries have financial resources to procure necessary medical goods and services

The intervention is to be in GCA with more focus on 20 km contact line. 
According to HNO2019, the overall problematic in the area of intervention described as following: 

*Around 1.3 million people within 20 km of the contact line in need of life-saving and essential health services (HNO 2019).
*Physiological signs of distress, such as difficulty sleeping, and emotional difficulties, including grief, fear and crying for no reason (2018 IMC MHPSS Assessment)
Core causes related to access: 
*According to the Health Cluster, two-thirds of households do not know where to access psycho-social services, and 17 per cent of rural households report that there is no place to access services in their settlements (2018 REACH Winter Assessment)
* Lack of access to medications and treatments remains life-threatening for many patients, who have diabetes, cancer, and cardio-vascular conditions, including hypertension, which affects over 50 per cent of people of over 50 years old in the conflict-affected area. (HNO 2019)
*The conflict has isolated rural GCA health facilities from major health centers located in urban areas in NGCA due to increased distances, travel times to essential health services and impeded access to referral hospitals and pharmacies (HNO 2019)
Core cause related to purchasing ability: 
*Conflict affected older people are particularly at risk. Most rely solely on their pension to cover basic cost of living, and this is often insufficient to cover food, medicines and utilities. (2018 Baseline report, HelpAge International)

Framework of project intervention for 2019-2020 to eliminate core causes and contribute to resolve main problems is following:
Overall goal: Basic needs of 12080 IDPs and residents of buffer zone are secured

Physical Health
Outcome: Beneficiary has improved or stabilized physical health condition. 
Output: Beneficiary obtained conditional and restricted cash/voucher for life-saving medicine and services amounting 1000 UAH per months 4 times or 4000 UAH as one payment.

Securing the basic needs of especially vulnerable conflict-affected people in Ukraine 2018-2019 Securing of basic needs in physical and mental health of people affected by conflict in Ukraine, 2019-2020 (funded by German Federal Foreign Office) Overall context of crises in Ukraine
The human toll of the armed conflict in eastern Ukraine is critical, with 4.4 million people affected by the crisis, of whom 3.4 million require humanitarian assistance and protection. The shelling of urban areas and civilian infrastructure means that 60 per cent of 200,000 people living along the 457-kilometre ‘contact line’ in the Government-controlled area (GCA) are affected by shelling regularly, and almost 40 per cent are affected every day. There is just under a million individual crossings of the ‘contact line’ each month, which is rapidly becoming one of the most mine contaminated stretches of land in the world. Food insecurity has doubled since 2016, with 1.2 million people food insecure, and there are escalating cases of multi-drug resistant TB, HIV and even polio. HIV prevalence among pregnant women in conflict-affected oblasts is significantly higher than the national average. These impacts are aggravated by Ukraine’s extremely harsh winter, severe restrictions on humanitarian access and limited livelihood opportunities for those affected by the crisis. As hopes of a political solution have waned, so have people’s savings and their ability to cope. Four years into the crisis, millions of people, including 1.6 million internally displaced persons (IDPs), half of whom are the elderly, are being forced to make impossible choices between food, medicine, shelter, heating or their children’s education. The unique demographics of the crisis in Ukraine is that the elderly make up almost 30 per cent of people in need. Those who are most vulnerable are increasingly resorting to risky means to cope, including survival sex, trafficking and alcoholism. Today, the dire humanitarian crisis in eastern Ukraine is protracted and complex, whilst the response is severely underfunded and largely forgotten by the international community.

Basic needs of affected population in health are not secured

basic needs of affected people  in  mental and physical health are secured
Core cause 1	
Lack of access of beneficiaries to needed goods and services
Eliminated if:
Access to necessary goods and services or to appropriate product/service providers is ensured. Beneficiaries have appropriate conditions to keep goods.
Core cause 2
Lack of purchasing ability of beneficiaries  to cover basic medical needs

Beneficiaries have financial resources to procure necessary medical goods and services

The intervention is to be in GCA with more focus on 20 km contact line.

*Around 1.3 million people within 20 km of the contact line in need of life-saving and essential health services (HNO 2019).

*According to the Health Cluster, two-thirds of households do not know where to access psycho-social services, and 17 per cent of rural households report that there is no place to access services in their settlements (2018 REACH Winter Assessment)

Core cause related to purchasing ability: 
*Conflict affected older people are particularly at risk. Most rely solely on their pension to cover basic cost of living, and this is often insufficient to cover food, medicines and utilities. (2018 Baseline report, HelpAge International)

destinationObjects_Emergency.name: Syrian Arab Republic - Civil Unrest (from 2012)
project_text:
Mitigate identified protection risks, reduce vulnerabilities and enhance the protection of displaced persons, returnees and conflict affected host communities in Syria through integrated, community based protection activities to prevent and respond to rights violations. The project aims to assist IDPs, returnees and crisis-affected communities by fostering an improved protection environment through the provision of community-based protection services. Protection interventions include 1) legal counselling and assistance 2) protection monitoring, referrals and information sharing on services 3)  social protection and support on PSS; GBV prevention and response programmes 4) child protection; 5) case management; 6) provision of in kind assistance covering basic needs and programmes of elderly and persons with disabilities; 7) non-formal education support for children at risk; 8) social protection through small-scale vocational skills training and socio-economic support specifically directed to the most vulnerable individuals, ; 9) campaigns and awareness  session including on mine risk education for communities targeting women, men, boys and girls and; 10) capacity building of first responders working in communities, volunteers, partners and government counterparts to provide better protection services. Legal aid interventions will facilitate access to civil/HLP documentation for IDPs and returnees and provide support in legal matters related to GBV, CP and other protection issues. Support to community initiatives will also be implemented engaging communities to address their own protection concerns. Intervention in the context of refugee returnees will focus on, legal aid, coordination with government counterparts and stakeholders, information management and return tracking systems and sub – district profiling to better inform return programming and interventions. In addition, the project will support coordinated protection interventions with UNHCR Syria continuing to lead Protection Sector.
Accountability to affected population in the project will be realized through participatory engagement of communities and outreach programmes conducted through community volunteers’ network. Over 2844 outreach volunteers and 112 CC were mobilized in 2018 and this project will build on this approach, to ensure a continuous link with communities, including to receive feedback on project programmes.

Through the project intervention approximately 3.35 million IDPs, returnees and crises affected individuals in host communities (70.5%, 15.5% and 14% respectively) will be reached in government and non-government controlled areas redressing their protection concerns. In addition 4,140 humanitarian workers and local authority staff will be trained and 624 communities assessed. 30% of the project beneficiaries are girls, 25% are boys, 26% are women, and 15% are men and 2% elderly women and 2% elderly men.

reportDetails_organization: Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
project_text: Renforcement de la coordination et du plaidoyer humanitaire au Tchad Le projet vise à renforcer la mobilisation et la coordination  de la réponse humanitaire au Tchad afin de sauver des vies et protéger les personnes affectées par les crises, notamment celles affectées par la crise du lac Tchad. Une coordination humanitaire efficace et performante permet aux acteurs humanitaires de mieux identifier et répondre aux priorités humanitaires. OCHA jouera un rôle clé dans la création d'espaces d'échange et d'analyse d'informations, pour mieux guider les actions humanitaires, répondre aux besoins les plus aigus et être mieux préparé face aux urgences soudaines. Le projet permettra également d’assurer conjointement avec la communauté humanitaire le plaidoyer en faveur du respect des principes humanitaires, de la protection des civils, de l'accès humanitaire et pour la mobilisation et l'allocation efficace de ressources humanitaires. OCHA continuera de jouer  également un rôle moteur dans le renforcement du lien entre les acteurs humanitaires et de développement et la transformation de la réponse humanitaire, en lien avec les engagements pris au Sommet mondial de l'action humanitaire de 2016 et ceci à travers la nouvelle façon de travailler (NWOW).OCHA continue de mettre en oeuvre sa mission à travers ses fonctions clés (Coordination, Gestion de l' information et plaidoyer). Un accent a été mis sur l' opérationalisation de la nouvelle façon de travailler, la mise en oeuvre des plans d' action de la redevabilité envers les populations affectées (AAP) et la PSEA, la préparation aux urgences et le plaidoyer pour plus de visibilités et de mobilisation de ressources pour les différentes crises au Tchad (Bassin du Lac Tchad, insécurité alimentaire et malnutrition, épidémie sanitaires). De même, OCHA à travers sa participation dans le groupe de travail sur le CASH, continu de faire le plaidoyer pour renforcer l' utilisation du CASH pour la réponse humanitaire dans tous les secteurs et du Cash à usage multiple (Multipurpose CASH)

project_text:
Resilience Building through Income Generation for Conflict-Affected Households in Iraq To sustainably reduce the recurrent needs of vulnerable conflict-affected households in Iraq through introducing viable income generation opportunities.

The livelihoods project is part of a larger program implemented by the Cash Consortium of Iraq (CCI) addressing critical needs of newly displaced households and returnees, and extremely vulnerable host and protracted displaced households through multi-purpose cash assistance. Based on an evolved understanding of the crisis in Iraq, the program has incorporated viable income generating interventions and skills building into the program to provide vulnerable households with the means to support their household needs beyond the immediate cash assistance. This two pronged intervention will help sustainably address recurrent needs of a growing population-of-concern through meeting their immediate needs and providing livelihood opportunities for recovery, with a particular focus on women and youth for income generating activities. In 2017, the pilot in Diyala would be continued and the approach scaled up to new areas.

project_text:
Country Strategic Plan for food assistance to the poor and severely food insecure population in the West Bank and the Gaza Strip WFP is committed to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and is guided by a strategic, programmatic and governance instrument to operationalize its plan and achieve its project objectives to: 
• End Hunger by protecting access to food and by improving dietary diversity;
• Support the implementation of the SDGs by enhancing the capacities of national institutions to implement food security strategies and operations;
This project directly contributes to strategic objectives two and three of the Humanitarian Response Plan 2018 2020, by meeting the basic food needs of severely vulnerable Palestinians and by improving their dietary diversity. 
WFP’s interventions focus on high food insecurity levels, including the malnutrition levels recorded by national surveys. By assisting the poor and severely food insecure Palestinian households in Gaza and Bedouin and herding communities in West Bank’s Area C, and by disseminating information on food and nutrition practices, WFP addresses the basic needs of vulnerable Palestinians and tackles one of the or root causes of some of the food insecurity levels recorded by the government institutions.
These interventions aim at improving the overall food security levels including nutrition and health status of the vulnerable Palestinians and therefore at increasing their coping abilities to sudden shocks in the market for access to food. 
The project also contributes to the Food Security Sector’s three objectives as well as to the National Policy Agenda 2017-2022 (policies on escaping poverty and strengthening social protection as well as meeting the basic needs of the communities) to ensure that the vulnerable Palestinians households basic food needs are met, by assisting households in enhancing their food security levels and by strengthening national institutions in implementing food security strategies and social security safety net programs to best identify and target food insecure and vulnerable Palestinians.
