project_text: Promoting civil documentation and HLP rights of displacement affected populations in the Far North region of Cameroon.				 This project aims to promote the HLP rights of internally displaced people and affected communities and prevent HLP related conflicts in displacement and return areas. The displaced population faces various kinds of HLP related issues such as lack of land for agriculture, forced eviction from housing and land, secondary occupation in return areas, etc. Women are more vulnerable and face more HLP issues as according to the customary law in the region, women do not inherit land. While their gender roles expect them to bring food home form farming, their access to secure land is very limited. Even though, they had money to buy a piece of land, they will need authorisation from their husband or family related male. Women widows are evicted form land inherit after marriage and have to struggle to meet their basic needs. This project will pay specific attention to the most vulnerable such as women, the elderly and other marginalised groups.

project_text:
Pro- Resilient Action inside Syria- Oxfam HRP EFSVL Project Oxfam aims at addressing systemic risks (agro-ecological, local governance, gender inequalities, social tensions) by enhancing socio-economic rights and capacities of 3000 conflict affected households in Qalamoun- Rural Damascus of Syria; all family members (M&F inclusive) lost the ability to enjoy equal access to livelihood opportunities then fulfill their basic rights. Women and adolescent’s girls may face particularly protection risks as a harmful coping mechanism such as child marriage, physical and sexual harassments, etc.   EFSVL team is addressing this vulnerability through immediate and sustainable solutions for start-up of micro-businesses, efficient linkages with suppliers and markets, entitlements and enhancing community resilience, including local capacities for  social cohesion. 

The results will be achieved through a range of outputs including setting-up 60 greenhouses, 1000 kitchen garden toolkits; immediate support to 1000 conflict affected vulnerable livestock breeders; strengthened productive capacity of 35 dairy, bakery and other food processors; technical and managerial skill building of 35 participants; training of 7 local veterinarian, drilling  3 new wells, powering  3 existing wells with solar system and  rehabilitation of 3 boreholes will provide income generation opportunities to conflict impacted vulnerable women, men and their families ; bring improvements in market services, soil and water conservation; provision of agricultural inputs; technical support for improved agricultural production; collaboration, networking and alliance building with a range of stakeholders and enhancing communities’ capacity to respond to shock and stresses as a result of conflict.
During the project duration, agricultural and food production will focus on two agricultural seasons of critical crops in the targeted locations. These commodities will be selected based on local seasonal calendar, farmers’ skills and their access to inputs, consultation with communities and potential for supplementing food needs and will directly support the targeted beneficiaries and indirectly their supported families (elderly, boys and girls all inclusive).Furthermore, the project design is paying attention to very specific needs of targeted women and men; distributed kits will be designed to accommodate the differences between women and men. Time and distribution locations will be gender sensitive. Special attention will be paid for impact of intervention on power dynamics in targeted communities to avoid stressing the negative social norms in roles and responsivities of women and men.
This action is based on Oxfam’s approach on developing resilient livelihoods, which integrates humanitarian relief, socioeconomic development, and empowered advocacy through improving social protection/safety nets and strengthening market system. This approach provides a coherent and gender sensitive framework to achieve the action objective, through its processes that concurrently address short-term targeted agricultural outcomes and spillover effects from strengthening of market system. 
Through this action, target households will increase capacity to cope with shocks and avoid the harmful survival mechanism such as early, forced and child marriages, child laboring, etc.  It increase the levels of agriculture production and income. Through Oxfam’s approach, this will strengthen community organizations, and enhance their ability to access services.

project_text:
Building Resilient Communities for Child Survival, Growth and Development in 15 States This project aims at building the resilience of the poorest, most-in-need and hardest-to-reach children. It targets 1,500 communities and 329,000 vulnerable children (50% girls and 2% children with disabilities) with below breakdown:
•	IDPs Children: 54,000
•	Returnees Children: 23,000
•	Vulnerable Residents: 252,000
The project should provide integrated and sustainable assistance through interventions that promote resilience amongst affected populations and strengthen human security. The whole child approach using the Child Friendly Schools (CFS) framework needs to be clearly reflected with the following five thematic components: (i) Inclusiveness; (ii) Effective Teaching and Learning; (iii) Safe, Healthy and Protective Learning Environment; (iv) Gender Responsiveness; (v) Community and Child Participation.
The activities will be implemented under three outcomes as follows:
Outcome 1: More out-of-school children, especially girls, marginalized groups and those in the most vulnerable situations, are enabled to access quality pre-primary, primary and alternative learning opportunities with zero tolerance to hazards
To increase enrolment and reduce dropout of children from schools, multitude of interventions will be provided in a customised package based on actual underlying reasons. Target schools will be supported to enrol additional 50,000 Out of school children, to open ALP classrooms for 50,000 children and to establish ECE centres/ pre-school classrooms for 75,000 Children. Also, 6,580 Children with disabilities will be targeted in an integrated manner whether through training of teachers, providing specialized supplies, adding rams to Classrooms and latrines, etc... 
Schooling supplies will be provided in form of Teacher kits, student kits, Recreational Kits, ECD kits, dignity Kits for girls, uniform sets, books and school furniture for a total of 329,000 children to attend schools. Cash assistance to 100,000 vulnerable children (1,000 SDG per school year) and income generating activities to women-headed households and to children with disabilities will be provided to support continuity of learning.
Outcome 2: Individuals, Education providers, parents and communities have improved knowledge, skills and pro-social capacity to contribute to quality learning outcome.
Building capacity of 1,500 communities and civil society to promote, enable and sustain behaviour change related to access to quality education. 22,500 PTA members will be trained on School Improvement Planning SIP before being supported with school grant (max 270,000 SDG per school) for income generating activity that will cover local school feeding, teachers’ incentives (ALP, Pre-School, School), school running costs and at least 50% reduction in school fees.
Also 1,500 school clubs will be formed and trained on upshift programme to build skills and create opportunity for the most disadvantaged young people and empowers them to identify challenges in their communities and create entrepreneurial solutions to address them. Also, the package of Unlocking literacy programme including its assessment pre- and post will be scaled up to support quality learning at 1,500 schools/ communities
Outcome 3: More communities have strengthened mechanisms to protect children from violence, abuse, and exploitation including FGM/C and child marriage for inclusive, safe and protective school environments.
The integrated approach of Education and Child Protection will be reflected in all education activities. It targets increasing awareness of 150,000 education personnel and community structures on the CP issues with signing of Code of Conduct (CoC).  Moreover, safe referral pathways and complaint mechanisms between CBCPN, PTA and Education personnel will be established with estimated 6,000 cases referred to CP agencies/networks by education staff each month from the target 1,500 schools.

project_text:
Renforcement des mécanismes de coordination et de plaidoyer pour la protection humanitaire et l’assistance aux populations les plus vulnérables au Mali. La situation humanitaire demeure complexe et instable, principalement en raison des conflits armés et intercommunautaires dans les régions du Centre et du Nord. Le retard dans la mise en œuvre de l’Accord pour la paix et la réconciliation au Mali paraphé en juin 2015 et dans le processus de désarmement, démobilisation, réintégration (DDR) contribuent à la persistance de l’instabilité sécuritaire dans les régions de Kidal, Gao, Tombouctou, Ségou et Mopti ainsi qu’à l’aggravation des tensions sociales. La présence limitée de l’État et l’insécurité dans ces régions demeurent l’un des facteurs clés obligeant les civils à fuir leurs communautés.
Le nombre de Personnes Déplacées Internes (PDI) a atteint la barre des 199 385 en octobre 2019 en comparaison aux 80 302 enregistrés en octobre 2018. Les risques et les besoins de protection des populations fuyant leurs communautés sous la pression de la violence armée ou des tensions intercommunautaires, sont élevés. De graves abus et attaques contre les personnes, les biens et les services (écoles, centres de santé) sont régulièrement signalées alors que l’accès aux services appropriés est compromis. Comme les déplacements internes sont durables, les risques de protection et les violations des droits fondamentaux augmentent, en particulier pour les plus vulnérables (femmes, enfants, personnes âgées, personnes handicapées ou malades). De graves conséquences humanitaires ont donc été notées, telles que des taux élevés d’insécurité alimentaire et de malnutrition ainsi que le faible accès aux services sociaux de base.

En référence au Cadre Harmonisé (nov. 2019), à l'heure actuelle, 3,6 million d'hommes, de femmes, de garçons et de filles souffrent d'insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle, dont 670 000 souffrent d'une insécurité alimentaire sévère (phase 3 à 5 du Cadre Harmonisé). La situation devrait se détériorer au cours de la période de soudure 2020, avec près de 4,9 million d'hommes, de femmes, de garçons et de filles souffrant d'insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle, dont près de 1,2 million de personnes souffrant d'insécurité alimentaire sévère (phase 3 à 5). Les capacités de réponse existantes au Mali représentent plus de 160 organisations humanitaires, acteurs du développement ainsi que des forces militaires (MINUSMA, Forces maliennes de défense et de sécurité, Barkhane, Mission européenne de formation, G5 Sahel). Le contexte susmentionné exigera une coordination efficace et la présence d’OCHA demeure très importante. OCHA maintiendra sa présence à Bamako, Mopti, Tombouctou et Gao et ouvrira une antenne à Ségou tout en couvrant à distance les régions de Taoudénit, Ménaka, Kidal et les régions du sud.

Sept clusters actifs (Éducation, Sécurité alimentaire, Santé, Nutrition, Protection, Abris/BNA et WASH), des sous-clusters et des groupes de travail spécialisés (Accès, CM-Coord, Redevabilité, Genre et Cash) sont en place au niveau national et local. Le Bureau d’OCHA au Mali continuera ainsi à jouer un rôle central dans la mobilisation, la coordination et le soutien des acteurs humanitaires dans les domaines de la coordination, la gestion de l’information, le financement humanitaire et le plaidoyer. OCHA jouera un rôle essentiel dans la mobilisation adéquate des fonds en faveur des personnes dans le besoin, en plus de contribuer à dynamiser les efforts déployés par le gouvernement et les acteurs du développement pour s’attaquer aux causes structurelles de la vulnérabilité.

OCHA continuera à jouer son rôle central dans la mobilisation des partenaires, l’utilisation des instruments et des mécanismes de financement tout en veillant à ce que les besoins humanitaires croissants soient prises en compte. OCHA assumera son rôle clé dans la coordination militaire au niveau national et régional de concert avec les forces militaires présentes dans le pays tout en renforçant les capacités des autorités nationales en matière de coordination et de préparation des interventions d’urgence.

project_text:
Renforcement de la coordination et du plaidoyer humanitaire au Tchad Le projet vise à renforcer le rôle de OCHA dans la mise en œuvre sa mission à travers ses fonctions clés que sont la Coordination, Gestion de l’information et plaidoyer. Un accent a été mis sur la mise en œuvre des plans d’action de la redevabilité envers les populations affectées (AAP) et la PSEA, la préparation aux urgences et le plaidoyer pour plus de visibilités et de mobilisation de ressources pour les différentes crises au Tchad (mouvement de population – crise du Bassin du Lac Tchad, insécurité alimentaire et malnutrition, urgences sanitaires) à travers le bureau OCHA à N’Djaména et ses trois Sous bureaux à Abéché, Goré et Lac. Il sera également renforcé l’opérationnalisation du nexus humanitaire, développement et paix dans le cadre de la nouvelle façon de travailler., 

Le projet a pour but de renforcer la coordination d’une réponse humanitaire rapide afin de sauver des vies et protéger les personnes affectées par les situations de crises au Tchad. Une coordination humanitaire efficace et performante permettra aux acteurs humanitaires de mieux identifier et répondre aux besoins humanitaires, de renforcer la préparation de réponse aux urgences à travers le renforcement des mécanismes de coordination et plus spécifiquement l‘Equipe humanitaire pays, la coordination inter-clusters, la coordination civilo-militaire, les clusters et les mécanismes de coordination au niveau de terrain.
Le projet vise aussi à assurer le plaidoyer humanitaire à travers l’analyse des besoins faites par l’ensemble de la communauté humanitaire et ses partenaires en vue une compréhension commune des problématiques auxquels fait face le Tchad, ses causes profondes, l’impact sur les populations. OCHA jouera un rôle clé dans la création d'espaces de collection et d'analyse et gestion d’ informations, pour assurer une stratégie de réponse coordonnée menant à des actions humanitaires répondant aux besoins les plus aigus et être mieux préparé face aux urgences soudaines. Le projet permettra également d’assurer conjointement avec la communauté humanitaire le plaidoyer en faveur du respect des principes humanitaires, de la protection des civils, de l'accès humanitaire et pour la mobilisation et l'allocation efficace de ressources humanitaires.

OCHA continuera de jouer également un rôle moteur dans le renforcement du lien entre les acteurs humanitaires et de développement et la transformation de la réponse humanitaire, en lien avec les engagements pris au Sommet humanitaire mondial  de 2016 et ceci à travers la nouvelle façon de travailler (NWOW) et le renforcement de l’utilisation de la modalité de transfert monétaire.

Le projet vise aussi à assurer le plaidoyer humanitaire à travers l’analyse des besoins faites par l’ensemble de la communauté humanitaire et ses partenaires en vue une compréhension commune des problématiques auxquels fait face le Tchad, ses causes profondes, l’impact sur les populations. OCHA jouera un rôle clé dans la création d'espaces de collection et d'analyse et gestion d’ informations, pour assurer une stratégie de réponse coordonnée menant à des actions humanitaires répondant aux besoins les plus aigus et être mieux préparé face aux urgences soudaines. Le projet permettra également d’assurer conjointement avec la communauté humanitaire le plaidoyer en faveur du respect des principes humanitaires, de la protection des civils, de l'accès humanitaire et pour la mobilisation et l'allocation efficace de ressources humanitaires.

OCHA continuera de jouer également un rôle moteur dans le renforcement du lien entre les acteurs humanitaires et de développement et la transformation de la réponse humanitaire, en lien avec les engagements pris au Sommet humanitaire mondial  de 2016 et ceci à travers la nouvelle façon de travailler (NWOW) et le renforcement de l’utilisation de la modalité de transfert monétaire.

project_text:
Niger Country Strategic Plan La vision de la réponse aux urgences dans le cadre du Plan Stratégique Pays (PSP) 2020-2024 du PAM Niger est la réduction de l’empreinte humanitaire dans la mise en œuvre de l’Activité 1, relative aux urgences du PSP à travers la promotion de l’approche NEXUS. Cette réponse s’inscrit dans la Stratégie de Prévention et de Gestion des Crises Alimentaires 2021 – 2025 du Dispositif National de Prévention et de Gestion de Crises Alimentaires (DNPGCA). Ce plan s’inscrit aussi dans le Plan d’Action 2021-2023 du Comité Technique Tripartite sur le Nexus Urgence-Développement (CTTNUD), en vue d’une mobilisation des ressources financières pour une planification et une mise en œuvre concertée des activités relatives à la promotion du NEXUS.  Dans le cas spécifique de l’assistance aux retournés dans leurs villages d’origine, qui est envisagée en 2022, la Loi 2018-74, relative à la protection et à l’assistance aux Personnes Déplacées Internes (PDI) cadrera le processus. Rappelons que l’Activité 1, relative aux urgences s’inscrit dans l’effet direct stratégique 1 du CSP (2020-2024) du PAM Niger « Les populations affectées, y compris les réfugiés, les personnes déplacées internes, les communautés hôtes et les retournés dans les zones ciblées sont en mesure de répondre aux besoins alimentaires minimums pendant et après la crise ».  La réponse aux urgences du PAM concernant la SECAL, basée sur une approche flexible, concernera toutes les trois (3) composantes de cette réponse en 2022 :
•	Le Mécanisme de Réponse Rapide (RRM)
•	La réponse aux crises prolongées.
•	La réponse à la soudure agricole et pastorale.
Par ailleurs la prévention de la malnutrition aux enfants 6-23 mois est combinée aux trois composantes ci-dessus.

project_text:
Evidence-based planning and programming for humanitarian actors in Syria REACH, a joint initiative of IMPACT, ACTED and the United Nations Operational Satellite Applications Programme (UNOSAT), aims to facilitate evidence-based planning, technical advisory and coordination support for humanitarian actors in Syria by providing information management, technical advisory and coordination support to at least 225 humanitarian organizations. REACH will be leading on the implementation of project activities. More specifically, this will be done through the following activities:
•	Producing Monthly Humanitarian Situation Overviews in Syria (HSOS)
•	Emergency assessments on the humanitarian situation situation in Syria
•	Cash and markets assessments in collaboration with CBR-TWG
•	Camps and sites profiling and mapping
•	Remote sensing to support IDP site identification and shelter counts
•	Technical advisory to the humanitarian coordination structure, among other towards the successful implementation of the 2020 Syria MSNA
•	Thematic assessments/specialised assessments to meet information gaps

REACH has designed this intervention based on feedback from humanitarian actors and seven years of experience in implementation in Syria. REACH maintains regular discussions with Whole of Syria coordination structures including the deputy regional humanitarian coordinator, OCHA, clusters/working groups, and the NES forum, and sits as well at the ICCG in Turkey and the ISWG in NES/Iraq. Additionally, REACH is part of the NGO Forum and the SIRF and also joins the SIRF Policy and Advocacy working group. These engagements enable a timely and efficient identification of information needs and gaps as well as opportunities for partnerships and collaboration. Activities included in this proposal have thus been designed based on these interactions. For example, conversations with the NES Forum, OCHA, SSWG and CCCM cluster have confirmed a general lack of information on camps and sites in northern Syria, which was flagged as of particular concern given the worsened emergency situation in both NWS and NES. REACH Camps and Sites sweeps conducted in 2019 in NWS also revealed a significant number of sites that were not yet registered by the CCCM cluster, which outlined an information gap and a need to support CCCM processes.

This project is already fully funded, but may require additional top-ups later in the year.

IMPACT is a leading Geneva based think-and-do-tank, created in Switzerland in 2010 on the initiative of ACTED and firstly operationalised in 2012. While autonomous organizations, IMPACT and ACTED operate together thanks to a formalised global partnership. Together, IMPACT, ACTED and UNOSAT set up the REACH program in order to promote and facilitate the development of information products that enhance the humanitarian community’s decision making and planning capacity. IMPACT is the lead-organization in REACH and hosts the REACH global team in its Geneva HQ. As sister organizations, IMPACT and ACTED coordinate on field implementation. In all field operations of the REACH program, ACTED provides operational support (security management, office space, cars, national HR recruitment, etc.), while IMPACT provides strategic and programmatic oversight through its global team and is in charge of the validation and dissemination of reports, and external relations

project_text:
Fostering Resilience through Early Recovery response for the Most Crisis-impacted Communities in Syria The Integrated Response for Resilience Programme aims at providing a comprehensive response through Early Recovery support in 80 communities  impacted by the crisis. 
Communities, particularly those most dramatically affected – and under additional stress because of IDPs returns and other displacements - need assistance in reinforcing their resilience to address these shocks as well as the consequences of the protracted crisis, and to address their needs on seriously depleted infrastructures and service capacities.
The essence of the Programme is about providing Syrian communities with – still limited - support to regain control over their basic needs (livelihoods, access to essential services) and reduce their dependency on humanitarian assistance. Prioritization of locations, is the outcome of a context analysis and needs assessment conducted on more than 5,000 Syrian communities, based on the following three criteria:
1) Hard to Reach Areas
2) Areas of major IDPs presence and IDPs returns
3) Highest scoring in the Severity Scale

The integrated response consists of the following components: strengthening of social services-related capacities (access and coverage), livelihoods creation and rural recovery, PWDs support, social cohesion/community safety, reducing gender inequality and youth marginality, women empowerment, tensions reduction and rehabilitation of basic infrastructure and public services.
The program is built in a modular manner both in terms of geographical and sectoral/thematic interventions and foresees the allotment of average 1 Million US$ per community. Hence, donors willing to support this approach will be able to pre-select certain location(s) and/or area(s) of intervention of their preference, within the 200 prioritized communities.
The programme relates directly to the sector objectives:
1. Living conditions
2. Livelihoods
3. Access to social services
4. Access to productive and market infrastructure
5. Social protection
6. Strengthening of local public services delivery capacity
7. Reinforcing opportunities and capacities for civic engagement

project_text:
Enhancement of protection of displaced persons, returnees and conflict affected host communities in Syria through integrated, community-based protection activities. The project aims to strengthen protection and resilience of Syrian IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities to enjoy rights, legal and physical protection and access to services through advocacy, identification of risks and response, coordination and provision of community-based protection services.  It will capitalize on UNHCR’s community- centers network in Syria to help identify protection needs and facilitate response to people in need of protection and access to services to enhance their legal and physical protection. As such protection interventions including legal counselling and assistance, protection monitoring, referrals and information sharing, social protection through livelihoods support to most vulnerable people, psychosocial support, GBV prevention and response, child protection, case management, in- kind assistance covering basic needs of elderly and persons with disabilities, education support to vulnerable children, campaigns and awareness including on mine education for communities targeting women, men, boys and girls and capacity building of first responders working in communities, volunteers, partners and government counterparts will be provided through the project. Outreach to communities will be convened through static and mobile facilities including outreach volunteers, through which people in need of protection services in areas of SGBV, CP, civil documentation, psychosocial support and community empowerment will be provided and enhanced. Activities on community initiatives will also be implemented engaging communities to address own protection concerns and enhance participation, inclusion, ownership and social cohesion.  Legal aid interventions will enhance access to civil/HLP documentation of IDPs and refugee returnees and provide support in legal matters related to GBV, CP and other protection risks. Accountability to affected people will be realized through meaningful participation of communities, structured focus group discussions and enhancement of community- based complaints mechanism to receive feedback with regards to programmes delivered through the project and complains including regarding sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) and the redressal of incidents.  

Intervention to refugee returnees will focus on humanitarian assistance, legal aid, coordination with government counterparts and UN and NGO stakeholders, information management and return tracking systems and sub – district profiling to better inform return programming and interventions. In addition, the project will support coordination fora between protection actors ensuring coordinated protection interventions as well as providing technical training to local stakeholders and HLP Technical Working Group. UNHCR Syria will continue to lead Protection Sector in coordination of response plans of IDPs and affected people as well it will execute leadership roles in refugee return programmes in collaboration with the Government. In North West Syria, it will lead Protection Monitoring Task Force (PMTF). 

Through the project intervention approximately 3 million IDPs, returnees and affected host communities (60 %, 25 % and 15% respectively) will be reached in government and non-government-controlled areas redressing their protection concerns.  3,000 humanitarian workers and local authority staff will be trained, and 2,700 communities consulted through FGDs and 2,310 communities through protection monitoring. 30% of the project beneficiaries are girls, 25% are boys, 24% are women, and 15% are men and 3% elderly women and 3% elderly men. 840 humanitarian workers and local authority staff are to be trained and 120 communities will be assessed through protection monitoring activities. 

The project will ensure GBV prevention through community-based mechanisms, such as women committees.

, Total estimated beneficiaries = 7801

sourceObjects_Organization.name: Save the Children

destinationObjects_Project.name: Supporting the most vulnerable with in kind food assistance, multi purpose cash assistance, and ensuring economic resilience of MSMEs
destinationObjects_Emergency.name: Beirut Port Explosion - August 2020
project_text:
Supporting the most vulnerable with in kind food assistance, multi purpose cash assistance, and ensuring economic resilience of MSMEs  Blanket distribution of hot meals in areas severely affected by the explosion, through local NGO partners with industrial or community kitchens and existing food safety standards; provision of provision of ready to eat packages for families without access to cooking facilities. Distribution of food parcels for affected and displaced families, including high vulnerability groups like FHH and the elderly, who are at high risk of COVID or have no access to markets. Parcels also include essential hygiene items including menstrual pads, and baby items. Targeting for hot meals and food parcels includes area-based coordination with the Food Security sector, priority for locations with known economic vulnerabilities and/or explosion-effected, and categorical targeting of households with children, female-headed, and other high risk groups. For food parcels, eligibility related to income poverty will also be calculated.
Multi-purpose cash assistance (MPCA) enables the most vulnerable families to meet their basic needs with dignity, and prepares them with financial stability and increased choices to access decent work. This activity is essential both in terms of economic stability while Lebanon continues to address COVID-19 pandemic and aftermath of the Beirut blast, and as a response to ongoing economic distress. Social assistance is a right for the most vulnerable, and for those with labor capacity it is also an essential stepping stone for families to pursue future livelihoods and decent work. For families directly affected by the explosion, a separate cash envelope will also be available as an immediate protection need, in line with sector guidance.
Finalizing a coordinated and joint assessment with 8 other international and national NGOs to assess the damage to MSMEs in areas most affected by the Beirut blast. This assessment will conclude in a report as well as determine eligibility of the MSME for a cash grant, the value harmonized with other livelihood agencies. Small to medium cash grants and in-kind rehabilitation to MSMEs to help restart their business that have been damaged by the explosion, addressing damage to structures, assets, restocking, and other immediate needs to reopen. Only viable businesses are eligible, meaning they must meet certain criteria related to customer base and cash flow, and have the capacity to recover within the current economic context. Priority will be given to MSMEs in productive sectors or those linked with provision of essential goods and services such as food and vegetables, or repair services such as carpentry, electricity, etc. Grants will be combined with business development services, including tailored coaching sessions on business risk resilience, to continue in Phase III.
Targeting mothers and children under two years, those that influence and support their decisions (men, fathers, grandmothers) with integrated approaches to address the many underlying causes of malnutrition so to increase access to safe and nutritious food, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), protection, and ensure that women are supported so to make the right decisions for their children and themselves. This will be achieved through partners and referrals, aligned with the Nutrition Sub Working Group members to improve the delivery of quality nutrition services, including Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) practices. Providing support to mothers and caregivers to navigate difficult conditions in a humanitarian setting so they can feed and care for their youngest children safely, and we do this through different actions at the household, community, health system and national level. Establishing private and secure breastfeeding safe areas as needed, with trained IYCF staff to support mothers to initiate and continue recommended IYCF practices. Training volunteers and community workers to conduct support and education sessions for families with young children on IYCF topics.
all_text:
Beirut Blast response - Food Parcels, Ready to Eat, Community Kitchen Supporting the most vulnerable with in kind food assistance, multi purpose cash assistance, and ensuring economic resilience of MSMEs  Blanket distribution of hot meals in areas severely affected by the explosion, through local NGO partners with industrial or community kitchens and existing food safety standards; provision of provision of ready to eat packages for families without access to cooking facilities. Distribution of food parcels for affected and displaced families, including high vulnerability groups like FHH and the elderly, who are at high risk of COVID or have no access to markets. Parcels also include essential hygiene items including menstrual pads, and baby items. Targeting for hot meals and food parcels includes area-based coordination with the Food Security sector, priority for locations with known economic vulnerabilities and/or explosion-effected, and categorical targeting of households with children, female-headed, and other high risk groups. For food parcels, eligibility related to income poverty will also be calculated.
Multi-purpose cash assistance (MPCA) enables the most vulnerable families to meet their basic needs with dignity, and prepares them with financial stability and increased choices to access decent work. This activity is essential both in terms of economic stability while Lebanon continues to address COVID-19 pandemic and aftermath of the Beirut blast, and as a response to ongoing economic distress. Social assistance is a right for the most vulnerable, and for those with labor capacity it is also an essential stepping stone for families to pursue future livelihoods and decent work. For families directly affected by the explosion, a separate cash envelope will also be available as an immediate protection need, in line with sector guidance.
Finalizing a coordinated and joint assessment with 8 other international and national NGOs to assess the damage to MSMEs in areas most affected by the Beirut blast. This assessment will conclude in a report as well as determine eligibility of the MSME for a cash grant, the value harmonized with other livelihood agencies. Small to medium cash grants and in-kind rehabilitation to MSMEs to help restart their business that have been damaged by the explosion, addressing damage to structures, assets, restocking, and other immediate needs to reopen. Only viable businesses are eligible, meaning they must meet certain criteria related to customer base and cash flow, and have the capacity to recover within the current economic context. Priority will be given to MSMEs in productive sectors or those linked with provision of essential goods and services such as food and vegetables, or repair services such as carpentry, electricity, etc. Grants will be combined with business development services, including tailored coaching sessions on business risk resilience, to continue in Phase III.
Targeting mothers and children under two years, those that influence and support their decisions (men, fathers, grandmothers) with integrated approaches to address the many underlying causes of malnutrition so to increase access to safe and nutritious food, water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), protection, and ensure that women are supported so to make the right decisions for their children and themselves. This will be achieved through partners and referrals, aligned with the Nutrition Sub Working Group members to improve the delivery of quality nutrition services, including Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) practices. Providing support to mothers and caregivers to navigate difficult conditions in a humanitarian setting so they can feed and care for their youngest children safely, and we do this through different actions at the household, community, health system and national level. Establishing private and secure breastfeeding safe areas as needed, with trained IYCF staff to support mothers to initiate and continue recommended IYCF practices. Training volunteers and community workers to conduct support and education sessions for families with young children on IYCF topics.

project_text:
Food Security and Livelihoods Project In North Darfur,  GOAL works closely with the Ministries of Agriculture and Animal Resources in Khartoum and in North Darfur as well as FAO on identifying needs, gaps in coverage, and on programme implementation. In addition, GOAL remains an active participant in the FSL Cluster at both national and state levels  where FSL programming is implemented, including North Darfur. GOAL’s FSL programming is closely integrated with other sectors, especially nutrition, health, and protection through targeting vulnerable households (including affected by malnutrition, people living with disabilities, and women-headed households) in catchment areas of supported clinics. GOAL will also incorporate protection and women’s empowerment approaches. With OFDA funding, GOAL proposes to focus on the IDP populations in Kutum Town as well as Kassab and Fata Borno Camps near Kutum, and complementary funding (SHF) will be used to reach vulnerable host communities in Kutum and Al Waha localities to ensure all relevant communities have their needs addressed. Activities are closely coordinated with other FSL actors in North Darfur to eliminate any duplication of effort. Through the FSL Cluster and Cash Working Groups, GOAL incorporates and shares lessons learned and harmonized approaches to livelihoods activities in order to maintain high technical standards in its work.
In South Kordofan, GOAL will work with Village Development Committee (VDC) in areas where they are already established and functional. If the VDC are not available, GOAL will work community leaders to form a VDC consisting of community leaders, influential community members (such as teachers, health workers, religious leaders etc.) as selected by community members. A close effort will be made to ensure that gender representation is observed in the composition of VDC members. And then, GOAL will work with the VDC to identify 200 households in each locality (400 total) to benefit from the first and second phase distribution. The first 100 households will receive 3 local species female goats per family directly from GOAL in the first phase of distribution and this group will make commitment with the VDC to pass on the first generation to the remaining 100 households. The commitment will be between among the first phase beneficiaries, VDC and the second phase beneficiary. This means each beneficiary from the second phase is tied with specific households from the first phase. Male goats will be distributed to the VDC and managed by them to ensure that they are accessed equally by all recipients of female goats. 

GOAL will identify and support existing Community Animal Health Workers (CAHWs) in the targeted areas to provide training and ongoing monitoring and care for the distributed animals. GOAL will provide refresher training to CAHWs and facilitate their work, in particular by supporting their transportation to rural and IDPs areas, as the lack of vehicles or resources for transport has been identified as a major challenge to effective support for animal welfare services across South Kordofan.

project_text:
Food Assistance for conflict affected populations in South Sudan Meet the lifesaving food requirements of people in South Sudan who are facing food security crises, including those living in (ex)-POCs and IDP camps, and those otherwise affected by conflict, natural disaster and/or seasonal food insecurity.

WFP will provide general food distributions (GFD) to the most food insecure people in South Sudan. At the field level, food assistance will be overseen by the WFP Field Offices and implemented by NGO partners or provided through the Integrated Rapid Response Mechanism (IRRM). IRRM is a Delivering as One approach, in which UNICEF supports WASH and nutrition activities, FAO provides emergency seeds and livelihood kits, and WFP provides food assistance and common services through a comprehensive and collaborative humanitarian intervention by deploying  mobile teams, supported by cooperating partners to reach populations facing the most urgent needs in the most inaccessible areas of the South Sudan. 

Complementary to food distributions, WFP will seek to offer value-added solutions (GFD+), in response to needs and priorities identified by the community. Through GFD+, WFP together with its cooperating partners and other stakeholders will provide unconditional opportunities, identified through a community-based, people-centric participatory approach to targeted beneficiaries. GFD+ adds value to emergency food assistance with a focus on solutions that address the root causes of food and nutrition insecurity and better equip beneficiaries to fight hunger. The GFD+ activity type, duration, frequency, and participation will be catered to specific local sites and may range from COVID-19 awareness and mitigation measures to nutrition education, dyke rehabilitation and communal asset management, income-generating activities, or other solution. 

Mitigation measures to reduce and prevent the potential the spread of COVID-19 have been incorporated into standard operating procedures for all interactions with beneficiaries, including training of partners and stakeholders, increasing general awareness among partners and beneficiaries, enforcing social distancing, promoting handwashing, disinfecting sites, reducing the frequency of distribution cycles, and mandating the utilization of personal protective equipment (PPE). These measures are mainstreamed into all WFP activities and are part of the ‘new way of working’.

project_text:
Renforcement de la coordination et du plaidoyer humanitaire au Tchad Le projet vise à renforcer le rôle de OCHA dans la mise en œuvre de son mandat et son rôle auprès des partenaires humanitaires et gouvernementaux au niveau des fonctions coordination, gestion de l’information et plaidoyer. Le bureau national d’OCHA à N’Djaména et ses trois sous-bureaux régionaux à l’Est (Abéché) au Sud (Goré) et la province du Lac (Baga Sola) mettent l’accent sur l’opérationnalisation de ses fonctions y compris en assurant une lien entre les activités humanitaires et de développement (nexus) en vue de promouvoir une solution durable visant à ne pas perpétuer une situation de dépendance humanitaire. Dans le cadre de cette nouvelle façon de travailler outre l’opérationnalisation du nexus, le lien avec les objectifs commun des programmes développement, paix et sécurité sera mis en avant. L’accent est aussi mis sur le renforcement de la coordination civilo-militaire afin de faciliter l’accès et la protection des civils.

Le projet a pour but de renforcer la coordination d’une réponse humanitaire rapide et efficace afin de sauver des vies et protéger les personnes affectées par les situations de crises au Tchad. Une coordination humanitaire rapide et correctement évaluée au niveau des besoins de la population affectée permettra aux acteurs humanitaires de mieux identifier et répondre aux besoins humanitaires, de renforcer la préparation de réponse aux urgences à travers le renforcement des mécanismes de coordination et plus spécifiquement l‘Equipe humanitaire pays, la coordination inter-clusters, la coordination civilo-militaire, les clusters et les mécanismes de coordination au niveau de terrain.
Le projet vise aussi à assurer le plaidoyer humanitaire à travers l’analyse des besoins faites par l’ensemble de la communauté humanitaire et ses partenaires en vue une compréhension commune des problématiques auxquels fait face le Tchad, ses causes profondes, l’impact sur les populations. OCHA jouera un rôle clé dans la création d'espaces de collection et d'analyse et gestion d’informations, pour assurer une stratégie de réponse coordonnée menant à des actions humanitaires répondant aux besoins les plus aigus et être mieux préparé face aux urgences soudaines. Le projet permettra également d’assurer conjointement avec la communauté humanitaire le plaidoyer en faveur du respect des principes humanitaires, de la protection des civils, de l'accès humanitaire et pour la mobilisation et l'allocation efficace de ressources humanitaires.

Un accent a été mis sur la mise en œuvre des plans d’action de la redevabilité envers les populations affectées (AAP), la PSEA et la préparation aux urgences en plus d'intégrer une attention au genre et de renforcer la centralité de la protection.
Un plaidoyer pour plus de visibilité des résultats tangibles au niveau de la réponse facilitant la mobilisation de ressources pour les différentes crises au Tchad (mouvement de population – crise du Bassin du Lac Tchad, insécurité alimentaire et malnutrition, urgences sanitaires) est aussi défini comme une priorité dans ce projet 

OCHA continuera de jouer également un rôle moteur dans le renforcement du lien entre les acteurs humanitaires et de développement et la transformation de la réponse humanitaire, en lien avec les engagements pris au Sommet humanitaire mondial de 2016 et ceci à travers la nouvelle façon de travailler (NWOW) et le renforcement de l’utilisation de la modalité de transfert monétaire.

Le bureau national d’OCHA à N’Djaména et ses trois sous-bureaux régionaux à l’Est (Abéché) au Sud (Goré) et la province du Lac (Baga Sola) mettent l’accent sur l’opérationnalisation de ses fonctions y compris en assurant une lien entre les activités humanitaires et de développement (nexus) en vue de promouvoir une solution durable visant à ne pas perpétuer une situation de dépendance humanitaire. Dans le cadre de cette nouvelle façon de travailler outre l’opérationnalisation du nexus, le lien avec les objectifs commun des programmes développement, paix et sécurité sera mis en avant. L’accent est aussi mis sur le renforcement de la coordination civilo-militaire afin de faciliter l’accès et la protection des civils.

Le projet a pour but de renforcer la coordination d’une réponse humanitaire rapide et efficace afin de sauver des vies et protéger les personnes affectées par les situations de crises au Tchad. Une coordination humanitaire rapide et correctement évaluée au niveau des besoins de la population affectée permettra aux acteurs humanitaires de mieux identifier et répondre aux besoins humanitaires, de renforcer la préparation de réponse aux urgences à travers le renforcement des mécanismes de coordination et plus spécifiquement l‘Equipe humanitaire pays, la coordination inter-clusters, la coordination civilo-militaire, les clusters et les mécanismes de coordination au niveau de terrain.
Le projet vise aussi à assurer le plaidoyer humanitaire à travers l’analyse des besoins faites par l’ensemble de la communauté humanitaire et ses partenaires en vue une compréhension commune des problématiques auxquels fait face le Tchad, ses causes profondes, l’impact sur les populations. OCHA jouera un rôle clé dans la création d'espaces de collection et d'analyse et gestion d’informations, pour assurer une stratégie de réponse coordonnée menant à des actions humanitaires répondant aux besoins les plus aigus et être mieux préparé face aux urgences soudaines. Le projet permettra également d’assurer conjointement avec la communauté humanitaire le plaidoyer en faveur du respect des principes humanitaires, de la protection des civils, de l'accès humanitaire et pour la mobilisation et l'allocation efficace de ressources humanitaires.

Un accent a été mis sur la mise en œuvre des plans d’action de la redevabilité envers les populations affectées (AAP), la PSEA et la préparation aux urgences en plus d'intégrer une attention au genre et de renforcer la centralité de la protection.
Un plaidoyer pour plus de visibilité des résultats tangibles au niveau de la réponse facilitant la mobilisation de ressources pour les différentes crises au Tchad (mouvement de population – crise du Bassin du Lac Tchad, insécurité alimentaire et malnutrition, urgences sanitaires) est aussi défini comme une priorité dans ce projet 

OCHA continuera de jouer également un rôle moteur dans le renforcement du lien entre les acteurs humanitaires et de développement et la transformation de la réponse humanitaire, en lien avec les engagements pris au Sommet humanitaire mondial de 2016 et ceci à travers la nouvelle façon de travailler (NWOW) et le renforcement de l’utilisation de la modalité de transfert monétaire.

project_text:
Improved food security and dietary diversity of vulnerable conflict affected and food insecure populations Although the formation of transitional government of national unity in February 2020 resulted in improved security however the subsequent shocks including COVID-19, flooding, inter-communal violence and political conflict in part of country continue to exacerbate the already fragile humanitarian context in South Sudan. The livelihood and food insecurity was prompted by years of conflict, climate shocks, wrecked economy and extreme poverty. According to the IPC situation analysis released on 18, December 2020, an estimated 6.35 million people (52.6% of the population) faced Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worst acute food insecurity, over two million faced Emergency (IPC Phase 4) acute food insecurity and 24,000 people were likely in Catastrophe (IPC Phase 5). The projection for the lean session estimate that over 60% of population will likely to be in IPC Phase 3 or worse.

The proposed FSL interventions aim to improve food production, strengthen the household’s ability to enhance their productive assets, create livelihood opportunities, build resilience and contribute toward overall improved nutrition status of the affected communities. Concern will support vulnerable IDP, returnee and host community households with emergency access to agricultural and fishing inputs to improve food production and access to nutritious foods. In Aweil West and Aweil North, NBeG, Concern will continue to provide access to seeds, agriculture tools and crop production through block farming as well as technical support and training on seed multiplication and seed saving. Community Agricultural Extension Workers and lead farmers will be supported to train vulnerable farmers on Climate Smart Agriculture, bio-pesticide production and post-harvest handling. Concern will support dry season vegetable production to support income generation opportunities and access to nutritious foods. In Juba IDP camp and Bentiu PoC, Concern will build on its approach of nutrition gardens to support improving dietary diversity through training lead mothers on sack gardening where space is limited in IDP/PoC sites and they will train Mother-to-Mother Support Groups. Focus will be on households with members in OTP and TSFP. In Rubkona and Guit, Concern having supported vegetable gardens to improve access to nutritious foods will expand its FSL interventions considering the gaps in FSL support and most of the population being dependent on food assistance. Vegetable production and fishing will be supported to provide income generation opportunities and increase dietary diversity. Considering asset depletion, crop losses due to flooding, inflation and limited access to livelihood, hunger  is expected to deepen due mainly to depleted food stocks and high food prices therefore Concern in partnership with WFP in NBeG continue to provide emergency food assistance through General Food Distribution, School Feeding Program and Cash/Food for Asset program.

project_text:
Improving access to inclusive and quality primary education in protective and inclusive learning environments for children in the Far North region, Cameroon. The project “Improving access to inclusive and quality primary education in protective and inclusive learning environments for children in the Far North region, Cameroon” is proposed to support children out of school and those at risk of dropping out as a direct result of the attacks on education (children, teachers, parents, school infrastructure, etc.) and insecurity. The actions will focus on creating and maintaining the protective learning environment for children and teachers, as well as strengthening their knowledge and skills cope with threats and attacks; special focus will also be put on developing and expanding relevant non-formal and informal education opportunities for the adolescents. Cash transfer as a modality will also be applied to support parents and communities in enrolling and retaining their children in school and learning centers. 
The project will target children, girls and boys (3-18 years) affected by the crisis in the Far-North Region, particularly in Mayo-Sava, Mayo-Tsanaga and Logone-and-Chari divisions.
This project is designed to carry out activities in collaboration with the Ministry of Basic Education aimed at ameliorating the situation of children with focus on education in emergencies.  
Equitable access to safe and protective learning environments shall be facilitated through the Construction (classrooms, latrines and water points), school facilities built and used by all students, girls and boys, including children living with disabilities.
Access to quality alternative education adapted to the needs of girls and boys (3-18 years old) who are out of school because of the crisis shall be reinforced through learning or training activities.
Rights of girls and boys shall be protected from immediate and future threats through access to conflict-sensitive education, disaster and conflict risk reduction, strengthening psychosocial coping and protecting schools from attack.

project_text:
Emergency lifesaving interventions for most vulnerable affected populations in IPC phase 4 and 5 to meet food and livelihoods needs The proposed HRP 2021 intervention will target locations with IPC 4 and 5 with emergency food security and livelihoods assistance for the most vulnerable populations affected by shocks including floods and conflict, which has contributed to the elevation of food security outcomes to include Famine Likely. The convergence of shocks including floods, conflict and hyperinflation of prices for basic commodities compounded with the social and economic impacts of COVID-19 have increased the population's vulnerability deepening the humanitarian situation. The proposed interventions are aligned to cluster objectives 1: Provide food assistance to prevent famine and improve food consumption, dietary diversity and coping strategies for vulnerable populations (in IPC 5, 4 & some 3 and 2), and 2: Enhance and sustain emergency food production through complementary vegetable and crop livelihood inputs, fishing and livestock support. The delivery of the assistance will be via two modalities (IRRM and static operations) in the proposed locations: Jonglei (Akobo, Nyirol) and Greater Pibor Administrative areas (Pibor). 

With the impact of interwoven shocks, the population of South Sudan is in dire support of humanitarian assistance. Years of conflict have ravaged the country and the population's resilience capacity to withstand shocks without humanitarian assistance has been depleted. As a consequence of the conflict, there are multi-dimensional outcomes which have aggravated the suffering of the most vulnerable households and communities, who have been exposed to recurrent inter-communal violence due to a security vacuum, limited access to food due to reduced farming capacity as a result of displacement and depleted households farming inputs (seeds). The prices of commodities have skyrocketed due to devaluation of the local currency and limited flow of supplies due to insecurity as well as physical inaccessibility resulting from poor road networks. The proposed HRP project is designed to ensure the most vulnerable households have access to immediate food and livelihood assistance to avert the worsening food security outcomes in IPC phase 4 and 5. The proposed interventions will focus on livelihoods assistance and access to food. Livelihood assistance will be implemented for the main season and dry season to ensure continuous production of food at household level, to enable vulnerable households and communities meet their dietary needs. The proposed activities are designed to achieve the objectives of the HRP 2021. The interventions will integrate safe programming principles of Do No Harm, COVID-19 SOPs, and ensure Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP). 

The project will be implemented by Oxfam directly but in close coordination with key Clusters, including FSL cluster, TWGs AAP and partners operational in targeted project locations. At field level, the coordination will be with county line departments of agriculture and fisheries and other stakeholders. This coordination will be of essential importance to ensure that the project delivery consistent with AAP principles, avoidance of duplication of exclusion of vulnerable communities. The project will pay attentions to other cross cutting issues in delivery of the assistance such as safe programming with Do No Harm lenses, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse, inclusion of other groups such as disability and conflict sensitive programming.

project_text:
Amelioration de  l'acces  a l'education et a  la formation professionnelle des enfants, jeunes et des femmes  vulnerables  des regions de Tahoua et Maradi Ce projet vise d'une part,  a améliorer l’Environnement d’apprentissage sûrs et protecteur pour  15 360  enfants  dont  7680 filles et garçons, 645 handicapes  affectés par les crises humanitaires  pour leur bien-être physique et psychosocial  et d'autre part a renforcer la  résilience des écoles, enfants, et des communautés à travers le développement des plans de préparation et de réponses aux risques conjointement élaborés par la communauté éducatives (élèves, enseignants, CGDES) dans les regions de Maradi et Tahoua.  il s'agira aussi de promouvoir l’accès à des offres innovantes  d’éducation inclusive et de qualité pour les garçons et filles de 4 à 17 ans affectés par les crises avec un accent particulier sur le développement professionnel de 307 enseignants retournés, déplacés et réfugiés dans les 51 ecoles ou  centres de regroupement des ecoles.
La reponse aux besoins de ces   15 360  enfants filles et garcons, 307 enseignantes et enseignants,  familles  touchees par les  differentes crises securiatires et sanitaires se  fera en terme  d'appui en infrastrures d'acces,  mobiles ou fixes,  par l'amelioration de l'environnement d'apprentissage sur, invclusif, securisant et portecteur qui favorise la protection et le bien-être congnitif, emotionnel et psychosocial des apprenants, particulierement les filles,  des enseignants et des autres personnels de l'education. Une place de choix sera accordee a la formation des eneignants, la  gestion des risques et de catastrophe par la mise en place des plans de prévention, de préparation et de réponse aux risques de catastrophes et de conflits armés et de la COVID 19, soutien  aux familles vunerables surtout les femmes.  Parallement,  la reponse  sera axee sur  des offres éducatives formelle et non formelle innovantes  de qualité  et des opportunités de formation professionnelle pour les enfants retournés, déplacés, réfugiés et des communautés d’accueil vulnérables.   Enfin, le projet appuyera les centres de regoupement des ecoles pour leur assurer les minmums de conditions d'ensEIgnement et d'apprntissage et leur  suivi par les encadreurs pedagogiaues.

destinationObjects_Project.name: Improving access to emergency life-saving  and  sustainable WASH services to vulnerable IDPs and host communities in Gedo, Somalia
project_text:
Improving access to emergency life-saving  and  sustainable WASH services to vulnerable IDPs and host communities in Gedo, Somalia The proposed project will improve access to sustainable WASH services namely safe water, sanitation facilities and promote good hygiene practices for 7,846 female and 7,539 male beneficiaries in underserved and hard-to-reach villages and IDP camps in Belet Xawa, Dollow, Garbaharey and Luuq districts in Gedo. Among the target beneficiaries will be 2,308 persons with disabilities (1177 male, 1131 female).
The below-average rainfall forecast for the upcoming Deyr season (Oct to Dec) which may be compounded by a harsh Jilaal dry season in 2021 calls for a greater focus on WASH and a re-prioritization of life-saving approaches in Gedo. Access to improved water sources remains low in Gedo with a significant portion of the population relying on the rivers and other seasonal streams as their primary water sources. A joint multi-sectoral assessment led by Trócaire in Dollow riverine communities in December 2019 indicated that 90% of households consume untreated water from the Juba river. The same assessment identified poor latrine coverage as a challenge, with 80% of the population lacking access to latrines. This results in wider open defecation, which is suspected to be one of the factors contributing to the frequent occurrence of diarrheal diseases in the area. A detailed site assessment by REACH in February 2020 further reported widespread open defecation at 64 and 100 percent respectively in assessed sites in Luuq and Dollow. The most severely affected community members are women and girls, who are often forced to use nearby bushes, putting them at a greater risk of SGBV. The ongoing COVID-19 pandemic has further compounded WASH needs in communities, with Trocaire noting serious gaps in knowledge, skills and resources to prevent and control the pandemic especially in IDP and rural communities. 
The project aims to contribute to the achievement of specific objectives of the WASH cluster: delivering life-saving WASH assistance to reduce acute needs, and restoring access to safe and equitable basic WASH services in target locations. This will be done through the construction of one (1) solar powered shallow well with piping to communities in Dollow, rehabilitation of one flood-damaged water system in Dollow and provision of Genset, construction of 110 permanent gender-sensitive latrines with handwashing stations, desludging of 85 latrines, hygiene promotion sessions with distribution of hygiene kits, and environmental cleanup campaigns. In addition, Trocaire will conduct water testing and treatment of water facilities in target locations, and conduct trainings and refresher trainings for representative Water Management Committees while equipping them with tools necessary for effective management of water points. Trocaire will collaborate with Somali Humanitarian Relief Action (SHRA) and Active in Development Aid (ADA), national NGOs with strong experience in implementing WASH projects in Gedo, in delivery of this project in the four target districts.
Trocaire shall work closely with local partners identified to promote protection of beneficiaries and ensure access to services especially for people living with disabilities. The Water Management Committees will particularly be sensitized on inclusivity in water access for people with disabilities and their families. Hygiene promotion outreach teams will be trained to identify and deliver services in homes with people living with disabilities. Gender inclusivity will be ensured through creation or support to adequately representative community structures, as well as working closely with women groups in target location. All data collected will be dis aggregated by gender, age and disability, to inform adaptive programming in meeting the different needs of the different social groups reached.

project_text:
Protection and Assistance for Refugees, Returnees and Asylum Seekers in South Sudan As of January 2021, there are more than 314,000 refugees from neighbouring countries sheltering in South Sudan. Despite enormous socio-economic, security and political challenges, as well as the COVID-19 pandemic, South Sudan has maintained its open-door policy for people seeking international protection, the majority of whom are women and children, including from Sudan, Democratic Republic of Congo and Central African Republic.

At the same time, against a backdrop of fragile peace and cautious optimism for long-term stability, some 357,500 South Sudanese refugees have spontaneously returned to the country since November 2017, 122,000 of those in 2020 alone. While UNHCR is not promoting or facilitating return to South Sudan at this stage, the increase in numbers warrants a scaling-up of support following an area-based approach, including strengthening linkages with development actors, to help returnees and the communities they settle in live in safety and dignity, with greater security and services.

Refugees largely reside in conﬂict-affected regions, challenged by an unpredictable security environment as well as at times fragile relations with host communities. Displaced communities will continue to rely on life-saving humanitarian assistance provided by UNHCR and its partners as a result of enduring economic hardship, weak rule of law, limited development support and a lack of social services and infrastructure in refugee-hosting areas as well as in areas of origin. A reduction of basic assistance, especially during a global pandemic, will immediately lead to the deterioration of the humanitarian situation to emergency levels, due to the absence of a safety net, including social services, community support networks and limited access to livelihoods in displacements sites hosting refugees and South Sudanese refugee returnees.

Under the refugee response, all refugees and asylum seekers registered with UNHCR will beneﬁt from various forms of protection interventions, including individual registration and documentation, and multi-sector assistance. Speciﬁc protection services, such as SGBV response and child protection will focus on the identiﬁed at-risk groups. While water, health, nutrition and education services will continue to maintain indicators within global standards for refugees living in camps, provision of other assistance, including shelter, non-food items and livelihoods support, will be undertaken in a targeted manner, focusing on persons with speciﬁc protection needs and vulnerabilities. This will primarily be achieved through participatory assessments, surveys as well as veriﬁcation exercise to identify vulnerable refugees and their needs. Impact monitoring will be used to gauge the eﬃciency of projects implemented and for the purposes of course-correction in terms of better targeting of assistance. The needs of persons with disabilities and the elderly will be further mainstreamed in various multi-sector response services. Vulnerable refugees in urban settings will also continue to beneﬁt from targeted protection interventions and facilitation of their access to national services.

project_text:
Renforcement de la coordination et du plaidoyer humanitaire au Tchad Le projet vise à renforcer le rôle de OCHA dans la mise en œuvre de son mandat et son rôle auprès des partenaires humanitaires et gouvernementaux au niveau des fonctions coordination, gestion de l’information et plaidoyer. Le bureau national d’OCHA à N’Djaména et ses trois sous-bureaux régionaux à l’Est (Abéché) au Sud (Goré) et la province du Lac (Baga Sola) mettent l’accent sur l’opérationnalisation de ses fonctions y compris en assurant une lien entre les activités humanitaires et de développement (nexus) en vue de promouvoir une solution durable visant à ne pas perpétuer une situation de dépendance humanitaire. Dans le cadre de cette nouvelle façon de travailler outre l’opérationnalisation du nexus, le lien avec les objectifs commun des programmes développement, paix et sécurité sera mis en avant. L’accent est aussi mis sur le renforcement de la coordination civilo-militaire afin de faciliter l’accès et la protection des civils.

Le projet a pour but de renforcer la coordination d’une réponse humanitaire rapide et efficace afin de sauver des vies et protéger les personnes affectées par les situations de crises au Tchad. Une coordination humanitaire rapide et correctement évaluée au niveau des besoins de la population affectée permettra aux acteurs humanitaires de mieux identifier et répondre aux besoins humanitaires, de renforcer la préparation de réponse aux urgences à travers le renforcement des mécanismes de coordination et plus spécifiquement l‘Equipe humanitaire pays, la coordination inter-clusters, la coordination civilo-militaire, les clusters et les mécanismes de coordination au niveau de terrain.
Le projet vise aussi à assurer le plaidoyer humanitaire à travers l’analyse des besoins faites par l’ensemble de la communauté humanitaire et ses partenaires en vue une compréhension commune des problématiques auxquels fait face le Tchad, ses causes profondes, l’impact sur les populations. OCHA jouera un rôle clé dans la création d'espaces de collection et d'analyse et gestion d’informations, pour assurer une stratégie de réponse coordonnée menant à des actions humanitaires répondant aux besoins les plus aigus et être mieux préparé face aux urgences soudaines. Le projet permettra également d’assurer conjointement avec la communauté humanitaire le plaidoyer en faveur du respect des principes humanitaires, de la protection des civils, de l'accès humanitaire et pour la mobilisation et l'allocation efficace de ressources humanitaires.

Un accent a été mis sur la mise en œuvre des plans d’action de la redevabilité envers les populations affectées (AAP), la PSEA et la préparation aux urgences en plus d'intégrer une attention au genre et de renforcer la centralité de la protection.
Un plaidoyer pour plus de visibilité des résultats tangibles au niveau de la réponse facilitant la mobilisation de ressources pour les différentes crises au Tchad (mouvement de population – crise du Bassin du Lac Tchad, insécurité alimentaire et malnutrition, urgences sanitaires) est aussi défini comme une priorité dans ce projet 

OCHA continuera de jouer également un rôle moteur dans le renforcement du lien entre les acteurs humanitaires et de développement et la transformation de la réponse humanitaire, en lien avec les engagements pris au Sommet humanitaire mondial de 2016 et ceci à travers la nouvelle façon de travailler (NWOW) et le renforcement de l’utilisation de la modalité de transfert monétaire.

project_text:
Critical agricultural livelihoods support to conflict- and pandemic-affected households in northeast Nigeria In 2021, FAO will improve food security, nutritional status and incomes among vulnerable, conflict- and pandemic-affected households in Borno, Adamawa and Yobe states in Northeast Nigeria. The now more than decade-long insurgency has decimated agricultural livelihoods upon which more than 80 percent of the population relies as a primary source of household income. The COVID-19 pandemic has further compounded this already highly vulnerable humanitarian context, generating interconnected vulnerabilities that negatively affect availability and access to food, agriculture inputs, finance, farming land, extension services, markets and the fundamental viability of agricultural livelihoods. 
Support to crop production and the rebuilding of a robust crop value chain have been identified by FAO as key to the restoration of livelihoods and to improving the food and nutrition security of vulnerable populations in the BAY states. FAO will support vulnerable households with critical inputs for rainy and dry season cultivation as well as for micro-/backyard gardening and seed production.   
Prior to the insurgency, close to 80 percent of households in northeast Nigeria reared livestock and/or poultry as a vital source of food and household income. The conflict has caused the wide-scale loss of these assets either through looting, property destruction, disease, or abandonment when fleeing attacks by armed insurgents. In addition to being a source of income generation through breeding for sale, livestock and poultry restocking increases the availability of meat, milk and eggs at the household level. FAO will increase support to livestock and poultry production in 2021 in support of affected households.
Prior to the crisis, the fisheries sector had significant economic importance and fish from the northeast were supplied to the rest of Nigeria. With increased land and areas retaken by the military, the return of IDPs to their communities of origin is ongoing, thereby enabling some to access fishing grounds and resume their traditional livelihood. However, the lack of quality inputs remains a limiting factor for the majority of fishers who continue to rely on humanitarian assistance to meet their food and livelihood needs. By leveraging FAO’s extensive experience and capacity, conflict-affected fisherfolk households will be supported to resume their livelihoods and meet their food and nutritional needs. 
The ongoing crisis is also termed a ‘protection crisis’ with vulnerable social groups – particularly children, women and the elderly – disproportionately affected by the impact of the ongoing conflict and the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and are at heightened risk of adopting negative coping strategies such as child labour, borrowing, street begging, basic needs deprivation, transactional sex, early and forced marriage as their families seek to reduce the number of mouths to feed in their homes, and collection of fuelwood in insecure areas, which remains a high-risk livelihood. FAO will support vulnerable households by way of fuel-efficient stoves to reduce exposure to potential protection risks, and stove production and briquette production centres for income generation. 
Access to credit is a particular challenge for vulnerable groups in Northeast Nigeria, particularly women. Through the establishment of Group Savings and Loans Associations (GSLA), in 2021 FAO will extend its GSLA programme and will identify vulnerable groups to enhance their access to credit and financial services as an important social safety net.  
FAO is the co-lead of the Food Security Sector (FSS) which plays a critical role in coordinating food security programming in the BAY states. Food security data collection and analysis are also key and upon which food security actors base their intervention. In 2021, FAO will continue to support and host the Food Security Sector to facilitate the required coordination and analyses required to reach people most in need.

project_text: Health-related vulnerabilities of Rohingya and Host Communities are reduced through increased quality access to comprehensive health services The aims of IOMs’ health interventions aim to respond to the lifesaving needs and improve the resilience of affected populations, with special attention to gender and age considerations, and vulnerable groups. In the camps,34% Rohingya refugee populations, have reported going into debt to pay for health expenses, and 27% seeking lower-quality care or medication, due to a lack of money (Joint Multi-Sector Needs Assessment J-MSNA 2020). This demonstrates some challenges in the already strained health service system in Cox’s Bazar. To address this, this intervention aims to contribute  to  i) increased safe, dignified and meaningful access and utilization of quality comprehensive healthcare services, focusing on sexual, reproductive, maternal, neonatal, child and adolescent health; mental health and psychosocial support; and non-communicable diseases (NCD); ii) improved health seeking behavior, encouragement of  healthy living and promotion of the  utilization of essential service package and community engagement, with special attention to vulnerable groups iii) measures to prepare and (timely) respond  to health emergencies, during disaster (including monsoon and cyclone) and outbreaks of communicable disease (e.g.  COVID-19 and AWD). IOM also aims to contribute to the improvement of quality of services through performance monitoring, evaluation, coordination and capacity building.
