project_text:
Emergency Holistic Protection Services for Migrant Women facing Exploitation, Trauma and Abuse Women migrant domestic workers (WMDWs) – an already marginalized group, continue to be disproportionately impacted by Lebanon’s manifold humanitarian crisis. Due to the Kafala system, WMDWs live with almost no legal and social protection, facing high levels of exploitation and different types of abuse while facing huge obstacles to access justice. They rarely resort to the authorities to seek redress, often due to isolation in their place of work, fear from the authorities, lack of awareness about legal procedures and their rights, the absence of financial means, and language barriers.
In light of this situation, UN Women in partnership with Kafa (enough) Violence & Exploitation and GIZ are partnering to address the emergency protection needs of WMDWs in Lebanon. This project works towards the achievement of the ERP Objective 3: to enhance timely, unhindered, and equitable access to protection assistance for migrants. Under this project, migrant women will have access to a 24/7 helpline, increased access to legal and protection services, better access to quality MHPSS services, and basic and humanitarian return assistance. Socioeconomically marginalized migrant women will be targeted across all regions in Lebanon. UN Women will oversee and monitor the overall project implementation. Services will be provided directly by KAFA, with support on Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) technical assistance provided by GIZ. 

Under 1.1, UN Women and Kafa will conduct mass awareness raising of legal information as a first step to increase their access to protection and obtainment of their legal rights. The campaign will utilize both social media platforms and traditional communication materials, including fliers and leaflets in high traffic areas. Given the fuel and electricity crisis, expanding outreach interventions to migrant women who are not online or have access to internet and mobile phones, is essential. All materials will be translated in the languages of migrant workers. Legal aid will also be provided via individual and group legal counseling, and legal representation for specific cases. 

Under 2.1, Kafa will continue the operation of an established 24/7 helpline dedicated to MDWs. The helpline provides information counseling and provide referrals to specialized legal actors and service providers. Victims of physical and sexual abuse, they will be provided with immediate socio-legal protection information and/or measures. MHPSS will be implemented through different modalities. Social workers operating the helpline will provide immediate psycho-social counseling for WMDWs in psychological distress and make specialized refers. KAFA will also provide direct PSS interventions, including targeting the mental health of migrant community leaders in order to help them manage stress and prevent burnout. GIZ has been a key actor in the MHPSS response for migrants in Lebanon, and will provide quality assurance, and advise on technical referrals to specialized services, as well as coordination with the MHPSS task-force for migrant domestic workers.  
Under 3.1, While protection data will be collected and monitored across all project activity implementation, UN Women will specifically collect and analyze data on female migrant population in North Lebanon (Tripoli and Akkar), with a focus on gender and protection in order to respond to data gaps in that region and improve it service provision outreach. 
Under 6.1, UN Women and Kafa will provide multi-purpose cash assistance to address urgent needs of WMDWs. The cash assistance will be provided to the most vulnerable WMDWs to cover rent, and other basic needs. 
Under 7.1, UN Women and Kafa will facilitate voluntary humanitarian return assistance for WMDWs facing high-risk protection issues. A specific focus will be given to scaling up voluntary return support to migrant women who are in detention, and arbitrary detention – a violation of human rights.

project_text: Enhancement of protection of displaced persons, returnees and conflict affected host communities in Syria through integrated, community-based protection activities. The project aims to strengthen protection and resilience of Syrian IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities through advocacy, coordination, provision of community-based protection services and legal services UNHCR Syria will continue to lead the Protection Sector/Cluster to ensure coordinated protection interventions programming for safe refugees return. UNHCR’s protection interventions include legal counselling and assistance, protection monitoring, referrals and information sharing, social protection through livelihoods support to most vulnerable people, GBV prevention and response, child protection, psychosocial support and in-kind assistance for persons with specific needs including persons with disabilities, non-formal education, and awareness activities on various subjects targeting women, men, boys and girls. In addition to over 125 community centres providing integrated protection services, outreach to communities will be convened through over 2,800 outreach volunteers. Accountability to affected people will be realized through meaningful participation of communities based on age, gender and diversity approach, structured focus group discussions and enhancement of the community-based feedback and complaint mechanisms. UNHCR will continue its capacity building efforts to ensure services are delivered according to the standards and that accountability to affected population and do no harm principles are respected. UNHCR Syria will continue to lead Protection Sector in coordination of response plans of IDPs and affected people as well it will execute leadership roles in refugee return programmes in collaboration with the Government. Monitoring and evaluation of the planned interventions is based on the reports and observations by the partners and on regular direct observation and ongoing assessment by UNHCR and the comparison of achievements and related financial expenditures with objectives. Evaluation is conducted through different channels including the post distribution monitoring to determine the effectiveness of/measure the satisfaction of POCs with the service and the distribution process in addition to multiple satisfaction surveys and tracking tools related to different protection interventions. Monitoring and evaluation activities are carried out at various levels by partners and agencies implementing subprojects, UNHCR Branch Office, Sub Office and Field Offices. Situation reports are submitted by all UNHCR Field Offices to their respective Supervising Office and Branch Offices submit a corresponding report to Headquarters.

project_text:
WFP SOMALIA 2022 HRP - FSC Somalia has been impacted by multiple shocks in 2020, including desert locust invasion, flash floods and COVID-19. This has negatively affected the ability of vulnerable households to meet their food security needs. The urban poor, including IDP households, have been disproportionally affected due to the socio-economic effects from COVID-19 due their heavy reliance on food purchases from the market and casual labor as the main sources of income. These households are likely to face food consumption gaps due to declines in employment and income-earning opportunities. The desert locust caused significant damage to cereal crops, fruits, vegetables and pasture in the northern and central regions. Control efforts of the government and partners in Somaliland and Puntland made progress, but an increasing number of adult locust groups was reported in central regions. In addition, in the northeast, remained swarms have matured, and some have moved towards central areas. As per FAO, the hatching and band formation is occurring now and more swarms are likely to move to other areas in central Somalia and at later stages are expected to move towards crop producing areas in the south; which can have some negative impact to the crops and pasture up to early next year.

The impact of localized flooding particularly in riverine areas destroyed farmland and crops and caused population displacement, leading to significant crop losses and the loss of income from agricultural employment.

Jointly with the Government and other humanitarian actors, WFP Somalia has supported communities and vulnerable houses impacted by the multiple shocks. The high levels of sustained humanitarian assistance in 2020 have played a critical role in stabilizing the situation. The immediate food security outlook for Somalia however looks bleak despite the efforts sustained in 2020. According to the latest Post-Gu Assessment, 2.1 million people are expected to be food insecure (IPC 3 and 4) across Somalia through December 2020. An additional 3 million people are expected to be Stressed (IPC 2), bringing the total number of people facing cute food insecurity to 5.1 million until the end of this year. Based on results of the 2020 Post Gu assessment, an estimated 849,900 children under the age of five years face acute malnutrition between September 2020 and August 2021, including 143,400 likely to be severely malnourished.

WFP SOMALIA 2022 HRP - FSC Somalia has been impacted by multiple shocks in 2020, including desert locust invasion, flash floods and COVID-19. This has negatively affected the ability of vulnerable households to meet their food security needs. The urban poor, including IDP households, have been disproportionally affected due to the socio-economic effects from COVID-19 due their heavy reliance on food purchases from the market and casual labor as the main sources of income. These households are likely to face food consumption gaps due to declines in employment and income-earning opportunities. The desert locust caused significant damage to cereal crops, fruits, vegetables and pasture in the northern and central regions. Control efforts of the government and partners in Somaliland and Puntland made progress, but an increasing number of adult locust groups was reported in central regions. In addition, in the northeast, remained swarms have matured, and some have moved towards central areas. As per FAO, the hatching and band formation is occurring now and more swarms are likely to move to other areas in central Somalia and at later stages are expected to move towards crop producing areas in the south; which can have some negative impact to the crops and pasture up to early next year.

The impact of localized flooding particularly in riverine areas destroyed farmland and crops and caused population displacement, leading to significant crop losses and the loss of income from agricultural employment.

Jointly with the Government and other humanitarian actors, WFP Somalia has supported communities and vulnerable houses impacted by the multiple shocks. The high levels of sustained humanitarian assistance in 2020 have played a critical role in stabilizing the situation. The immediate food security outlook for Somalia however looks bleak despite the efforts sustained in 2020. According to the latest Post-Gu Assessment, 2.1 million people are expected to be food insecure (IPC 3 and 4) across Somalia through December 2020. An additional 3 million people are expected to be Stressed (IPC 2), bringing the total number of people facing cute food insecurity to 5.1 million until the end of this year. Based on results of the 2020 Post Gu assessment, an estimated 849,900 children under the age of five years face acute malnutrition between September 2020 and August 2021, including 143,400 likely to be severely malnourished.

project_text:
CCCM Assistance to conflict and disaster-induced displaced persons in South Sudan According to Round 11 of IOM DTM’s monitoring of displacement and return movement, 2,017,236 people remain displaced in South Sudan, 78% of which are sheltering with already crisis-affected host communities. In a number of displacement sites and collective centers, including current and former PoCs, more than 440,000 individuals continue to live in situations of protracted displacement. Displacement figures have continued to increase despite the signing of the R-ARCSS in 2018 due to an increase of displacement-inducing incidents such as sub-national conflict and unprecedented climate-related disasters.

IOM CCCM aims to target 523,000 people of the total 1.4 million people targeted under the CCCM Cluster Response Plan. IOM will continue to provide displaced communities with basic and emergency camp management services, ensuring that the provision of protection and cross-sectoral humanitarian assistance is equitable, coordinated, monitored and adhering to standards. Of critical relevance to the current displacement environment in the country, IOM CCCM’s interventions will also integrate a robust, community-led disaster-mitigation lens in all care & maintenance interventions and capacity building exercises to enhance protective environments to increase resilience of infrastructure and communities to climate shocks. Further, fully committed to ensuring that AAP is streamlined in any and all activities, IOM will continue to develop and improve AAP mechanisms to ensure that the organization is accountable to the people that it serves and that programmes are informed by the voices of the displaced communities.

IOM intends to contribute to the sectoral objectives through the following interventions:

1)	Continued and adapted provision of critical CCCM activities to IDPs living in Bentiu, Naivasha and Hai Masna IDP Sites as well as critical care & maintenance activities in Malakal PoC.
2)	Deployment of emergency CCCM teams to deliver sustainable mobile responses promoting self-governance, community ownership and resilience in hard-to-reach locations following triggers at the ICCG-level.
3)	Co-lead the CCCM Cluster at national level and continue acting as SFP in WBeG, Jonglei and Upper Nile States in order to support national and state-level partner agencies in accountable CCCM responses and systems.
4)	Continue chairing the CCEWG in order to provide technical CCE support to partner organizations and to operationalize outputs under the 2021 South Sudan AAP Framework.

project_text:
Enhancing capacities of women, men, girls, and boys in IPC 3, 4 and 5 in South Sudan to withstand and recover from food insecurity Project Summary The proposed HRP 2022 interventions will target locations with IPC 4 and 5 with emergency food security and livelihoods assistance to the most vulnerable populations affected by shocks including floods, conflicts which has contributed to the elevation of food insecurity outcomes with 31 counties of extreme or severe concern and 36 very high or high concern. The convergence of shocks such as floods, conflicts, hyperinflation of prices for basic commodities and now compounded with social and economic impact of Covid 19 at glance have made the population vulnerable deepening the humanitarian situation. The proposed interventions are aligned to the HRP 2022 cluster objectives; CO1: Provide food assistance to prevent famine and improve food consumption, dietary diversity and coping strategies for vulnerable populations, CO2: Enhance and sustain emergency food production through complementary vegetable and crop livelihood inputs, fishing and livestock support and CO3: Reduce dependency on food and agricultural inputs to support and strengthen households’ ability to absorb shocks. The project is planned to be implemented in Kajo Keji, Yirol east, Akobo, Pibor, Uror, Nyirol, Rumbek centre, Pochalla.
This HRP project will complement Oxfam ongoing resilient programming to provide immediate quick impact activities while protecting the gains of resilience programming. Protection and Gender will be mainstreamed throughout the project lifetime, a Do No Harm approach as enshrined in Oxfam safe programming approach will be mainstreamed by ensuring participation and accountability to affected population. This project will be implemented by Oxfam and its local partners.

project_text:
Food assistance to address increasing levels of severe food insecurity in South Sudan Meet the lifesaving food requirements of people in South Sudan who are facing food security crises, including those living in (ex)-POCs and IDP and those otherwise affected by conflict, natural disaster and/or seasonal food insecurity. WFP will provide general food distributions (GFD) to the most food insecure people in South Sudan. At the field level, food assistance will be overseen by the WFP Field Offices and implemented by NGO partners or provided through the Integrated Rapid Response Mechanism (IRRM). IRRM is a Delivering as One approach, in which UNICEF supports WASH and nutrition activities, FAO provides emergency seeds and livelihood kits, and WFP provides food assistance and common services through a comprehensive and collaborative humanitarian intervention by deploying mobile teams, supported by cooperating partners to reach populations facing the most urgent needs in the most inaccessible areas of the South Sudan, subject to the availability of resources.

Complementary to food distributions, WFP will seek to offer value-added solutions (GFD+), in response to needs and priorities identified by the community. Through GFD+, WFP together with its cooperating partners and other stakeholders will provide unconditional opportunities, identified through a community-based, people-centric participatory approach to targeted beneficiaries. GFD+ adds value to emergency food assistance with a focus on solutions that address the root causes of food and nutrition insecurity and better equip beneficiaries to fight hunger. The GFD+ activity type, duration, frequency, and participation will be catered to specific local sites and may range from COVID-19 awareness and mitigation measures to nutrition education, dyke rehabilitation and communal asset management, income-generating activities which lead to women's economic empowerment and have positive impact on household food security, or other solutions. WFP will also implement resilience building activities including Food Assistance for Assets (FFA) to support communities to improve their food security, restore their livelihoods, strengthen their resilience to shocks and build self-reliance, while contributing to peace.

Mitigation measures to reduce and prevent the potential the spread of COVID-19, including new variants, and other potential viral outbreaks have been incorporated into standard operating procedures for all interactions with beneficiaries, including training of partners and stakeholders, increasing general awareness among partners and beneficiaries, enforcing social distancing, promoting handwashing, disinfecting sites, reducing the frequency of distribution cycles, and mandating the utilization of personal protective equipment (PPE). These measures are mainstreamed into all WFP activities and are part of the ‘new way of working’.

description: FAOs drought response aims to immediately increase urgent access to food, water, and basic necessities and protect livelihoods for 61,200  severely drought-affected individuals in south and central Somalia.

destinationObjects_Project.name: Emergency Lifesaving Cash and Livelihood Support to IDP and Non- IDP Communities in Somalia
project_text:
Emergency Lifesaving Cash and Livelihood Support to IDP and Non- IDP Communities in Somalia Somalia is facing a severe and deteriorating humanitarian crisis as we enter 2022 as a result of the compounding effects of conflict, recurrent climate shocks, diseases and pests outbreaks with increased levels of vulnerability and substantial increase in the humanitarian caseload (Somalia HNO, 2022). There is a serious risk that the impact of consecutive below average to poor rainfall in most parts of the country will develop into a severe drought by early to mid- 2022 with the number of people facing acute food insecurity on the rise. It is likely that minority groups, women, children, people with disabilities, will experience heightened protection risks as a result, unless they are intentionally targeted to receive tailored assistance.

With approximately 3.5 million individuals in IPC 3 and 4 through at least December 2021, FAO proposes to target 160,300 households (961,800 individuals- 91,500 IDPs and 870,300 non- IDPs) in IPC 3 and IPC 4 caseloads respectively. This will include 216,790 women, 254,492 girls, 264,880 boys and 225,638 men and 144,270 people living with disabilities (PWD) across 59 districts in Somalia through its flagship Cash+ approach combining short-term cash transfers with tailored livelihood support in accordance with technical and humanitarian standards. Vulnerable households will identified from at-risk pastoral, agro-pastoral, fishing, riverine farmers, IDPs and Non- IDP communities in IPC 3 and 4 areas. This intervention will integrate short-term cash transfers aimed at enabling the most vulnerable households to meet their immediate needs, with livelihood support to allow crisis-affected households to get back into production. FAO will employ community- led beneficiary selection processes and ensure adequate targeting and representation of extremely vulnerable and minority groups in community committees. Interventions proposed will employ a Do No Harm approach with a gender lens that ensures conflict- sensitivity to reduce protection risks for all individuals, and to mitigate the risk of conflict or community tensions. 

Under Food Security Cluster (FSC) Objective 1, to improve access to food, FAO will deliver lifesaving cash assistance to 160,300 households through a blend of conditional (Cash-for-Work) and unconditional (UCT) transfers. Under UCT, FAO will prioritize Cash+ interventions including Cash+ Agriculture, Cash+ livestock and Cash+ fisheries. These modalities will increase households’ immediate access to food by providing sufficient cash to access the minimum expenditure basket (MEB), while supporting the rehabilitation of critical productive and community infrastructure. It will also boost household food production, increase household incomes and create employment opportunities. Cash transfer values will be informed by the Cash Working Group and are expected to differ per district/ region of intervention. They, however, will be valued at 80 percent of the food MEB, which can range from USD 50- 100 per month. All cash-based programmes will include training on good nutrition practices. 

Under FSC Objective 2, to protect livelihoods and related food sources, FAO will provide in-kind, technical support and tailored trainings to 112,500 HHs to anticipate, mitigate and respond to food security and nutrition threats, including the delivery of integrated cash and livelihood support to targeted HHs. In addition, FAO shall provide transitional cash support to 13,100 HHs across agro pastoral, pastoral and fishing livelihood zones to augment the adaptive capacity of HHs, strengthen and foster resilience to future shocks, cushioning them from food insecurity and malnutrition. Trainings shall be delivered alongside input provision to build skills in sustainable use of resources provided, build skills in livelihoods management including harvest, post- harvest management, linking beneficiaries to long- term interventions that provide them opportunities to enhance their livelihoods and skills.

project_text:
Provision of lifesaving assistance and sustainable solutions through safe Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) services, for people in crises and their host communities in multiple regions in Somalia. IOM WASH is proposing to contribute to lifesaving of access to safe and equitable basic WASH services to overall 281,400 beneficiaries from vulnerable Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) and host-communities in multiple regions in Somalia. 

Specifically, the project will target 168,840 Non displaced people (children 104,681; women 27,014; Disabled 25,326; and elderly 11,819) and 112,560 displaced populations (children 69,787; Women 18,010; Disabled 16,884; and elderly 7,879)
IOM will rehabilitate 60 strategic water sources for multi-use (human and animals) and further 55 community berkads (water reservoirs) that will provide continued, equitable, safe, sufficient and sustainable water to regions, targeted by the cluster, prone to natural disasters.
IOM further proposes to construct 3,300 new emergency sanitation facilities (following cluster specifications) targeting populations without access to basic sanitation and hygiene.

The project will also strengthen the capacity of the Federal Government of Somalia and Federal Members States, community leaders and water committees/technicians for better coordination with government authorities and communities and sustainability of the constructed/ rehabilitated WASH infrastructures. In addition, the project will nurture community participation in good hygiene practices through training and community sensitization campaigns.

The project is aligned with protection mainstreaming to ensure safety and dignity of affected populations without causing harm. Affected populations and all relevant stakeholders including men, women, boys, girls, elderly and people with disability will be involved in decision making throughout the project activities/cycle. Furthermore, the project will be a part of an IOM integrated emergency response program and resilience building, where possible, efforts will be made to integrate IOM health, nutrition, shelter, CCCM and protection activities.

description: WFP Integrated Response to Prevent Famine in Bay, Banadir and Mudug regions of Somalia.

destinationObjects_Project.name: WFP SOMALIA 2022 HRP - FSC
project_text:
WFP SOMALIA 2022 HRP - FSC Somalia has been impacted by multiple shocks in 2020, including desert locust invasion, flash floods and COVID-19. This has negatively affected the ability of vulnerable households to meet their food security needs. The urban poor, including IDP households, have been disproportionally affected due to the socio-economic effects from COVID-19 due their heavy reliance on food purchases from the market and casual labor as the main sources of income. These households are likely to face food consumption gaps due to declines in employment and income-earning opportunities. The desert locust caused significant damage to cereal crops, fruits, vegetables and pasture in the northern and central regions. Control efforts of the government and partners in Somaliland and Puntland made progress, but an increasing number of adult locust groups was reported in central regions. In addition, in the northeast, remained swarms have matured, and some have moved towards central areas. As per FAO, the hatching and band formation is occurring now and more swarms are likely to move to other areas in central Somalia and at later stages are expected to move towards crop producing areas in the south; which can have some negative impact to the crops and pasture up to early next year.

The impact of localized flooding particularly in riverine areas destroyed farmland and crops and caused population displacement, leading to significant crop losses and the loss of income from agricultural employment.

Jointly with the Government and other humanitarian actors, WFP Somalia has supported communities and vulnerable houses impacted by the multiple shocks. The high levels of sustained humanitarian assistance in 2020 have played a critical role in stabilizing the situation. The immediate food security outlook for Somalia however looks bleak despite the efforts sustained in 2020. According to the latest Post-Gu Assessment, 2.1 million people are expected to be food insecure (IPC 3 and 4) across Somalia through December 2020. An additional 3 million people are expected to be Stressed (IPC 2), bringing the total number of people facing cute food insecurity to 5.1 million until the end of this year. Based on results of the 2020 Post Gu assessment, an estimated 849,900 children under the age of five years face acute malnutrition between September 2020 and August 2021, including 143,400 likely to be severely malnourished.

project_text:
Emergency WASH Response in South Sudan UNICEF will provide women, men, girls, and boys affected by multiple shocks and hazards
in South Sudan with critical water, sanitation, and hygiene services, items, and facilities.
The objective of this project is to provide lifesaving emergency water supply, sanitation
and hygiene promotion services for con􀂧ict affected people, vulnerable host communities
and people in disease prone (high GAM famine and outbreak related) areas including
protection related actions to mitigate GBV, strengthening of communities’ resilience to
cope with the impact of emergencies and recurrent shocks. This emergency WASH project
will comprise of situation assessments, preparedness, transitional programs, frontline
emergency WASH response, strengthening of partners’ capacity, and cluster coordination
including sector information management. UNICEF will deliver emergency lifesaving
support by providing access to WASH services as per Sphere and WASH Cluster
standards.
The project will focus on addressing the following:
- Effective Cluster coordination mechanism in the country
- Provide timely equitable access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene for IDPs/host
communities and returnees, including transitional programming
- WASH in Nutrition for famine prevention with a minimum package of interventions.
- WASH in Health for outbreak control at wider community level (i.e. Ebola, Cholera, etc.)
- While implementing projects a special attention will be given to mitigate WASH-related
GBV.
The project will also support expansion of partnerships with local and international NGOs
and CBOs in highly affected areas to ensure basic services are provided and long-term
capacity built. The activities will be implemented in complementarity with other sectors
such as Health, Nutrition, Protection and where possible Education projects including
disaster risk reduction (DRR) focusing on strengthening community coping mechanisms.

Ethiopia CO (WFP) continues to provide emergency and lifesaving food assistance in conflict, post-conflict or disaster situations based on government request. project_text: Assistance inconditionnelle en cash et kits AGRs pour renforcer la résilience des ménages PDIs et communautés hôtes du département de Ouallam, région de Tillabery L'objectif dudit projet vise à améliorer la sécurité alimentaire et renforcer la résilience des ménages vulnérables à travers le cash reçu et les Kits AGRs de protection sociale. Les activités de ce projet seront mises en œuvre au niveau des communes de Ouallam et de Tondikiwindi (Mangaizé, Tondikiwindi et Diney) au profit des ménages vulnérables PDIs et communautés hôtes. Au total, 1 600 ménages seront identifiés à travers l'enquête d'Analyse de l'Economie des Ménages/Household Economic Analysis (HEA).  Cette identification tiendra compte du genre (chefs de ménages hommes et chefs de ménages femmes), de l'inclusion sociale : personnes vivant avec handicap, vieilles personnes, ménage avec enfant non accompagné, femmes enceintes ou allaitantes, etc…). Le présent projet touchera 11 200 personnes (soient 4,72% de la cible présentée dans le document « PIN & Cibles SECAL 2022"""""""") pendant six (6) mois allant de Mars 2022 à Aout 2022 afin de satisfaire leurs besoins alimentaires au cours des périodes de pré-soudure et soudure surtout qu’il y’a risque d’épuisement précoce des stocks céréaliers cette année (décembre/janvier) et des disponibilités fourragères aggravées par l’inaccessibilité dans les zones de conflits et les pertes dues aux feux de brousse. Chaque ménage bénéficiaire recevra une somme de 32 500 F CFA par mois pour lui permettre de se procurer de vivres pour le besoin du ménage. Le paiement des bénéficiaires sera facilité par une Institution de Microfinance. En plus, ces ménages recevront de kits AGRs de protection sociale (les femmes des 1 600 ménages bénéficiaires seront organisés en groupe de 20 femmes, ce qui donne 80 groupes de femmes et chaque groupe recevra un kit AGRs), des séances de sensibilisation communautaire sur les Engins Explosifs Improvisées (EEI) seront conduites par les agents de GOAL et des actions de plaidoyer à l’échelle locale et communautaire seront menées afin d’avoir un meilleur impact national. Le projet sera mis en œuvre avec la participation de tous les acteurs concernés (les autorités : administratives, Communales, Coutumières ; les services techniques et les communautés concernés).

destinationObjects_Project.name: Provision of shelter and NFI support to communities affected by displacement and environmental shocks in Somalia and Somaliland.
reportDetails_organization: European Commission's Humanitarian Aid and Civil Protection Department; Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
project_text:
Provision of shelter and NFI support to communities affected by displacement and environmental shocks in Somalia and Somaliland. As conflicts and recurrent environmental shocks continue to drive people out of their places of origin, resulting in unpredictable and sudden displacements, requiring a quick response from humanitarian actors to deliver essential relief.  According to the CCCM cluster, 2,241,328 people will need humanitarian assistance in 2022 due to the lack of durable solutions, continued conflicts, and recurrent shocks. 
As such, shelter and non-food item needs remain significant across displacement-affected communities in Somalia, with recurrent displacement trends underpinning protracted needs for shelter and NFI assistance in the proposed locations. Therefore, the proposed action will target locations in Kismayo, Hargeysa, Ceel Afweyn, Laasqoray and Baidoa districts. The project will benefit 16,446 individuals (2,741 HHs without double counting). Under this, ACTED proposes an in-kind distribution methodology instead of a voucher system to allow for prepositioning and rapid emergency response when the need arises. The storage and transportation of the materials to the distribution points and related costs are managed by the selected competent and qualified suppliers, a requirement in the contract signed between ACTED and the suppliers.  In parallel with the provision of emergency shelter and NFI support, and in line with the primary objective of working towards facilitating recovery and access to durable solutions, ACTED will provide transitional shelters to IDP households living on land protected by land tenure agreements in IDP sites that have stable land tenure agreements. Significant rates of eviction render durable shelter solutions appropriate only in cases where land tenure agreements exist and provide a critical foundation for persons facing protracted displacement in the assertion of pathways to recovery. 
In order to assess the efficiency of the assistance provided, level of satisfaction of the beneficiaries with the items received and the overall impact, ACTED will conduct post distribution monitoring 6 weeks after the distribution of ESK/NFI and post construction monitoring 3 months after the handover of transitional shelters to analyze the impact and draw lessons learnt for future programming.

project_text:
Humanitarian coordination and provision of CCCM-integrated responses to displacement-affected populations in Juba and Bor former PoC sites (semi-static) in hard-to-reach areas (mobile) In line with the CCCM cluster strategy, ACTED will continue to provide humanitarian coordination and CCCM integrated response to displacement affected population in Juba former PoC sites and will provide mobile support in hard-to-reach areas in response to displacement shocks.  Due to natural hazards, localized and state conflicts, displacement waves remain high in South Sudan with 1.64 million people currently being Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) in need of CCCM assistance according to the South Sudan HNO 2022. The trend has been increasing in 2022 following massive natural hazards such as floodings in Jonglei state, leading to the multiplication of displacement sites. 
As South Sudan has been subject to displacement waves since its creation, and particularly following the 2013 civil war, some IDP sites have existed for several years with residents not willing to return to their areas of origin and ongoing humanitarian aid. To address this issue, ACTED aims to provide a more sustainable solution and support these IDP communities to become more empowered and increase their integration into host communities settings. Following a strategy implemented since 2021 in agreement with CCCM cluster, ACTED handed over camp management responsibilities to the community representatives and local authorities, especially Relief and Rehabilitation Commission (RRC) in Bor and Juba former PoC camps in 2022. In 2023, ACTED will strengthen social cohesion between IDPs and host communities in Juba to foster peaceful coexistence and will provide ad-hoc support to community representatives if needed to ensure a smooth transition. 
In parallel, ACTED provides emergency CCCM assistance in response to displacement shocks across the country. Through a well-established coordination system with REACH, the Inter Cluster Coordination Group, the Needs Analysis Working Group and the clusters, ACTED has access to timely information on displacements, allowing for a rapid multi-sectoral intervention whose core is CCCM services. Within its CCCM rapid response, ACTED aims to provide life saving coordination activities among humanitarian actors and build local communities’ capacities to self manage the sites. 
Therefore, ACTED will continue implementing CCCM interventions in line with the following cluster objectives: CO1: Improve living condition of IDPs by facilitating safe, equitable and dignified access to cross-sectoral humanitarian services, including CCCM CO2: Enhance the protective environment, respond to vulnerable population with priority on addressing protection gaps and strengthen the predictability and effectiveness of multi sectorial interventions at site level CO3: Support vulnerable IDPs to recover from the crisis by strengthening community self-management, build resilience to promote solutions for displaced people in sites.

reportDetails_organization: European Commission's Humanitarian Aid and Civil Protection Department
project_text:
Assurer la continuité de l'éducation des enfants affectés par la crise sécuritaire dans la région de Tillaberi au Niger L’escalade de l’insécurité dans les zones frontalières durant continue d’impacter tous les secteurs, mais encore plus durablement le secteur de l’Education.  En effet, selon les résultats de l’analyse de l’impact de l’insécurité sur l’éducation, 579 écoles sont fermées dans la région de Tillaberi avec une situation très critique dans les départements frontaliers, tels que Torodi avec plus 50% d’écoles fermées, Téra, 45% et Ayorou avec 37%. Cette fermeture a affecté plus de 53 562 enfants dont 48% de filles. Les efforts de l’Etat et ses partenaires, ont permis le retour à l’école et l’inscription de certains enfants, soit 18% des enfants (19% chez les filles) issus des écoles fermées (DREN Tillaberi, Novembre 2021). Au cours de l’année académique 2021/2022, plus de 82% des élèves issus des écoles fermées, sans compter les enfants qui devraient s’inscrire cette année en cours d’initiation (CI) sont en dehors de l’école. Selon qu’on soit dans les zones de conflits ou dans les zones d’accueil des populations déplacés, les problèmatiques en matière d’éducation ne sont pas les mêmes.
Il est plus que nécessaire de développer des alternatives éducatives adaptées au contexte sécuritaire de chaque zone (zone de conflit et zone d’accueil) pour favoriser le retour à l’école des enfants affectés par cette crise sécuritaire. C’est ainsi qu’un consortium composé de la Fundacion Education Y Cooperacion ( Educo) et l’ Association Nigérienne pour le Traitement de la Délinquance et la prévention du crime (ANTD) ont initié ce projet dont l’objectif global est de contribuer à la réinsertion et à la continuité de l’accès à une éducation inclusive, sure et de qualité des filles et garçons affectés par les crises humanitaires dans la région de Tillaberi au Niger. De manière spécifique, cette initiative vise à réduire les obstacles à l’éducation des filles et des garçons de 6 à 17 ans hors du système éducatif affectés par la crise sécuritaire et sanitaire dans les départements de Tera, Bankilaré et Ouallam, de la région de Tillaberi. Pour concrétiser ces objectifs, le projet prévoit les strategies éducatives suivante : 1)   le transfert de 734 élèves de 12 à 17 ans en particulier les filles et porteurs de handicap, issus des zones de conflits, vers les écoles des zones les plus sécurisées , 2) la mise en place d’Espaces communautaire d’apprentissage ouvert au profit de 1101 enfants de 6 à 12 ans dans les zones à conflits modéré, 3) la promotion de l’éducation à distance (radio) au profit de 1468 enfants de 9 à 12ans dans les zones à conflits modéré, 4) la réinsertion scolaire par la Stratégie de scolarisation accélérée/passerelle (SSAP) au profit de 734 enfants de 9 à 14 ans en dehors de l’écoles dans les zones d’accueil des PDI et des Réfugiés, 5) l’inscription, réinscription de 2568 enfants de 6 à 17 ans en dehors de l’écoles dans les zones d’accueil des PDI et des Réfugiés et 6) le maintien scolaire de 734 enfants non accompagnés de 13 à 17 ans issus des zones de conflits réinscrit dans les écoles sécurisé. Le projet touchera un total de 7338 enfants, y compris les enfants porteurs d’handicap de 6 à 17 ans dont 60% de filles.

destinationObjects_Project.name: Renforcement de la protection pour les personnes vulnérables, en particulier les enfants, les survivants de violence basée sur le genre (VBG) et victimes de traite dans les régions de Diffa, Tillabéry, Maradi et Tahoua
project_text:
Renforcement de la protection pour les personnes vulnérables, en particulier les enfants, les survivants de violence basée sur le genre (VBG) et victimes de traite dans les régions de Diffa, Tillabéry, Maradi et Tahoua Les risques de violations des droits des hommes et femmes, y compris les risques de traite et de VBG, seront amoindris à travers la promotion d’un environnement communautaire protecteur et d’un accès renforcé aux services de protection, y compris aux services Santé mentale soutien psychosocial (SMSPS), dans les régions de Tillabéri, Diffa, Maradi et Tahoua.
Les activités cibleront les retournés, déplacés et membres des populations hôtes. Le projet prévoit 4 axes d’intervention.
1. Renforcement des capacités étatiques et des services sociaux de base dans les départements cibles pour une meilleure prise en charge des personnes en mobilité et notamment des enfants, y compris des survivant-e-s VBG et des victimes de traite : Un cycle de formation sur la protection des victimes de traite en situation de crise, permettant aussi de vulgariser le mécanisme national de référencement des victimes de traite, sera organisé pour tout acteur de la chaine de protection dans les communes cibles, dont les travailleurs sociaux de la protection de l’enfance et des organisations de la société civile (OSC). Il comprendra également des sessions sur la spécificité de la prise en charge des enfants non accompagnés en contexte humanitaire, et les besoins spécifiques des survivantes de VBG. 
2. Prévention des violences notamment envers les enfants, les femmes et les personnes en situation d'handicap, y compris de survivants de  VBG et diverses exploitations, à travers le renforcement des mécanismes communautaires de protection, l’appui aux leaders communautaires et la mobilisation des filles et garçons : En collaboration avec les DDPFPE, les mairies et les OSC, une cartographie et évaluation des besoins des structures communautaires, y compris les comités de protection, les espaces amis des enfants, les espaces surs et les écoles coraniques accueillant des enfants déplacés, seront réalisées. Suite à cette analyse, l’OIM les appuiera en matériel, afin que ces dernières puissent jouer leur rôle de protection. Leurs compétences seront renforcées afin qu’ils puissent signaler et référer les cas de protection, mais aussi qu’ils développent des actions de prévention qui encouragent des normes et comportements positifs favorisant des communautés respectueuses, égalitaires, et non violentes à l'égard des femmes et des filles. Des appuis aux initiatives des jeunes pour qu’ils sensibilisent leurs pairs seront réalisés. 
3. Atténuation des risques de protection dans les zones ciblées : En vue de prévenir l’adoption de stratégies de survie négatives des populations et de promouvoir leur dignité, l’OIM poursuivra la distribution des kits de protection adaptés aux besoins,  identifiés avec les populations. Enfin, l'organisation continuera le renforcement de la sécurité sur les sites d'intervention de l'équipe Abris et BNA & WASH afin de contribuer à la réduction des risques de protection. 
4. Offre de services de soutien psychosocial et de santé mentale (SMSPS) aux personnes déplacées, notamment les enfants, aux survivants de VBG et aux communautés hôtes : La stratégie de services de SMSPS de l’OIM est basée sur son expertise acquise auprès des migrants vulnérables et conformément aux principes développés par le « manuel de santé mentale et soutien psychosocial communautaire en situations d’urgence et de déplacement » (OIM, 2021). Des activités de sensibilisation et de formations des leaders communautaires et d’agents de santé sont organisées au préalable. Des équipes mobiles composées notamment d’un-e travailleur-se social-e, d’un-e infirmier-ère, d’un-e pyschologue, d’un-e mobilisateur-trice communautaire, se déplaceront pour offrir des activités psychosociales aux populations hôtes et déplacées, notamment là où les structures communautaires sont inexistantes. Tout au long du projet, l’OIM s’engagera avec les partenaires dans la Protection contre l’exploitation et les abus sexuels et le renforcement de la redevabilité envers les personnes affectées.

destinationObjects_Project.name: Appui à la protection des moyens de subsistance des pasteurs, Agropasteurs impactés par l'insécurité et le défficit fourrager des régions de Tillabéri, Tahoua, Diffa et Maradi ,Agadez, Zinder, Dosso
project_text:
Appui à la protection des moyens de subsistance des pasteurs, Agropasteurs impactés par l'insécurité et le défficit fourrager des régions de Tillabéri, Tahoua, Diffa et Maradi ,Agadez, Zinder, Dosso Le projet vise à apporter une assistance à 40363 ménages pastoraux, agropastoraux et déplacés dans  les zones à la fois affectées par un important déficit fourrager et un problème très critique d'insécurité induite par les  GANES à travers:   

    - la mise en place d'un appui en aliment  bétail de 14531 tonnes d'aliments bétail à la disposition de 40363 ménages pasteurs et agropasteurs vulnérables pour un total de 284541 personnes. un minimum de 13% de ces bénéficiaires seront  des femmes chefs de menages, veuves ou handicapés. soit 5247 ménages dirigés ar les femmes. l'assisttace en aliment profitera à un minimum 375376 têtes bénéficiaeront de cette assistance qui sera mise en place sous deux formes: en nature et via coupon. 20000 ménages d'éleveurs vulnérables de la catégorie des très pauvre disposant de 10 têtes de 375376 dont 363267 petits ruminantsou appartenant à 36327 petits éleveurs  propriétaires d'une UBT et 12109 petits éleveurs disposant de 3 bovins maximum . Chacun d'eux pourra accéder à une quantité  d'aliment bétail lui permettant d'apporter une complémentation alimentaire de 250 g et 2,5 kg par jour respectivement par petit ruminant et gros ruminant  pendant les  4 mois de période de soudure. La mise en place de cet important stock se fera à travers deux approches: (1) vente à prix modéré aux bénéficiaires de la carégorie des très pauvres préidentifiés  ; (2) et  distribution gratuite par voucher de 20% de ce stocks aux femmes allaitantes, aux  handicapés et  des veuves sans bras valides dans le menage. la priorité de l'assistance ira aux petits ruminants connus être le grenier de la femme pour palier au départ en exode de leur maris mais aussi supplier au difficulté d'accès au paturage naturel du fait de la présence des  GANESaui guettent les éleveurs dans les zones pourvues en paturage pour confisquer leurs animaux.  . Les paturages de la zone agricole n'offrant pas grand chose en termes de fourrage car envahis par Sida cordifolia non appétée, la seule alternative sera de mantenir les animaux dans leur terroir d'attache ou au piquet pour les agropasteur mais le niveau de déficit rend cette option peu crédible. project_text: Assistance d'urgence aux personnes déplacées dans les régions de Tahoua et Tillabéry Dans le cadre du HRP 2021, partant de la stratégie du GTABNA et en étroite collaboration avec le Ministère de l’Action Humanitaire, l'OIM poursuit l'objectif général de contribuer à l'amélioration les conditions de vie des populations. En particulier des populations déplacées vulnérables victimes des crises armées et l'activisme de GANEs spécialement dans les zones frontalières, dans les régions de Tahoua et de Tillabéry, par la fourniture d'abris d'urgence et de Biens Non Alimentaires. En tant que Co-Lead du Cluster,  l'OIM va contribuer au  renforcement de la coordination du Groupe de travail Abris et Biens Non Alimentaires, renforcer la collecte des informations, d'informer les intervenants sur la localisation, la nature et l'ampleur des besoins exprimés, sensibiliser les partenaires et membres du secteur à mener les activités dans le respect de la stratégie du secteur et les principes humanitaires et d'appuyer les services étatiques locaux dans leurs rôles de coordination et suivi des activités du secteur. La situation sécuritaire dans les régions de Tahoua et Tillabéry étant toujours volatile, le GTABNA reste attentif à tout mouvement de population et suit la situation au travers des annonces de sécurité, les MSA de RRM et le monitoring de protection du cluster protection fournissant les informations indicatives à la réponse en abris d’urgence et Biens Non Alimentaires.  Partant de la cible du HRP 2022, le secteur abris et bien non alimentaire mettra à disposition 7 000 kits abris d’urgence et 7 000 kits BNA en vue de répondre aux nouveaux mouvements de population, aux mouvements secondaires ainsi qu'au renouvèlement des abris détériorés des ménages. L’assistance basée sur la vulnérabilité ciblera également les familles hôtes vulnérables. Sur base de la stratégie du Secteur abris/BNA et dépendamment de la faisabilité, les interventions pourront se faire en transfert monétaires conditionnels. Cette modalité offrira la réduction considérable des coûts logistiques qui sont très élevés en période hivernale à cause du mauvais état des routes et permettra de résoudre le problème d’accès lié à l'insécurité qui retarde les interventions. Les activités de la réponse d'urgence se conformeront aux Principes de Protection transversales et au Cadre institutionnel de l'OIM de lutte contre les violences basées sur le genre en situation de crise (GBV), intégrera des mesures visant à assurer la sécurité, la dignité et le bien-être de la population touchée. Ce projet s'inscrira dans le respect des principes humanitaires et portera une attention particulière au principe ne pas nuire, de sécurité et non-discrimination. Les activités du projet seront mises en œuvre dans le respect soutenu des règles de lutte contre la COVID-19 par l'observation de mesures barrières telles que le port du masque, le lavage des mains, le respect de la distanciation sociale afin d'endiguer tout risque de contamination et de propagation de la maladie auprès des bénéficiaires. Dans le cadre de la redevabilité des sessions d'information sur le projet seront organisées avec les bénéficiaires, la phase d'évaluation des besoins sera réalisée de commun accord avec les populations dans les communes ciblées, la communication avec les communautés et les autorités locales sur les critères de ciblage seront organisées et après intervention, les feedbacks de la communauté cible seront collectés à travers des évaluations post-distribution et des séances de discussion de groupe séparées par genre et âge avant et après l'assistance. Aussi, en tant qu’acteur humanitaire, l'OIM et ses partenaires de mise en œuvre s’assureront que les actions n’induisent aucune tension ou problème dans la zone et n’exposent pas les bénéficiaires en affichant les compositions de kits BNA et Abris. A cet effet, une collaboration étroite sera faite avec les acteurs de protection pour un suivi de prêt de toute question de protection. Le coût total du projet sera de 4 161 500 USD.

project_text: Assurer une prise en charge holistique, adaptée et opportune aux survivantes de VGB  pour les déplacées internes, populations hotes des regions de Diffa, Tillaberi, Tahoua, et Maradi et Niamey Le projet vise à assurer dans un cadre bien coordonné, une prise en charge holistique qualitative de proximité adaptée au sexe, à l’âge, au handicap et au statut de déplacement pour les personnes survivant(e)s de VBG et réduire les risques de Violences Sexuelles et Basées sur le Genre, les exploitations et abus sexuels chez les personnes à risque. Il cible les populations, non déplacées /hôtes , les déplacées internes, les  retournées incluant les femmes, les hommes, les filles , y compris  les adolescentes et les personnes handicapées dans les régions de Tillaberi (départements de:  Téra, Torodi, Banibangou, Oullam, Say , Tillaberi , Ayerou, Bankilaré, Abala , Flingué,  Balleyara, Gotheye) ;  Tahoua( départements de : Abalak, Bagaroua, Birnin Koni, Illela, Madaoua , Tahoua, Tchintabaraden, Tillia, Tassara ), Maradi (départements de : Guidan Roundji , Madarounfa, Maradi ville ), et Diffa( départements de Bosso, Diffa, Goudoumaria, Maine-soroa, Ngourti, N'Nguigmi)  et Niamey affectées par les crises sécuritaires et transfrontalières. Le projet mobilisera les autres acteurs humanitaires des secteurs clés, les services déconcentrés de l’Etat, les communautés incluant les femmes, les hommes, les filles, les garçons et les personnes handicapées, pour assurer une participation inclusive dans la mise en œuvre des activités de façon intégrée en veillant au caractère adaptés et opportun pour survivantes de VBG. Ainsi tout en renforçant (formation équipements, suivi) les services de prise en charge, les outils (cartographie, SOP et chemin de référencement ; messages et module de formation à jours et compréhensifs) seront développés et mis à disposition des acteurs. Les acteurs communautaires (para juristes, comités de vigilances, chefs traditionnels, radio communautaires) seront formés et dotés de supports adaptés pour mener les activités de prévention et réduction des risques de VBG et assurer l'orientation des cas selon la stratégie communautaire (information et sensibilisation et orientation vers les services disponibles de qualités sur la base de des cartographie et chemin de référencement). Un mécanisme de gestion de l'information VBG (collecte analyse et partage) basé sur le GBVIMS garantira la qualité des données des cas et des évaluations périodiques renforceront le suivi de la situation pour une réponse adaptée et opportune. Des mécanismes de feed-back et de plaintes à la portée des communautés seront mis en place et opérationnalisés afin de mieux garantir la participation des communautés tout le long du cycle du projet et renforcer la qualité des interventions. Dans ce cadre chaque trimestre des rencontres inter acteurs et bénéficiaires seront organisées au niveau de chaque département où il sera partagé les résultats les insuffisances constatées et dégager les besoins d'amélioration pour la suite. Pour la redevabilité envers les mécanismes de coordination et les partenaires (bailleurs) des réunions mensuelles de coordination au niveau national et sous nationale de l'ensemble des acteurs membres du sous cluster renforcées par des missions de suivi et appui technique de la coordination nationale du sous cluster sur le terrain permettront de faire le suivi de la qualité, la veille de la situation, des rapports et des fac-sheet seront produits et partagés chaque trimestre..

project_text:
Niger Country Strategic Plan La vision de la réponse aux urgences dans le cadre du Plan Stratégique Pays (PSP) 2020-2024 du PAM Niger est la réduction de l’empreinte humanitaire dans la mise en œuvre de l’Activité 1, relative aux urgences du PSP à travers la promotion de l’approche NEXUS. Cette réponse s’inscrit dans la Stratégie de Prévention et de Gestion des Crises Alimentaires 2021 – 2025 du Dispositif National de Prévention et de Gestion de Crises Alimentaires (DNPGCA). Ce plan s’inscrit aussi dans le Plan d’Action 2021-2023 du Comité Technique Tripartite sur le Nexus Urgence-Développement (CTTNUD), en vue d’une mobilisation des ressources financières pour une planification et une mise en œuvre concertée des activités relatives à la promotion du NEXUS.  Dans le cas spécifique de l’assistance aux retournés dans leurs villages d’origine, qui est envisagée en 2022, la Loi 2018-74, relative à la protection et à l’assistance aux Personnes Déplacées Internes (PDI) cadrera le processus. Rappelons que l’Activité 1, relative aux urgences s’inscrit dans l’effet direct stratégique 1 du CSP (2020-2024) du PAM Niger « Les populations affectées, y compris les réfugiés, les personnes déplacées internes, les communautés hôtes et les retournés dans les zones ciblées sont en mesure de répondre aux besoins alimentaires minimums pendant et après la crise ».  La réponse aux urgences du PAM concernant la SECAL, basée sur une approche flexible, concernera toutes les trois (3) composantes de cette réponse en 2022 :
•	Le Mécanisme de Réponse Rapide (RRM)
•	La réponse aux crises prolongées.
•	La réponse à la soudure agricole et pastorale.
Par ailleurs la prévention de la malnutrition aux enfants 6-23 mois est combinée aux trois composantes ci-dessus.

destinationObjects_Project.name: Provision of Life Saving assistance to the disaster affected communities in Somalia
project_text:
Provision of Life Saving assistance to the disaster affected communities in Somalia Recurrent drought has severely and directly affected communities whose sources of food, income and water are diminishing and increasingly at risk. This has led to HH food insecurity, sharp increase in debt levels among poor HHs and poor animal health and produce. 
A delayed and poor Deyr season, worsened drought conditions in the target regions resulting in majority of HHs having inadequate access to food and water while staple food and commodity prices have risen at an average of 8.5% in Gedo and 24% in Bay regions over the past year (COOPI PNA, Oct 2021). From October to December 2021, food insecurity is expected to further deteriorate among poor rural, urban, and displaced populations due to the impacts of anticipated, below-average 2021 Deyr (October-December) season rainfall, continued insecurity and other food security related risk factors, including rising food prices and cost of living, declining availability of milk for both consumption and sale, and a likely reduction in agricultural employment opportunities during the forthcoming Deyr season.
The project focuses on the delivery of basic lifesaving and protection/restoration of livelihoods of the target population with a special focus on all locations with FSC prioritized persons in need, including IDPs and host communities that are classified in IPC Phase 3 & 4 in terms of response. 
The project is aimed at improving the ability of vulnerable HHs to meet their basic needs, supports protection and recovery of livelihood assets through life-saving UCT, animal treatment services, provision of locally preferred high quality seeds kits and trainings, and rehabilitation of community productive assets through CFW to support the resilience of vulnerable populations against shocks and prevent them from slipping into acute food insecurity. The proposed project aims to target at least 6,600 HHs (39,600) pastoral, agro-pastoral and IDP HHs in Bay, Banadir, Gedo and Togdheer regions in crisis and emergency with delivery of life saving interventions in line with the strategic objectives of the HRP and FSC response plan.
The project is informed by the centrality of protection and a gender, age and diversity-sensitive approach which is mainstreamed throughout the project cycle. Moreover, the project reflects the principles of COOPI Protection Policy and is built consistently with COOPI Protection SOPs and Protection Mainstreaming guidelines. The project will be guided by the principles of DO NO HARM, ensuring safety and dignity of target population is upheld and at the same time providing for accountability, participation and empowerment. COOPI prioritizes respect for the rights, dignity and safety of the people affected by crisis and is committed to taking account of, giving account to, and being held to account by the populations benefiting from the intervention. During implementation, the beneficiary women, girls and the disabled will be included in decision making processes and in monitoring so as ensure that the most marginalized and vulnerable are represented and have influence.
In summary the following activities will be carried out:
1.	Provide UCT to 3,100 HHs that are faced with severe levels of food insecurity (crisis and emergency) with the aim of improving immediate access to food for 3 months.
2.	Rehabilitation of community productive assets through CFW targeting 1,000 vulnerable HHs.
3.	Provision of locally preferred high quality seed kits, trainings and fuel for irrigation for 500 flood affected female and male headed vulnerable riverine farmers in Bele-Hawa Gedo region.
4.	Provision of locally preferred high quality seeds kit (drought tolerant) and trainings for 1,000 female and male headed vulnerable agro-pastoral farmers in Burhakaba district, Bay region.
5.	Emergency livestock treatment (treatment and deworming) campaigns for animals belonging to 1,000 HHs will be dewormed and treated against endemic &prevalent diseases.

destinationObjects_Project.name: Strengthening protective environment for displacement affected populations In Banadir, Galmudug, Lower Jubba and Gedo Regions through HLP interventions to improve tenure security situation and address post-eviction complications.
project_text:
Strengthening protective environment for displacement affected populations In Banadir, Galmudug, Lower Jubba and Gedo Regions through HLP interventions to improve tenure security situation and address post-eviction complications. The intervention is geared toward preventing and responding to eviction, monitoring of threats to evictions by assessing potential eviction sites, monitoring, documentation and reporting to relevant authorities and relevant clusters to mobilize support for advocacy. The advocacy and campaigns will aim to ensure actors facilitate lawful eviction processes. Capacity development targeting settlement managers, local authorities on Housing, Land and proper protection monitoring through ensuring collection of information based on the methodology of the Somalia Protection Monitoring System (SPMS).
Protection, monitoring and response mechanisms with regards to land, housing and property is lacking in most of protection programming. Most often legal Aid services, land, houses and property rights are not prioritized hence leaving big gaps in the protection response mechanism. There is poor coordination among protection and response service providers especially on land, housing and property rights. Furthermore, the protection response mechanisms have limited or no provision of free legal aid services to IDPs, survivors of GBV and HLP.
Therefore, this project seeks to improve and strengthen coordination among service providers and to enhance legal protection and response mechanism for IDPs on land, housing and property rights. These will be achieved through, improved referral pathways, on spot monitoring and response to assist IDPs reclaim housing, land and properties, awareness raising, free legal aid and innovative and sustainable alternative dispute resolution mechanisms.
NoFYL has presence in Banadir, Galmudug, Lower Jubba and Gedo Regions and has built strong linkages with communities and other actors which will facilitate the access and smooth implementation of project activities. NoFYL has an excellent record in linking with beneficiary communities (returnee, IDPs and host) affected by disasters and conflict, enabling them to cope with life threatening situations and recovery, and have good working relations with the local authorities and camp leaders. The progress of project activities will be monitored by NoFYL field offices in Kismayo and Mogadishu office. NoFYL has developed monitoring tools to monitor the progress. According to the agreed work plan, each activity will be monitored using participatory, results-based feedback mechanisms.

project_text:
Shelter and NFIs Assistance for Conflict and Drought-Affected Populations in Banadir, Lower Shabelle, Bay, and Hiiraan Regions - Somalia According to 2022 HNO, an estimated 3.6 million people are in need of shelter and NFIs assistance resulted by recurrent conflict, drought, flooding, evictions and cyclones as key drivers of humanitarian issues and caused vulnerability and migration from rural to urban and peri-urban centers resulted in inadequate shelter conditions, overcrowding, economic hardship, and lack of security of tenure. Those in need of shelter and NFI assistance include displaced and non-displaced populations. A total of 30,800 refugee and asylum seekers and 90,583 refugee returnees need shelter and NFIs assistance in 2022 as they do not have sufficient access to basic and domestic items and shelter assistance as well as financial capacity to build adequate shelters. As per UNHCR post return monitoring data, there is a high proportion of returnees live in housing they do not own and have no documentation as this leads to protection concerns, including housing insecurity and risk of eviction. On 2022 HNO, a total of 593,058 IDPs are to settle in informal and largely unplanned settlements facing unsafe living conditions, they do not have financial capacity to build adequate shelters. They usually do not own the land they occupy and also are not allowed to build any permanent structure. Due to lack of tenure agreements and housing options, minority and marginalized groups including women headed households as the main income earner have no alternative residence options. 
Importantly, Women and girls living in sub-standard and overcrowded shelters are particularly vulnerable. They tend not to feel safe in makeshift shelters which do not offer privacy and sufficient protection from weather elements and increase the risk of gender based violence. Over a quarter, 27%, of IDPs reported that their bathing facilities are not safe as their main shelter concern. In addition, marginalized groups and people with special needs also require additional support and should be prioritized as resources are limited.
As a result, this project is to address shelter and NFIs needs of IDP families and refugee (90%), while  poor host communities  (10%) will receive NFIs only in Kaxda  and Daynile districts of Banadir region, Afgoye and Marka districts of Lower Shabelle region, Baidoa district of Bay region, and Beletweyne of Hiiraan region in South and Central Somalia including women-headed household families, extended families, families with disabled and elderly persons who are most in need of humanitarian assistance to mitigate risk and its consequences on crisis-affected populations at the target areas. The main objective is to improve the living conditions and safe access to services of IDP families including refugee returnees and poor host communities in the targeted locations. HINNA aims at providing 5000 ESKs and NFI kits to 5000 HHs (30,000 beneficiaries/Individuals) while 3000 (10%) people of them will be poor host communities through in-kind distribution to improve the living conditions of the target beneficiaries who faced inadequate shelter/NFIs conditions. The reason we can't use cash transfer programming for this project is that we have had several meetings with the communities in some of the project target areas and most of them have told us that cash transfer program can cause insecurity, family violence that can lead to family breakdown and other things including missing kits or rising market prices.
Disaggregation of gender will be promoted in full consideration with protection mainstreaming. The total beneficiaries of the project (30,000 people) of the drought, floods, and conflict-affected populations including (4,800 women, 4,800 men, 9,600 boys, and 9,600 girls) including 1200 elderly people (4%) in the project target locations will directly be receiving any benefits of the project through selection criteria set by the shelter cluster.

project_text:
Appui à la protection des moyens de subsistance des pasteurs, Agropasteurs impactés par l'insécurité et le défficit fourrager des régions de Tillabéri, Tahoua, Diffa et Maradi ,Agadez, Zinder, Dosso Le projet vise à apporter une assistance à 40363 ménages pastoraux, agropastoraux et déplacés dans  les zones à la fois affectées par un important déficit fourrager et un problème très critique d'insécurité induite par les  GANES à travers:   

    - la mise en place d'un appui en aliment  bétail de 14531 tonnes d'aliments bétail à la disposition de 40363 ménages pasteurs et agropasteurs vulnérables pour un total de 284541 personnes. un minimum de 13% de ces bénéficiaires seront  des femmes chefs de menages, veuves ou handicapés. soit 5247 ménages dirigés ar les femmes. l'assisttace en aliment profitera à un minimum 375376 têtes bénéficiaeront de cette assistance qui sera mise en place sous deux formes: en nature et via coupon. 20000 ménages d'éleveurs vulnérables de la catégorie des très pauvre disposant de 10 têtes de 375376 dont 363267 petits ruminantsou appartenant à 36327 petits éleveurs  propriétaires d'une UBT et 12109 petits éleveurs disposant de 3 bovins maximum . Chacun d'eux pourra accéder à une quantité  d'aliment bétail lui permettant d'apporter une complémentation alimentaire de 250 g et 2,5 kg par jour respectivement par petit ruminant et gros ruminant  pendant les  4 mois de période de soudure. La mise en place de cet important stock se fera à travers deux approches: (1) vente à prix modéré aux bénéficiaires de la carégorie des très pauvres préidentifiés  ; (2) et  distribution gratuite par voucher de 20% de ce stocks aux femmes allaitantes, aux  handicapés et  des veuves sans bras valides dans le menage. la priorité de l'assistance ira aux petits ruminants connus être le grenier de la femme pour palier au départ en exode de leur maris mais aussi supplier au difficulté d'accès au paturage naturel du fait de la présence des  GANESaui guettent les éleveurs dans les zones pourvues en paturage pour confisquer leurs animaux.  . Les paturages de la zone agricole n'offrant pas grand chose en termes de fourrage car envahis par Sida cordifolia non appétée, la seule alternative sera de mantenir les animaux dans leur terroir d'attache ou au piquet pour les agropasteur mais le niveau de déficit rend cette option peu crédible. Le déficit de 15 millions de tonnes de matière sèche confirmé par la Direction du Developpement Pastoral  laisse entrevoir une situation très critiques durantla période de soudure particulièrement pour les petits éléveurs sans ressources pour pouvoir  se constituer un important stock de paille de brousse ou de SPAI. la probabilité reste très élévée pour cette catégorie d'éleveurs de connaitre de fortes  mortalités de bétail ou  un imprtant transfert du  capital reproducteur des petits éleveurs  vers les nantis de  la zone agricole ou les commerçants qui les achèteront à vil prix. la criticité de la situation s'annonce déjà eu egard au cours des sous produits agroindustriels quiamorcent déjàune hausse vertigineuse  atteingnant 6000 à 6500 CFA le sac de 50 kg et la 25000 celui d  cereale de 100 kg sur les marchés moins de 2 mois des récoltes de 2021.
- distribution de 4600 petits ruminants par kit de 3 chèvres et un bouc aux ménages ayant connu une forte décapitalisation de leurs animaux reproducteurs et/ou dont les animaux ont été confisqués par les ganes. ces derniers devront appartenir à la catégorie des très pauvres des régions de Maradi (Bermo),  de Tahoua (Tchintabaradene ), de tillabéri et de Dosso (Nord Doutchi). project_text:

Ce plan s’inscrit aussi dans le Plan d’Action 2021-2023 du Comité Technique Tripartite sur le Nexus Urgence-Développement (CTTNUD), en vue d’une mobilisation des ressources financières pour une planification et une mise en œuvre concertée des activités relatives à la promotion du NEXUS. La réponse aux urgences du PAM concernant la SECAL, basée sur une approche flexible, concernera toutes les trois (3) composantes de cette réponse en 2022 :
•	Le Mécanisme de Réponse Rapide (RRM)
•	La réponse aux crises prolongées.
•	La réponse à la soudure agricole et pastorale.
Par ailleurs la prévention de la malnutrition aux enfants 6-23 mois est combinée aux trois composantes ci-dessus.

project_text:
Food assistance to address increasing levels of severe food insecurity in South Sudan Meet the lifesaving food requirements of people in South Sudan who are facing food security crises, including those living in (ex)-POCs and IDP and those otherwise affected by conflict, natural disaster and/or seasonal food insecurity. WFP will provide general food distributions (GFD) to the most food insecure people in South Sudan. At the field level, food assistance will be overseen by the WFP Field Offices and implemented by NGO partners or provided through the Integrated Rapid Response Mechanism (IRRM). IRRM is a Delivering as One approach, in which UNICEF supports WASH and nutrition activities, FAO provides emergency seeds and livelihood kits, and WFP provides food assistance and common services through a comprehensive and collaborative humanitarian intervention by deploying mobile teams, supported by cooperating partners to reach populations facing the most urgent needs in the most inaccessible areas of the South Sudan, subject to the availability of resources.

Complementary to food distributions, WFP will seek to offer value-added solutions (GFD+), in response to needs and priorities identified by the community. Through GFD+, WFP together with its cooperating partners and other stakeholders will provide unconditional opportunities, identified through a community-based, people-centric participatory approach to targeted beneficiaries. GFD+ adds value to emergency food assistance with a focus on solutions that address the root causes of food and nutrition insecurity and better equip beneficiaries to fight hunger. The GFD+ activity type, duration, frequency, and participation will be catered to specific local sites and may range from COVID-19 awareness and mitigation measures to nutrition education, dyke rehabilitation and communal asset management, income-generating activities which lead to women's economic empowerment and have positive impact on household food security, or other solutions. WFP will also implement resilience building activities including Food Assistance for Assets (FFA) to support communities to improve their food security, restore their livelihoods, strengthen their resilience to shocks and build self-reliance, while contributing to peace.

Mitigation measures to reduce and prevent the potential the spread of COVID-19, including new variants, and other potential viral outbreaks have been incorporated into standard operating procedures for all interactions with beneficiaries, including training of partners and stakeholders, increasing general awareness among partners and beneficiaries, enforcing social distancing, promoting handwashing, disinfecting sites, reducing the frequency of distribution cycles, and mandating the utilization of personal protective equipment (PPE). These measures are mainstreamed into all WFP activities and are part of the ‘new way of working’.
