project_text:
Renforcement des mécanismes de Coordination et de Plaidoyer pour la protection humanitaire et l’assistance aux populations les plus vulnérables au Mali En 2021, la crise humanitaire au Mali s'est aggravée en raison de l'augmentation et de l'expansion des de la violence intercommunautaire et des attaques des groupes armés non étatiques (GANE) dans les régions du centre, du sud et de l'ouest. Cette crise a été aggravée par les bouleversements politiques marqués par deux coups d'état en août 2020 et mai 2021, et l'incertitude persistante de la transition politique laisse l'État dans l'incapacité de répondre aux services sociaux de base des populations. 
Les déplacements internes de personnes ont augmenté de 100 000 en 2021, atteignant plus de 401 000 personnes soit quatre fois plus qu'il y a deux ans. Au total, 156 000 réfugiés maliens résident dans les pays voisins tandis que le Mali accueille 48 000 réfugiés et leur fournit protection et assistance. Les gains économiques du Mali se sont érodés, avec 900 000 personnes (0,04% de la population) qui sont retombées dans la pauvreté en raison de la crise socioéconomique de la COVID-19. la capacité des ménages est fragilisée à cause de la perte de revenus, de la réduction des transferts de fonds et à l'augmentation du coût de la vie. 
La Banque mondiale prévoit une augmentation du taux de pauvreté à 4,8 % en 2022. La crise de protection est également aggravée avec une augmentation des incidents de sécurité.  Les acteurs de la violence basée sur le genre (VBG) ont signalé 5 486 incidents de VBG, soit une augmentation de 41 % comparativement à la même période en 2020. Plus de 1 640 écoles sont fermées en raison de l'insécurité, affectant plus de 2,9 millions d'enfants dont 40 % se trouvent dans la région centrale de Mopti. Quatre districts centraux ont signalé que 40 % des écoles étaient fermées. Dans les régions du sud, 10 pour cent des écoles sont fermées à Koulikoro, Koutiala et Sikasso, privant 30 000 enfants de leur éducation. A ce jour, le Mali a rapporté plus de 15 800 cas de COVID-19.
En 2021, 1,3 million de personnes ont connu un niveau élevé d'insécurité alimentaire aiguë. le niveau le plus élevé depuis 2015, et 3 055 253 personnes ont été touchées par les mauvaises pluies et une saison de soudure prolongée. La situation humanitaire reste entravée par l'augmentation des besoins et la faiblesse des financements, avec 32 % des fonds mobilisés au 31 octobre 2021. Malgré les contraintes opérationnelles, les partenaires humanitaires ont aidé plus de 2,45 millions des 4,7 millions de personnes ciblées au 30 septembre 2021. 
Les capacités de réponse existantes au Mali représentent plus de 160 organisations humanitaires, acteurs du développement ainsi que des forces militaires (MINUSMA, Forces maliennes de défense et de sécurité, Barkhane, Mission européenne de formation, G5 Sahel). Le contexte susmentionné exigera une coordination efficace et la présence d’OCHA demeure très importante. OCHA maintiendra sa présence à Bamako, Mopti, Tombouctou, Gao et ouvrira une antenne à Ségou tout en couvrant à distance les régions de Taoudénit, Ménaka, Kidal et les régions du sud Est et Ouest. 

Sept clusters actifs (Éducation, Sécurité alimentaire, Santé, Nutrition, Protection, Abris/BNA et WASH), des sous-clusters et des groupes de travail spécialisés (Accès, CM-Coord, Redevabilité, Genre et Cash) sont en place au niveau national et local. Le Bureau d’OCHA au Mali continuera ainsi à jouer un rôle central dans la mobilisation, la coordination et le soutien des acteurs humanitaires dans les domaines de la coordination, la gestion de l’information, le financement humanitaire et le plaidoyer. 

OCHA continuera à jouer son rôle central dans la mobilisation des partenaires, l’utilisation des instruments et des mécanismes de financement tout en veillant à ce que les besoins humanitaires croissants soient prises en compte. OCHA assumera son rôle clé dans la coordination militaire au niveau national et régional de concert avec les forces militaires présentes dans le pays tout en renforçant les capacités des autorités nationales en matière de coordination

project_text:
Programa de seguridad alimentaria basado en la escuela Con el objetivo de contribuir a la seguridad alimentaria de la población con mayores necesidades, el Programa Mundial de Alimentos de Naciones Unidas (WFP, por sus siglas en inglés) en Venezuela desarrolla un programa de asistencia humanitaria basado en la escuela para garantizar el acceso de los más vulnerables a una alimentación adecuada y nutritiva en el entorno escolar, familiar y comunitario. 
Este programa inició en 2021 con comidas escolares en emergencias priorizando escuelas iniciales y de educación especial.

WFP proporciona comidas escolares acompañado de un paquete integrado de intervenciones para mejorar el acceso a alimentos nutritivos y diversificados a través de las escuelas, contribuyendo al mismo tiempo a mejorar la salud y la nutrición de los niños en edad escolar, los estudiantes con discapacidad y el personal escolar, y apoyando a las comunidades a reducir la dependencia en estrategias de afrontamiento. De manera gradual, el WFP está realizando compras locales de alimentos, e incluyendo acciones para apoyar los mercados locales con compras a pequeños productores y apoyo técnico para acceso a mercados.

En este sentido, el programa de comidas escolares en emergencias tiene los siguientes componentes, para asegurar un enfoque integral que apoye al estudiante en el entorno escolar y familiar:

1. Entrega de comidas escolares nutritivas para estudiantes y personal escolar, promoviendo las compras locales y a pequeños productores.
2. Apoyo a la seguridad alimentaria del hogar a través de comida en especie o transferencias monetarias.
3. Rehabilitación de cocinas escolares para garantizar condiciones adecuadas de preparación de alimentos.
4. Comunicación para sensibilizar acerca de los principios humanitarios, la adecuada preparación de alimentos, nutrición, higiene y mantenimiento de cocinas escolares.
5. Fortalecimiento de capacidades de socios implementadores y personal escolar.
6. Acciones sensibles a la nutrición, que incluyen, tamizaje en las escuelas, educación nutricional, referencia a servicios especializados y entrega de alimento complementario fortificado (Supercereal Plus).

description: MULTISECTORAL INTERVENTION IN RESPONSE TO THE HUMANITARIAN CRISIS AND ENVIRONMENTAL EMERGENCIES IN SOMALIA AID 12255

destinationObjects_Project.name: Provision of Life Saving assistance to the disaster affected communities in Somalia
project_text:
Provision of Life Saving assistance to the disaster affected communities in Somalia Recurrent drought has severely and directly affected communities whose sources of food, income and water are diminishing and increasingly at risk. This has led to HH food insecurity, sharp increase in debt levels among poor HHs and poor animal health and produce. 
A delayed and poor Deyr season, worsened drought conditions in the target regions resulting in majority of HHs having inadequate access to food and water while staple food and commodity prices have risen at an average of 8.5% in Gedo and 24% in Bay regions over the past year (COOPI PNA, Oct 2021). From October to December 2021, food insecurity is expected to further deteriorate among poor rural, urban, and displaced populations due to the impacts of anticipated, below-average 2021 Deyr (October-December) season rainfall, continued insecurity and other food security related risk factors, including rising food prices and cost of living, declining availability of milk for both consumption and sale, and a likely reduction in agricultural employment opportunities during the forthcoming Deyr season.
The project focuses on the delivery of basic lifesaving and protection/restoration of livelihoods of the target population with a special focus on all locations with FSC prioritized persons in need, including IDPs and host communities that are classified in IPC Phase 3 & 4 in terms of response. 
The project is aimed at improving the ability of vulnerable HHs to meet their basic needs, supports protection and recovery of livelihood assets through life-saving UCT, animal treatment services, provision of locally preferred high quality seeds kits and trainings, and rehabilitation of community productive assets through CFW to support the resilience of vulnerable populations against shocks and prevent them from slipping into acute food insecurity. The proposed project aims to target at least 6,600 HHs (39,600) pastoral, agro-pastoral and IDP HHs in Bay, Banadir, Gedo and Togdheer regions in crisis and emergency with delivery of life saving interventions in line with the strategic objectives of the HRP and FSC response plan.
The project is informed by the centrality of protection and a gender, age and diversity-sensitive approach which is mainstreamed throughout the project cycle. Moreover, the project reflects the principles of COOPI Protection Policy and is built consistently with COOPI Protection SOPs and Protection Mainstreaming guidelines. The project will be guided by the principles of DO NO HARM, ensuring safety and dignity of target population is upheld and at the same time providing for accountability, participation and empowerment. COOPI prioritizes respect for the rights, dignity and safety of the people affected by crisis and is committed to taking account of, giving account to, and being held to account by the populations benefiting from the intervention. During implementation, the beneficiary women, girls and the disabled will be included in decision making processes and in monitoring so as ensure that the most marginalized and vulnerable are represented and have influence.
In summary the following activities will be carried out:
1.	Provide UCT to 3,100 HHs that are faced with severe levels of food insecurity (crisis and emergency) with the aim of improving immediate access to food for 3 months.
2.	Rehabilitation of community productive assets through CFW targeting 1,000 vulnerable HHs.
3.	Provision of locally preferred high quality seed kits, trainings and fuel for irrigation for 500 flood affected female and male headed vulnerable riverine farmers in Bele-Hawa Gedo region.
4.	Provision of locally preferred high quality seeds kit (drought tolerant) and trainings for 1,000 female and male headed vulnerable agro-pastoral farmers in Burhakaba district, Bay region.
5.	Emergency livestock treatment (treatment and deworming) campaigns for animals belonging to 1,000 HHs will be dewormed and treated against endemic &prevalent diseases.

The project is aimed at improving the ability of vulnerable HHs to meet their basic needs, supports protection and recovery of livelihood assets through life-saving UCT, animal treatment services, provision of locally preferred high quality seeds kits and trainings, and rehabilitation of community productive assets through CFW to support the resilience of vulnerable populations against shocks and prevent them from slipping into acute food insecurity. The proposed project aims to target at least 6,600 HHs (39,600) pastoral, agro-pastoral and IDP HHs in Bay, Banadir, Gedo and Togdheer regions in crisis and emergency with delivery of life saving interventions in line with the strategic objectives of the HRP and FSC response plan.
The project is informed by the centrality of protection and a gender, age and diversity-sensitive approach which is mainstreamed throughout the project cycle. Moreover, the project reflects the principles of COOPI Protection Policy and is built consistently with COOPI Protection SOPs and Protection Mainstreaming guidelines. The project will be guided by the principles of DO NO HARM, ensuring safety and dignity of target population is upheld and at the same time providing for accountability, participation and empowerment. COOPI prioritizes respect for the rights, dignity and safety of the people affected by crisis and is committed to taking account of, giving account to, and being held to account by the populations benefiting from the intervention. During implementation, the beneficiary women, girls and the disabled will be included in decision making processes and in monitoring so as ensure that the most marginalized and vulnerable are represented and have influence.
In summary the following activities will be carried out:
1.	Provide UCT to 3,100 HHs that are faced with severe levels of food insecurity (crisis and emergency) with the aim of improving immediate access to food for 3 months.
2.	Rehabilitation of community productive assets through CFW targeting 1,000 vulnerable HHs.
3.	Provision of locally preferred high quality seed kits, trainings and fuel for irrigation for 500 flood affected female and male headed vulnerable riverine farmers in Bele-Hawa Gedo region.
4.	Provision of locally preferred high quality seeds kit (drought tolerant) and trainings for 1,000 female and male headed vulnerable agro-pastoral farmers in Burhakaba district, Bay region.
5.	Emergency livestock treatment (treatment and deworming) campaigns for animals belonging to 1,000 HHs will be dewormed and treated against endemic &prevalent diseases.

reportDetails_organization: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
project_text:
Provision of Integrated Protection and Site Management Services to Internally displaced people, Returnees, Host Community  and Other Persons With Specific Needs in Ethiopia UNHCR’s 2022 protection programme builds on the scale up of 2021 response and will be implemented in nine regions. The programme, builds on evidence gathered from ongoing protection monitoring using the revamped Ethiopia Protection Monitoring Tool (E-PMT) in the operational areas to ensure the ongoing identification of protection and specific needs and changes in the protection landscape for IDPs, IDP returnees, host communities and other persons with specific needs requiring protection services. 
As the Protection Cluster-lead agency, UNHCR ensures the coordination of its activities, implemented directly or through partnerships, through the Protection Cluster at national and sub-national level as appropriate.
Based on the protection monitoring, UNHCR will implement an integrated set of protection services and interventions tailored to the needs and priorities of the affected, which include:
•	the provision of information, counselling, identification of protection and specific needs, referrals to services/assistance, 
•	direct provision of services and assistance to persons at risk or with specific needs; 
•	GBV awareness, prevention and response activities;
•	child protection awareness raising and case management;
•	strengthening of MHPSS, 
•	emergency EORE as required by the Mine Action AOR,
•	provision of legal awareness and legal aid for GBV case management, HLP, legal identity and civil document restoration, 
•	and strengthen social cohesion and community-based peacebuilding.

Through its CCCM intervention, UNHCR will provide care and maintenance service of site infrastructure for IDPs living in 63 sites in Tigray, 4 sites in Afar and 11 sites in Amhara for at least 230,000 vulnerable IDP children of under 18 (120,000 girls, 110,000 boys) and assisting more than 230,000 adult IDP population (103,000 Adult Men, 107,000 Adult Women(18-59 years), 11,000 Elderly Men and 10,000 Elderly Women (60 and above) which include 32,000 people with disabilities to ensure protection and assistance while striving for durable solutions.

sourceObjects_Organization.name: European Commission's Humanitarian Aid and Civil Protection Department

destinationObjects_Location.name: South Sudan

destinationObjects_Project.name: Protection and Assistance for Refugees, Returnees and Asylum Seekers in South Sudan
reportDetails_organization: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
project_text:
Protection and Assistance for Refugees, Returnees and Asylum Seekers in South Sudan As of January 2022, there are some 335,000 refugees and asylum seekers from neighbouring countries sheltering in South Sudan. Despite enormous socio-economic, security and political challenges, compounded by the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, South Sudan has maintained its open-door policy for people seeking international protection, the majority of whom are women and children, primarily from Sudan, the Democratic Republic of Congo and the Central African Republic.
At the same time, against a backdrop of fragile peace and cautious optimism for longer term stability, hundreds of thousands of South Sudanese refugees have spontaneously returned to the country since the signing of the 2018 Revitalized Peace Agreement. While UNHCR is not promoting or facilitating return to South Sudan, this spontaneous movement has prompted the development of an area-based approach, to support refugees, returnees and host communities, through enhanced engagement with development actors, to support greater access to services where possible.
Refugees largely reside in conflict-affected regions, challenged by an unpredictable security environment as well as at times fragile relations with host communities. Displaced communities will continue to rely on life-saving humanitarian assistance provided by UNHCR and its partners as a result of enduring economic hardship, weak rule of law, limited development support and a lack of social services and infrastructure in refugee-hosting areas as well as in areas of origin. A reduction in basic assistance, especially during a global pandemic, will immediately lead to the deterioration of the humanitarian situation to emergency levels, due to the absence of a safety net, including social services, community support networks and limited access to livelihoods in displacements sites hosting refugees and South Sudanese refugee returnees.
Under the refugee response, all refugees and asylum seekers registered with UNHCR will benefit from various forms of protection interventions, including individual registration and documentation, and multi-sector assistance. Specific protection services, such as SGBV response and child protection will focus on the identified at-risk groups. While water, health, nutrition and education services will continue to maintain indicators within global standards for refugees living in camps, provision of other assistance, including shelter, non-food items and livelihoods support, will be undertaken in a targeted manner, focusing on persons with specific protection needs and vulnerabilities. This will primarily be achieved through participatory assessments, surveys as well as verification exercise to identify vulnerable refugees and their needs. Impact monitoring will be used to gauge the efficiency of projects implemented and for the purposes of course-correction in terms of better targeting of assistance. The needs of persons with disabilities and the elderly will be further mainstreamed in various multi-sector response services. Vulnerable refugees in urban settings will also continue to benefit from targeted protection interventions and facilitation of their access to national services.

project_text:
Niger Country Strategic Plan La vision de la réponse aux urgences dans le cadre du Plan Stratégique Pays (PSP) 2020-2024 du PAM Niger est la réduction de l’empreinte humanitaire dans la mise en œuvre de l’Activité 1, relative aux urgences du PSP à travers la promotion de l’approche NEXUS. Cette réponse s’inscrit dans la Stratégie de Prévention et de Gestion des Crises Alimentaires 2021 – 2025 du Dispositif National de Prévention et de Gestion de Crises Alimentaires (DNPGCA). Ce plan s’inscrit aussi dans le Plan d’Action 2021-2023 du Comité Technique Tripartite sur le Nexus Urgence-Développement (CTTNUD), en vue d’une mobilisation des ressources financières pour une planification et une mise en œuvre concertée des activités relatives à la promotion du NEXUS.  Dans le cas spécifique de l’assistance aux retournés dans leurs villages d’origine, qui est envisagée en 2022, la Loi 2018-74, relative à la protection et à l’assistance aux Personnes Déplacées Internes (PDI) cadrera le processus. Rappelons que l’Activité 1, relative aux urgences s’inscrit dans l’effet direct stratégique 1 du CSP (2020-2024) du PAM Niger « Les populations affectées, y compris les réfugiés, les personnes déplacées internes, les communautés hôtes et les retournés dans les zones ciblées sont en mesure de répondre aux besoins alimentaires minimums pendant et après la crise ».  La réponse aux urgences du PAM concernant la SECAL, basée sur une approche flexible, concernera toutes les trois (3) composantes de cette réponse en 2022 :
•	Le Mécanisme de Réponse Rapide (RRM)
•	La réponse aux crises prolongées.
•	La réponse à la soudure agricole et pastorale.
Par ailleurs la prévention de la malnutrition aux enfants 6-23 mois est combinée aux trois composantes ci-dessus.

project_text:
Life-saving food assistance in North-East Nigeria WFP will provide unconditional food assistance to the most food-insecure, crisis-affected populations. Life-saving general food assistance (in-kind food and cash-based transfers) will be delivered to IDPs, returnees, and host populations in North-East Nigeria (Borno, Yobe, and Adamawa States). Early recovery and resilience to shocks will be promoted through asset creation and preservation, increased livelihoods opportunities, and enhanced agricultural value chains. Joint multi-sectoral assessments and Emergency Food Security Analysis will be conducted regularly to monitor the food security, and markets situation in crisis-affected states. 
A gender-transformative approach that meets the needs of women, men, girls, and boys will be adopted. WFP will mainstream protection throughout its work, supported by a solid understanding of the operational context and protection analysis. Training and capacity building of staff and partners in the protection and humanitarian principles will include on-the-job coaching. WFP will ensure that affected populations (women and men) will be consulted throughout the programme cycle; beneficiary feedback mechanisms will be tailored to their preferred means of communication. Beneficiaries will continue to be empowered with knowledge on their food assistance entitlements and their rights, including WFP’s zero-tolerance policy on Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA). Protection against Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) will be embedded in M&E tools, complaint feedback mechanisms, and training of partners and staff.
WFP will continue the collection of key information on beneficiaries and assistance provided as part of its M&E activities. Monthly monitoring will include distribution and activity site management; beneficiary and entitlement verification; and ensuring adequate protection and gender measures. Lessons will be regularly drawn from monthly process and biannual outcome monitoring and reporting, and periodic reviews and evaluation to inform strategic and operational decisions.
WFP will further consolidate partnerships to enhance national and state-level emergency preparedness and response systems, including food security and nutrition assessment and monitoring, early warning, protection, gender analysis, targeting and registration processes, safety nets, cash-based transfer capacities, and supply chain.
Where security and access to land allow, increasing livelihood activities will complement food assistance to support access to productive assets, income-generating activities, and self-reliance in the long term. Assistance will be coordinated with government distributions, ensure food assistance is complimentary and no gaps. self-reliance in the long term. project_text: Respuesta integral en seguridad alimentaria y nutricional de emergencia para la población más vulnerable afectada por la crisis en Venezuela. Acción Contra el Hambre (ACH) en Venezuela atiende las necesidades humanitarias de los grupos más vulnerables en riesgo de desnutrición aguda: < de 5 años, 5 – 14 años, mujeres embarazadas y lactantes (MEL), personas con discapacidades o con problemas de salud, en particular adultos mayores. Son agravantes las situaciones de pobreza y necesidades básicas no satisfechas como la falta de acceso a: alimentos, condiciones higiénico-sanitarias adecuadas, servicios de salud, y medios de vida. La desnutrición y el deterioro de la salud repercuten en una mayor exposición a factores agravantes como la violencia de género, embarazos adolescentes y criminalidad. A través del HRP, ACH brindará una respuesta humanitaria para la reducción del sufrimiento y ayudar a salvar vidas, identificando casos de desnutrición aguda y severa en las familias más a riesgo. Se trabajará a nivel comunitario y se coordinará con instituciones locales, en particular con escuelas y centros de salud. ACH trabaja con un enfoque de programa país y dentro de una estrategia regional, con intervenciones complementarias e integrales en: 1) Nutrición: sensibilización y consejerías; detección, tratamiento de la desnutrición aguda, y derivación de los casos con complicaciones médicas; capacitación en el manejo preventivo de la desnutrición aguda; 2) Salud: atención primaria, equipos, insumos, medicamentos, métodos anticonceptivos; 3) Seguridad Alimentaria y medios de vida: distribución de alimentos y apoyo para la producción de alimentos; 4) ASH: acceso a servicios de agua, saneamiento, e higiene, en escuelas y centros comunitarios; distribución de kits de higiene, y rehabilitación/reparación de sistemas de abastecimiento de agua y de saneamiento en comunidades. El sector de Protección y género, de manera transversal, trabajará en prevención de VBG, nuevas masculinidades y DSSR; establecimiento y/o fortalecimiento de espacios seguros para mujeres y niñas; atención psico-social, distribución de kits de higiene menstrual y protección para mujeres en riesgo. La respuesta actual de ACH se concentra en Caracas DC, Guárico, Carabobo, Miranda, Zulia, Bolívar, y próximamente en Falcón, Amazonas y Sucre.

(2022 portion)

project_text:
Emergency Water Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) support to population affected by conflict and climate induced crises in Ethiopia IOM is leading WASH activities in many IDP sites and host communities across Ethiopia, including distribution of hygiene kits, water trucking, construction and rehabilitation of water points, emergency latrines, and handwashing stations, establishment of community-based water or sanitation management committees, and hygiene promotion activities through contextualized campaigns and mobilization of gender-balanced hygiene promoters. 

In Ethiopia currently the internal displacement and humanitarian needs are mainly derived by the ongoing conflicts and droughts in some parts of the country. The displacement level in Ethiopia doubled in 2021, with over 2 million additional people displaced during 2021. According to IOM’s latest Displacement Tracking Matrix (DTM) National Displacement Report released in December 2021, a total of 4.2 million people were internally displaced across Ethiopia. This includes around 2.11 million IDPs identified in Tigray and neighbouring zones in Afar and Amhara regions as a result of the Northern Ethiopia Crisis. The ongoing displacements continue to pose serious protection concerns for the affected population. The majority of the displaced population live-in collective sites or in spontaneous settlements where they have limited access to essential services, dignified and safe living conditions to sustain their families and communities. A large number of the displaced population are women and children under 18.
 
IOM works under the framework of the 2021 HRP and 2022 draft HRP to enhance understanding of the crisis and assist joint, strategic response planning. This is particularly relevant to address new shocks and the confluence of needs. All interventions occur based on assessed needs, inter-cluster Initial Rapid Needs Assessments (IRNA) and cluster-specific assessments. All assessments integrate specific gender analyses. IOM further considers key protection needs including the risk of exposure to harm, exploitation, harassment, deprivation and abuse, including forms of violence that are gender-based; the ability to meet basic needs; access to basic services; and coping mechanisms. IOM uses both qualitative and quantitative assessment methodologies, including IOM's DTM; questionnaires; household and key informant interviews (including with local authorities and key community leaders); focus group discussions with women and youth; direct observation and review of secondary information. 

IOM has existing WASH programming in Tigray, Amhara, Afar, Oromia (East Hararghe and Borena), Somali (Dawa and Fafan zone), and SNNP regions (Konso zone) covering IDPs, returnees and host communities. Limited access to WASH NFIs, inadequate sources of safe water, inadequate sanitation facilities and prevalence of poor hygiene practices can render the populations living in collective centers/sites at risk of preventable diseases and overcrowded and congested IDP sites also pose a high level of risk to waterborne diseases, such as cholera. Assessments indicated that integrated WASH services are critical to ensure that facilities are maintained at a good standard and can be scaled up in case of population influxes, both in terms of the provision of safe water and increased hygiene promotion to prevent disease outbreaks.

In 2022, IOM appeals for USD 23,5 million to reach 1,6 million individuals through its WASH activities in IDP sites and host communities across Ethiopia. Interventions will comprise water trucking, construction and rehabilitation of water points, emergency latrines including distribution of hygiene kits, and handwashing stations, establishment of community-based water or sanitation management committees, and hygiene promotion activities through contextualized campaigns and mobilization of gender-balanced hygiene promoters. IOM will also support implementing partners, particularly national NGOs to provide access to safe water, WASH NFIs and hygiene promotion.

reportDetails_organization: United Kingdom, Government of; United Nations Children's Fund
project_text:
Northeast Nigeria Nutrition Response 2022 The Nutrition response in 2022 will prioritise implementation of the nutrition lifesaving activities (inpatient, outpatient, and targeted supplemental feeding programmes) and targeting of LGAs with high rates of GAM (above 10%) such as MMC/Jere, Nganzai, Bama, Machina. Hard-to-reach areas (such as Gubio, Rann, Magumeri), areas with large IDP  and returnee populations (like Monguno) and high-risk/inaccessible locations such as Marte LGA will also be prioritised for nutrition assistance. 
UNICEF will primarily target acutely malnourished children and PLW who are at a significantly high risk of death. The nutrition response will also target the total under-five and PLW with preventive nutrition services e.g. micronutrient supplementation to ensure levels of acute malnutrition are not above average thresholds, and to also reduce morbidity and mortality. The response will prioritise households with persons living with disabilities, who face barriers in accessing health, nutrition and WASH services and are disproportionately food insecure due to high levels of exclusion. 
The nutrition status of the targeted population in the BAY states significantly deteriorates during the period from May-August every year, which is the lean season and coincides with the rainy season. The season is characterised by very high rates of acute malnutrition with medical complications due to poor food access and a high prevalence of diarrhoea and malaria. UNICEF will need to adequately prepare for the lean season period by prepositioning supplies, increasing the overall sector capacity to treat acute malnutrition with a focus on inpatient care and IYCF-E
The nutrition response in BAY states will be contextualised in 2022 based on the following categorisation: 
1. Protracted crisis e.g north and central Borno LGAs where the rates of acute malnutrition are high, worsened by poor access to food and health systems. The approach in these areas will include INGO/NNGO direct support to the affected population, and prioritisation of lifesaving nutrition activities. 
3. New emergencies – locations of new crisis and fluctuations such as relocations, displacements and spike in acute malnutrition. The approach will focus on the Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) with a focus on lifesaving activities. 
4. Hard-to-reach / inaccessible areas – locations with limited humanitarian footprints and access e.g Gubio and Magumeri. The approach will include RRM and remote management strategy (where feasible) with a focus on life-saving interventions. UNICEF will also strengthen the implementation of nutrition interventions through local organizations or community-based structures to implement nutrition services in hard-to-reach/inaccessible areas. 
UNICEF response is primarily through services and in-kind deliveries. UNICEF will employ the use of cash and voucher assistance (CVA) to fill the nutrient gap in the Nutrition/Food Minimum Expenditure Basket to ensure that populations have access to a varied diet e.g CVA for meats and vegetables. 
The nutrition status of the affected population is an outcome of various underlying issues including access to health, WASH, food security, child protection, and gender issues. The main cause of acute malnutrition among children and women in BAY states is the high morbidity rates. High diarrhoea prevalence is the major cause of acute malnutrition among the IDPs and urban poor population due to the prevailing poor hygiene and sanitation conditions worsened by congested living conditions. The response will strengthen the integration of nutrition-sensitive interventions including WASH, food security, health, livelihoods and child protection, and gender-based violence risk mitigation.
UNICEF will prioritise projects that include basic nutrition packages such as integrated treatment of acute malnutrition (SAM and MAM) and prevention services including integration with WASH, food security, health and protections services.

project_text:
Food assistance to address increasing levels of severe food insecurity in South Sudan Meet the lifesaving food requirements of people in South Sudan who are facing food security crises, including those living in (ex)-POCs and IDP and those otherwise affected by conflict, natural disaster and/or seasonal food insecurity. WFP will provide general food distributions (GFD) to the most food insecure people in South Sudan. At the field level, food assistance will be overseen by the WFP Field Offices and implemented by NGO partners or provided through the Integrated Rapid Response Mechanism (IRRM). IRRM is a Delivering as One approach, in which UNICEF supports WASH and nutrition activities, FAO provides emergency seeds and livelihood kits, and WFP provides food assistance and common services through a comprehensive and collaborative humanitarian intervention by deploying mobile teams, supported by cooperating partners to reach populations facing the most urgent needs in the most inaccessible areas of the South Sudan, subject to the availability of resources.

Complementary to food distributions, WFP will seek to offer value-added solutions (GFD+), in response to needs and priorities identified by the community. Through GFD+, WFP together with its cooperating partners and other stakeholders will provide unconditional opportunities, identified through a community-based, people-centric participatory approach to targeted beneficiaries. GFD+ adds value to emergency food assistance with a focus on solutions that address the root causes of food and nutrition insecurity and better equip beneficiaries to fight hunger. The GFD+ activity type, duration, frequency, and participation will be catered to specific local sites and may range from COVID-19 awareness and mitigation measures to nutrition education, dyke rehabilitation and communal asset management, income-generating activities which lead to women's economic empowerment and have positive impact on household food security, or other solutions. WFP will also implement resilience building activities including Food Assistance for Assets (FFA) to support communities to improve their food security, restore their livelihoods, strengthen their resilience to shocks and build self-reliance, while contributing to peace.

Mitigation measures to reduce and prevent the potential the spread of COVID-19, including new variants, and other potential viral outbreaks have been incorporated into standard operating procedures for all interactions with beneficiaries, including training of partners and stakeholders, increasing general awareness among partners and beneficiaries, enforcing social distancing, promoting handwashing, disinfecting sites, reducing the frequency of distribution cycles, and mandating the utilization of personal protective equipment (PPE). These measures are mainstreamed into all WFP activities and are part of the ‘new way of working’.

project_text:
Niger Country Strategic Plan La vision de la réponse aux urgences dans le cadre du Plan Stratégique Pays (PSP) 2020-2024 du PAM Niger est la réduction de l’empreinte humanitaire dans la mise en œuvre de l’Activité 1, relative aux urgences du PSP à travers la promotion de l’approche NEXUS. Cette réponse s’inscrit dans la Stratégie de Prévention et de Gestion des Crises Alimentaires 2021 – 2025 du Dispositif National de Prévention et de Gestion de Crises Alimentaires (DNPGCA). Ce plan s’inscrit aussi dans le Plan d’Action 2021-2023 du Comité Technique Tripartite sur le Nexus Urgence-Développement (CTTNUD), en vue d’une mobilisation des ressources financières pour une planification et une mise en œuvre concertée des activités relatives à la promotion du NEXUS.  Dans le cas spécifique de l’assistance aux retournés dans leurs villages d’origine, qui est envisagée en 2022, la Loi 2018-74, relative à la protection et à l’assistance aux Personnes Déplacées Internes (PDI) cadrera le processus. Rappelons que l’Activité 1, relative aux urgences s’inscrit dans l’effet direct stratégique 1 du CSP (2020-2024) du PAM Niger « Les populations affectées, y compris les réfugiés, les personnes déplacées internes, les communautés hôtes et les retournés dans les zones ciblées sont en mesure de répondre aux besoins alimentaires minimums pendant et après la crise ».  La réponse aux urgences du PAM concernant la SECAL, basée sur une approche flexible, concernera toutes les trois (3) composantes de cette réponse en 2022 :
•	Le Mécanisme de Réponse Rapide (RRM)
•	La réponse aux crises prolongées.
•	La réponse à la soudure agricole et pastorale.
Par ailleurs la prévention de la malnutrition aux enfants 6-23 mois est combinée aux trois composantes ci-dessus.

project_text:
Programa de seguridad alimentaria basado en la escuela Con el objetivo de contribuir a la seguridad alimentaria de la población con mayores necesidades, el Programa Mundial de Alimentos de Naciones Unidas (WFP, por sus siglas en inglés) en Venezuela desarrolla un programa de asistencia humanitaria basado en la escuela para garantizar el acceso de los más vulnerables a una alimentación adecuada y nutritiva en el entorno escolar, familiar y comunitario. 
Este programa inició en 2021 con comidas escolares en emergencias priorizando escuelas iniciales y de educación especial.

WFP proporciona comidas escolares acompañado de un paquete integrado de intervenciones para mejorar el acceso a alimentos nutritivos y diversificados a través de las escuelas, contribuyendo al mismo tiempo a mejorar la salud y la nutrición de los niños en edad escolar, los estudiantes con discapacidad y el personal escolar, y apoyando a las comunidades a reducir la dependencia en estrategias de afrontamiento. De manera gradual, el WFP está realizando compras locales de alimentos, e incluyendo acciones para apoyar los mercados locales con compras a pequeños productores y apoyo técnico para acceso a mercados.

En este sentido, el programa de comidas escolares en emergencias tiene los siguientes componentes, para asegurar un enfoque integral que apoye al estudiante en el entorno escolar y familiar:

1. Entrega de comidas escolares nutritivas para estudiantes y personal escolar, promoviendo las compras locales y a pequeños productores.
2. Apoyo a la seguridad alimentaria del hogar a través de comida en especie o transferencias monetarias.
3. Rehabilitación de cocinas escolares para garantizar condiciones adecuadas de preparación de alimentos.
4. Comunicación para sensibilizar acerca de los principios humanitarios, la adecuada preparación de alimentos, nutrición, higiene y mantenimiento de cocinas escolares.
5. Fortalecimiento de capacidades de socios implementadores y personal escolar.
6. Acciones sensibles a la nutrición, que incluyen, tamizaje en las escuelas, educación nutricional, referencia a servicios especializados y entrega de alimento complementario fortificado (Supercereal Plus).

project_text:
Protection and Assistance for Refugees, Returnees and Asylum Seekers in South Sudan As of January 2022, there are some 335,000 refugees and asylum seekers from neighbouring countries sheltering in South Sudan. Despite enormous socio-economic, security and political challenges, compounded by the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, South Sudan has maintained its open-door policy for people seeking international protection, the majority of whom are women and children, primarily from Sudan, the Democratic Republic of Congo and the Central African Republic.
At the same time, against a backdrop of fragile peace and cautious optimism for longer term stability, hundreds of thousands of South Sudanese refugees have spontaneously returned to the country since the signing of the 2018 Revitalized Peace Agreement. While UNHCR is not promoting or facilitating return to South Sudan, this spontaneous movement has prompted the development of an area-based approach, to support refugees, returnees and host communities, through enhanced engagement with development actors, to support greater access to services where possible.
Refugees largely reside in conflict-affected regions, challenged by an unpredictable security environment as well as at times fragile relations with host communities. Displaced communities will continue to rely on life-saving humanitarian assistance provided by UNHCR and its partners as a result of enduring economic hardship, weak rule of law, limited development support and a lack of social services and infrastructure in refugee-hosting areas as well as in areas of origin. A reduction in basic assistance, especially during a global pandemic, will immediately lead to the deterioration of the humanitarian situation to emergency levels, due to the absence of a safety net, including social services, community support networks and limited access to livelihoods in displacements sites hosting refugees and South Sudanese refugee returnees.
Under the refugee response, all refugees and asylum seekers registered with UNHCR will benefit from various forms of protection interventions, including individual registration and documentation, and multi-sector assistance. Specific protection services, such as SGBV response and child protection will focus on the identified at-risk groups. While water, health, nutrition and education services will continue to maintain indicators within global standards for refugees living in camps, provision of other assistance, including shelter, non-food items and livelihoods support, will be undertaken in a targeted manner, focusing on persons with specific protection needs and vulnerabilities. This will primarily be achieved through participatory assessments, surveys as well as verification exercise to identify vulnerable refugees and their needs. Impact monitoring will be used to gauge the efficiency of projects implemented and for the purposes of course-correction in terms of better targeting of assistance. The needs of persons with disabilities and the elderly will be further mainstreamed in various multi-sector response services. Vulnerable refugees in urban settings will also continue to benefit from targeted protection interventions and facilitation of their access to national services.

project_text:
Protection and Assistance for Refugees, Returnees and Asylum Seekers in South Sudan As of January 2022, there are some 335,000 refugees and asylum seekers from neighbouring countries sheltering in South Sudan. Despite enormous socio-economic, security and political challenges, compounded by the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, South Sudan has maintained its open-door policy for people seeking international protection, the majority of whom are women and children, primarily from Sudan, the Democratic Republic of Congo and the Central African Republic.
At the same time, against a backdrop of fragile peace and cautious optimism for longer term stability, hundreds of thousands of South Sudanese refugees have spontaneously returned to the country since the signing of the 2018 Revitalized Peace Agreement. While UNHCR is not promoting or facilitating return to South Sudan, this spontaneous movement has prompted the development of an area-based approach, to support refugees, returnees and host communities, through enhanced engagement with development actors, to support greater access to services where possible.
Refugees largely reside in conflict-affected regions, challenged by an unpredictable security environment as well as at times fragile relations with host communities. Displaced communities will continue to rely on life-saving humanitarian assistance provided by UNHCR and its partners as a result of enduring economic hardship, weak rule of law, limited development support and a lack of social services and infrastructure in refugee-hosting areas as well as in areas of origin. A reduction in basic assistance, especially during a global pandemic, will immediately lead to the deterioration of the humanitarian situation to emergency levels, due to the absence of a safety net, including social services, community support networks and limited access to livelihoods in displacements sites hosting refugees and South Sudanese refugee returnees.
Under the refugee response, all refugees and asylum seekers registered with UNHCR will benefit from various forms of protection interventions, including individual registration and documentation, and multi-sector assistance. Specific protection services, such as SGBV response and child protection will focus on the identified at-risk groups. While water, health, nutrition and education services will continue to maintain indicators within global standards for refugees living in camps, provision of other assistance, including shelter, non-food items and livelihoods support, will be undertaken in a targeted manner, focusing on persons with specific protection needs and vulnerabilities. This will primarily be achieved through participatory assessments, surveys as well as verification exercise to identify vulnerable refugees and their needs. Impact monitoring will be used to gauge the efficiency of projects implemented and for the purposes of course-correction in terms of better targeting of assistance. The needs of persons with disabilities and the elderly will be further mainstreamed in various multi-sector response services. Vulnerable refugees in urban settings will also continue to benefit from targeted protection interventions and facilitation of their access to national services.

project_text:
Assistance d’urgence EAH aux personnes déplacées internes (PDIs) et population affectée par les problématiques et conséquences humanitaires au Niger Ce projet cible 450 352 personnes dont 216,169 hommes et 234,183 femmes affectées par des crises humanitaires de type mouvements de populations relatifs aux conflits, aux épidémies (COVID-19, choléra, hépatite E, etc.) et aux inondations, à travers la fourniture d’un paquet d'interventions d'urgence en EHA sur les sites d'installation de déplacés, au sein des communautés locales ainsi que dans les écoles, structures de santé et autres lieux publics. Les activités prévues incluent :
•	L’approvisionnement en eau par des mesures d'urgences (water trucking, traitement de l'eau à domicile) et durables dont la réhabilitation/construction des points d'eau l’extension/renforcement de systèmes d'alimentation en eau potable.
•	La fourniture d’infrastructures d’assainissement, notamment la construction de latrines et douches y compris à travers l’approche ATPC en situation d’urgence
•	La promotion de l’hygiène y compris la prévention /riposte contre le choléra et COVID-19 et la distribution de kits d’hygiène y compris du savon, des récipients de collecte, transport et stockage d’eau.   
•	Une meilleure préparation en amont à travers la mise en place de plans de contingences multirisques (inondation, épidémie, mouvement de population, etc) y compris le pré positionnement d’intrants, la signature de partenariats de standby avec des ONG nationales et internationales afin de pouvoir répondre de façon rapide et efficace sur l’ensemble du territoire. 
•	L'implication des services de l'Etat pour l'appui technique qu’ils offrent sera aussi considérée dans la réalisation des activités en vue de l’atteinte des résultats.

project_text:
Provision of lifesaving assistance and sustainable solutions through safe Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) services, for people in crises and their host communities in multiple regions in Somalia. IOM WASH is proposing to contribute to lifesaving of access to safe and equitable basic WASH services to overall 281,400 beneficiaries from vulnerable Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) and host-communities in multiple regions in Somalia. 

Specifically, the project will target 168,840 Non displaced people (children 104,681; women 27,014; Disabled 25,326; and elderly 11,819) and 112,560 displaced populations (children 69,787; Women 18,010; Disabled 16,884; and elderly 7,879)
IOM will rehabilitate 60 strategic water sources for multi-use (human and animals) and further 55 community berkads (water reservoirs) that will provide continued, equitable, safe, sufficient and sustainable water to regions, targeted by the cluster, prone to natural disasters.
IOM further proposes to construct 3,300 new emergency sanitation facilities (following cluster specifications) targeting populations without access to basic sanitation and hygiene.

The project will also strengthen the capacity of the Federal Government of Somalia and Federal Members States, community leaders and water committees/technicians for better coordination with government authorities and communities and sustainability of the constructed/ rehabilitated WASH infrastructures. In addition, the project will nurture community participation in good hygiene practices through training and community sensitization campaigns.

The project is aligned with protection mainstreaming to ensure safety and dignity of affected populations without causing harm. Affected populations and all relevant stakeholders including men, women, boys, girls, elderly and people with disability will be involved in decision making throughout the project activities/cycle. Furthermore, the project will be a part of an IOM integrated emergency response program and resilience building, where possible, efforts will be made to integrate IOM health, nutrition, shelter, CCCM and protection activities.

project_text:
Appui à la protection des moyens de subsistance des pasteurs, Agropasteurs impactés par l'insécurité et le défficit fourrager des régions de Tillabéri, Tahoua, Diffa et Maradi ,Agadez, Zinder, Dosso Le projet vise à apporter une assistance à 40363 ménages pastoraux, agropastoraux et déplacés dans  les zones à la fois affectées par un important déficit fourrager et un problème très critique d'insécurité induite par les  GANES à travers:   

    - la mise en place d'un appui en aliment  bétail de 14531 tonnes d'aliments bétail à la disposition de 40363 ménages pasteurs et agropasteurs vulnérables pour un total de 284541 personnes. un minimum de 13% de ces bénéficiaires seront  des femmes chefs de menages, veuves ou handicapés. soit 5247 ménages dirigés ar les femmes. l'assisttace en aliment profitera à un minimum 375376 têtes bénéficiaeront de cette assistance qui sera mise en place sous deux formes: en nature et via coupon. 20000 ménages d'éleveurs vulnérables de la catégorie des très pauvre disposant de 10 têtes de 375376 dont 363267 petits ruminantsou appartenant à 36327 petits éleveurs  propriétaires d'une UBT et 12109 petits éleveurs disposant de 3 bovins maximum . Chacun d'eux pourra accéder à une quantité  d'aliment bétail lui permettant d'apporter une complémentation alimentaire de 250 g et 2,5 kg par jour respectivement par petit ruminant et gros ruminant  pendant les  4 mois de période de soudure. La mise en place de cet important stock se fera à travers deux approches: (1) vente à prix modéré aux bénéficiaires de la carégorie des très pauvres préidentifiés  ; (2) et  distribution gratuite par voucher de 20% de ce stocks aux femmes allaitantes, aux  handicapés et  des veuves sans bras valides dans le menage. la priorité de l'assistance ira aux petits ruminants connus être le grenier de la femme pour palier au départ en exode de leur maris mais aussi supplier au difficulté d'accès au paturage naturel du fait de la présence des  GANESaui guettent les éleveurs dans les zones pourvues en paturage pour confisquer leurs animaux.  . Les paturages de la zone agricole n'offrant pas grand chose en termes de fourrage car envahis par Sida cordifolia non appétée, la seule alternative sera de mantenir les animaux dans leur terroir d'attache ou au piquet pour les agropasteur mais le niveau de déficit rend cette option peu crédible. Le déficit de 15 millions de tonnes de matière sèche confirmé par la Direction du Developpement Pastoral  laisse entrevoir une situation très critiques durantla période de soudure particulièrement pour les petits éléveurs sans ressources pour pouvoir  se constituer un important stock de paille de brousse ou de SPAI. la probabilité reste très élévée pour cette catégorie d'éleveurs de connaitre de fortes  mortalités de bétail ou  un imprtant transfert du  capital reproducteur des petits éleveurs  vers les nantis de  la zone agricole ou les commerçants qui les achèteront à vil prix. la criticité de la situation s'annonce déjà eu egard au cours des sous produits agroindustriels quiamorcent déjàune hausse vertigineuse  atteingnant 6000 à 6500 CFA le sac de 50 kg et la 25000 celui d  cereale de 100 kg sur les marchés moins de 2 mois des récoltes de 2021.
- distribution de 4600 petits ruminants par kit de 3 chèvres et un bouc aux ménages ayant connu une forte décapitalisation de leurs animaux reproducteurs et/ou dont les animaux ont été confisqués par les ganes. ces derniers devront appartenir à la catégorie des très pauvres des régions de Maradi (Bermo),  de Tahoua (Tchintabaradene ), de tillabéri et de Dosso (Nord Doutchi). La distribution interviendra après installation du nouvel paturage vert en début de la saison pluvieuse prochaine les beneficiaires seront à 70% des femmes.
- Distribution de 1900 anes aux femmes pour les corvées d'eau (l'hexaure et transport d'eau) en saison sèche. L'impact de la gourme couplée au deficit ont occasionne une mortalité élevée sans précédent dans les départements de Tchintabaradene, Abalak et Bermo. quelques rares mares temporaires  permettent l'abreuvemebt des animaux jusqu'en decembre puis deviennent hors service. pendant la saison sèche,. les femmes passent de 2 à 4 he

destinationObjects_Project.name: Food assistance to address increasing levels of severe food insecurity in South Sudan
project_text:
Food assistance to address increasing levels of severe food insecurity in South Sudan Meet the lifesaving food requirements of people in South Sudan who are facing food security crises, including those living in (ex)-POCs and IDP and those otherwise affected by conflict, natural disaster and/or seasonal food insecurity. WFP will provide general food distributions (GFD) to the most food insecure people in South Sudan. At the field level, food assistance will be overseen by the WFP Field Offices and implemented by NGO partners or provided through the Integrated Rapid Response Mechanism (IRRM). IRRM is a Delivering as One approach, in which UNICEF supports WASH and nutrition activities, FAO provides emergency seeds and livelihood kits, and WFP provides food assistance and common services through a comprehensive and collaborative humanitarian intervention by deploying mobile teams, supported by cooperating partners to reach populations facing the most urgent needs in the most inaccessible areas of the South Sudan, subject to the availability of resources.

Complementary to food distributions, WFP will seek to offer value-added solutions (GFD+), in response to needs and priorities identified by the community. Through GFD+, WFP together with its cooperating partners and other stakeholders will provide unconditional opportunities, identified through a community-based, people-centric participatory approach to targeted beneficiaries. GFD+ adds value to emergency food assistance with a focus on solutions that address the root causes of food and nutrition insecurity and better equip beneficiaries to fight hunger. The GFD+ activity type, duration, frequency, and participation will be catered to specific local sites and may range from COVID-19 awareness and mitigation measures to nutrition education, dyke rehabilitation and communal asset management, income-generating activities which lead to women's economic empowerment and have positive impact on household food security, or other solutions. WFP will also implement resilience building activities including Food Assistance for Assets (FFA) to support communities to improve their food security, restore their livelihoods, strengthen their resilience to shocks and build self-reliance, while contributing to peace.

Mitigation measures to reduce and prevent the potential the spread of COVID-19, including new variants, and other potential viral outbreaks have been incorporated into standard operating procedures for all interactions with beneficiaries, including training of partners and stakeholders, increasing general awareness among partners and beneficiaries, enforcing social distancing, promoting handwashing, disinfecting sites, reducing the frequency of distribution cycles, and mandating the utilization of personal protective equipment (PPE). These measures are mainstreamed into all WFP activities and are part of the ‘new way of working’.

Il cible les populations, non déplacées /hôtes , les déplacées internes, les  retournées incluant les femmes, les hommes, les filles , y compris  les adolescentes et les personnes handicapées dans les régions de Tillaberi (départements de:  Téra, Torodi, Banibangou, Oullam, Say , Tillaberi , Ayerou, Bankilaré, Abala , Flingué,  Balleyara, Gotheye) ;  Tahoua( départements de : Abalak, Bagaroua, Birnin Koni, Illela, Madaoua , Tahoua, Tchintabaraden, Tillia, Tassara ), Maradi (départements de : Guidan Roundji , Madarounfa, Maradi ville ), et Diffa( départements de Bosso, Diffa, Goudoumaria, Maine-soroa, Ngourti, N'Nguigmi)  et Niamey affectées par les crises sécuritaires et transfrontalières. Le projet mobilisera les autres acteurs humanitaires des secteurs clés, les services déconcentrés de l’Etat, les communautés incluant les femmes, les hommes, les filles, les garçons et les personnes handicapées, pour assurer une participation inclusive dans la mise en œuvre des activités de façon intégrée en veillant au caractère adaptés et opportun pour survivantes de VBG. Ainsi tout en renforçant (formation équipements, suivi) les services de prise en charge, les outils (cartographie, SOP et chemin de référencement ; messages et module de formation à jours et compréhensifs) seront développés et mis à disposition des acteurs. Les acteurs communautaires (para juristes, comités de vigilances, chefs traditionnels, radio communautaires) seront formés et dotés de supports adaptés pour mener les activités de prévention et réduction des risques de VBG et assurer l'orientation des cas selon la stratégie communautaire (information et sensibilisation et orientation vers les services disponibles de qualités sur la base de des cartographie et chemin de référencement). Un mécanisme de gestion de l'information VBG (collecte analyse et partage) basé sur le GBVIMS garantira la qualité des données des cas et des évaluations périodiques renforceront le suivi de la situation pour une réponse adaptée et opportune. Des mécanismes de feed-back et de plaintes à la portée des communautés seront mis en place et opérationnalisés afin de mieux garantir la participation des communautés tout le long du cycle du projet et renforcer la qualité des interventions. Dans ce cadre chaque trimestre des rencontres inter acteurs et bénéficiaires seront organisées au niveau de chaque département où il sera partagé les résultats les insuffisances constatées et dégager les besoins d'amélioration pour la suite. Pour la redevabilité envers les mécanismes de coordination et les partenaires (bailleurs) des réunions mensuelles de coordination au niveau national et sous nationale de l'ensemble des acteurs membres du sous cluster renforcées par des missions de suivi et appui technique de la coordination nationale du sous cluster sur le terrain permettront de faire le suivi de la qualité, la veille de la situation, des rapports et des fac-sheet seront produits et partagés chaque trimestre..

project_text:
WFP SOMALIA 2022 HRP - FSC Somalia has been impacted by multiple shocks in 2020, including desert locust invasion, flash floods and COVID-19. This has negatively affected the ability of vulnerable households to meet their food security needs. The urban poor, including IDP households, have been disproportionally affected due to the socio-economic effects from COVID-19 due their heavy reliance on food purchases from the market and casual labor as the main sources of income. These households are likely to face food consumption gaps due to declines in employment and income-earning opportunities. The desert locust caused significant damage to cereal crops, fruits, vegetables and pasture in the northern and central regions. Control efforts of the government and partners in Somaliland and Puntland made progress, but an increasing number of adult locust groups was reported in central regions. In addition, in the northeast, remained swarms have matured, and some have moved towards central areas. As per FAO, the hatching and band formation is occurring now and more swarms are likely to move to other areas in central Somalia and at later stages are expected to move towards crop producing areas in the south; which can have some negative impact to the crops and pasture up to early next year.

The impact of localized flooding particularly in riverine areas destroyed farmland and crops and caused population displacement, leading to significant crop losses and the loss of income from agricultural employment.

Jointly with the Government and other humanitarian actors, WFP Somalia has supported communities and vulnerable houses impacted by the multiple shocks. The high levels of sustained humanitarian assistance in 2020 have played a critical role in stabilizing the situation. The immediate food security outlook for Somalia however looks bleak despite the efforts sustained in 2020. According to the latest Post-Gu Assessment, 2.1 million people are expected to be food insecure (IPC 3 and 4) across Somalia through December 2020. An additional 3 million people are expected to be Stressed (IPC 2), bringing the total number of people facing cute food insecurity to 5.1 million until the end of this year. Based on results of the 2020 Post Gu assessment, an estimated 849,900 children under the age of five years face acute malnutrition between September 2020 and August 2021, including 143,400 likely to be severely malnourished.

project_text:
WFP Emergency relief response The World Food Programme (WFP) is United Nations frontline agency in the fight against hunger and working closely with the Government of Ethiopia (GoE) and humanitarian partners to save lives as well as strengthen and support the resilience of the most vulnerable population.
Ethiopia CO (WFP) continues to provide emergency and lifesaving food assistance in conflict, post-conflict or disaster situations based on government request. WFP has been supporting the Government of Ethiopia in its effort to tackle the country’s food insecurity problems through providing humanitarian food assistance and addressing underlying causes.  Hence, WFP supports the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP), providing General Food Distribution (GFD) to close to 6 million food insecure beneficiaries in Somali, Tigray, Amhara and Afra regions. The majority of GFD is provided through in-kind (food assistance) with an increasing portion in cash-based transfers (CBT).

project_text:
Niger Country Strategic Plan La vision de la réponse aux urgences dans le cadre du Plan Stratégique Pays (PSP) 2020-2024 du PAM Niger est la réduction de l’empreinte humanitaire dans la mise en œuvre de l’Activité 1, relative aux urgences du PSP à travers la promotion de l’approche NEXUS. Cette réponse s’inscrit dans la Stratégie de Prévention et de Gestion des Crises Alimentaires 2021 – 2025 du Dispositif National de Prévention et de Gestion de Crises Alimentaires (DNPGCA). Ce plan s’inscrit aussi dans le Plan d’Action 2021-2023 du Comité Technique Tripartite sur le Nexus Urgence-Développement (CTTNUD), en vue d’une mobilisation des ressources financières pour une planification et une mise en œuvre concertée des activités relatives à la promotion du NEXUS.  Dans le cas spécifique de l’assistance aux retournés dans leurs villages d’origine, qui est envisagée en 2022, la Loi 2018-74, relative à la protection et à l’assistance aux Personnes Déplacées Internes (PDI) cadrera le processus. Rappelons que l’Activité 1, relative aux urgences s’inscrit dans l’effet direct stratégique 1 du CSP (2020-2024) du PAM Niger « Les populations affectées, y compris les réfugiés, les personnes déplacées internes, les communautés hôtes et les retournés dans les zones ciblées sont en mesure de répondre aux besoins alimentaires minimums pendant et après la crise ».  La réponse aux urgences du PAM concernant la SECAL, basée sur une approche flexible, concernera toutes les trois (3) composantes de cette réponse en 2022 :
•	Le Mécanisme de Réponse Rapide (RRM)
•	La réponse aux crises prolongées.
•	La réponse à la soudure agricole et pastorale.
Par ailleurs la prévention de la malnutrition aux enfants 6-23 mois est combinée aux trois composantes ci-dessus.

project_text:
Strengthening food and livelihood security of conflict and disaster affected vulnerable IDPs and host communities through support to agricultural production and cash assistance to meet their immediate basic needs. In the face of increasing food insecurity and the need to meet other basic urgent needs, initiatives to  address immediate food needs of the most vulnerable and food insecure population are paramount in saving lives and protecting assets of the most vulnerable. The proposed project is in-line with Humanitarian Needs Overview 2022, Food Security Cluster (FSC) priorities and objectives. The project aims at improving the ability of 66,610 vulnerable people including 41,280 IDPs and 9,991 people with disability to meet their food and basic needs and reduce consumption gaps through life-saving cash assistance and agriculture inputs. Of these 52,965 people under FSC CO1 and 13,645 people under FSC CO2. 
These households are affected by multiple shocks – including conflicts and facing wide consumption gaps, due to successive below-average agricultural and pastoral yields, and a lack of casual labour income opportunities in urban and IDP communities. Unconditional cash transfer (UCT) and agriculture input assistance will improve beneficiary household’s access to food and other basic needs, while preventing households from resorting to negative coping mechanisms which erode long-term resilience. Community and stakeholder engagement, gender sensitive vulnerability and eligibility criteria for beneficiary selection and emphasis on participation of men, women, boys and girls of different ages and other at-risk groups will improve gender equality and women’s empowerment and inclusion of marginalized population. Target population will be provided with six months of UCT totaling 3,675,965$ - based on the monthly transfer value recommended by Cash Working Group (CWG). In addition, 2,047 farmers households will be supported with agricultural inputs including seeds and tractor services through in kind and voucher and consumption support of 30$/month for 4 months. Cash for work will generate employment of 22,742 person days to create community assets.
Settlement and beneficiary targeting will follow a participatory and community-based process. To target the settlements, Concern will conduct stakeholder consultations and key informants interview at regional and district level. Village Relief Committees (VRC) with average 8 to 10 members in each comprising both men and women, including representatives from marginalized population groups will be established (or existing ones mobilized) and receive information on the project and the beneficiary selection process. VRCs will lead community based participatory beneficiary selection process, this will also help project to empower participating communities – including women in decision making. A key component in the beneficiary selection criteria will be gender, age and disability considerations. 
In line with Concern’s approach and quality standard for Cash and Voucher based assistance and Accountability to Affected Populations, Concern will disseminate information on its Complaints Response Mechanism (CRM) channels during sensitization to ensure that beneficiaries, target communities and project stakeholders are fully aware of and are able to raise any feedback or issues of concern for timely action. Concern’s independent Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) unit will regularly monitor the project and will conduct Post Distribution Monitoring (PDM).
Concern with its local NGO partners is implementing both emergency response and longer term programmes in proposed districts in this project. The proposed project will further leverage upon Concern’s efforts and strengthen envisaged resilience outcomes in the target districts, while providing the project with opportunity to ensure convergence and integration while addressing the underlying causes of vulnerability – including gender inequalities and poverty.

project_text:
Improved Access to Food and Livelihood Options for Vulnerable Households in Somalia Ongoing armed conflicts and insecurity, with recurring climate shocks, has resulted in a protracted economic vulnerability and internal displacements across Somalia.Somalis are vulnerable to various shocks such as drought and flood that contribute to poverty and displacement. The Center for Global Development  places Somalia at the top of the list of 167 countries for overall vulnerability to climate change adjusted for coping capacity.
The Cyclical climatic shocks and ongoing conflict are challenging traditional rural livelihoods and causing 
growing number of urban poor and internally displaced people in Somalia. Displacements due to armed 
conflict and political tensions, drought, and lack of livelihoods are expected to continue in 2022, further 
exacerbating food insecurity in many areas.
According to FSNAU,out of the total 3.5 million people in need of urgent food assistance, 640,000 people face significant food consumption gaps. In addition, 3.7 million people are classified in IPC phase 2 (Stressed), engaging in negative coping strategies to meet their food and non-food needs, bringing the total number of Somalis experiencing acute food insecurity to 7.2 million by late 2021.

Furthermore,COVID-19 pandemic and related containment measures seem to have affected the urban poor population more than rural poor population. As a result, the urban poor face moderate to large food consumption gaps, partly due to a slowdown in economic activities in urban areas and the rising costs of food and other essential non-food items.
World Vision proposes a multi pronged interventions  to reverse the current trajectory at which Somalia is going.The interventions would include immediate access to food needs by vulnerable households facing hunger and starvation, improving livelihoods and creating opportunities for diversified livelihoods by protecting key livelihood assets .
The proposed project intends to address the food insecurity situation, loss of livelihood strategies, poor HH and community livelihood assets, as well as minimum interventions integrated to address the environmental degradation on which most livelihoods hinge upon. 
These activities will target IDPs, pastoral and agro-pastoral communities across Somalia, in districts where World Vision operates in.

project_text:
Improving Food security for vulnerable populations in Somaliland, particularly  IDPs in Hargeisa, Togdheer, and Sool Somalia is facing a growing number of threats to its food security. The ongoing desert locust invasion, socio-economic effects of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic and recurrent climate shocks, including frequent flooding and drought, continue to severely impact the lives and livelihoods of the vulnerable population. With this multifaceted crises, 7.7 Million people across Somalia need in emergency food assistance. With humanitarian needs expected to further increase in 2022, it is critical to enhance immediate food access, protect and restore livelihoods and strengthen the resilience of vulnerable households. Sustained humanitarian assistance is required to prevent the further deterioration of food security and nutrition.
Through this project, Plan International and Partners will effectively provide emergency assistance for food and promote dignity and choices among project participants by increasing purchasing power with short term injection of unconditional cash transfers for 1182 HH (7092 beneficiaries; 3546F, 3546M) for six months. Through field monitoring, government reports, and sector coordination, Plan and Partners will target households in areas identified as IPC3 or worse, risk of drought, and/or IDP communities, including those recently evicted by Somaliland government. These families have insufficient income to cover rising cost of food particularly during periods of drought and other shocks due to COVID19, instability and climate change, and will qualify per criteria, e.g. female headed household, household with person with disability, etc. Partners will ensure the crises affected families receive messages on Infant, Young Child Feeding and Hygiene and have access to sufficient, safe and nutritious foods to meet their dietary needs and food preferences for an active and healthy life. Partners have complementary programs running in these areas to enable consultant and selection within communities. By targeting vulnerable families particularly with children and delivering this intervention in a gender sensitive manner, Plan strives for secondary outcomes of improved the protection environment with reduced risks to women and girls.

project_text:
Providing Access to Emergency WASH Services in Gedo, Somalia The project proposes to improve access to safe water, sanitation facilities and promote good hygiene practices in an effort to improve the health conditions of 16,000 ( 8,759F, 6,600M and 640 elderly) drought affected individuals including internally displaced, marginalized riverine and vulnerable host women, men, boys and girls in Belet Xawa, Ceel Waaq, Dollow, Garbaharey and Luuq districts in Gedo region. Among the target beneficiaries will be 2,400 persons with disabilities.				 
The recurrent drought in Gedo has largely contributed to inadequate population access to potable water and resulted in frequent disease outbreaks, mainly AWD/cholera. WASH conditions are particularly poor (inadequate access to water to meet basic needs, lack of access to latrines, reliance on poor quality water sources). An assessment by REACH in June 2020 shows 93% of the households in Gedo have a WASH Living Standards Gap (LSG), with access to improved water sources below 41%. The region is served by small, seasonal, open water sources which are rapidly depleted with the recurrent droughts, leaving communities vulnerable to new outbreaks as they lack access to water for consumption and personal hygiene. Further, the assessment shows that 36% of the households have no access to a functional and improved sanitation facility. Serious protection concerns, and rights violations persist, where persons with disabilities, children and women are among the most affected social groups due to compounded vulnerabilities. The REACH DSA in March 2021 further shows that people with disabilities (100%), children (50%) and women (50%) are the top 3 groups reportedly facing impediments in accessing latrines. 
As part of the WASH cluster’s efforts to address the critical WASH needs in priority populations, this intervention will respond to the WASH gaps in the five target districts through the construction of two (2) solar powered water systems with piping to communities, rehabilitation of two existing shallow wells and training of 4 five-member water management committee. In addition, 8 existing high volume water points will be provided with fuel subsidies for three months during the hot and dry Jilaal season while water trucking will be done for 2,000 persons in rural villages for three months. The project will also construct150 universally design emergency latrines  with handwashing stations and distribute 150 latrine cleaning kits as well as 3,000 hygiene kits through Cash Vouchers. Hygiene promotion messaging will also be conducted in all the five districts. 
Trócaire will collaborate with Somali Humanitarian Relief Action (SHRA) and Active in Development Aid (ADA), national NGOs with strong experience in implementing WASH projects in Gedo, in the implementation of this project in the five target districts.
