project_text:
Assistance d’urgence EAH aux personnes déplacées internes (PDIs) et population affectée par les problématiques et conséquences humanitaires au Niger Ce projet cible 450 352 personnes dont 216,169 hommes et 234,183 femmes affectées par des crises humanitaires de type mouvements de populations relatifs aux conflits, aux épidémies (COVID-19, choléra, hépatite E, etc.) et aux inondations, à travers la fourniture d’un paquet d'interventions d'urgence en EHA sur les sites d'installation de déplacés, au sein des communautés locales ainsi que dans les écoles, structures de santé et autres lieux publics. Les activités prévues incluent :
•	L’approvisionnement en eau par des mesures d'urgences (water trucking, traitement de l'eau à domicile) et durables dont la réhabilitation/construction des points d'eau l’extension/renforcement de systèmes d'alimentation en eau potable.
•	La fourniture d’infrastructures d’assainissement, notamment la construction de latrines et douches y compris à travers l’approche ATPC en situation d’urgence
•	La promotion de l’hygiène y compris la prévention /riposte contre le choléra et COVID-19 et la distribution de kits d’hygiène y compris du savon, des récipients de collecte, transport et stockage d’eau.   
•	Une meilleure préparation en amont à travers la mise en place de plans de contingences multirisques (inondation, épidémie, mouvement de population, etc) y compris le pré positionnement d’intrants, la signature de partenariats de standby avec des ONG nationales et internationales afin de pouvoir répondre de façon rapide et efficace sur l’ensemble du territoire. 
•	L'implication des services de l'Etat pour l'appui technique qu’ils offrent sera aussi considérée dans la réalisation des activités en vue de l’atteinte des résultats.

project_text:
Provision of Integrated Protection and Site Management Services to Internally displaced people, Returnees, Host Community  and Other Persons With Specific Needs in Ethiopia UNHCR’s 2022 protection programme builds on the scale up of 2021 response and will be implemented in nine regions. The programme, builds on evidence gathered from ongoing protection monitoring using the revamped Ethiopia Protection Monitoring Tool (E-PMT) in the operational areas to ensure the ongoing identification of protection and specific needs and changes in the protection landscape for IDPs, IDP returnees, host communities and other persons with specific needs requiring protection services. 
As the Protection Cluster-lead agency, UNHCR ensures the coordination of its activities, implemented directly or through partnerships, through the Protection Cluster at national and sub-national level as appropriate.
Based on the protection monitoring, UNHCR will implement an integrated set of protection services and interventions tailored to the needs and priorities of the affected, which include:
•	the provision of information, counselling, identification of protection and specific needs, referrals to services/assistance, 
•	direct provision of services and assistance to persons at risk or with specific needs; 
•	GBV awareness, prevention and response activities;
•	child protection awareness raising and case management;
•	strengthening of MHPSS, 
•	emergency EORE as required by the Mine Action AOR,
•	provision of legal awareness and legal aid for GBV case management, HLP, legal identity and civil document restoration, 
•	and strengthen social cohesion and community-based peacebuilding.

Through its CCCM intervention, UNHCR will provide care and maintenance service of site infrastructure for IDPs living in 63 sites in Tigray, 4 sites in Afar and 11 sites in Amhara for at least 230,000 vulnerable IDP children of under 18 (120,000 girls, 110,000 boys) and assisting more than 230,000 adult IDP population (103,000 Adult Men, 107,000 Adult Women(18-59 years), 11,000 Elderly Men and 10,000 Elderly Women (60 and above) which include 32,000 people with disabilities to ensure protection and assistance while striving for durable solutions.

project_text: Mejor acceso a los servicios de salud sexual y reproductiva para la población vulnerable afectada por la crisis socioeconómica venezolana y la recesión económica relacionada con el COVID-19 En el contexto complejo de crisis económica y pandemia de Covid19, PUI tiene como objetivo mejorar la situación de atención en salud sexual y reproductiva y apoyo psicosocial específicamente en el ambulatorio Jesús Maestre del Barrio José Félix Rivas zona 10 de Petare, estado Miranda. En este ambulatorio acude una población de estrato socio económico muy bajo y sus principales problemas de salud son las enfermedades de transmisión sexual, complicaciones que genera un embarazo no controlado sobre todo en adolescentes, violencia urbana  que genera ansiedad  e interrupción de las actividades cotidiana que influye en la calidad de vida aunado a esto el deterioro  de  los servicios de salud mental disponibles a nivel público, el déficit de  transporte en la zona ocasiona que las mujeres no tengan acceso a otros centros de salud más lejanos. Por consiguiente,  PUI incluirá ayuda en planificación familiar con la implementación de métodos anticonceptivos, consulta prenatal y psicológica, capacitaciones al personal de salud y sensibilizaciones a la comunidad sobre temas de autocuidado, empoderamiento de la mujer . La población meta será de 3504 su desagregación para adquirir beneficios es de 1440 población femenina en edad fértil para métodos anticonceptivos y 2064  mujeres y hombres   que se le dará beneficio incluyendo tratamiento para enfermedades de transmisión sexual, kit de parto, consulta prenatal  y orientación sobre aspectos de salud mental.

project_text: Enhancement of protection of displaced persons, returnees and conflict affected host communities in Syria through integrated, community-based protection activities. The project aims to strengthen protection and resilience of Syrian IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities through advocacy, coordination, provision of community-based protection services and legal services UNHCR Syria will continue to lead the Protection Sector/Cluster to ensure coordinated protection interventions programming for safe refugees return. UNHCR’s protection interventions include legal counselling and assistance, protection monitoring, referrals and information sharing, social protection through livelihoods support to most vulnerable people, GBV prevention and response, child protection, psychosocial support and in-kind assistance for persons with specific needs including persons with disabilities, non-formal education, and awareness activities on various subjects targeting women, men, boys and girls. In addition to over 125 community centres providing integrated protection services, outreach to communities will be convened through over 2,800 outreach volunteers. Accountability to affected people will be realized through meaningful participation of communities based on age, gender and diversity approach, structured focus group discussions and enhancement of the community-based feedback and complaint mechanisms. UNHCR will continue its capacity building efforts to ensure services are delivered according to the standards and that accountability to affected population and do no harm principles are respected. UNHCR Syria will continue to lead Protection Sector in coordination of response plans of IDPs and affected people as well it will execute leadership roles in refugee return programmes in collaboration with the Government. Monitoring and evaluation of the planned interventions is based on the reports and observations by the partners and on regular direct observation and ongoing assessment by UNHCR and the comparison of achievements and related financial expenditures with objectives. Evaluation is conducted through different channels including the post distribution monitoring to determine the effectiveness of/measure the satisfaction of POCs with the service and the distribution process in addition to multiple satisfaction surveys and tracking tools related to different protection interventions. Monitoring and evaluation activities are carried out at various levels by partners and agencies implementing subprojects, UNHCR Branch Office, Sub Office and Field Offices. Situation reports are submitted by all UNHCR Field Offices to their respective Supervising Office and Branch Offices submit a corresponding report to Headquarters.

project_text:
Food assistance to address increasing levels of severe food insecurity in South Sudan Meet the lifesaving food requirements of people in South Sudan who are facing food security crises, including those living in (ex)-POCs and IDP and those otherwise affected by conflict, natural disaster and/or seasonal food insecurity. destinationObjects_Project.name: Provision of Inclusive, Protective & Effective Education Services to Conflict-affected Children & Youth in Ayod, Uror, Duk, Ulang, Nasir and Longechuk Counties of Jonglei & Upper Nile States.
project_text:
Provision of Inclusive, Protective & Effective Education Services to Conflict-affected Children & Youth in Ayod, Uror, Duk, Ulang, Nasir and Longechuk Counties of Jonglei & Upper Nile States. This CMD’s Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) for 2022 seeks to provide inclusive, protective and effective education services to accelerate learning recovery and make schools more equitable, efficient and resilient for 7, 339 (3, 302 girls) school-aged children, 250 (50 female) teachers, 275 (82 female) PTA members and 60 (10 female) local education officials in 6 Counties of Jonglei & Upper Nile States by building on investments made during the Pandemic and previous years of EiE programming in South Sudan.

The expected results are equalised participation and improved learning outcomes across gender and disability for 7, 339 (45% female) children and youth through provision of essential school facilities and supplies, psychosocial support, gender-sensitive delivery of curriculum, classroom management, teacher conduct and schoolyard dynamics in 25 target schools (5 ECD centers, 15 primary schools, and 5 secondary schools) in Ayod, Uror & Duk Counties of Jonglei State and Ulang, Nasir and Longechuk Counties of Upper Nile State respectively. These 7, 339 children (5-17) and 250 teachers will be provided with teaching and learning materials in the form of 10 ECD learner kits, 250 learner kits for primary and 10 learner kits for secondary schools. 250 recreational kits will be provided to enhance learning and play and psychosocial wellbeing during schooling.

For their protective and safe school environment, 30 temporary learning spaces will be established in line with Inter-INEE's Minimum Standards for Education in Emergencies and Standards in Education Cluster Strategy 2019; and 30 gender segregated latrines and 30 water points in line with INEE and sphere standards. (unit of measurement: 1:60 for boys, 1:30 for girls). CMD will distribute 95 (500-litre) plastic water tanks with taps, 95 (50-litre) hand-washing tanks with taps and on their metal stands; 285 (1-litre) liquid sanitisers, 190 cartons of toilet soap, 95 bags (20 kgs) of detergent/powder soap, 95, 000 face masks, and 375 pairs of gumboots to provide sanitation and PPE for students and teachers. 2, 000 adolescent girls will receive dignity kits and undergo MHM sessions to better enhance their self-esteem and school attendance.

The plan targets 2, 339 (935 girls & 1, 404 boys) children in Ayod; 1, 000 (400 girls & 600 boys) in Uror; 1, 000 (400 girls & 600 boys) in Duk; 1, 000(400 girls & 600 boys) in Ulang; 1, 000 (400 girls & 600 boys) in Nasir; and 1, 000 (400 girls & 600 boys) in Longechuk. 50 (10 female) teachers in Ayod; 40 (10 female) in Uror; 40 (10 female) in Duk; 40 (10 female) in Ulang; 40 (5 female) in Nasir; and 40 (5 female) in Longechuk will benefit from active EiE pedagogy that is centered on children and adolescents and their full development, and that responds to school needs and favours the equitable achievement of learning goals. These teachers will Improve the quality of gender and disability-inclusive education services and teachers' capacity to protect the wellbeing of all children and prevent the negative impact of the emergencies on learning environments.

Equally important, 75 (27 female) PTA members in Ayod; 40 (11 female) in Uror; 40 (11 female) in Duk; 40(11female) in Ulang; 40(11 female) in Nasir; and 40 (11 female) in Longechuk and 10 (1 female) education officials in Ayod, 10 (1) in Uror; 10 (1) in Duk; 10(1) in Ulang; 10(1) in Nassir; and 10 (1 female) in Longechuk will be trained in School Management, Psychosocial Support (PSS) and Disaster Risk Reduction in Education (DRR).

CMD will also conduct 12 Back to Learning (BTL) campaigns through public information campaigns intended for the entire affected population and/or awareness raising activities aimed at specific segments of the out-of-schoolchildren (OOSC) as well as current learners identified as most at-risk.

reportDetails_organization: European Commission's Humanitarian Aid and Civil Protection Department
project_text: Respuesta integral en seguridad alimentaria y nutricional de emergencia para la población más vulnerable afectada por la crisis en Venezuela. Acción Contra el Hambre (ACH) en Venezuela atiende las necesidades humanitarias de los grupos más vulnerables en riesgo de desnutrición aguda: < de 5 años, 5 – 14 años, mujeres embarazadas y lactantes (MEL), personas con discapacidades o con problemas de salud, en particular adultos mayores. Son agravantes las situaciones de pobreza y necesidades básicas no satisfechas como la falta de acceso a: alimentos, condiciones higiénico-sanitarias adecuadas, servicios de salud, y medios de vida. La desnutrición y el deterioro de la salud repercuten en una mayor exposición a factores agravantes como la violencia de género, embarazos adolescentes y criminalidad. A través del HRP, ACH brindará una respuesta humanitaria para la reducción del sufrimiento y ayudar a salvar vidas, identificando casos de desnutrición aguda y severa en las familias más a riesgo. Se trabajará a nivel comunitario y se coordinará con instituciones locales, en particular con escuelas y centros de salud. ACH trabaja con un enfoque de programa país y dentro de una estrategia regional, con intervenciones complementarias e integrales en: 1) Nutrición: sensibilización y consejerías; detección, tratamiento de la desnutrición aguda, y derivación de los casos con complicaciones médicas; capacitación en el manejo preventivo de la desnutrición aguda; 2) Salud: atención primaria, equipos, insumos, medicamentos, métodos anticonceptivos; 3) Seguridad Alimentaria y medios de vida: distribución de alimentos y apoyo para la producción de alimentos; 4) ASH: acceso a servicios de agua, saneamiento, e higiene, en escuelas y centros comunitarios; distribución de kits de higiene, y rehabilitación/reparación de sistemas de abastecimiento de agua y de saneamiento en comunidades. El sector de Protección y género, de manera transversal, trabajará en prevención de VBG, nuevas masculinidades y DSSR; establecimiento y/o fortalecimiento de espacios seguros para mujeres y niñas; atención psico-social, distribución de kits de higiene menstrual y protección para mujeres en riesgo. La respuesta actual de ACH se concentra en Caracas DC, Guárico, Carabobo, Miranda, Zulia, Bolívar, y próximamente en Falcón, Amazonas y Sucre.

project_text: Respuesta integral en seguridad alimentaria y nutricional de emergencia para la población más vulnerable afectada por la crisis en Venezuela. Acción Contra el Hambre (ACH) en Venezuela atiende las necesidades humanitarias de los grupos más vulnerables en riesgo de desnutrición aguda: < de 5 años, 5 – 14 años, mujeres embarazadas y lactantes (MEL), personas con discapacidades o con problemas de salud, en particular adultos mayores. Son agravantes las situaciones de pobreza y necesidades básicas no satisfechas como la falta de acceso a: alimentos, condiciones higiénico-sanitarias adecuadas, servicios de salud, y medios de vida. La desnutrición y el deterioro de la salud repercuten en una mayor exposición a factores agravantes como la violencia de género, embarazos adolescentes y criminalidad. A través del HRP, ACH brindará una respuesta humanitaria para la reducción del sufrimiento y ayudar a salvar vidas, identificando casos de desnutrición aguda y severa en las familias más a riesgo. Se trabajará a nivel comunitario y se coordinará con instituciones locales, en particular con escuelas y centros de salud. ACH trabaja con un enfoque de programa país y dentro de una estrategia regional, con intervenciones complementarias e integrales en: 1) Nutrición: sensibilización y consejerías; detección, tratamiento de la desnutrición aguda, y derivación de los casos con complicaciones médicas; capacitación en el manejo preventivo de la desnutrición aguda; 2) Salud: atención primaria, equipos, insumos, medicamentos, métodos anticonceptivos; 3) Seguridad Alimentaria y medios de vida: distribución de alimentos y apoyo para la producción de alimentos; 4) ASH: acceso a servicios de agua, saneamiento, e higiene, en escuelas y centros comunitarios; distribución de kits de higiene, y rehabilitación/reparación de sistemas de abastecimiento de agua y de saneamiento en comunidades. El sector de Protección y género, de manera transversal, trabajará en prevención de VBG, nuevas masculinidades y DSSR; establecimiento y/o fortalecimiento de espacios seguros para mujeres y niñas; atención psico-social, distribución de kits de higiene menstrual y protección para mujeres en riesgo. La respuesta actual de ACH se concentra en Caracas DC, Guárico, Carabobo, Miranda, Zulia, Bolívar, y próximamente en Falcón, Amazonas y Sucre.

project_text:
Niger Country Strategic Plan La vision de la réponse aux urgences dans le cadre du Plan Stratégique Pays (PSP) 2020-2024 du PAM Niger est la réduction de l’empreinte humanitaire dans la mise en œuvre de l’Activité 1, relative aux urgences du PSP à travers la promotion de l’approche NEXUS. Cette réponse s’inscrit dans la Stratégie de Prévention et de Gestion des Crises Alimentaires 2021 – 2025 du Dispositif National de Prévention et de Gestion de Crises Alimentaires (DNPGCA). Ce plan s’inscrit aussi dans le Plan d’Action 2021-2023 du Comité Technique Tripartite sur le Nexus Urgence-Développement (CTTNUD), en vue d’une mobilisation des ressources financières pour une planification et une mise en œuvre concertée des activités relatives à la promotion du NEXUS.  Dans le cas spécifique de l’assistance aux retournés dans leurs villages d’origine, qui est envisagée en 2022, la Loi 2018-74, relative à la protection et à l’assistance aux Personnes Déplacées Internes (PDI) cadrera le processus. Rappelons que l’Activité 1, relative aux urgences s’inscrit dans l’effet direct stratégique 1 du CSP (2020-2024) du PAM Niger « Les populations affectées, y compris les réfugiés, les personnes déplacées internes, les communautés hôtes et les retournés dans les zones ciblées sont en mesure de répondre aux besoins alimentaires minimums pendant et après la crise ».  La réponse aux urgences du PAM concernant la SECAL, basée sur une approche flexible, concernera toutes les trois (3) composantes de cette réponse en 2022 :
•	Le Mécanisme de Réponse Rapide (RRM)
•	La réponse aux crises prolongées.
•	La réponse à la soudure agricole et pastorale.
Par ailleurs la prévention de la malnutrition aux enfants 6-23 mois est combinée aux trois composantes ci-dessus.

project_text:
WFP SOMALIA 2022 HRP - FSC Somalia has been impacted by multiple shocks in 2020, including desert locust invasion, flash floods and COVID-19. This has negatively affected the ability of vulnerable households to meet their food security needs. The urban poor, including IDP households, have been disproportionally affected due to the socio-economic effects from COVID-19 due their heavy reliance on food purchases from the market and casual labor as the main sources of income. These households are likely to face food consumption gaps due to declines in employment and income-earning opportunities. The desert locust caused significant damage to cereal crops, fruits, vegetables and pasture in the northern and central regions. Control efforts of the government and partners in Somaliland and Puntland made progress, but an increasing number of adult locust groups was reported in central regions. In addition, in the northeast, remained swarms have matured, and some have moved towards central areas. As per FAO, the hatching and band formation is occurring now and more swarms are likely to move to other areas in central Somalia and at later stages are expected to move towards crop producing areas in the south; which can have some negative impact to the crops and pasture up to early next year.

The impact of localized flooding particularly in riverine areas destroyed farmland and crops and caused population displacement, leading to significant crop losses and the loss of income from agricultural employment.

Jointly with the Government and other humanitarian actors, WFP Somalia has supported communities and vulnerable houses impacted by the multiple shocks. The high levels of sustained humanitarian assistance in 2020 have played a critical role in stabilizing the situation. The immediate food security outlook for Somalia however looks bleak despite the efforts sustained in 2020. According to the latest Post-Gu Assessment, 2.1 million people are expected to be food insecure (IPC 3 and 4) across Somalia through December 2020. An additional 3 million people are expected to be Stressed (IPC 2), bringing the total number of people facing cute food insecurity to 5.1 million until the end of this year. Based on results of the 2020 Post Gu assessment, an estimated 849,900 children under the age of five years face acute malnutrition between September 2020 and August 2021, including 143,400 likely to be severely malnourished.

reportDetails_organization: Canada, Government of; World Food Programme
project_text:
Food assistance to address increasing levels of severe food insecurity in South Sudan Meet the lifesaving food requirements of people in South Sudan who are facing food security crises, including those living in (ex)-POCs and IDP and those otherwise affected by conflict, natural disaster and/or seasonal food insecurity. WFP will provide general food distributions (GFD) to the most food insecure people in South Sudan. At the field level, food assistance will be overseen by the WFP Field Offices and implemented by NGO partners or provided through the Integrated Rapid Response Mechanism (IRRM). IRRM is a Delivering as One approach, in which UNICEF supports WASH and nutrition activities, FAO provides emergency seeds and livelihood kits, and WFP provides food assistance and common services through a comprehensive and collaborative humanitarian intervention by deploying mobile teams, supported by cooperating partners to reach populations facing the most urgent needs in the most inaccessible areas of the South Sudan, subject to the availability of resources.

Complementary to food distributions, WFP will seek to offer value-added solutions (GFD+), in response to needs and priorities identified by the community. Through GFD+, WFP together with its cooperating partners and other stakeholders will provide unconditional opportunities, identified through a community-based, people-centric participatory approach to targeted beneficiaries. GFD+ adds value to emergency food assistance with a focus on solutions that address the root causes of food and nutrition insecurity and better equip beneficiaries to fight hunger. The GFD+ activity type, duration, frequency, and participation will be catered to specific local sites and may range from COVID-19 awareness and mitigation measures to nutrition education, dyke rehabilitation and communal asset management, income-generating activities which lead to women's economic empowerment and have positive impact on household food security, or other solutions. WFP will also implement resilience building activities including Food Assistance for Assets (FFA) to support communities to improve their food security, restore their livelihoods, strengthen their resilience to shocks and build self-reliance, while contributing to peace.

Mitigation measures to reduce and prevent the potential the spread of COVID-19, including new variants, and other potential viral outbreaks have been incorporated into standard operating procedures for all interactions with beneficiaries, including training of partners and stakeholders, increasing general awareness among partners and beneficiaries, enforcing social distancing, promoting handwashing, disinfecting sites, reducing the frequency of distribution cycles, and mandating the utilization of personal protective equipment (PPE). These measures are mainstreamed into all WFP activities and are part of the ‘new way of working’.

project_text:
Respuesta multisectorial humanitaria en Venezuela En Venezuela, DRC busca proporcionar asistencia humanitaria a poblaciones vulnerables y afectadas por la crisis actual como son las consecuencias socioeconómicas de la pandemia del COVID-19, de los flujos migratorios mixtos hacia fuera de Venezuela y de las problemáticas fronterizas relacionados a actividades ilícitas y conflictos de grupos armados que vive la población que reside en Venezuela, tales como desplazamientos y/o confinamientos masivos. Por medio de una intervención multisectorial, DRC brindará asistencia de emergencia con un enfoque de protección tanto para refugiados en Venezuela, venezolanos con la intención de migrar, venezolanos retornados, desplazados internos y a población de acogida afectada, aplicando de manera transversal un enfoque sensible a la edad, el género y la discapacidad para llegar a un total de 21,288 personas vulnerables. Los perfiles priorizados por DRC serán aquellos que presenten altos niveles de vulnerabilidad como lo son las personas con necesidades específicas de protección (NNA, mujeres, LGBTI, ancianos, etc.), personas con discapacidad, sobrevivientes o personas en riesgo de violencia basada en género, víctimas de desplazamiento masivo o confinamiento, grupos indígenas entre otros. Este proyecto será implementado en todas las regiones en las cuales DRC trabaja en Venezuela, que, al mismo tiempo, son zonas de mayor proporción de necesidades humanitarias severas de acuerdo con el HRP 2022/23: Zulia, Sucre y Apure. Esta acción tiene como objetivo ofrecer una intervención de protección integrada que combina la protección y asistencia de emergencia para mejorar las condiciones de las poblaciones vulnerables antes mencionadas. 
La acción propuesta incluye los siguientes sectores/actividades: Coordinación, Protección, Seguridad Alimentaria, Salud, Agua, saneamiento e higiene y Educación. El presente proyecto tendrá como línea de intervención principal, el abordaje de las necesidades de protección encontradas en una evaluación de campo llevada a cabo en noviembre del 2021 en los estados de Sucre (municipios de Arismendi, Cajigal, Mariño y Valdés), Zulia (municipios de Maracaibo, Rosario de Perijá, Machiques de Perijá, Páez) y Apure (municipio Páez) y como líneas complementarias a los sectores de salud, WASH, educación y seguridad alimentaria. Es por ello que DRC plantea una respuesta integral no solo a necesidades de  protección como son, el acceso a información, asistencia legal y acceso a documentación para población vulnerable, incluidas las personas sobrevivientes y en riesgo de VbG,  el acceso a asistencia individualizada y especifica de protección y prevención de trata sino también a cubrir necesidades básicas de seguridad alimentaria;  mediante distribuciones mensuales de kits familiares alimenticios por 10 meses en las zonas de intervención, salud; con la rehabilitación de centros médicos seleccionados y educación; proveyendo suministros escolares y de higiene personal y familiar, a través de una intervención multisectorial y previamente coordinada con autoridades y comunidades locales. Uno de los hallazgos de la evaluación de campo fue la falta de data relacionada a protección para poder producir análisis confiables, es por esto por lo que DRC plantea implementar un análisis de protección basado en evidencia a través de un monitoreo continuo de protección en las localidades de intervención, con la finalidad de tener información a tiempo para poder identificar riesgos y priorizar necesidades.

project_text:
Respuesta multisectorial humanitaria en Venezuela En Venezuela, DRC busca proporcionar asistencia humanitaria a poblaciones vulnerables y afectadas por la crisis actual como son las consecuencias socioeconómicas de la pandemia del COVID-19, de los flujos migratorios mixtos hacia fuera de Venezuela y de las problemáticas fronterizas relacionados a actividades ilícitas y conflictos de grupos armados que vive la población que reside en Venezuela, tales como desplazamientos y/o confinamientos masivos. Por medio de una intervención multisectorial, DRC brindará asistencia de emergencia con un enfoque de protección tanto para refugiados en Venezuela, venezolanos con la intención de migrar, venezolanos retornados, desplazados internos y a población de acogida afectada, aplicando de manera transversal un enfoque sensible a la edad, el género y la discapacidad para llegar a un total de 21,288 personas vulnerables. Los perfiles priorizados por DRC serán aquellos que presenten altos niveles de vulnerabilidad como lo son las personas con necesidades específicas de protección (NNA, mujeres, LGBTI, ancianos, etc.), personas con discapacidad, sobrevivientes o personas en riesgo de violencia basada en género, víctimas de desplazamiento masivo o confinamiento, grupos indígenas entre otros. Este proyecto será implementado en todas las regiones en las cuales DRC trabaja en Venezuela, que, al mismo tiempo, son zonas de mayor proporción de necesidades humanitarias severas de acuerdo con el HRP 2022/23: Zulia, Sucre y Apure. Esta acción tiene como objetivo ofrecer una intervención de protección integrada que combina la protección y asistencia de emergencia para mejorar las condiciones de las poblaciones vulnerables antes mencionadas. 
La acción propuesta incluye los siguientes sectores/actividades: Coordinación, Protección, Seguridad Alimentaria, Salud, Agua, saneamiento e higiene y Educación. El presente proyecto tendrá como línea de intervención principal, el abordaje de las necesidades de protección encontradas en una evaluación de campo llevada a cabo en noviembre del 2021 en los estados de Sucre (municipios de Arismendi, Cajigal, Mariño y Valdés), Zulia (municipios de Maracaibo, Rosario de Perijá, Machiques de Perijá, Páez) y Apure (municipio Páez) y como líneas complementarias a los sectores de salud, WASH, educación y seguridad alimentaria. Es por ello que DRC plantea una respuesta integral no solo a necesidades de  protección como son, el acceso a información, asistencia legal y acceso a documentación para población vulnerable, incluidas las personas sobrevivientes y en riesgo de VbG,  el acceso a asistencia individualizada y especifica de protección y prevención de trata sino también a cubrir necesidades básicas de seguridad alimentaria;  mediante distribuciones mensuales de kits familiares alimenticios por 10 meses en las zonas de intervención, salud; con la rehabilitación de centros médicos seleccionados y educación; proveyendo suministros escolares y de higiene personal y familiar, a través de una intervención multisectorial y previamente coordinada con autoridades y comunidades locales. Uno de los hallazgos de la evaluación de campo fue la falta de data relacionada a protección para poder producir análisis confiables, es por esto por lo que DRC plantea implementar un análisis de protección basado en evidencia a través de un monitoreo continuo de protección en las localidades de intervención, con la finalidad de tener información a tiempo para poder identificar riesgos y priorizar necesidades.

project_text:
Emergency WASH and ESNFI Response to Conflict Affected People in Tigray Region As of February 2022, a total of 4.51 million IDPs have been identified thus far across the country. Of the total displaced population, the main causes of displacement were conflict which displaced 3.63 million IDPs (81%). Tigray has remained to be the priority region and continues to have significant IDPs and affected host population that remains vulnerable under the current circumstances- conflict. According to the Emergency Site Assessment (ESA) round 8, 386,741 households comprising 1,814,284 IDPs were identified in 581 accessible sites in Tigray region due to the Northern Ethiopia Crisis. 
Humanitarian needs remain significantly high as the current response is not meeting the increasing needs of those in need as the resources available are not matching the requirements to ensure that minimum lifesaving humanitarian standards are maintained for the targeted population. According to the northern Ethiopia humanitarian update shared (OCHA, 14 April 2022), between 1 January and 4 April 2022, only 42.11% of the targeted people were reached with ESNFI response in Tigray region. Critical needs prioritized include, provision of adequate shelters and NFIs for IDPs living in highly congested and substandard living conditions, provision of shelter and NFI assistance to IDPs willing to return to their areas of origin, and to IDPs currently living within host communities, and rental assistance schemes or other arrangements for IDPs living in host communities. 
Inadequate provision of WASH services poses a risk of disease outbreaks at IDP sites. About 9,300 water points or more than 54 per cent of the 17,080 water points in Tigray are not functional affecting the access of more than 3.5 million people to safe drinking water. About 418,000 IDPs in 131 sites require 295 trips of water trucking every day which requires 1,990 liters of fuel daily. Construction of more than 17,000 latrines at IDP sites are required to mitigate the risks of disease transmission. Low stock of key WASH NFIs, including water treatment chemical, water containers and hygiene supplies have also been reported in Tigray. Priority WASH needs include, emergency water trucking, rehabilitation of  water schemes, rehabilitation of sanitation facilities, distribution of WASH NFIs, and hygiene promotion activities.
The locations and activities considered for the WASH and ES/NFI interventions under this project plan are identified in the HRP 2022 prioritization list to address the immediate and life-saving needs of crisis-affected communities in line with the respective clusters' priority activities. The actions will be WASH and ESNFI services and carried out in line with cluster objectives CLWSH/CO1 (Deliver conflict-sensitive essential life-saving WASH services to affected people), CLWSH/CO3 (To enhance vulnerable households’ ability to withstand recurrent and future shocks in Ethiopia through early recovery and resilience interventions), and CLSHL/CO1, (Ensure contextualized access to lifesaving shelter and NFIs for displacement affected population with a focus on the most vulnerable and at-risk population group to safeguard their health security, privacy, and dignity  )and CLSHL/CO2 (Contribute to improving protection outcomes by ensuring the conflict/displacement affected people have adequate safety, dignity, well-being, and equitable access to shelter solutions).
The projects aim to enhance the protection, health, and well-being of the conflict affected IDPs and host communities, and will directly reach 43,765 people through WASH and 40,055 people through ES/NFI prioritizing the most vulnerable, including women, girls, children, elderly, and people with disabilities in particular.
The project will ensure the active participation of the targeted beneficiaries and stakeholders throughout the project cycle. Protection and safety concerns will be given priority and DRC will ensure providing safe, easy, and dignified access to the facilities by the most vulnerable.

destinationObjects_Project.name: Provision of integrated, equitable, and timely WASH services to emergency affected populations in South Sudan
project_text:
Provision of integrated, equitable, and timely WASH services to emergency affected populations in South Sudan Protracted crises in South Sudan, including climactic shocks and continued conflict, have resulted in 8.9 million people projected to be in need of humanitarian assistance in 2022. As a result of the shocks, such as flooding, inter-communal violence (ICV) and ongoing armed clashes, the majority of the population are facing increased food insecurity, lack of access to basic services, and protection risks. As per the Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) 2022, lack of or inadequate access to clean water and improved sanitation and hygiene practices in South Sudan will negatively impact an estimated 6.1 million people in 2022. 

Since 2006, Solidarites International has become a key WASH actor in South Sudan, implementing emergency lifesaving responses across the country and providing integrated WASH services to crisis-affected populations in areas of static presence in Upper Nile, Jonglei, and Western Bahr el Ghazal. Since 2012 SI has played a key role in the Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPR) strategy in South Sudan, implementing multi-sectoral assessments and delivering emergency responses to crisis-affected populations all over the country. 

In 2022, SI will continue to provide emergency live-saving  WASH responses across the South Sudan to restore basic access to safe water, hygiene, and sanitation while ensuring equitable access, safety, and accountability to supported populations. Through its roving Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPR) team, SI will deploy to emergency-affected locations to provide first phase and second phase responses including distribution of household water treatment items and soap, emergency provision of safe water, and rapid repair of emergency-affected infrastructure.

At the same time, SI will expand its static presence in Upper Nile and Jonglei to provide basic integrated WASH services that target the most vulnerable, including those suffering malnutrition, food insecurity and protection threats. Static programs will focus on providing community-based solutions for sustainable WASH services that ensure that improvements in access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene are durable and can be maintained independently by communities. Engagement and joint programming with Protection and Nutrition actors will ensure that WASH services can be accessed by the most vulnerable and will have a tangible impact on reducing overall priority humanitarian needs. The increased integration of protection, inclusion, and conflict sensitivity analysis in all programming will ensure that WASH services and resources can be safely accessed by all in the community. Greater engagement of communities and local markets will support the design of long term and flood resistant WASH infrastructure and supply chains to ensure that interventions produce durable results for communities.

project_text:
WFP SOMALIA 2022 HRP - FSC Somalia has been impacted by multiple shocks in 2020, including desert locust invasion, flash floods and COVID-19. This has negatively affected the ability of vulnerable households to meet their food security needs. The urban poor, including IDP households, have been disproportionally affected due to the socio-economic effects from COVID-19 due their heavy reliance on food purchases from the market and casual labor as the main sources of income. These households are likely to face food consumption gaps due to declines in employment and income-earning opportunities. The desert locust caused significant damage to cereal crops, fruits, vegetables and pasture in the northern and central regions. Control efforts of the government and partners in Somaliland and Puntland made progress, but an increasing number of adult locust groups was reported in central regions. In addition, in the northeast, remained swarms have matured, and some have moved towards central areas. As per FAO, the hatching and band formation is occurring now and more swarms are likely to move to other areas in central Somalia and at later stages are expected to move towards crop producing areas in the south; which can have some negative impact to the crops and pasture up to early next year.

The impact of localized flooding particularly in riverine areas destroyed farmland and crops and caused population displacement, leading to significant crop losses and the loss of income from agricultural employment.

Jointly with the Government and other humanitarian actors, WFP Somalia has supported communities and vulnerable houses impacted by the multiple shocks. The high levels of sustained humanitarian assistance in 2020 have played a critical role in stabilizing the situation. The immediate food security outlook for Somalia however looks bleak despite the efforts sustained in 2020. According to the latest Post-Gu Assessment, 2.1 million people are expected to be food insecure (IPC 3 and 4) across Somalia through December 2020. An additional 3 million people are expected to be Stressed (IPC 2), bringing the total number of people facing cute food insecurity to 5.1 million until the end of this year. Based on results of the 2020 Post Gu assessment, an estimated 849,900 children under the age of five years face acute malnutrition between September 2020 and August 2021, including 143,400 likely to be severely malnourished.

destinationObjects_Project.name: Life Saving emergency WASH and basic needs   for drought affected community in East Bale Zone
project_text:
Life Saving emergency WASH and basic needs   for drought affected community in East Bale Zone IRC assessment identified a significant number of livestock deaths, highly weakening livestock, and mass migration in search of water and fodder.  As of January 2022, the number of reported livestock death was: 37,722 in Dawe Sarar, 368 in Lagahidha, and 847 in Dawe Kachen,. According to the July 2021 hot-spot classification done by the National Disaster Risk Management Commission, a total of 126 woredas in Oromia including targeted woredas, and 71% of the districts in the East Bale Zone are classified as hotspot priority 1and in need of urgent response.

The IRC proposed intervention will be implemented to support drought affected communities in three woredas (districts) namely Dawe Serer, Legehidha and Sewena woredas of East Bale Zone, oromoiya region, Ethiopia. The IRC has prioritized and select these woredas for project intervention after analysis the avialabe data and in consultation with the main partners - regional government bureaus. Some of the main rationales considered for geographical targeting includes complement and synergy with ongoing IRC projects for better impact, scale and magnitude of the drought and its impact, multifaceted crisis (drought, conflict induced IDPs and returnees), limited number of active partners and responses, etc.  
The project aims People affected by drought have increased access to safe drinking water and improved their awareness on sanitation and hygiene and have improved access to food and meet other basic needs and minimize negative coping strategies through provision of unconditional multipurpose cash response in Dawe Serer, Legehidha and Sewena woredas of East Bale Zone. the project will be implemented in the coming Six months and 20901 individuals will be benefited.

reportDetails_organization: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
project_text: Enhancement of protection of displaced persons, returnees and conflict affected host communities in Syria through integrated, community-based protection activities. The project aims to strengthen protection and resilience of Syrian IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities through advocacy, coordination, provision of community-based protection services and legal services UNHCR Syria will continue to lead the Protection Sector/Cluster to ensure coordinated protection interventions programming for safe refugees return. UNHCR’s protection interventions include legal counselling and assistance, protection monitoring, referrals and information sharing, social protection through livelihoods support to most vulnerable people, GBV prevention and response, child protection, psychosocial support and in-kind assistance for persons with specific needs including persons with disabilities, non-formal education, and awareness activities on various subjects targeting women, men, boys and girls. In addition to over 125 community centres providing integrated protection services, outreach to communities will be convened through over 2,800 outreach volunteers. Accountability to affected people will be realized through meaningful participation of communities based on age, gender and diversity approach, structured focus group discussions and enhancement of the community-based feedback and complaint mechanisms. UNHCR will continue its capacity building efforts to ensure services are delivered according to the standards and that accountability to affected population and do no harm principles are respected. UNHCR Syria will continue to lead Protection Sector in coordination of response plans of IDPs and affected people as well it will execute leadership roles in refugee return programmes in collaboration with the Government. Monitoring and evaluation of the planned interventions is based on the reports and observations by the partners and on regular direct observation and ongoing assessment by UNHCR and the comparison of achievements and related financial expenditures with objectives. Evaluation is conducted through different channels including the post distribution monitoring to determine the effectiveness of/measure the satisfaction of POCs with the service and the distribution process in addition to multiple satisfaction surveys and tracking tools related to different protection interventions. Monitoring and evaluation activities are carried out at various levels by partners and agencies implementing subprojects, UNHCR Branch Office, Sub Office and Field Offices. Situation reports are submitted by all UNHCR Field Offices to their respective Supervising Office and Branch Offices submit a corresponding report to Headquarters.

reportDetails_organization: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development; United States of America, Government of; Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
project_text:
Humanitarian coordination and provision of CCCM-integrated responses to displacement-affected populations in Juba and Bor former PoC sites (semi-static) in hard-to-reach areas (mobile) In line with the CCCM cluster strategy, ACTED will continue to provide humanitarian coordination and CCCM integrated response to displacement affected population in Juba former PoC sites and will provide mobile support in hard-to-reach areas in response to displacement shocks.  Due to natural hazards, localized and state conflicts, displacement waves remain high in South Sudan with 1.64 million people currently being Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) in need of CCCM assistance according to the South Sudan HNO 2022. The trend has been increasing in 2022 following massive natural hazards such as floodings in Jonglei state, leading to the multiplication of displacement sites. 
As South Sudan has been subject to displacement waves since its creation, and particularly following the 2013 civil war, some IDP sites have existed for several years with residents not willing to return to their areas of origin and ongoing humanitarian aid. To address this issue, ACTED aims to provide a more sustainable solution and support these IDP communities to become more empowered and increase their integration into host communities settings. Following a strategy implemented since 2021 in agreement with CCCM cluster, ACTED handed over camp management responsibilities to the community representatives and local authorities, especially Relief and Rehabilitation Commission (RRC) in Bor and Juba former PoC camps in 2022. In 2023, ACTED will strengthen social cohesion between IDPs and host communities in Juba to foster peaceful coexistence and will provide ad-hoc support to community representatives if needed to ensure a smooth transition. 
In parallel, ACTED provides emergency CCCM assistance in response to displacement shocks across the country. Through a well-established coordination system with REACH, the Inter Cluster Coordination Group, the Needs Analysis Working Group and the clusters, ACTED has access to timely information on displacements, allowing for a rapid multi-sectoral intervention whose core is CCCM services. Within its CCCM rapid response, ACTED aims to provide life saving coordination activities among humanitarian actors and build local communities’ capacities to self manage the sites. 
Therefore, ACTED will continue implementing CCCM interventions in line with the following cluster objectives: CO1: Improve living condition of IDPs by facilitating safe, equitable and dignified access to cross-sectoral humanitarian services, including CCCM CO2: Enhance the protective environment, respond to vulnerable population with priority on addressing protection gaps and strengthen the predictability and effectiveness of multi sectorial interventions at site level CO3: Support vulnerable IDPs to recover from the crisis by strengthening community self-management, build resilience to promote solutions for displaced people in sites.

project_text: Apoyo integral para la mejora del acceso a la educación de calidad y de la permanencia escolar de alumnos y docentes Este proyecto pretende mejorar las condiciones ofrecidas en las escuelas referentes a alimentación escolar (para 406,338 niños, niñas y adolescentes- NNAs), disponibilidad de material educativo para incentivar el acceso y la asistencia regular de los estudiantes (1,250,000 NNA). También pretende mejorar las condiciones de trabajo y la capacidad técnica de los docentes mediante actividades de formación y distribución de incentivos (23,734 docentes) que reduzcan el absentismo y la deserción de los docentes. El proyecto ofrece soluciones a 150,000 NNAs que han abandonado el sistema escolar para que se reincorporen a la escuela o a oportunidades de aprendizaje alternativas. Igualmente se ofrecen actividades de apoyo socioemocinal para 300,000 NNA. También se pretende fortalecer las capacidades del sector para alcanzar a 400,000 con actividades de educación a distancia y llegar a 70,000 adolescentes con actividades de nivelación escolar y la promoción de habilidades para la vida. Todas estas actividades se desarrollarán primando un enfoque intersectorial que tenga en cuenta aspectos de protección infantil, WASH, nutrición y componentes de sensibilización dirigidos a promover cambios de conducta, todo ello con un enfoque inclusivo y de protección de derechos.

project_text:
Food assistance to address increasing levels of severe food insecurity in South Sudan Meet the lifesaving food requirements of people in South Sudan who are facing food security crises, including those living in (ex)-POCs and IDP and those otherwise affected by conflict, natural disaster and/or seasonal food insecurity. WFP will provide general food distributions (GFD) to the most food insecure people in South Sudan. At the field level, food assistance will be overseen by the WFP Field Offices and implemented by NGO partners or provided through the Integrated Rapid Response Mechanism (IRRM). IRRM is a Delivering as One approach, in which UNICEF supports WASH and nutrition activities, FAO provides emergency seeds and livelihood kits, and WFP provides food assistance and common services through a comprehensive and collaborative humanitarian intervention by deploying mobile teams, supported by cooperating partners to reach populations facing the most urgent needs in the most inaccessible areas of the South Sudan, subject to the availability of resources.

Complementary to food distributions, WFP will seek to offer value-added solutions (GFD+), in response to needs and priorities identified by the community. Through GFD+, WFP together with its cooperating partners and other stakeholders will provide unconditional opportunities, identified through a community-based, people-centric participatory approach to targeted beneficiaries. GFD+ adds value to emergency food assistance with a focus on solutions that address the root causes of food and nutrition insecurity and better equip beneficiaries to fight hunger. The GFD+ activity type, duration, frequency, and participation will be catered to specific local sites and may range from COVID-19 awareness and mitigation measures to nutrition education, dyke rehabilitation and communal asset management, income-generating activities which lead to women's economic empowerment and have positive impact on household food security, or other solutions. WFP will also implement resilience building activities including Food Assistance for Assets (FFA) to support communities to improve their food security, restore their livelihoods, strengthen their resilience to shocks and build self-reliance, while contributing to peace.

Mitigation measures to reduce and prevent the potential the spread of COVID-19, including new variants, and other potential viral outbreaks have been incorporated into standard operating procedures for all interactions with beneficiaries, including training of partners and stakeholders, increasing general awareness among partners and beneficiaries, enforcing social distancing, promoting handwashing, disinfecting sites, reducing the frequency of distribution cycles, and mandating the utilization of personal protective equipment (PPE). These measures are mainstreamed into all WFP activities and are part of the ‘new way of working’.

project_text:
Emergency WASH Response in South Sudan UNICEF will provide women, men, girls, and boys affected by multiple shocks and hazards
in South Sudan with critical water, sanitation, and hygiene services, items, and facilities.
The objective of this project is to provide lifesaving emergency water supply, sanitation
and hygiene promotion services for con􀂧ict affected people, vulnerable host communities
and people in disease prone (high GAM famine and outbreak related) areas including
protection related actions to mitigate GBV, strengthening of communities’ resilience to
cope with the impact of emergencies and recurrent shocks. This emergency WASH project
will comprise of situation assessments, preparedness, transitional programs, frontline
emergency WASH response, strengthening of partners’ capacity, and cluster coordination
including sector information management. UNICEF will deliver emergency lifesaving
support by providing access to WASH services as per Sphere and WASH Cluster
standards.
The project will focus on addressing the following:
- Effective Cluster coordination mechanism in the country
- Provide timely equitable access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene for IDPs/host
communities and returnees, including transitional programming
- WASH in Nutrition for famine prevention with a minimum package of interventions.
- WASH in Health for outbreak control at wider community level (i.e. Ebola, Cholera, etc.)
- While implementing projects a special attention will be given to mitigate WASH-related
GBV.
The project will also support expansion of partnerships with local and international NGOs
and CBOs in highly affected areas to ensure basic services are provided and long-term
capacity built. The activities will be implemented in complementarity with other sectors
such as Health, Nutrition, Protection and where possible Education projects including
disaster risk reduction (DRR) focusing on strengthening community coping mechanisms.

project_text:
Shelter and NFI Assistance for IDPs and host community members in Northern Syria The proposed project aims at addressing emergency and more sustainable shelter and NFI needs of vulnerable households with acute needs (both IDPs and host community members) in Northeast and Northwest Syria.  

The intervention will target a total of 123,625 beneficiaries under shelter activities, and 153,004 beneficiaries under NFI activities across Northwest and Northeast Syria for a total budget of 5,472,963$ including 4,209,680$ of program budget. To note, some beneficiaries will receive more than one type of assistance. As a result, some of them if will double-counted under the activities in section 4. 

In Northwest Syria, ACTED will provide fuel for heaters to better equip the residents for winter in A’zaz and Idleb sub-districts for 111,095 individuals for 1,148,474$ (program budget). Under this intervention, the same number of camp residents will also receive emergency NFI kits -composed of, for example, tarpaulin, jerry can, mattresses/sleeping mats, blankets, solar lamps, floor mat, stove, cooking pot, bowl for food, and cutlery - as well as winterization kits, to guarantee shelter and dignified living conditions to newly displaced household, for 196,296$ (program budget). Through contractors, ACTED will rehabilitate private off-camp shelter units to 600 individuals in A’zaz sub-district for 131,046$ (program budget). In addition, ACTED will rehabilitate shelters in-camp to 500 individuals in Jarablus sub-district for 135,061$ (program budget). project_text: Respuesta multi-sectorial para mejorar el acceso a una educación de calidad y segura para NNA afectados por la situación humanitaria La intervención educativa forma parte de la respuesta integrada de NRC Venezuela. El equipo de Educación continuará trabajando en colaboración con los programas Información, Orientación y Asistencia legal (ICLA), Agua Higiene y Saneamiento (ASH) y Medios de vida y seguridad alimentaria (LFS) para permitir que las poblaciones afectadas por la situación humanitaria y desplazamientos satisfagan sus necesidades básicas, disfruten de sus derechos y se beneficien de los caminos hacia soluciones duraderas. La acción propuesta por el NRC tiene como objetivo garantizar la permanencia y los caminos de regreso al aprendizaje y la integración en la educación formal, particularmente luego del cierre de las escuelas por dos años durante la pandemia COVID-19 y su reciente reapertura. NRC responderá a los diversos problemas y necesidades que enfrentan los niños, niñas y adolescentes vulnerables en cuatro estados en Venezuela (Delta Amacuro, Bolívar, Táchira y Zulia) a través de una estrategia de respuesta basada en el Programa de Educación infantil (CEP), Programa Puente (PP) y Programa de Nivelación, así como una versión contextualizada del Better Learning Program (BLP) de NRC. Todos estos programas están adaptados al contexto venezolano.

reportDetails_organization: European Commission's Humanitarian Aid and Civil Protection Department
project_text: Protección y asistencia humanitaria a personas en movilidad y en riesgo, así como comunidades de acogida vulnerables afectadas por el desplazamiento  El objetivo principal de la intervención busca brindar protección legal a personas afectadas con necesidades específicas y vulnerables, la mitigación de riesgos asociados a la movilidad tanto interna como externa y el fortalecimiento de la resiliencia de la población venezolana afectada, incluyendo a las comunidades de acogida. Dentro de los objetivos específicos se encuentran promover el empoderamiento de las personas en movilidad o en riesgos de movilidad, así como identificar, derivar y atender a personas con necesidades de alta vulnerabilidad y riesgos de protección.  Las actividades de información y orientación a personas en tránsito y desplazadas, retornados, comunidades de acogida y otras personas de interés se realizarán por medio de la atención personal y confidencial en los puntos de información como el centro comunitario y activación de equipos móviles en las comunidades meta de los estados prioritarios (Bolívar, Delta Amacuro, Táchira, Zulia). Las mesas de información y los equipos móviles brindarán información sobre derechos, riesgos, documentación civil y rutas para la migración segura, y asegurarán una atención inmediata y derivaciones pertinentes a las personas con necesidades específicas. La derivación de los casos se hará en base a las rutas de atención existentes, ya sea para la Red de Espacios Seguros para la atención de supervivientes de violencia sexual o de género y niñez en riesgo, como a miembros de las Redes de Protección. NRC también hará derivaciones a organizaciones prestadoras de servicios de respuesta multisectorial a sobrevivientes de VBG. Temáticas como el acceso a la documentación civil será parte de la asistencia humanitaria con enfoque de derechos a implementar. Además, se priorizarán los servicios de información, asesoría y asistencia legal que puedan necesitar la población retornada por causa de la pandemia COVID-19. De esta forma se asegura un mejor proceso de integración de poblaciones retornadas. Por último, ICLA pondrá en marcha su componente Digital ICLA como parte de sus modalidades de prestación de servicios, a fin de mejorar su capacidad para brindar soporte remoto y llegar a las personas en el área de difícil acceso (H2R). Nuestra población meta recibirá información sobre rutas migratorias seguras. NRC utilizará las alianzas y el apoyo brindado a otras ONG, agencias o autoridades que gestionan puntos de atención y explorarán colaboraciones para ampliar aún más el alcance de Digital ICLA. Se explorará el uso de chatbots u otras herramientas tecnológicas.

project_text:
Northeast Nigeria Nutrition Response 2022 The Nutrition response in 2022 will prioritise implementation of the nutrition lifesaving activities (inpatient, outpatient, and targeted supplemental feeding programmes) and targeting of LGAs with high rates of GAM (above 10%) such as MMC/Jere, Nganzai, Bama, Machina. Hard-to-reach areas (such as Gubio, Rann, Magumeri), areas with large IDP  and returnee populations (like Monguno) and high-risk/inaccessible locations such as Marte LGA will also be prioritised for nutrition assistance. 
UNICEF will primarily target acutely malnourished children and PLW who are at a significantly high risk of death. The nutrition response will also target the total under-five and PLW with preventive nutrition services e.g. micronutrient supplementation to ensure levels of acute malnutrition are not above average thresholds, and to also reduce morbidity and mortality. The response will prioritise households with persons living with disabilities, who face barriers in accessing health, nutrition and WASH services and are disproportionately food insecure due to high levels of exclusion. 
The nutrition status of the targeted population in the BAY states significantly deteriorates during the period from May-August every year, which is the lean season and coincides with the rainy season. The season is characterised by very high rates of acute malnutrition with medical complications due to poor food access and a high prevalence of diarrhoea and malaria. UNICEF will need to adequately prepare for the lean season period by prepositioning supplies, increasing the overall sector capacity to treat acute malnutrition with a focus on inpatient care and IYCF-E
The nutrition response in BAY states will be contextualised in 2022 based on the following categorisation: 
1. Protracted crisis e.g north and central Borno LGAs where the rates of acute malnutrition are high, worsened by poor access to food and health systems. The approach in these areas will include INGO/NNGO direct support to the affected population, and prioritisation of lifesaving nutrition activities. 
3. New emergencies – locations of new crisis and fluctuations such as relocations, displacements and spike in acute malnutrition. The approach will focus on the Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) with a focus on lifesaving activities. 
4. Hard-to-reach / inaccessible areas – locations with limited humanitarian footprints and access e.g Gubio and Magumeri. The approach will include RRM and remote management strategy (where feasible) with a focus on life-saving interventions. UNICEF will also strengthen the implementation of nutrition interventions through local organizations or community-based structures to implement nutrition services in hard-to-reach/inaccessible areas. 
UNICEF response is primarily through services and in-kind deliveries. UNICEF will employ the use of cash and voucher assistance (CVA) to fill the nutrient gap in the Nutrition/Food Minimum Expenditure Basket to ensure that populations have access to a varied diet e.g CVA for meats and vegetables. 
The nutrition status of the affected population is an outcome of various underlying issues including access to health, WASH, food security, child protection, and gender issues. The main cause of acute malnutrition among children and women in BAY states is the high morbidity rates. High diarrhoea prevalence is the major cause of acute malnutrition among the IDPs and urban poor population due to the prevailing poor hygiene and sanitation conditions worsened by congested living conditions. The response will strengthen the integration of nutrition-sensitive interventions including WASH, food security, health, livelihoods and child protection, and gender-based violence risk mitigation.
UNICEF will prioritise projects that include basic nutrition packages such as integrated treatment of acute malnutrition (SAM and MAM) and prevention services including integration with WASH, food security, health and protections services.

project_text:
Food assistance to address increasing levels of severe food insecurity in South Sudan Meet the lifesaving food requirements of people in South Sudan who are facing food security crises, including those living in (ex)-POCs and IDP and those otherwise affected by conflict, natural disaster and/or seasonal food insecurity. WFP will provide general food distributions (GFD) to the most food insecure people in South Sudan. At the field level, food assistance will be overseen by the WFP Field Offices and implemented by NGO partners or provided through the Integrated Rapid Response Mechanism (IRRM). IRRM is a Delivering as One approach, in which UNICEF supports WASH and nutrition activities, FAO provides emergency seeds and livelihood kits, and WFP provides food assistance and common services through a comprehensive and collaborative humanitarian intervention by deploying mobile teams, supported by cooperating partners to reach populations facing the most urgent needs in the most inaccessible areas of the South Sudan, subject to the availability of resources.

Complementary to food distributions, WFP will seek to offer value-added solutions (GFD+), in response to needs and priorities identified by the community. Through GFD+, WFP together with its cooperating partners and other stakeholders will provide unconditional opportunities, identified through a community-based, people-centric participatory approach to targeted beneficiaries. GFD+ adds value to emergency food assistance with a focus on solutions that address the root causes of food and nutrition insecurity and better equip beneficiaries to fight hunger. The GFD+ activity type, duration, frequency, and participation will be catered to specific local sites and may range from COVID-19 awareness and mitigation measures to nutrition education, dyke rehabilitation and communal asset management, income-generating activities which lead to women's economic empowerment and have positive impact on household food security, or other solutions. WFP will also implement resilience building activities including Food Assistance for Assets (FFA) to support communities to improve their food security, restore their livelihoods, strengthen their resilience to shocks and build self-reliance, while contributing to peace.

Mitigation measures to reduce and prevent the potential the spread of COVID-19, including new variants, and other potential viral outbreaks have been incorporated into standard operating procedures for all interactions with beneficiaries, including training of partners and stakeholders, increasing general awareness among partners and beneficiaries, enforcing social distancing, promoting handwashing, disinfecting sites, reducing the frequency of distribution cycles, and mandating the utilization of personal protective equipment (PPE). These measures are mainstreamed into all WFP activities and are part of the ‘new way of working’.

Le HCR collabore avec des partenaires à travers des projets axés sur des solutions à long terme. Ces activités contribuent grandement à créer un environnement de protection favorable dans lequel ces groupes de population peuvent devenir autonomes.

project_text:
Provision of integrated, equitable, and timely WASH services to emergency affected populations in South Sudan Protracted crises in South Sudan, including climactic shocks and continued conflict, have resulted in 8.9 million people projected to be in need of humanitarian assistance in 2022. As a result of the shocks, such as flooding, inter-communal violence (ICV) and ongoing armed clashes, the majority of the population are facing increased food insecurity, lack of access to basic services, and protection risks. As per the Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) 2022, lack of or inadequate access to clean water and improved sanitation and hygiene practices in South Sudan will negatively impact an estimated 6.1 million people in 2022. 

Since 2006, Solidarites International has become a key WASH actor in South Sudan, implementing emergency lifesaving responses across the country and providing integrated WASH services to crisis-affected populations in areas of static presence in Upper Nile, Jonglei, and Western Bahr el Ghazal. Since 2012 SI has played a key role in the Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPR) strategy in South Sudan, implementing multi-sectoral assessments and delivering emergency responses to crisis-affected populations all over the country. 

In 2022, SI will continue to provide emergency live-saving  WASH responses across the South Sudan to restore basic access to safe water, hygiene, and sanitation while ensuring equitable access, safety, and accountability to supported populations. Through its roving Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPR) team, SI will deploy to emergency-affected locations to provide first phase and second phase responses including distribution of household water treatment items and soap, emergency provision of safe water, and rapid repair of emergency-affected infrastructure.

project_text:
Protection and Assistance for Refugees, Returnees and Asylum Seekers in South Sudan As of January 2022, there are some 335,000 refugees and asylum seekers from neighbouring countries sheltering in South Sudan. Despite enormous socio-economic, security and political challenges, compounded by the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, South Sudan has maintained its open-door policy for people seeking international protection, the majority of whom are women and children, primarily from Sudan, the Democratic Republic of Congo and the Central African Republic.
At the same time, against a backdrop of fragile peace and cautious optimism for longer term stability, hundreds of thousands of South Sudanese refugees have spontaneously returned to the country since the signing of the 2018 Revitalized Peace Agreement. While UNHCR is not promoting or facilitating return to South Sudan, this spontaneous movement has prompted the development of an area-based approach, to support refugees, returnees and host communities, through enhanced engagement with development actors, to support greater access to services where possible.
Refugees largely reside in conflict-affected regions, challenged by an unpredictable security environment as well as at times fragile relations with host communities. Displaced communities will continue to rely on life-saving humanitarian assistance provided by UNHCR and its partners as a result of enduring economic hardship, weak rule of law, limited development support and a lack of social services and infrastructure in refugee-hosting areas as well as in areas of origin. A reduction in basic assistance, especially during a global pandemic, will immediately lead to the deterioration of the humanitarian situation to emergency levels, due to the absence of a safety net, including social services, community support networks and limited access to livelihoods in displacements sites hosting refugees and South Sudanese refugee returnees.
Under the refugee response, all refugees and asylum seekers registered with UNHCR will benefit from various forms of protection interventions, including individual registration and documentation, and multi-sector assistance. Specific protection services, such as SGBV response and child protection will focus on the identified at-risk groups. While water, health, nutrition and education services will continue to maintain indicators within global standards for refugees living in camps, provision of other assistance, including shelter, non-food items and livelihoods support, will be undertaken in a targeted manner, focusing on persons with specific protection needs and vulnerabilities. This will primarily be achieved through participatory assessments, surveys as well as verification exercise to identify vulnerable refugees and their needs. Impact monitoring will be used to gauge the efficiency of projects implemented and for the purposes of course-correction in terms of better targeting of assistance. The needs of persons with disabilities and the elderly will be further mainstreamed in various multi-sector response services. Vulnerable refugees in urban settings will also continue to benefit from targeted protection interventions and facilitation of their access to national services.

project_text:
Building the resilience of crisis-affected Syrian women, men, boys, and girls through adequate WASH Needs: In 2024, there are 16.7 million people in Syria requiring humanitarian aid, up from 15.3 million in 2023. Of these, 5.5 million are displaced, with over 2 million living in precarious conditions. The situation worsened due to earthquakes in February 2023, which uprooted hundreds of thousands, caused nearly 5,900 deaths, and over 12,800 injuries. The earthquakes further damaged already weakened infrastructure and left many families without their main breadwinner, exacerbating an already dire economic crisis and increasing the vulnerability of millions.
Interventions: Oxfam, drawing on its experience in Syria since 2013, continues to collaborate with local authorities and communities to address water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) needs in vulnerable populations across several districts and subdistricts, including Aleppo, Hama, Idlib, Latakia, Rural Damascus, Dar’a, and Deir Ezzor. This involves assessing needs, prioritizing based on severity, and adapting to emerging needs. Through integrated assessments conducted from January 2022 onwards, covering approximately 50 communities, Oxfam consulted with local and international NGOs, utilized secondary data, and considered the Humanitarian Needs Overview. The targeted areas face significant WASH challenges, categorized under severity scales 3, 4, and 5. In 2024, the project will emphasize life-saving WASH interventions, bolstering existing systems, such as water supply and sewage networks, wastewater treatment, and solid waste management. Additionally, it will integrate public health and hygiene promotion activities, including providing hygiene NFIs. Gender sensitivity is prioritized throughout the project, with a response strategy guided by community engagement and safe programming approaches, tailored to access and security concerns.
Protection Risk Analysis
Risk: Due to access restrictions& limited funds, Oxfam cannot always adopt a blanket distribution, and at the same time is unable to directly identify beneficiaries eligible to NFI in alignment with its vulnerability/selection criteria, which generates a risk of selection bias, inclusion/exclusion errors and community perceptions of unfair eligibility criteria or discriminatory practices. Likelihood: Medium. Impact: High MM: community-based targeting and selection; Risk-informed selection criteria; multi-layer verification of the list of selected beneficiaries; Programme data is disaggregated per gender, disability, and status i.e., displaced, returnee, host, so red flags are identified if any. Oxfam, in 2024, will also review its conflict-sensitive framework to ensure building on the connectors and not exacerbating dividers throughout the project cycle. Risk: limited options of sites for distributions & bureaucratic/admin impediments that further condense the timeframe for implementation, could lead to compromising on essential safe& inclusive requirements e.g., access ramps for PWD or elderly, proximate distance from ben. residences, limited number of beneficiaries approaching the site per day (crowded setting can increase the risk of GBV and tensions). Likelihood: Medium. Impact: High MM: operational CFM, planning more in advance with considering external barriers, consider CVA modalities to improve dignified outcomes. (continued in extended project summary)
