project_text:
WFP SOMALIA 2022 HRP - FSC Somalia has been impacted by multiple shocks in 2020, including desert locust invasion, flash floods and COVID-19. This has negatively affected the ability of vulnerable households to meet their food security needs. The urban poor, including IDP households, have been disproportionally affected due to the socio-economic effects from COVID-19 due their heavy reliance on food purchases from the market and casual labor as the main sources of income. These households are likely to face food consumption gaps due to declines in employment and income-earning opportunities. The desert locust caused significant damage to cereal crops, fruits, vegetables and pasture in the northern and central regions. Control efforts of the government and partners in Somaliland and Puntland made progress, but an increasing number of adult locust groups was reported in central regions. In addition, in the northeast, remained swarms have matured, and some have moved towards central areas. As per FAO, the hatching and band formation is occurring now and more swarms are likely to move to other areas in central Somalia and at later stages are expected to move towards crop producing areas in the south; which can have some negative impact to the crops and pasture up to early next year.

The impact of localized flooding particularly in riverine areas destroyed farmland and crops and caused population displacement, leading to significant crop losses and the loss of income from agricultural employment.

Jointly with the Government and other humanitarian actors, WFP Somalia has supported communities and vulnerable houses impacted by the multiple shocks. The high levels of sustained humanitarian assistance in 2020 have played a critical role in stabilizing the situation. The immediate food security outlook for Somalia however looks bleak despite the efforts sustained in 2020. According to the latest Post-Gu Assessment, 2.1 million people are expected to be food insecure (IPC 3 and 4) across Somalia through December 2020. An additional 3 million people are expected to be Stressed (IPC 2), bringing the total number of people facing cute food insecurity to 5.1 million until the end of this year. Based on results of the 2020 Post Gu assessment, an estimated 849,900 children under the age of five years face acute malnutrition between September 2020 and August 2021, including 143,400 likely to be severely malnourished.

project_text: Apoyo integral para la mejora del acceso a la educación de calidad y de la permanencia escolar de alumnos y docentes Este proyecto pretende mejorar las condiciones ofrecidas en las escuelas referentes a alimentación escolar (para 406,338 niños, niñas y adolescentes- NNAs), disponibilidad de material educativo para incentivar el acceso y la asistencia regular de los estudiantes (1,250,000 NNA). También pretende mejorar las condiciones de trabajo y la capacidad técnica de los docentes mediante actividades de formación y distribución de incentivos (23,734 docentes) que reduzcan el absentismo y la deserción de los docentes. El proyecto ofrece soluciones a 150,000 NNAs que han abandonado el sistema escolar para que se reincorporen a la escuela o a oportunidades de aprendizaje alternativas. Igualmente se ofrecen actividades de apoyo socioemocinal para 300,000 NNA. También se pretende fortalecer las capacidades del sector para alcanzar a 400,000 con actividades de educación a distancia y llegar a 70,000 adolescentes con actividades de nivelación escolar y la promoción de habilidades para la vida. Todas estas actividades se desarrollarán primando un enfoque intersectorial que tenga en cuenta aspectos de protección infantil, WASH, nutrición y componentes de sensibilización dirigidos a promover cambios de conducta, todo ello con un enfoque inclusivo y de protección de derechos.

project_text:
Programa de seguridad alimentaria basado en la escuela Con el objetivo de contribuir a la seguridad alimentaria de la población con mayores necesidades, el Programa Mundial de Alimentos de Naciones Unidas (WFP, por sus siglas en inglés) en Venezuela desarrolla un programa de asistencia humanitaria basado en la escuela para garantizar el acceso de los más vulnerables a una alimentación adecuada y nutritiva en el entorno escolar, familiar y comunitario. 
Este programa inició en 2021 con comidas escolares en emergencias priorizando escuelas iniciales y de educación especial.

WFP proporciona comidas escolares acompañado de un paquete integrado de intervenciones para mejorar el acceso a alimentos nutritivos y diversificados a través de las escuelas, contribuyendo al mismo tiempo a mejorar la salud y la nutrición de los niños en edad escolar, los estudiantes con discapacidad y el personal escolar, y apoyando a las comunidades a reducir la dependencia en estrategias de afrontamiento. De manera gradual, el WFP está realizando compras locales de alimentos, e incluyendo acciones para apoyar los mercados locales con compras a pequeños productores y apoyo técnico para acceso a mercados.

En este sentido, el programa de comidas escolares en emergencias tiene los siguientes componentes, para asegurar un enfoque integral que apoye al estudiante en el entorno escolar y familiar:

1. Entrega de comidas escolares nutritivas para estudiantes y personal escolar, promoviendo las compras locales y a pequeños productores.
2. Apoyo a la seguridad alimentaria del hogar a través de comida en especie o transferencias monetarias.
3. Rehabilitación de cocinas escolares para garantizar condiciones adecuadas de preparación de alimentos.
4. Comunicación para sensibilizar acerca de los principios humanitarios, la adecuada preparación de alimentos, nutrición, higiene y mantenimiento de cocinas escolares.
5. Fortalecimiento de capacidades de socios implementadores y personal escolar.
6. Acciones sensibles a la nutrición, que incluyen, tamizaje en las escuelas, educación nutricional, referencia a servicios especializados y entrega de alimento complementario fortificado (Supercereal Plus).

project_text:
Food assistance to address increasing levels of severe food insecurity in South Sudan Meet the lifesaving food requirements of people in South Sudan who are facing food security crises, including those living in (ex)-POCs and IDP and those otherwise affected by conflict, natural disaster and/or seasonal food insecurity. WFP will provide general food distributions (GFD) to the most food insecure people in South Sudan. At the field level, food assistance will be overseen by the WFP Field Offices and implemented by NGO partners or provided through the Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM). WFP provides food assistance and common services through a comprehensive and collaborative humanitarian intervention by deploying mobile teams, supported by cooperating partners to reach populations facing the most urgent needs in the most inaccessible areas of the South Sudan, subject to the availability of resources.
Complementary to food distributions, WFP will seek to offer value-added solutions (light resilience- building activities, peace/conflict resolution training also called GFD+), in response to needs and priorities identified by the community. Through GFD+, WFP together with its cooperating partners and other stakeholders will provide unconditional opportunities, identified through a community-based, people-centric participatory approach to targeted beneficiaries. GFD+ adds value to emergency food assistance with a focus on solutions that address the root causes of food and nutrition insecurity and better equip beneficiaries to fight hunger. The GFD+ activity type, duration, frequency, and participation will be catered to specific local sites and may range from COVID-19 awareness, training, or sensitisation on peaceful resolution of conflicts, mitigation measures to nutrition education, dyke rehabilitation and communal asset management, income-generating activities which lead to women's economic empowerment and have positive impact on household food security, or other solutions. WFP will also implement resilience building activities including Food Assistance for Assets (FFA) to support communities to improve their food security, restore their livelihoods, strengthen their resilience to shocks and build self-reliance, while contributing to peace. 
Mitigation measures to reduce and prevent the potential the spread of COVID-19, including new variants, and other potential viral outbreaks have been incorporated into standard operating procedures for all interactions with beneficiaries, including training of partners and stakeholders, increasing general awareness among partners and beneficiaries, enforcing social distancing, promoting handwashing, disinfecting sites, reducing the frequency of distribution cycles, and mandating the utilization of personal protective equipment (PPE). These measures are mainstreamed into all WFP activities.

project_text:
Niger Country Strategic Plan La vision de la réponse aux urgences dans le cadre du Plan Stratégique Pays (PSP) 2020-2024 du PAM Niger est la réduction de l’empreinte humanitaire dans la mise en œuvre de l’Activité 1, relative aux urgences du PSP à travers la promotion de l’approche NEXUS. Cette réponse s’inscrit dans la Stratégie de Prévention et de Gestion des Crises Alimentaires 2021 – 2025 du Dispositif National de Prévention et de Gestion de Crises Alimentaires (DNPGCA). Ce plan s’inscrit aussi dans le Plan d’Action 2021-2023 du Comité Technique Tripartite sur le Nexus Urgence-Développement (CTTNUD), en vue d’une mobilisation des ressources financières pour une planification et une mise en œuvre concertée des activités relatives à la promotion du NEXUS.  Dans le cas spécifique de l’assistance aux retournés dans leurs villages d’origine, qui est envisagée en 2022, la Loi 2018-74, relative à la protection et à l’assistance aux Personnes Déplacées Internes (PDI) cadrera le processus. Rappelons que l’Activité 1, relative aux urgences s’inscrit dans l’effet direct stratégique 1 du CSP (2020-2024) du PAM Niger « Les populations affectées, y compris les réfugiés, les personnes déplacées internes, les communautés hôtes et les retournés dans les zones ciblées sont en mesure de répondre aux besoins alimentaires minimums pendant et après la crise ».  La réponse aux urgences du PAM concernant la SECAL, basée sur une approche flexible, concernera toutes les trois (3) composantes de cette réponse en 2022 :
•	Le Mécanisme de Réponse Rapide (RRM)
•	La réponse aux crises prolongées.
•	La réponse à la soudure agricole et pastorale.
Par ailleurs la prévention de la malnutrition aux enfants 6-23 mois est combinée aux trois composantes ci-dessus.

project_text: Life-Saving Child Protection Response to Conflict and Drought Affected Children and their Families in Ethiopia The proposed project aims to ensure protection of boys and girls and youth through psychosocial interventions, that include recreational and play activities in Youth and Child Friendly Spaces (Y/CFS, structured parenting without violence consecutive workshops and provision of NFIs and dignity kits for boys, girls and adolescent girls). Save the Children will provide psychosocial services through Child Friendly Spaces (CFS) such as Psychological First Aid/PFA and referral for traumatized boys, girls and families who have witnessed or personally experienced physical injuries including death due to conflict and/or to those displaced due to drought. project_text:
WFP SOMALIA 2022 HRP - FSC Somalia has been impacted by multiple shocks in 2020, including desert locust invasion, flash floods and COVID-19. This has negatively affected the ability of vulnerable households to meet their food security needs. The urban poor, including IDP households, have been disproportionally affected due to the socio-economic effects from COVID-19 due their heavy reliance on food purchases from the market and casual labor as the main sources of income. These households are likely to face food consumption gaps due to declines in employment and income-earning opportunities. The desert locust caused significant damage to cereal crops, fruits, vegetables and pasture in the northern and central regions. Control efforts of the government and partners in Somaliland and Puntland made progress, but an increasing number of adult locust groups was reported in central regions. In addition, in the northeast, remained swarms have matured, and some have moved towards central areas. As per FAO, the hatching and band formation is occurring now and more swarms are likely to move to other areas in central Somalia and at later stages are expected to move towards crop producing areas in the south; which can have some negative impact to the crops and pasture up to early next year.

The impact of localized flooding particularly in riverine areas destroyed farmland and crops and caused population displacement, leading to significant crop losses and the loss of income from agricultural employment.

Jointly with the Government and other humanitarian actors, WFP Somalia has supported communities and vulnerable houses impacted by the multiple shocks. The high levels of sustained humanitarian assistance in 2020 have played a critical role in stabilizing the situation. The immediate food security outlook for Somalia however looks bleak despite the efforts sustained in 2020. According to the latest Post-Gu Assessment, 2.1 million people are expected to be food insecure (IPC 3 and 4) across Somalia through December 2020. An additional 3 million people are expected to be Stressed (IPC 2), bringing the total number of people facing cute food insecurity to 5.1 million until the end of this year. Based on results of the 2020 Post Gu assessment, an estimated 849,900 children under the age of five years face acute malnutrition between September 2020 and August 2021, including 143,400 likely to be severely malnourished.

project_text:
Protection and Assistance for Refugees, Returnees and Asylum Seekers in South Sudan As of January 2022, there are some 335,000 refugees and asylum seekers from neighbouring countries sheltering in South Sudan. Despite enormous socio-economic, security and political challenges, compounded by the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, South Sudan has maintained its open-door policy for people seeking international protection, the majority of whom are women and children, primarily from Sudan, the Democratic Republic of Congo and the Central African Republic.
At the same time, against a backdrop of fragile peace and cautious optimism for longer term stability, hundreds of thousands of South Sudanese refugees have spontaneously returned to the country since the signing of the 2018 Revitalized Peace Agreement. While UNHCR is not promoting or facilitating return to South Sudan, this spontaneous movement has prompted the development of an area-based approach, to support refugees, returnees and host communities, through enhanced engagement with development actors, to support greater access to services where possible.
Refugees largely reside in conflict-affected regions, challenged by an unpredictable security environment as well as at times fragile relations with host communities. Displaced communities will continue to rely on life-saving humanitarian assistance provided by UNHCR and its partners as a result of enduring economic hardship, weak rule of law, limited development support and a lack of social services and infrastructure in refugee-hosting areas as well as in areas of origin. A reduction in basic assistance, especially during a global pandemic, will immediately lead to the deterioration of the humanitarian situation to emergency levels, due to the absence of a safety net, including social services, community support networks and limited access to livelihoods in displacements sites hosting refugees and South Sudanese refugee returnees.
Under the refugee response, all refugees and asylum seekers registered with UNHCR will benefit from various forms of protection interventions, including individual registration and documentation, and multi-sector assistance. Specific protection services, such as SGBV response and child protection will focus on the identified at-risk groups. While water, health, nutrition and education services will continue to maintain indicators within global standards for refugees living in camps, provision of other assistance, including shelter, non-food items and livelihoods support, will be undertaken in a targeted manner, focusing on persons with specific protection needs and vulnerabilities. This will primarily be achieved through participatory assessments, surveys as well as verification exercise to identify vulnerable refugees and their needs. Impact monitoring will be used to gauge the efficiency of projects implemented and for the purposes of course-correction in terms of better targeting of assistance. The needs of persons with disabilities and the elderly will be further mainstreamed in various multi-sector response services. Vulnerable refugees in urban settings will also continue to benefit from targeted protection interventions and facilitation of their access to national services.

reportDetails_organization: European Commission's Humanitarian Aid and Civil Protection Department
project_text:
Strengthening the Protection of Crisis Affected Communities through Timely and Effective Humanitarian Interventions in Somalia and Somaliland. The Humanitarian Crisis in Somalia continues to further aggravate with over 7.7 million people projected to require urgent and life-saving assistance in 2022, a significant increase from 2019 (4.9 million) and 2020 (5.2 million). The principle drivers being the deepened armed conflict in many parts of South-Central Somalia and erratic climatic conditions with flooding and drought happening simultaneously in different parts of the Country. 
This coupled with COVID 19 pandemic, not only hampers access to basic services but also leads to increased marginalization of minority groups, displaced persons and persons with special needs, heightened protection risks, loss of livelihoods and income, and limited freedom of movement. In addition, communities have reduced coping capacities and resilience, with women and girls, minority clan members, and people living with disabilities being disproportionately affected. With the country gearing for state and federal elections, there is the likelihood of displacements and disruptions of lives amid intensified attacks from non-state actors. Recent conflicts and violence in mid-2021 displaced 250,000 people in Banaadir, Bardaale and Badweyn, including nearly 207,000 people who were temporally displaced in Mogadishu owing to election-related violence in April 2021. This against a backdrop of limited and constrained humanitarian assistance will not only result in loss of lives, affected livelihoods and destroyed property, but also increased vulnerabilities and heightened protection risks for vulnerable groups.
Data from the PRMN, SPMS and MRM systems designates heightened protection risks in the country with over 4 million people projected to need lifesaving protection assistance (HNO, 2021).  The GBV AOR reported a spike in Intimate Partner Violence, rape, sexual exploitation, sexual harassment and abuse against women and girls in 2021 most of which are from displacement affected communities. Furthermore, accruing to the MRM data, Somalia is now the most dangerous conflict on earth for children, where over 23,000 grave violations were recorded in the last 5 year, and of concern is the number of child recruitment and abductions far exceeding any other country in the world. 
Thus, DRC will design and implement interventions targeting the most vulnerable persons in the communities including DACs, girls, women, boys, and men at risk of/ survivors of GBVs, minority groups/clans, persons with disabilities, children and adults affected by armed violence including explosive remnants of wars (ERWs) and other explosive devices, people at risk of forced evictions and most vulnerable host communities to strengthening capacity and the commitment of families and communities to protect communities especially children and women from violence, exploitation and harmful practices, through elimination of harmful practices and all forms of gender-based violence, provision of timely holistic and quality age and gender appropriate services to survivors, persons at risks and vulnerable persons including PSNs in addition to strengthened community-based protection systems.
The proposed interventions thus align with the general protection, GBV, Explosive Hazards (EH) and Housing, Land and Property (HLP) cluster objectives and indicators and the Strategic objectives 1, 2 and 3 of 2022 Humanitarian Response Plan.  The interventions will employ participatory and right based approaches, age, gender and diversity (AGD) approach and community-based child protection approaches which will involve, inclusion of children and caregivers from refugee’s/asylum seeker communities, migrants, IDPs, persons with disability and most vulnerable host communities in addition to local authorities in the project management cycle. 
DRC targets to reach 58,500 persons (10,000girls,2,500B,30,000W,16,000M) in selected districts in Somalia.

project_text: Improve food security through provision of emergency food and enhance food production of food insecure housholds in Aweil North, Aweil West, Aweil South, NBeG State, South Sudan  The project will provide access to food, agriculture inputs and improve agriculture production to prevent famine and support vegetable production and fishing kits to improve food consumption, dietary diversity and coping strategies for vulnerable populations. The project will target 57,430 (33,309 female and 24,121 male) beneficiaries in Aweil North, Aweil South and Aweil West. The integration with other multi-donor funded programmes will help in reaching this target.  Concern will provide access to agricultural inputs and trainings to the 3,000 vulnerable HHs who rely on subsistence agriculture as their main source of food and livelihoods in Aweil West, Aweil North and Aweil South in NBeG. Concern will engage with the County Agriculture Department (CAD), extension workers and lead farmers for training on agriculture extension services and Climate Smart Agriculture practices, informal seeds systems, pest and post-harvest management. destinationObjects_Project.name: Improving Food security for vulnerable populations in Somaliland, particularly  IDPs in Hargeisa, Togdheer, and Sool
project_text:
Improving Food security for vulnerable populations in Somaliland, particularly  IDPs in Hargeisa, Togdheer, and Sool Somalia is facing a growing number of threats to its food security. The ongoing desert locust invasion, socio-economic effects of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic and recurrent climate shocks, including frequent flooding and drought, continue to severely impact the lives and livelihoods of the vulnerable population. With this multifaceted crises, 7.7 Million people across Somalia need in emergency food assistance. With humanitarian needs expected to further increase in 2022, it is critical to enhance immediate food access, protect and restore livelihoods and strengthen the resilience of vulnerable households. Sustained humanitarian assistance is required to prevent the further deterioration of food security and nutrition.
Through this project, Plan International and Partners will effectively provide emergency assistance for food and promote dignity and choices among project participants by increasing purchasing power with short term injection of unconditional cash transfers for 1182 HH (7092 beneficiaries; 3546F, 3546M) for six months. Through field monitoring, government reports, and sector coordination, Plan and Partners will target households in areas identified as IPC3 or worse, risk of drought, and/or IDP communities, including those recently evicted by Somaliland government. These families have insufficient income to cover rising cost of food particularly during periods of drought and other shocks due to COVID19, instability and climate change, and will qualify per criteria, e.g. female headed household, household with person with disability, etc. Partners will ensure the crises affected families receive messages on Infant, Young Child Feeding and Hygiene and have access to sufficient, safe and nutritious foods to meet their dietary needs and food preferences for an active and healthy life. Partners have complementary programs running in these areas to enable consultant and selection within communities. By targeting vulnerable families particularly with children and delivering this intervention in a gender sensitive manner, Plan strives for secondary outcomes of improved the protection environment with reduced risks to women and girls.

project_text: Enhancement of protection of displaced persons, returnees and conflict affected host communities in Syria through integrated, community-based protection activities. The project aims to strengthen protection and resilience of Syrian IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities through advocacy, coordination, provision of community-based protection services and legal services UNHCR Syria will continue to lead the Protection Sector/Cluster to ensure coordinated protection interventions programming for safe refugees return. UNHCR’s protection interventions include legal counselling and assistance, protection monitoring, referrals and information sharing, social protection through livelihoods support to most vulnerable people, GBV prevention and response, child protection, psychosocial support and in-kind assistance for persons with specific needs including persons with disabilities, non-formal education, and awareness activities on various subjects targeting women, men, boys and girls. In addition to over 125 community centres providing integrated protection services, outreach to communities will be convened through over 2,800 outreach volunteers. Accountability to affected people will be realized through meaningful participation of communities based on age, gender and diversity approach, structured focus group discussions and enhancement of the community-based feedback and complaint mechanisms. UNHCR will continue its capacity building efforts to ensure services are delivered according to the standards and that accountability to affected population and do no harm principles are respected. UNHCR Syria will continue to lead Protection Sector in coordination of response plans of IDPs and affected people as well it will execute leadership roles in refugee return programmes in collaboration with the Government. Monitoring and evaluation of the planned interventions is based on the reports and observations by the partners and on regular direct observation and ongoing assessment by UNHCR and the comparison of achievements and related financial expenditures with objectives. Evaluation is conducted through different channels including the post distribution monitoring to determine the effectiveness of/measure the satisfaction of POCs with the service and the distribution process in addition to multiple satisfaction surveys and tracking tools related to different protection interventions. Monitoring and evaluation activities are carried out at various levels by partners and agencies implementing subprojects, UNHCR Branch Office, Sub Office and Field Offices. reportDetails_organization: United States of America, Government of; United Nations Children's Fund
project_text:
Northeast Nigeria Nutrition Response 2022 The Nutrition response in 2022 will prioritise implementation of the nutrition lifesaving activities (inpatient, outpatient, and targeted supplemental feeding programmes) and targeting of LGAs with high rates of GAM (above 10%) such as MMC/Jere, Nganzai, Bama, Machina. Hard-to-reach areas (such as Gubio, Rann, Magumeri), areas with large IDP  and returnee populations (like Monguno) and high-risk/inaccessible locations such as Marte LGA will also be prioritised for nutrition assistance. 
UNICEF will primarily target acutely malnourished children and PLW who are at a significantly high risk of death. The nutrition response will also target the total under-five and PLW with preventive nutrition services e.g. micronutrient supplementation to ensure levels of acute malnutrition are not above average thresholds, and to also reduce morbidity and mortality. The response will prioritise households with persons living with disabilities, who face barriers in accessing health, nutrition and WASH services and are disproportionately food insecure due to high levels of exclusion. 
The nutrition status of the targeted population in the BAY states significantly deteriorates during the period from May-August every year, which is the lean season and coincides with the rainy season. The season is characterised by very high rates of acute malnutrition with medical complications due to poor food access and a high prevalence of diarrhoea and malaria. UNICEF will need to adequately prepare for the lean season period by prepositioning supplies, increasing the overall sector capacity to treat acute malnutrition with a focus on inpatient care and IYCF-E
The nutrition response in BAY states will be contextualised in 2022 based on the following categorisation: 
1. Protracted crisis e.g north and central Borno LGAs where the rates of acute malnutrition are high, worsened by poor access to food and health systems. The approach in these areas will include INGO/NNGO direct support to the affected population, and prioritisation of lifesaving nutrition activities. 
3. New emergencies – locations of new crisis and fluctuations such as relocations, displacements and spike in acute malnutrition. The approach will focus on the Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM) with a focus on lifesaving activities. 
4. Hard-to-reach / inaccessible areas – locations with limited humanitarian footprints and access e.g Gubio and Magumeri. The approach will include RRM and remote management strategy (where feasible) with a focus on life-saving interventions. UNICEF will also strengthen the implementation of nutrition interventions through local organizations or community-based structures to implement nutrition services in hard-to-reach/inaccessible areas. 
UNICEF response is primarily through services and in-kind deliveries. UNICEF will employ the use of cash and voucher assistance (CVA) to fill the nutrient gap in the Nutrition/Food Minimum Expenditure Basket to ensure that populations have access to a varied diet e.g CVA for meats and vegetables. 
The nutrition status of the affected population is an outcome of various underlying issues including access to health, WASH, food security, child protection, and gender issues. The main cause of acute malnutrition among children and women in BAY states is the high morbidity rates. High diarrhoea prevalence is the major cause of acute malnutrition among the IDPs and urban poor population due to the prevailing poor hygiene and sanitation conditions worsened by congested living conditions. The response will strengthen the integration of nutrition-sensitive interventions including WASH, food security, health, livelihoods and child protection, and gender-based violence risk mitigation.
UNICEF will prioritise projects that include basic nutrition packages such as integrated treatment of acute malnutrition (SAM and MAM) and prevention services including integration with WASH, food security, health and protections services.

project_text:
WFP SOMALIA 2022 HRP - FSC Somalia has been impacted by multiple shocks in 2020, including desert locust invasion, flash floods and COVID-19. This has negatively affected the ability of vulnerable households to meet their food security needs. The urban poor, including IDP households, have been disproportionally affected due to the socio-economic effects from COVID-19 due their heavy reliance on food purchases from the market and casual labor as the main sources of income. These households are likely to face food consumption gaps due to declines in employment and income-earning opportunities. The desert locust caused significant damage to cereal crops, fruits, vegetables and pasture in the northern and central regions. Control efforts of the government and partners in Somaliland and Puntland made progress, but an increasing number of adult locust groups was reported in central regions. In addition, in the northeast, remained swarms have matured, and some have moved towards central areas. As per FAO, the hatching and band formation is occurring now and more swarms are likely to move to other areas in central Somalia and at later stages are expected to move towards crop producing areas in the south; which can have some negative impact to the crops and pasture up to early next year.

The impact of localized flooding particularly in riverine areas destroyed farmland and crops and caused population displacement, leading to significant crop losses and the loss of income from agricultural employment.

Jointly with the Government and other humanitarian actors, WFP Somalia has supported communities and vulnerable houses impacted by the multiple shocks. The high levels of sustained humanitarian assistance in 2020 have played a critical role in stabilizing the situation. The immediate food security outlook for Somalia however looks bleak despite the efforts sustained in 2020. According to the latest Post-Gu Assessment, 2.1 million people are expected to be food insecure (IPC 3 and 4) across Somalia through December 2020. An additional 3 million people are expected to be Stressed (IPC 2), bringing the total number of people facing cute food insecurity to 5.1 million until the end of this year. Based on results of the 2020 Post Gu assessment, an estimated 849,900 children under the age of five years face acute malnutrition between September 2020 and August 2021, including 143,400 likely to be severely malnourished.

reportDetails_organization: United States of America, Government of
project_text: Enhancement of protection of displaced persons, returnees and conflict affected host communities in Syria through integrated, community-based protection activities. The project aims to strengthen protection and resilience of Syrian IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities through advocacy, coordination, provision of community-based protection services and legal services UNHCR Syria will continue to lead the Protection Sector/Cluster to ensure coordinated protection interventions programming for safe refugees return. UNHCR’s protection interventions include legal counselling and assistance, protection monitoring, referrals and information sharing, social protection through livelihoods support to most vulnerable people, GBV prevention and response, child protection, psychosocial support and in-kind assistance for persons with specific needs including persons with disabilities, non-formal education, and awareness activities on various subjects targeting women, men, boys and girls. In addition to over 125 community centres providing integrated protection services, outreach to communities will be convened through over 2,800 outreach volunteers. Accountability to affected people will be realized through meaningful participation of communities based on age, gender and diversity approach, structured focus group discussions and enhancement of the community-based feedback and complaint mechanisms. UNHCR will continue its capacity building efforts to ensure services are delivered according to the standards and that accountability to affected population and do no harm principles are respected. UNHCR Syria will continue to lead Protection Sector in coordination of response plans of IDPs and affected people as well it will execute leadership roles in refugee return programmes in collaboration with the Government. Monitoring and evaluation of the planned interventions is based on the reports and observations by the partners and on regular direct observation and ongoing assessment by UNHCR and the comparison of achievements and related financial expenditures with objectives. Evaluation is conducted through different channels including the post distribution monitoring to determine the effectiveness of/measure the satisfaction of POCs with the service and the distribution process in addition to multiple satisfaction surveys and tracking tools related to different protection interventions. Monitoring and evaluation activities are carried out at various levels by partners and agencies implementing subprojects, UNHCR Branch Office, Sub Office and Field Offices. Situation reports are submitted by all UNHCR Field Offices to their respective Supervising Office and Branch Offices submit a corresponding report to Headquarters.

destinationObjects_Project.name: Renforcement de la protection pour les personnes vulnérables, en particulier les enfants, les survivants de violence basée sur le genre (VBG) et victimes de traite dans les régions de Diffa, Tillabéry, Maradi et Tahoua
reportDetails_organization: United States of America, Government of
project_text:
Renforcement de la protection pour les personnes vulnérables, en particulier les enfants, les survivants de violence basée sur le genre (VBG) et victimes de traite dans les régions de Diffa, Tillabéry, Maradi et Tahoua Les risques de violations des droits des hommes et femmes, y compris les risques de traite et de VBG, seront amoindris à travers la promotion d’un environnement communautaire protecteur et d’un accès renforcé aux services de protection, y compris aux services Santé mentale soutien psychosocial (SMSPS), dans les régions de Tillabéri, Diffa, Maradi et Tahoua.
Les activités cibleront les retournés, déplacés et membres des populations hôtes. Le projet prévoit 4 axes d’intervention.
1. Renforcement des capacités étatiques et des services sociaux de base dans les départements cibles pour une meilleure prise en charge des personnes en mobilité et notamment des enfants, y compris des survivant-e-s VBG et des victimes de traite : Un cycle de formation sur la protection des victimes de traite en situation de crise, permettant aussi de vulgariser le mécanisme national de référencement des victimes de traite, sera organisé pour tout acteur de la chaine de protection dans les communes cibles, dont les travailleurs sociaux de la protection de l’enfance et des organisations de la société civile (OSC). Il comprendra également des sessions sur la spécificité de la prise en charge des enfants non accompagnés en contexte humanitaire, et les besoins spécifiques des survivantes de VBG. 
2. Prévention des violences notamment envers les enfants, les femmes et les personnes en situation d'handicap, y compris de survivants de  VBG et diverses exploitations, à travers le renforcement des mécanismes communautaires de protection, l’appui aux leaders communautaires et la mobilisation des filles et garçons : En collaboration avec les DDPFPE, les mairies et les OSC, une cartographie et évaluation des besoins des structures communautaires, y compris les comités de protection, les espaces amis des enfants, les espaces surs et les écoles coraniques accueillant des enfants déplacés, seront réalisées. Suite à cette analyse, l’OIM les appuiera en matériel, afin que ces dernières puissent jouer leur rôle de protection. Leurs compétences seront renforcées afin qu’ils puissent signaler et référer les cas de protection, mais aussi qu’ils développent des actions de prévention qui encouragent des normes et comportements positifs favorisant des communautés respectueuses, égalitaires, et non violentes à l'égard des femmes et des filles. Des appuis aux initiatives des jeunes pour qu’ils sensibilisent leurs pairs seront réalisés. 
3. Atténuation des risques de protection dans les zones ciblées : En vue de prévenir l’adoption de stratégies de survie négatives des populations et de promouvoir leur dignité, l’OIM poursuivra la distribution des kits de protection adaptés aux besoins,  identifiés avec les populations. reportDetails_organization: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
project_text:
Protection and Assistance for Refugees, Returnees and Asylum Seekers in South Sudan As of January 2022, there are some 335,000 refugees and asylum seekers from neighbouring countries sheltering in South Sudan. Despite enormous socio-economic, security and political challenges, compounded by the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, South Sudan has maintained its open-door policy for people seeking international protection, the majority of whom are women and children, primarily from Sudan, the Democratic Republic of Congo and the Central African Republic.
At the same time, against a backdrop of fragile peace and cautious optimism for longer term stability, hundreds of thousands of South Sudanese refugees have spontaneously returned to the country since the signing of the 2018 Revitalized Peace Agreement. While UNHCR is not promoting or facilitating return to South Sudan, this spontaneous movement has prompted the development of an area-based approach, to support refugees, returnees and host communities, through enhanced engagement with development actors, to support greater access to services where possible.
Refugees largely reside in conflict-affected regions, challenged by an unpredictable security environment as well as at times fragile relations with host communities. Displaced communities will continue to rely on life-saving humanitarian assistance provided by UNHCR and its partners as a result of enduring economic hardship, weak rule of law, limited development support and a lack of social services and infrastructure in refugee-hosting areas as well as in areas of origin. A reduction in basic assistance, especially during a global pandemic, will immediately lead to the deterioration of the humanitarian situation to emergency levels, due to the absence of a safety net, including social services, community support networks and limited access to livelihoods in displacements sites hosting refugees and South Sudanese refugee returnees.
Under the refugee response, all refugees and asylum seekers registered with UNHCR will benefit from various forms of protection interventions, including individual registration and documentation, and multi-sector assistance. Specific protection services, such as SGBV response and child protection will focus on the identified at-risk groups. While water, health, nutrition and education services will continue to maintain indicators within global standards for refugees living in camps, provision of other assistance, including shelter, non-food items and livelihoods support, will be undertaken in a targeted manner, focusing on persons with specific protection needs and vulnerabilities. This will primarily be achieved through participatory assessments, surveys as well as verification exercise to identify vulnerable refugees and their needs. Impact monitoring will be used to gauge the efficiency of projects implemented and for the purposes of course-correction in terms of better targeting of assistance. The needs of persons with disabilities and the elderly will be further mainstreamed in various multi-sector response services. Vulnerable refugees in urban settings will also continue to benefit from targeted protection interventions and facilitation of their access to national services.

reportDetails_organization: Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
project_text:
Renforcement de la coordination et du plaidoyer humanitaire au Tchad Le projet vise à renforcer le rôle de OCHA dans la mise en œuvre de son mandat et son rôle auprès des partenaires humanitaires et gouvernementaux au niveau des fonctions coordination, gestion de l’information et plaidoyer. Le bureau national d’OCHA à N’Djaména et ses trois sous-bureaux régionaux à l’Est (Abéché) au Sud (Goré) et la province du Lac (Baga Sola) mettent l’accent sur l’opérationnalisation de ses fonctions y compris en assurant un lien entre les activités humanitaires et de développement (nexus) en vue de promouvoir une solution durable visant à ne pas perpétuer une situation de dépendance humanitaire. Dans le cadre de cette nouvelle façon de travailler outre l’opérationnalisation du nexus, le lien avec les objectifs commun des programmes développement, paix et sécurité sera mis en avant. L’accent est aussi mis sur le renforcement de la coordination civilo-militaire afin de faciliter l’accès et la protection des civils.

Le projet a pour but de renforcer la coordination d’une réponse humanitaire rapide et efficace afin de sauver des vies et protéger les personnes affectées par les situations de crises au Tchad. Une coordination humanitaire rapide et correctement évaluée au niveau des besoins de la population affectée permettra aux acteurs humanitaires de mieux identifier et répondre aux besoins humanitaires, de renforcer la préparation de réponse aux urgences à travers le renforcement des mécanismes de coordination et plus spécifiquement l‘Equipe humanitaire pays, la coordination inter-clusters, la coordination civilo-militaire, les clusters et les mécanismes de coordination au niveau de terrain.
Le projet vise aussi à assurer le plaidoyer humanitaire à travers l’analyse des besoins faites par l’ensemble de la communauté humanitaire et ses partenaires en vue une compréhension commune des problématiques auxquels fait face le Tchad, ses causes profondes, l’impact sur les populations. OCHA jouera un rôle clé dans la création d'espaces de collection et d'analyse et gestion d’informations, pour assurer une stratégie de réponse coordonnée menant à des actions humanitaires répondant aux besoins les plus aigus et être mieux préparé face aux urgences soudaines. Le projet permettra également d’assurer conjointement avec la communauté humanitaire le plaidoyer en faveur du respect des principes humanitaires, de la protection des civils, de l'accès humanitaire et pour la mobilisation et l'allocation efficace de ressources humanitaires.

Un accent a été mis sur la mise en œuvre des plans d’action de la redevabilité envers les populations affectées (AAP), la PSEA et la préparation aux urgences en plus d'intégrer une attention au genre et de renforcer la centralité de la protection.
Un plaidoyer pour plus de visibilité des résultats tangibles au niveau de la réponse facilitant la mobilisation de ressources pour les différentes crises au Tchad (mouvement de population – crise du Bassin du Lac Tchad, insécurité alimentaire et malnutrition, urgences sanitaires) est aussi défini comme une priorité dans ce projet

OCHA continuera de jouer également un rôle moteur dans le renforcement du lien entre les acteurs humanitaires et de développement et la transformation de la réponse humanitaire, en lien avec les engagements pris au Sommet humanitaire mondial de 2016 et ceci à travers la nouvelle façon de travailler (NWOW) et le renforcement de l’utilisation de la modalité de transfert monétaire.

Le bureau national d’OCHA à N’Djaména et ses trois sous-bureaux régionaux à l’Est (Abéché) au Sud (Goré) et la province du Lac (Baga Sola) mettent l’accent sur l’opérationnalisation de ses fonctions y compris en assurant un lien entre les activités humanitaires et de développement (nexus) en vue de promouvoir une solution durable visant à ne pas perpétuer une situation de dépendance humanitaire. Dans le cadre de cette nouvelle façon de travailler outre l’opérationnalisation du nexus, le lien avec les objectifs commun des programmes développement, paix et sécurité sera mis en avant. L’accent est aussi mis sur le renforcement de la coordination civilo-militaire afin de faciliter l’accès et la protection des civils.

Le projet a pour but de renforcer la coordination d’une réponse humanitaire rapide et efficace afin de sauver des vies et protéger les personnes affectées par les situations de crises au Tchad. Une coordination humanitaire rapide et correctement évaluée au niveau des besoins de la population affectée permettra aux acteurs humanitaires de mieux identifier et répondre aux besoins humanitaires, de renforcer la préparation de réponse aux urgences à travers le renforcement des mécanismes de coordination et plus spécifiquement l‘Equipe humanitaire pays, la coordination inter-clusters, la coordination civilo-militaire, les clusters et les mécanismes de coordination au niveau de terrain.
Le projet vise aussi à assurer le plaidoyer humanitaire à travers l’analyse des besoins faites par l’ensemble de la communauté humanitaire et ses partenaires en vue une compréhension commune des problématiques auxquels fait face le Tchad, ses causes profondes, l’impact sur les populations. OCHA jouera un rôle clé dans la création d'espaces de collection et d'analyse et gestion d’informations, pour assurer une stratégie de réponse coordonnée menant à des actions humanitaires répondant aux besoins les plus aigus et être mieux préparé face aux urgences soudaines. Le projet permettra également d’assurer conjointement avec la communauté humanitaire le plaidoyer en faveur du respect des principes humanitaires, de la protection des civils, de l'accès humanitaire et pour la mobilisation et l'allocation efficace de ressources humanitaires.

Un accent a été mis sur la mise en œuvre des plans d’action de la redevabilité envers les populations affectées (AAP), la PSEA et la préparation aux urgences en plus d'intégrer une attention au genre et de renforcer la centralité de la protection.
Un plaidoyer pour plus de visibilité des résultats tangibles au niveau de la réponse facilitant la mobilisation de ressources pour les différentes crises au Tchad (mouvement de population – crise du Bassin du Lac Tchad, insécurité alimentaire et malnutrition, urgences sanitaires) est aussi défini comme une priorité dans ce projet

OCHA continuera de jouer également un rôle moteur dans le renforcement du lien entre les acteurs humanitaires et de développement et la transformation de la réponse humanitaire, en lien avec les engagements pris au Sommet humanitaire mondial de 2016 et ceci à travers la nouvelle façon de travailler (NWOW) et le renforcement de l’utilisation de la modalité de transfert monétaire.

project_text:
Food assistance to address increasing levels of severe food insecurity in South Sudan Meet the lifesaving food requirements of people in South Sudan who are facing food security crises, including those living in (ex)-POCs and IDP and those otherwise affected by conflict, natural disaster and/or seasonal food insecurity. WFP will provide general food distributions (GFD) to the most food insecure people in South Sudan. At the field level, food assistance will be overseen by the WFP Field Offices and implemented by NGO partners or provided through the Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM). WFP provides food assistance and common services through a comprehensive and collaborative humanitarian intervention by deploying mobile teams, supported by cooperating partners to reach populations facing the most urgent needs in the most inaccessible areas of the South Sudan, subject to the availability of resources.
Complementary to food distributions, WFP will seek to offer value-added solutions (light resilience- building activities, peace/conflict resolution training also called GFD+), in response to needs and priorities identified by the community. Through GFD+, WFP together with its cooperating partners and other stakeholders will provide unconditional opportunities, identified through a community-based, people-centric participatory approach to targeted beneficiaries. GFD+ adds value to emergency food assistance with a focus on solutions that address the root causes of food and nutrition insecurity and better equip beneficiaries to fight hunger. The GFD+ activity type, duration, frequency, and participation will be catered to specific local sites and may range from COVID-19 awareness, training, or sensitisation on peaceful resolution of conflicts, mitigation measures to nutrition education, dyke rehabilitation and communal asset management, income-generating activities which lead to women's economic empowerment and have positive impact on household food security, or other solutions. WFP will also implement resilience building activities including Food Assistance for Assets (FFA) to support communities to improve their food security, restore their livelihoods, strengthen their resilience to shocks and build self-reliance, while contributing to peace. 
Mitigation measures to reduce and prevent the potential the spread of COVID-19, including new variants, and other potential viral outbreaks have been incorporated into standard operating procedures for all interactions with beneficiaries, including training of partners and stakeholders, increasing general awareness among partners and beneficiaries, enforcing social distancing, promoting handwashing, disinfecting sites, reducing the frequency of distribution cycles, and mandating the utilization of personal protective equipment (PPE). These measures are mainstreamed into all WFP activities.

Programa de seguridad alimentaria basado en la escuela Con el objetivo de contribuir a la seguridad alimentaria de la población con mayores necesidades, el Programa Mundial de Alimentos de Naciones Unidas (WFP, por sus siglas en inglés) en Venezuela desarrolla un programa de asistencia humanitaria basado en la escuela para garantizar el acceso de los más vulnerables a una alimentación adecuada y nutritiva en el entorno escolar, familiar y comunitario. 
Este programa inició en 2021 con comidas escolares en emergencias priorizando escuelas iniciales y de educación especial.

WFP proporciona comidas escolares acompañado de un paquete integrado de intervenciones para mejorar el acceso a alimentos nutritivos y diversificados a través de las escuelas, contribuyendo al mismo tiempo a mejorar la salud y la nutrición de los niños en edad escolar, los estudiantes con discapacidad y el personal escolar, y apoyando a las comunidades a reducir la dependencia en estrategias de afrontamiento. De manera gradual, el WFP está realizando compras locales de alimentos, e incluyendo acciones para apoyar los mercados locales con compras a pequeños productores y apoyo técnico para acceso a mercados.

En este sentido, el programa de comidas escolares en emergencias tiene los siguientes componentes, para asegurar un enfoque integral que apoye al estudiante en el entorno escolar y familiar:

1. Entrega de comidas escolares nutritivas para estudiantes y personal escolar, promoviendo las compras locales y a pequeños productores.
2. Apoyo a la seguridad alimentaria del hogar a través de comida en especie o transferencias monetarias.
3. Rehabilitación de cocinas escolares para garantizar condiciones adecuadas de preparación de alimentos.
4. Comunicación para sensibilizar acerca de los principios humanitarios, la adecuada preparación de alimentos, nutrición, higiene y mantenimiento de cocinas escolares.
5. Fortalecimiento de capacidades de socios implementadores y personal escolar.
6. Acciones sensibles a la nutrición, que incluyen, tamizaje en las escuelas, educación nutricional, referencia a servicios especializados y entrega de alimento complementario fortificado (Supercereal Plus).

Este programa inició en 2021 con comidas escolares en emergencias priorizando escuelas iniciales y de educación especial.

WFP proporciona comidas escolares acompañado de un paquete integrado de intervenciones para mejorar el acceso a alimentos nutritivos y diversificados a través de las escuelas, contribuyendo al mismo tiempo a mejorar la salud y la nutrición de los niños en edad escolar, los estudiantes con discapacidad y el personal escolar, y apoyando a las comunidades a reducir la dependencia en estrategias de afrontamiento. De manera gradual, el WFP está realizando compras locales de alimentos, e incluyendo acciones para apoyar los mercados locales con compras a pequeños productores y apoyo técnico para acceso a mercados.

En este sentido, el programa de comidas escolares en emergencias tiene los siguientes componentes, para asegurar un enfoque integral que apoye al estudiante en el entorno escolar y familiar:

1. Entrega de comidas escolares nutritivas para estudiantes y personal escolar, promoviendo las compras locales y a pequeños productores.
2. Apoyo a la seguridad alimentaria del hogar.
3. Rehabilitación de cocinas escolares para garantizar condiciones adecuadas de preparación de alimentos.
4. Comunicación para sensibilizar acerca de los principios humanitarios, la adecuada preparación de alimentos, nutrición, higiene y mantenimiento de cocinas escolares.
5. Fortalecimiento de capacidades de socios implementadores y personal escolar.
6. Acciones sensibles a la nutrición, que incluyen, tamizaje en las escuelas, educación nutricional, referencia a servicios especializados y entrega de alimento complementario fortificado (Super Cereal Plus).

reportDetails_organization: Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
project_text:
Renforcement de la coordination et du plaidoyer humanitaire au Tchad Le projet vise à renforcer le rôle de OCHA dans la mise en œuvre de son mandat et son rôle auprès des partenaires humanitaires et gouvernementaux au niveau des fonctions coordination, gestion de l’information et plaidoyer. Le bureau national d’OCHA à N’Djaména et ses trois sous-bureaux régionaux à l’Est (Abéché) au Sud (Goré) et la province du Lac (Baga Sola) mettent l’accent sur l’opérationnalisation de ses fonctions y compris en assurant un lien entre les activités humanitaires et de développement (nexus) en vue de promouvoir une solution durable visant à ne pas perpétuer une situation de dépendance humanitaire. Dans le cadre de cette nouvelle façon de travailler outre l’opérationnalisation du nexus, le lien avec les objectifs commun des programmes développement, paix et sécurité sera mis en avant. L’accent est aussi mis sur le renforcement de la coordination civilo-militaire afin de faciliter l’accès et la protection des civils.
Le projet a pour but de renforcer la coordination d’une réponse humanitaire rapide et efficace afin de sauver des vies et protéger les personnes affectées par les situations de crises au Tchad. Une coordination humanitaire rapide et correctement évaluée au niveau des besoins de la population affectée permettra aux acteurs humanitaires de mieux identifier et répondre aux besoins humanitaires, de renforcer la préparation de réponse aux urgences à travers le renforcement des mécanismes de coordination et plus spécifiquement l‘Equipe humanitaire pays, la coordination inter-clusters, la coordination civilo-militaire, les clusters, des groupes de travail et les mécanismes de coordination au niveau de terrain.
Le projet vise aussi à assurer le plaidoyer humanitaire à travers l’analyse des besoins faites par l’ensemble de la communauté humanitaire et ses partenaires en vue une compréhension commune des problématiques auxquels fait face le Tchad, ses causes profondes, l’impact sur les populations. OCHA jouera un rôle clé dans la création d'espaces de collection et d'analyse et gestion d’informations, pour assurer une stratégie de réponse coordonnée menant à des actions humanitaires répondant aux besoins les plus aigus et être mieux préparé face aux urgences soudaines. Le projet permettra également d’assurer conjointement avec la communauté humanitaire le plaidoyer en faveur du respect des principes humanitaires, de la protection des civils, de l'accès humanitaire et pour la mobilisation et l'allocation efficace de ressources humanitaires.
Un accent a été mis sur la mise en œuvre des plans d’action de la redevabilité envers les populations affectées (AAP), la PSEA et la préparation aux urgences en plus d'intégrer une attention au genre et de renforcer la centralité de la protection.
Un plaidoyer pour plus de visibilité des résultats tangibles au niveau de la réponse facilitant la mobilisation de ressources pour les différentes crises au Tchad (mouvement de population – crise du Bassin du Lac Tchad, insécurité alimentaire et malnutrition, urgences sanitaires, catastrophes naturelles) est aussi défini comme une priorité dans ce projet.
OCHA continuera de jouer également un rôle moteur dans le renforcement du lien entre les acteurs humanitaires et de développement et la transformation de la réponse humanitaire, en lien avec les engagements pris au Sommet humanitaire mondial de 2016 et ceci à travers la nouvelle façon de travailler (NWOW) et le renforcement de l’utilisation de la modalité de transfert monétaire.

Dans le cadre de cette nouvelle façon de travailler outre l’opérationnalisation du nexus, le lien avec les objectifs commun des programmes développement, paix et sécurité sera mis en avant. L’accent est aussi mis sur le renforcement de la coordination civilo-militaire afin de faciliter l’accès et la protection des civils.
Le projet a pour but de renforcer la coordination d’une réponse humanitaire rapide et efficace afin de sauver des vies et protéger les personnes affectées par les situations de crises au Tchad. Une coordination humanitaire rapide et correctement évaluée au niveau des besoins de la population affectée permettra aux acteurs humanitaires de mieux identifier et répondre aux besoins humanitaires, de renforcer la préparation de réponse aux urgences à travers le renforcement des mécanismes de coordination et plus spécifiquement l‘Equipe humanitaire pays, la coordination inter-clusters, la coordination civilo-militaire, les clusters, des groupes de travail et les mécanismes de coordination au niveau de terrain.
Le projet vise aussi à assurer le plaidoyer humanitaire à travers l’analyse des besoins faites par l’ensemble de la communauté humanitaire et ses partenaires en vue une compréhension commune des problématiques auxquels fait face le Tchad, ses causes profondes, l’impact sur les populations. OCHA jouera un rôle clé dans la création d'espaces de collection et d'analyse et gestion d’informations, pour assurer une stratégie de réponse coordonnée menant à des actions humanitaires répondant aux besoins les plus aigus et être mieux préparé face aux urgences soudaines. Le projet permettra également d’assurer conjointement avec la communauté humanitaire le plaidoyer en faveur du respect des principes humanitaires, de la protection des civils, de l'accès humanitaire et pour la mobilisation et l'allocation efficace de ressources humanitaires.
Un accent a été mis sur la mise en œuvre des plans d’action de la redevabilité envers les populations affectées (AAP), la PSEA et la préparation aux urgences en plus d'intégrer une attention au genre et de renforcer la centralité de la protection.
Un plaidoyer pour plus de visibilité des résultats tangibles au niveau de la réponse facilitant la mobilisation de ressources pour les différentes crises au Tchad (mouvement de population – crise du Bassin du Lac Tchad, insécurité alimentaire et malnutrition, urgences sanitaires, catastrophes naturelles) est aussi défini comme une priorité dans ce projet.
OCHA continuera de jouer également un rôle moteur dans le renforcement du lien entre les acteurs humanitaires et de développement et la transformation de la réponse humanitaire, en lien avec les engagements pris au Sommet humanitaire mondial de 2016 et ceci à travers la nouvelle façon de travailler (NWOW) et le renforcement de l’utilisation de la modalité de transfert monétaire.

project_text:
Gender-based Violence (GBV) Prevention and Response for Conflict-Affected Population in South Sudan 
The GBV prevention and response program of International Medical Corps (IMC) in South Sudan aims to empower communities and build resilience through promoting social and behavioral change to address the root causes of GBV in the country. The project targets key population to create a sustainable change in attitude and practices through male engagement, working with community leaders and building capacity of local stakeholders. Leveraging on the vast experiences, gains, and successes of IMC in implementing GBV prevention and response interventions through the FCDO-HARISS program, this project will be continued to implement in the states of Western Bahr el Ghazal (Wau IDP Camp and County), Upper Nile and Malakal PoC and County), Unity (Nyal County), and in Canal/Pigi County. It will directly benefit about 27495 vulnerable women and girls across the target locations. One of the project’s key priorities is to further strengthen core services to survivors of GBV and other vulnerable women and girls in the aforesaid intervention sites. These services include quality case management using a survivor-centered approach, along with psychosocial support to enhance healing and recovery. IMC UK works to ensure that survivors’ holistic needs are met by providing multi-sectoral services, referring to health centers for clinical management of rape, to legal justice services and to other kinds of support based on the needs of survivors. In addition to individual PSS for survivors, IMC UK will continue with PSS group activities for all vulnerable women and girls in the women girls’ safe spaces (WGSS). To ensure sustainability of the project and ownership by the community, especially of the WGSSs, in Wau, Nyal and Malakal, IMC already established, leadership committee comprise of 8 members from the community selected by their fellow women with the responsibility to give support, information, feedback, and suggestions that will foster empowerment and ownership of the space and the overall wellbeing of their members. The women committee members will be further empowered with knowledge and skills through hands-on management of the spaces and co-leading with them on the daily functioning of the WGSS. The women committee will be continuously mentored and trained on GBV basic concepts, safe referral, and referral pathways, and on leadership and conflict management and facilitation techniques and on various psychosocial support activities using IMC’s and IRC’s global WGSS toolkit. IMC UK will implement holistic community engagement strategies on the promotion of long-term positive change in the targeted communities. IMC will use the GBV community mobilization tool called SASA! - Phase-based strategy to help communities rethink about “power” and the positive use of power. “Preventing Violence against Women and Girls: Engaging Men in Accountable Practice (EMAP)” is also another tool that will be used to ensure men engagement with accountability to prevent GBV in the targeted community in Nyal, Wau and Malakal. In addition, IMC trains and collaborates with GBV Taskforce members in Wau, Malakal and Nyal. These will be supported by staff IMC UK staff to do awareness raising, and safe confidential referral of any survivors who disclose to them. IMC UK will provide emergency cash assistance for case management to the vulnerable women and girls. Cash assistance is one of the interagency minimum standards in GBV programming in emergency (Standard 11: Dignity Kits, Cash Assistance). In addition to this, IMC UK opts to implement cash assistance based on lesson learnt and feedback from women and girls on importance of cash assistance as lifesaving; for example, it can help a survivor meet the costs associated with fleeing an abusive relationship (e.g., rent, temporary shelter, transportation, food, clothing, etc).

project_text: Food and livelihood assistance to the most vulnerable and crisis affected population in South Sudan The proposed project aims to provide food assistance, livelihood and resilience support to 1,105,380 vulnerable populations in Upper Nile, Western Equatoria, Central Equatoria and Greater Bahr el Ghazal. The project will implement activities that will prevent famine and improve food consumption, dietary diversity and coping strategies of target beneficiaries in IPC 5, 4 and 3. The project will also seek to enhance emergency food production and contribute to the reduction of dependency to food and agricultural inputs. World Vision will adopt a mix of intervention approaches including but not limited to unconditional and General Food Distribution, cash transfers, complementary livelihood support, capacity building (e.g., modern agronomic practices, Integrated Pest Management, Natural Resource Management, etc.), and resilience building at the household level. The proposed project will also be implemented in synergy with other sectors implemented by World Vision in the targeted locations such as health, nutrition, WASH, gender and protection related programming while maintaining coordinating and complementarity with the efforts of other humanitarian actors and line ministries. In order to reach the target beneficiaries with prioritized cluster objectives, World Vision South Sudan proposed a total of $4,512,952 US project budget for 2022.

project_text: Comprehensive WASH response to affected children and displaced families in the South West and Littoral Regions of Cameroon The socio-political crisis in the NW and SW regions of Cameroon, now in its sixth year, characterized by continued fighting between State security forces (SSF) and non-State armed groups (NSAG, targeted attacks, destruction of property, arbitrary arrest, kidnappings for ransom, extortion of money and continued use of improvised explosive devices (IEDs) (OCHA, 2022), has left more than 1.08 million people from NW, SW, LIT and West region in need of humanitarian assistance (HNO, 2022). More especially, the insufficient investment of Cameroon Government in basic social services, poverty and limited response provided by Humanitarian actor in the Northwest and South west regions continue to exacerbate the water and sanitation need of affected population including neighboring regions (Littoral and West regions). The crisis has had serious negative effects on water, hygiene and sanitation with mostly children, women and girls highly affected, as they are the ones who often access WASH facilities. The situation further compounded with the public health crisis of COVID 19, cholera outbreak and monkey pox which have hit the already crisis affected communities. In September 2022 SitRep, Out of 12 517 cases and 254 deaths reported at national level, the South-West region represent 48% of cases (6017) and 36% (93) of deaths, marking 2022 as the second most affected year by cholera for the past 25 years with more than 13,000 cases and 284 deaths of cholera reported (HNO, 2023). The risk factors are still much evident in these affected regions such as lack safe of access to safe water, sanitation facilities (latrines) and poor hygiene practices that poses a thread to the lives of these vulnerable children and displaced families. It is therefore the responsibility of humanitarian actors and service providers to scale up humanitarian response and delivery of life saving humanitarian needs and services to the affected persons in most insecure and inaccessible locations. It is within this framework that this project in its response will prioritize the safety and dignity of the targeted children, women and girls, as well as affected host population and will reduce the risk and exposure to gender-based violence and other violence related to accessing WASH facilities. Our project will provide WASH humanitarian assistance through all modalities with specificity to 6500 individuals directly utilizing improve water supply service with systematic control of water quality at household level, 1750 households will directly utilize improve sanitation facilities through the support and construction of Eco-friendly boifil latrines, and the provision of latrine kits to displaced families and vulnerable host communities. 15,625 Individuals reached with community sensitization messaging on critical handwashing and good hygiene practices through information and communication materials, door-to-door and cholera tools to efficiently address cholera risk factors and other possible outbreaks associated to poor hygiene practices. 18750 individuals will benefits complete WASH kits through all modalities, 1875 vulnerable adolescent girls and women within reproductive age will be reached with menstrual hygiene kits. 600 beneficiaries will be trained on how to access humanitarian assistance as well as capacitated on how to provide feedback and complains to humanitarian actors. The adoption of community based approached will be the central response strategy through consultation and engagements of all relevant stakeholders and community groups for an impactful, dignify and sustainable WASH service delivery to the vulnerable affected population. For a more responsible intervention that respect the dignity of beneficiaries, the project will mainstream accountability to affected population (AAP) within the response from project inception to the exit strategy and ensure humanitarian principle are respected at all stage of the intervention.

project_text:
Renforcement de la coordination et du plaidoyer humanitaire au Tchad Le projet vise à renforcer le rôle de OCHA dans la mise en œuvre de son mandat et son rôle auprès des partenaires humanitaires et gouvernementaux au niveau des fonctions coordination, gestion de l’information et plaidoyer. Le bureau national d’OCHA à N’Djaména et ses trois sous-bureaux régionaux à l’Est (Abéché) au Sud (Goré) et la province du Lac (Baga Sola) mettent l’accent sur l’opérationnalisation de ses fonctions y compris en assurant un lien entre les activités humanitaires et de développement (nexus) en vue de promouvoir une solution durable visant à ne pas perpétuer une situation de dépendance humanitaire. Dans le cadre de cette nouvelle façon de travailler outre l’opérationnalisation du nexus, le lien avec les objectifs commun des programmes développement, paix et sécurité sera mis en avant. L’accent est aussi mis sur le renforcement de la coordination civilo-militaire afin de faciliter l’accès et la protection des civils.
Le projet a pour but de renforcer la coordination d’une réponse humanitaire rapide et efficace afin de sauver des vies et protéger les personnes affectées par les situations de crises au Tchad. Une coordination humanitaire rapide et correctement évaluée au niveau des besoins de la population affectée permettra aux acteurs humanitaires de mieux identifier et répondre aux besoins humanitaires, de renforcer la préparation de réponse aux urgences à travers le renforcement des mécanismes de coordination et plus spécifiquement l‘Equipe humanitaire pays, la coordination inter-clusters, la coordination civilo-militaire, les clusters, des groupes de travail et les mécanismes de coordination au niveau de terrain.
Le projet vise aussi à assurer le plaidoyer humanitaire à travers l’analyse des besoins faites par l’ensemble de la communauté humanitaire et ses partenaires en vue une compréhension commune des problématiques auxquels fait face le Tchad, ses causes profondes, l’impact sur les populations. OCHA jouera un rôle clé dans la création d'espaces de collection et d'analyse et gestion d’informations, pour assurer une stratégie de réponse coordonnée menant à des actions humanitaires répondant aux besoins les plus aigus et être mieux préparé face aux urgences soudaines. Le projet permettra également d’assurer conjointement avec la communauté humanitaire le plaidoyer en faveur du respect des principes humanitaires, de la protection des civils, de l'accès humanitaire et pour la mobilisation et l'allocation efficace de ressources humanitaires.
Un accent a été mis sur la mise en œuvre des plans d’action de la redevabilité envers les populations affectées (AAP), la PSEA et la préparation aux urgences en plus d'intégrer une attention au genre et de renforcer la centralité de la protection.
Un plaidoyer pour plus de visibilité des résultats tangibles au niveau de la réponse facilitant la mobilisation de ressources pour les différentes crises au Tchad (mouvement de population – crise du Bassin du Lac Tchad, insécurité alimentaire et malnutrition, urgences sanitaires, catastrophes naturelles) est aussi défini comme une priorité dans ce projet.
OCHA continuera de jouer également un rôle moteur dans le renforcement du lien entre les acteurs humanitaires et de développement et la transformation de la réponse humanitaire, en lien avec les engagements pris au Sommet humanitaire mondial de 2016 et ceci à travers la nouvelle façon de travailler (NWOW) et le renforcement de l’utilisation de la modalité de transfert monétaire.

project_text:
Food assistance to address increasing levels of severe food insecurity in South Sudan Meet the lifesaving food requirements of people in South Sudan who are facing food security crises, including those living in (ex)-POCs and IDP and those otherwise affected by conflict, natural disaster and/or seasonal food insecurity. WFP will provide general food distributions (GFD) to the most food insecure people in South Sudan. At the field level, food assistance will be overseen by the WFP Field Offices and implemented by NGO partners or provided through the Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM). WFP provides food assistance and common services through a comprehensive and collaborative humanitarian intervention by deploying mobile teams, supported by cooperating partners to reach populations facing the most urgent needs in the most inaccessible areas of the South Sudan, subject to the availability of resources.
Complementary to food distributions, WFP will seek to offer value-added solutions (light resilience- building activities, peace/conflict resolution training also called GFD+), in response to needs and priorities identified by the community. Through GFD+, WFP together with its cooperating partners and other stakeholders will provide unconditional opportunities, identified through a community-based, people-centric participatory approach to targeted beneficiaries. GFD+ adds value to emergency food assistance with a focus on solutions that address the root causes of food and nutrition insecurity and better equip beneficiaries to fight hunger. The GFD+ activity type, duration, frequency, and participation will be catered to specific local sites and may range from COVID-19 awareness, training, or sensitisation on peaceful resolution of conflicts, mitigation measures to nutrition education, dyke rehabilitation and communal asset management, income-generating activities which lead to women's economic empowerment and have positive impact on household food security, or other solutions. WFP will also implement resilience building activities including Food Assistance for Assets (FFA) to support communities to improve their food security, restore their livelihoods, strengthen their resilience to shocks and build self-reliance, while contributing to peace. 
Mitigation measures to reduce and prevent the potential the spread of COVID-19, including new variants, and other potential viral outbreaks have been incorporated into standard operating procedures for all interactions with beneficiaries, including training of partners and stakeholders, increasing general awareness among partners and beneficiaries, enforcing social distancing, promoting handwashing, disinfecting sites, reducing the frequency of distribution cycles, and mandating the utilization of personal protective equipment (PPE). These measures are mainstreamed into all WFP activities.
