destinationObjects_Project.name: Améliorer la sécurité alimentaire et restaurer les moyens de subsistance agro-pastoraux des populations vulnérables hôtes et déplacées dans les régions de Tahoua et Diffa touchées par les crises sécuritaire et climatique
reportDetails_organization: European Commission's Humanitarian Aid and Civil Protection Department
project_text:
Améliorer la sécurité alimentaire et restaurer les moyens de subsistance agro-pastoraux des populations vulnérables hôtes et déplacées dans les régions de Tahoua et Diffa touchées par les crises sécuritaire et climatique L’objectif général du projet est d’améliorer la sécurité alimentaire et de renforcer les moyens d’existence et la résilience des populations déplacées et hôtes, affectées par les crises sécuritaires dans les régions de Tahoua et de Diffa, en fournissant une assistance humanitaire et un support pour le renforcement des moyens d’existence aux communautés les plus touchées par les crises sécuritaires, les déficits pluviométriques et les faibles productions agricoles et pastorales en 2021. 
L’Action répondra aux besoins alimentaires immédiats des ménages vulnérables pendant les périodes critiques (pré soudure et soudure pastorale et agricole) et soutiendra les principaux moyens d’existence des ménages les plus vulnérables. Elle ciblera les localités agro-pastorales et pastorales des départements de Diffa, Nguigmi, dans la région de Diffa, et le département de Tilia, région de Tahoua, les plus affectées par les crises sécuritaires (nombre de déplacés, taux d’insécurité alimentaire et nutritionnelle) et climatiques (déficit agricoles et pastoraux). Les activités bénéficieront directement à 5 600 ménages (39 200 personnes) déplacés, hôtes, identifiés comme les plus vulnérables selon une approche de ciblage participative (Household Economy Approach) impliquant les communautés, les services techniques, les autorités locales, les partenaires locaux, et les organisations paysannes.

Dans le cadre de cette intervention, le premier axe d'intervention sera la réponse aux besoins urgents de sécurité alimentaire des ménages les plus vulnérables des départements de Diffa, Nguigmi (Diffa) et Tillia (Tahoua) par une assistance alimentaire sous forme de Cash for Work. Les transferts d'argent liquide permettront aux bénéficiaires d'avoir accès à une nourriture de qualité et ainsi de faire face à l'insécurité alimentaire aiguë. En effet, selon tous les acteurs rencontrés (services techniques, autorités locales, partenaires locaux et communautés) lors de l'évaluation interne des interventions FSLH de Diffa réalisée par ACF, le changement le plus significatif apporté par les activités CFW a été l'amélioration de la situation alimentaire des ménages grâce à l'augmentation du nombre de repas (jusqu'à 3 repas par jour), et l'augmentation de la durée des stocks alimentaires des ménages. Au niveau de Tillia, l'évaluation des besoins menée par ACF a montré que le besoin d'assistance alimentaire était l'un des besoins prioritaires cités par les communautés, en particulier parmi les personnes déplacées.
Le deuxième domaine d'intervention consistera à protéger et à renforcer les moyens de subsistance des populations les plus touchées dans les zones ciblées.  Les activités prévues sont basées sur les principaux moyens de subsistance des populations. L'agriculture (32,5% des ménages bénéficiaires), le petit commerce (31,7%) et l'élevage (19,9%) constituent les trois (3) principales activités des bénéficiaires (source : ACF, précédents projets).  Au niveau de Tillia, l'activité principale reste l'élevage et la zone a une vocation pastorale selon la classification du gouvernement du Niger. Ainsi, les activités s'articuleront autour de la restauration et du renforcement du patrimoine pastoral des communautés du département. Afin de renforcer les activités agricoles des bénéficiaires à Diffa, un soutien sera apporté à la culture maraîchère et à l'agriculture pluviale.

reportDetails_organization: European Commission's Humanitarian Aid and Civil Protection Department
project_text:
Fortalecimiento de capacidades de respuesta comunitaria e institucional ante la ocurrencia de desastres naturales y de origen antrópico en los estados Trujillo y Mérida El proyecto tiene por objeto disminuir la vulnerabilidad y fortalecer las capacidades de recuperación y la resiliencia de las personas afectadas por grupo de edad, género y diversidad en comunidades vulnerables ante eventos adversos de origen natural y antrópico en los estados Trujillo (municipio Urdaneta) y  Mérida (municipios Tovar y Pinto Salinas). 
Las zonas objeto de intervención son frecuentemente impactadas con inundaciones, crecidas torrenciales y  movimientos en masa producto de las características topográficas de la región, la inestabilidad geológica,  las frecuentes  lluvias y el impacto del cambio climático en la zona, el periodo de retorno de eventos con importantes consecuencias parece reducirse según investigaciones recientes de la Universidad de Los Andes y análisis hechos por los organismos de seguridad del estado, como protección civil. 
El último evento ocurrió en agosto del año 2021 y aún  se encuentran en  espacios de alojamiento temporal 80 familias afectadas para quienes, en el corto plazo, no se vislumbran alternativas de reubicación, según datos aportados por las autoridades locales.  Estas personas requieren de un apoyo inmediato con enfoque intersectorial, que incluya atención psicosocial, jornadas de salud (adultos, pediátrica y ginecobstétrica), entrega de kits de enseres e higiene que incluyan insumos para la higiene menstrual y   la implementación de un programa de formación  para el emprendimiento  que facilite  el empoderamiento económico de las mujeres cabeza de familia que han sido afectadas. 
Tomando en cuenta el nexo entre actividades humanitarias y de desarrollo, dadas las características de las zonas de intervención y sus  antecedentes, en función de mitigar el impacto en vidas humanas  y contribuir a  mejorar el restablecimiento de medios de vida, mantenimiento y protección de los hogares,  se prevé la capacitación para la gestión del riesgo y el fortalecimiento de la capacidad de respuesta de los habitantes de  5 comunidades vulnerables de los referidos municipios, así como la transversalización  del conocimiento de la gestión del riesgo mediante la formación  a docentes en tres escuelas. 
Asimismo, se hará  la identificación del riesgo y preparación para la respuesta en emergencia de los hospitales de Tovar y  Santa Cruz de Mora y el ambulatorio de Quebrada de Cueva en el municipio Urdaneta de Trujillo, con la capacitación del talento humano y la instalación de sistemas fotovoltaicos que  garanticen la atención en áreas vitales de estos centros de salud en momentos de emergencia.

project_text:
Fortalecimiento de la SAN y la resiliencia de las comunidades vulnerables, a través de un modelo de Alimentación Escolar saludable proveniente de la Agricultura Familiar local. La persistencia de la crisis económica y política en Venezuela durante los últimos años ha colocado a una parte importante de su población en situación de extrema precariedad. Las interrupciones de las actividades educativas y la cadena de suministro de alimentos locales debido a la pandemia COVID-19, ha afectado profundamente la oportunidad de la población vulnerable, incluidos niños en edad escolar y familias productoras, de acceder a alimentos esenciales y a insumos productivos que fortalezcan su SAN, respectivamente. 
En este sentido, durante el periodo 2020-2021, la cobertura del Programa de Alimentación Escolar (PAE) ha tenido deficiencia en frecuencia, ingesta nutricional y dieta equilibrada para no menos de 4.5 millones de niños y se estima que alrededor de 1.1 millones corren el riego de abandonar la Escuela. Al mismo tiempo, la disminución continua de la producción local de alimentos se agrava por el limitado acceso a insumos agrícolas esenciales -como semillas con calidad- por parte de los pequeños productores, agravando la inseguridad alimentaria y financiera preexistente en las comunidades.
Por lo anterior expuesto, la presente acción tiene como propósito principal el de mejorar la SAN de niños y niñas en edad escolar, además de los hogares rurales en situación de vulnerabilidad, esto, mediante el desarrollo de modelos de Alimentación Escolar basados en la producción local que FAO y UNICEF han pilotado y validad en cuatro estados del país. Complementariamente, la acción promoverá esquemas comunitarios de producción variada de semillas de forma artesanal, adaptadas climáticamente y que respetan la cultura y saberes locales productivos. 
Bajo este objetivo, se propone el desarrollo de los siguientes componentes:
PRODUCTO 1: Fortalecido el modelo de Alimentación Escolar basado en la producción local de la Agricultura Familiar (AF): A través de rehabilitar y/o mejorar las capacidades productivas de las Escuelas Técnicas Agrícolas (ETA) y Asociación Local de Productores (ALP) incrementando su productividad aplicando prácticas agroecológicas para producción de alimentos, huevos y semillas, además desarrollando acciones de asistencia técnica. Se espera que, con la disponibilidad de una producción local de huevos, hortalizas y frutas, se logre fomentar modelos alimentarios de circuito corto, saludables y sostenibles, en donde los niños y niñas de edad escolar en situación de vulnerabilidad - y de manera indirecta el de familias vulnerables de agricultores de pequeña escala - mejoran el consumo de alimentos diversificados, frescos y nutritivos.
PRODUCTO 2: Mejorado el acceso a semillas con calidad, por parte de los pequeños productores familiares locales; a través de una implementación de un modelo de producción de semillas comunitario, sostenibles y resilientes. En este modelo, las ETA jugarán un rol de motor de producción y difusión de conocimiento y los productores a través de las ALP, serán el factor de escalamiento de la capacidad de producción y accesibilidad de la semillas para los demás productores
Para la implementación del proyecto se han priorizado estados con población indígena y, cuando sea posible, se dará la prioridad de participación a agricultoras y agricultores indígenas y a mujeres líderes de hogar, en los estados Amazonas, Sucre, Monagas, Falcon, Zulia, Delta Amacuro, Bolívar y Apure. La acción espera dar cobertura a alrededor de 13 750 hogares de pequeños productores y productoras, aglutinando alrededor de 450 grupos productivos y/o Bancos de Semillas Comunitarios, que contribuyan a la protección y acumulación de sus medios de vida productivos esenciales y en conjunto con 50 ETAs y 25 escuelas de educación básica y primaria, puedan abastecer complementos alimentarios frescos y sanos para alrededor 27 000 niños y niñas en edad escolar.

destinationObjects_Project.name: Food assistance to address increasing levels of severe food insecurity in South Sudan
reportDetails_organization: European Commission's Humanitarian Aid and Civil Protection Department
project_text:
Food assistance to address increasing levels of severe food insecurity in South Sudan Meet the lifesaving food requirements of people in South Sudan who are facing food security crises, including those living in (ex)-POCs and IDP and those otherwise affected by conflict, natural disaster and/or seasonal food insecurity. WFP will provide general food distributions (GFD) to the most food insecure people in South Sudan. At the field level, food assistance will be overseen by the WFP Field Offices and implemented by NGO partners or provided through the Integrated Rapid Response Mechanism (IRRM). IRRM is a Delivering as One approach, in which UNICEF supports WASH and nutrition activities, FAO provides emergency seeds and livelihood kits, and WFP provides food assistance and common services through a comprehensive and collaborative humanitarian intervention by deploying mobile teams, supported by cooperating partners to reach populations facing the most urgent needs in the most inaccessible areas of the South Sudan, subject to the availability of resources.

Complementary to food distributions, WFP will seek to offer value-added solutions (GFD+), in response to needs and priorities identified by the community. Through GFD+, WFP together with its cooperating partners and other stakeholders will provide unconditional opportunities, identified through a community-based, people-centric participatory approach to targeted beneficiaries. GFD+ adds value to emergency food assistance with a focus on solutions that address the root causes of food and nutrition insecurity and better equip beneficiaries to fight hunger. The GFD+ activity type, duration, frequency, and participation will be catered to specific local sites and may range from COVID-19 awareness and mitigation measures to nutrition education, dyke rehabilitation and communal asset management, income-generating activities which lead to women's economic empowerment and have positive impact on household food security, or other solutions. WFP will also implement resilience building activities including Food Assistance for Assets (FFA) to support communities to improve their food security, restore their livelihoods, strengthen their resilience to shocks and build self-reliance, while contributing to peace.

Mitigation measures to reduce and prevent the potential the spread of COVID-19, including new variants, and other potential viral outbreaks have been incorporated into standard operating procedures for all interactions with beneficiaries, including training of partners and stakeholders, increasing general awareness among partners and beneficiaries, enforcing social distancing, promoting handwashing, disinfecting sites, reducing the frequency of distribution cycles, and mandating the utilization of personal protective equipment (PPE). These measures are mainstreamed into all WFP activities and are part of the ‘new way of working’.

project_text:
WFP SOMALIA 2022 HRP - FSC Somalia has been impacted by multiple shocks in 2020, including desert locust invasion, flash floods and COVID-19. This has negatively affected the ability of vulnerable households to meet their food security needs. The urban poor, including IDP households, have been disproportionally affected due to the socio-economic effects from COVID-19 due their heavy reliance on food purchases from the market and casual labor as the main sources of income. These households are likely to face food consumption gaps due to declines in employment and income-earning opportunities. The desert locust caused significant damage to cereal crops, fruits, vegetables and pasture in the northern and central regions. Control efforts of the government and partners in Somaliland and Puntland made progress, but an increasing number of adult locust groups was reported in central regions. In addition, in the northeast, remained swarms have matured, and some have moved towards central areas. As per FAO, the hatching and band formation is occurring now and more swarms are likely to move to other areas in central Somalia and at later stages are expected to move towards crop producing areas in the south; which can have some negative impact to the crops and pasture up to early next year.

The impact of localized flooding particularly in riverine areas destroyed farmland and crops and caused population displacement, leading to significant crop losses and the loss of income from agricultural employment.

Jointly with the Government and other humanitarian actors, WFP Somalia has supported communities and vulnerable houses impacted by the multiple shocks. The high levels of sustained humanitarian assistance in 2020 have played a critical role in stabilizing the situation. The immediate food security outlook for Somalia however looks bleak despite the efforts sustained in 2020. According to the latest Post-Gu Assessment, 2.1 million people are expected to be food insecure (IPC 3 and 4) across Somalia through December 2020. An additional 3 million people are expected to be Stressed (IPC 2), bringing the total number of people facing cute food insecurity to 5.1 million until the end of this year. Based on results of the 2020 Post Gu assessment, an estimated 849,900 children under the age of five years face acute malnutrition between September 2020 and August 2021, including 143,400 likely to be severely malnourished.

project_text:
Provision of integrated, equitable, and timely WASH services to emergency affected populations in South Sudan Protracted crises in South Sudan, including climactic shocks and continued conflict, have resulted in 8.9 million people projected to be in need of humanitarian assistance in 2022. As a result of the shocks, such as flooding, inter-communal violence (ICV) and ongoing armed clashes, the majority of the population are facing increased food insecurity, lack of access to basic services, and protection risks. As per the Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) 2022, lack of or inadequate access to clean water and improved sanitation and hygiene practices in South Sudan will negatively impact an estimated 6.1 million people in 2022. 

Since 2006, Solidarites International has become a key WASH actor in South Sudan, implementing emergency lifesaving responses across the country and providing integrated WASH services to crisis-affected populations in areas of static presence in Upper Nile, Jonglei, and Western Bahr el Ghazal. Since 2012 SI has played a key role in the Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPR) strategy in South Sudan, implementing multi-sectoral assessments and delivering emergency responses to crisis-affected populations all over the country. 

In 2022, SI will continue to provide emergency live-saving  WASH responses across the South Sudan to restore basic access to safe water, hygiene, and sanitation while ensuring equitable access, safety, and accountability to supported populations. Through its roving Emergency Preparedness and Response (EPR) team, SI will deploy to emergency-affected locations to provide first phase and second phase responses including distribution of household water treatment items and soap, emergency provision of safe water, and rapid repair of emergency-affected infrastructure.

At the same time, SI will expand its presence in Upper Nile, Unity and Jonglei to provide basic integrated WASH services that target the most vulnerable, including those suffering malnutrition, food insecurity and protection threats (including GBV survivors). Static programs will focus on providing community-based solutions for sustainable WASH services that ensure that improvements in access to safe water, sanitation, and hygiene are durable and can be maintained independently by communities. Engagement and joint programming with Protection and Nutrition actors will ensure that WASH services can be accessed by the most vulnerable and will have a tangible impact on reducing overall priority humanitarian needs. The increased integration of protection, inclusion, and conflict sensitivity analysis in all programming will ensure that WASH services and resources can be safely accessed by all in the community. Greater engagement of communities and local markets will support the design of long term and flood resistant WASH infrastructure and supply chains to ensure that interventions produce durable results for communities.

reportDetails_organization: European Commission's Humanitarian Aid and Civil Protection Department
project_text:
Respuesta multisectorial humanitaria en Venezuela En Venezuela, DRC busca proporcionar asistencia humanitaria a poblaciones vulnerables y afectadas por la crisis actual como son las consecuencias socioeconómicas de la pandemia del COVID-19, de los flujos migratorios mixtos hacia fuera de Venezuela y de las problemáticas fronterizas relacionados a actividades ilícitas y conflictos de grupos armados que vive la población que reside en Venezuela, tales como desplazamientos y/o confinamientos masivos. Por medio de una intervención multisectorial, DRC brindará asistencia de emergencia con un enfoque de protección tanto para refugiados en Venezuela, venezolanos con la intención de migrar, venezolanos retornados, desplazados internos y a población de acogida afectada, aplicando de manera transversal un enfoque sensible a la edad, el género y la discapacidad para llegar a un total de 21,288 personas vulnerables. Los perfiles priorizados por DRC serán aquellos que presenten altos niveles de vulnerabilidad como lo son las personas con necesidades específicas de protección (NNA, mujeres, LGBTI, ancianos, etc.), personas con discapacidad, sobrevivientes o personas en riesgo de violencia basada en género, víctimas de desplazamiento masivo o confinamiento, grupos indígenas entre otros. Este proyecto será implementado en todas las regiones en las cuales DRC trabaja en Venezuela, que, al mismo tiempo, son zonas de mayor proporción de necesidades humanitarias severas de acuerdo con el HRP 2022/23: Zulia, Sucre y Apure. Esta acción tiene como objetivo ofrecer una intervención de protección integrada que combina la protección y asistencia de emergencia para mejorar las condiciones de las poblaciones vulnerables antes mencionadas. 
La acción propuesta incluye los siguientes sectores/actividades: Coordinación, Protección, Seguridad Alimentaria, Salud, Agua, saneamiento e higiene y Educación. El presente proyecto tendrá como línea de intervención principal, el abordaje de las necesidades de protección encontradas en una evaluación de campo llevada a cabo en noviembre del 2021 en los estados de Sucre (municipios de Arismendi, Cajigal, Mariño y Valdés), Zulia (municipios de Maracaibo, Rosario de Perijá, Machiques de Perijá, Páez) y Apure (municipio Páez) y como líneas complementarias a los sectores de salud, WASH, educación y seguridad alimentaria. Es por ello que DRC plantea una respuesta integral no solo a necesidades de  protección como son, el acceso a información, asistencia legal y acceso a documentación para población vulnerable, incluidas las personas sobrevivientes y en riesgo de VbG,  el acceso a asistencia individualizada y especifica de protección y prevención de trata sino también a cubrir necesidades básicas de seguridad alimentaria;  mediante distribuciones mensuales de kits familiares alimenticios por 10 meses en las zonas de intervención, salud; con la rehabilitación de centros médicos seleccionados y educación; proveyendo suministros escolares y de higiene personal y familiar, a través de una intervención multisectorial y previamente coordinada con autoridades y comunidades locales. Uno de los hallazgos de la evaluación de campo fue la falta de data relacionada a protección para poder producir análisis confiables, es por esto por lo que DRC plantea implementar un análisis de protección basado en evidencia a través de un monitoreo continuo de protección en las localidades de intervención, con la finalidad de tener información a tiempo para poder identificar riesgos y priorizar necesidades.

project_text: Emergency Shelter and Non-Food Items Response to Assist IDPs, Returnees and Host Communities affected by conflict or natural disaster in Western Equatoria, Upper Nile, and Warrap States, South Sudan.  The 2022 Humanitarian Needs Overview (HNO) indicates that ‘’approximately 2.4 million people in South Sudan continue to be impacted by the destruction of housing and loss of essential goods caused by ongoing flooding and conflict. In addition, nearly 329,000 refugees and asylum seekers also require shelter and non-food item (NFI) support. At the end of 2021, nearly 1.9 million men, women, boys, girls, and older people live in inadequate shelter, while a total of 2.3 million require NFIs. The number of people in need increased in 2022 due to the increased displacement of approximately 300,000 people in 2021 and the returns of nearly 270,000 from neighboring countries. The top three shelter/NFI-related needs are access to emergency shelter, NFIs and housing, land and property (HLP) rights to ensure security of tenure’’. With the budget of $700,000, this project will enable World Vision International South Sudan to serve 55,000 (17,500 men, 17,500 women; 10,000 boys, 10,000 girls) IDPs, returnees and host communities with in-kind emergency shelter and non-food items in the counties of Tambura, Nagero and Yambio in Western Equatoria State, Tonj North, Tonj East, Tonj South, Gogrial East, Gogriel West and Aweil South counties in Warrap State, Laukpiny/Nasir, Ulang Melut and Baliet counties of Upper Nile State. In areas with existing functional markets, 18 % of the targeted beneficiaries will be supported through unconditional but restricted modality of cash-based interventions. Beneficiaries for both in-kind SNFI and cash interventions will be identified during needs assessments, where methodologies like Focused Group Discussions (FGD), Key informants (KI), Observation will be deployed to collect data for decision making and before beneficiary registration and distribution missions. Post distribution missions would also be effected to get feedback from affected population. In the course of the project, WVISS team will continuously conduct community awareness meetings and workshops on issues like climate change, AAP, Covid-19 etc. The project would contribute to the two Cluster objectives; (1). Percentage of the targeted population are able to access shelter material and non-food items in situations of emergency and transition, (2). Enhance the community’s dignity by increasing their ability to respond to new shocks and building on existing skills. World Vision International South Sudan will implement the project in adherence with the SNFI cluster standards where the cluster coordination team is closely consulted on operations at national and sub-national levels. The organization will also collaborate with men, women, boys, girls, persons with special needs, government authorities and partners like UNHAS, UNOCHA, IOM/pipeline, local and international organizations to realize durable solutions for emergency shelter and non-food items. The affected populations will be encouraged to actively participate in the project through the mainstreaming of AAP (accountability to affected populations) approach into project activities. Existing local community structures would be strengthened to support the project and where they are non-existent, WVISS will facilitate the formation to enhance full participation of affected populations in area. The CFM, (Complaint Feedback Mechanism) will be introduced in each project site and community members would be sensitized on how to use it throughout the project period. The awareness creation sessions will be tailored to complement efforts for conflict mitigation, long-term solutions for floods, Sexual Exploitation and Abuse, Housing, Land & Property, and COVID-19 pandemic. WVISS will continue to respond through the mobile response mechanism by deploying teams in hard to access locations or where there is urgent need of intervention across the country based on SNFI request.

project_text:
Provide Lifesaving WASH Assistance to Vulnerable Populations in North West Syria NGO X proposes to provide lifesaving safe water to approximately 518,999 vulnerable individuals in Idleb Governorate and North Aleppo, Northwest Syria. This will be implemented via the provision of essential support to 37 Water Stations (WSs) that are currently functioning and 4 Water Units (WUs).
NGO X has extensive experience delivering water supply programming in Idleb since 2014. In 2022 NGO X provided clean safe water to the homes of over 800,000 people in Idleb via 51 WS and 12,190 people in North Aleppo via 2 water stations. 
The proposed project builds upon the experience of having successfully delivered several similar projects funded by OCHA, FCDO, ECHO and BHA. The aim of the action is to ensure access to reliable, safe, and clean drinking water to vulnerable conflict-affected communities and IDP sites including host and displaced populations in high priority northern sub-districts of Idleb Governorate and North Aleppo. 
Core activities under water supply sector will include procurement of electricity and/or fuel, minor infrastructure rehabilitation, training the water station operators, coaching of WUs and water quality monitoring. The proposed action will enable people living in the targeted areas to get enough clean and safe drinking water. Improving the access to safe water will reduce the time spent on collecting water, reduce protection risks and prevent the spread of waterborne diseases, often affecting children. Following WASH cluster standards, between 30 - 40 liters/person/day (LPD) will be piped directly to households (HH) to ensure equitable access for all community members. It should be noted that due to funding constraints and limited water network capacity, it may not be possible to go over 35 LPD. 
Under sanitation sub sector: the activities will include the rehabilitation of sewage infrastructure in 4 locations including IDP sites, through converting the open sewer system to closed sewer system in order to reduce the impact of open sewage system and to ensure the sustainability in the sanitation services.    
In addition to that NGO X proposes to implement infrastructure rehabilitation or improvement in targeted sites including roads / shelter rehabilitation to ensure complementarity, sustainability, and access to WASH facilities.
In target areas, to complement WASH activities, HHs—including school children, WU staff and vulnerable individuals benefiting from NGO X food or cash distributions will be reached with essential hygiene promotion sessions adapted to COVID-19 and cholera best working practices as outlined by the WASH cluster. Themes covered will include water safety, water conservation, COVID-19, cholera prevention and safe hygiene practices.

project_text:
Emergency Child Protection, GBV & Mine Action: Prevention, Mitigation & Response to assist IDPs, Returnees and Host Communities in conflict-affected & high risk areas of Warrap, Upper Nile, Western Equatoria and Central Equatoria States, South Sudan  The already high needs of critical child protection services in South Sudan has been exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, protracted displacement, and limited access to basic services which continues to significantly affect the physical, mental, and social well-being of children, adolescents and caregivers. This situation has been worsened by the limited availability of mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) services and the low level of core child protection services, including family tracing and reunification, case management, and reintegration services for children affected by armed forces and groups, leaving many children untreated and unable to access the needed services. Climate shocks, severe drought, massive flooding, and conflicts have contributed to the increase in GBV risks in the country which requires to strengthen GBV case management, psychosocial support, legal service, livelihood, economic support, GBV referral pathways and to integrate GBV into other sectoral responses. The high contamination with landmines and explosive remnants of war (ERW), especially in the Greater Equatoria region, along major supply routes and areas for returnees from Uganda, and the increase in expected returns require to prevent, mitigate and respond to mine risk issues through enhanced preparedness and resilience.
This proposed integrated CP, GBV and EORE project is in line with the Protection Cluster Objectives and will ensure the provision of critical protection-related assistance and specialized services and the prevention and mitigation of Protection risks through enhanced preparedness. The project targets to reach an average of 60,000 (20,000 women, 20,000 men, 10,000 girls, 10,000 men) (CP), 50,000 (20,000 women, 10,000 men, 10,000 girls, 10,000 boys) (GBV) and 20,000 (5000 men, 5000 women, 5000 girls, 5000 boys) (MA) including people with disabilities.
Using the 2023 Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP), World Vision International South Sudan (WVI-SS) aims to reach the most vulnerable populations in 11 counties in Warrap, Upper Nile, Western Equatoria and Central Equatoria States with improved access to quality lifesaving child protection for vulnerable girls, boys, men and women including children with disabilities who are at risk of mortality and morbidity and protection incidents/threats. Through the provision of specialized / lifesaving child protection and multi sectoral services WVI-SS seeks to reduce the suffering of boys, girls, women and men including children with disabilities who are at risk or experience violence, abuse, exploitation and neglect including GBV.
The proposed project will reduce the suffering of GBV survivors including women, men, girls, boys and people with disabilities by providing multi-sectoral specialized GBV response services. Furthermore, WVI-SS seeks to ensure that vulnerable women, men, girls, boys including people with disabilities have improved access to the provision of GBV prevention and risk mitigation interventions. Through protection monitoring, advocacy, awareness-raising and prevention and response services the project aims to reduce the vulnerability of women, men, girls and boys including people with disabilities at increased risk of mortality and morbidity and protection incidents/threats in priority areas.
In line with the Core Humanitarian Standards, WVI-SS will maintain its commitment to engage with affected communities at all phases of the project cycle, through focus group discussions with women, men, boys and girls. Establishing/strengthening local structures such as Project Management Committee is one example of how WVI-SS engages the community in a sustainable and accountable manner to determine and support appropriate need-based responses. WVI's Quality Assurance framework ensures that each project implemented is carried out effectively and continually reviewed in line with community needs and in line with other humanitarian frameworks.

project_text:
Fostering Resilience through Early Recovery response for the most Crisis impacted Communities in Syria The Integrated Response for Resilience Programme aims at providing a comprehensive response through Early Recovery support in 80 communities impacted by the crisis. Communities, particularly  those most dramatically affected – and under additional stress because of IDPs returns and other displacements - need  assistance in reinforcing their resilience to address these shocks as well as the consequences of the protracted crisis, and to address their needs on seriously depleted infrastructures and service capacities.
The essence of the Programme is about providing Syrian communities with – still limited - support to regain  control  over their basic needs (livelihoods, access to essential services) and reduce their dependency on humanitarian assistance. Prioritization of locations, is the outcome of a context analysis and needs assessment conducted on more than  5,000
Syrian communities, based on the following three criteria:
1) Hard to Reach  Areas
2) Areas of major IDPs presence and IDPs returns
3) Highest scoring in the Severity Scale
The integrated response consists of the following components: strengthening of social services-related capacities (access and coverage), livelihoods creation and rural recovery, PWDs support, social cohesion/community safety, reducing gender inequality  and youth marginality, women empowerment, tensions reduction and rehabilitation of basic infrastructure and public services.
The program is built in a modular manner both in terms of geographical and sectoral/thematic interventions and foresees the allotment of average 1 Million US$ per community. Hence, donors willing to support this approach will be able to pre-select certain location(s) and/or area(s) of intervention of their preference, within the 200 prioritized  communities.
The programme relates directly to the sector objectives:
1. Living conditions
2. Livelihoods
3. Access to social services
4. Access to productive and market infrastructure
5.social protection
6. Strengthening of local public services delivery capacity
7. Reinforcing  opportunities and capacities for civic engagement

Post-earthquake debris management and recycling project to facilitate local level recovery and rehabilitation in quake affected NW Syria. Fostering Resilience through Early Recovery response for the most Crisis impacted Communities in Syria The Integrated Response for Resilience Programme aims at providing a comprehensive response through Early Recovery support in 80 communities impacted by the crisis. Communities, particularly  those most dramatically affected – and under additional stress because of IDPs returns and other displacements - need  assistance in reinforcing their resilience to address these shocks as well as the consequences of the protracted crisis, and to address their needs on seriously depleted infrastructures and service capacities.
The essence of the Programme is about providing Syrian communities with – still limited - support to regain  control  over their basic needs (livelihoods, access to essential services) and reduce their dependency on humanitarian assistance. Prioritization of locations, is the outcome of a context analysis and needs assessment conducted on more than  5,000
Syrian communities, based on the following three criteria:
1) Hard to Reach  Areas
2) Areas of major IDPs presence and IDPs returns
3) Highest scoring in the Severity Scale
The integrated response consists of the following components: strengthening of social services-related capacities (access and coverage), livelihoods creation and rural recovery, PWDs support, social cohesion/community safety, reducing gender inequality  and youth marginality, women empowerment, tensions reduction and rehabilitation of basic infrastructure and public services.
The program is built in a modular manner both in terms of geographical and sectoral/thematic interventions and foresees the allotment of average 1 Million US$ per community. Hence, donors willing to support this approach will be able to pre-select certain location(s) and/or area(s) of intervention of their preference, within the 200 prioritized  communities.
The programme relates directly to the sector objectives:
1. Living conditions
2. Livelihoods
3. Access to social services
4. Access to productive and market infrastructure
5.social protection
6. Strengthening of local public services delivery capacity
7. Reinforcing  opportunities and capacities for civic engagement

project_text:
WASH static and emergency response for vulnerable IDPs, host communities and returnees in South Sudan. NRC’s planned and proposed Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) intervention for 2023 is continuation of 2022 and   is designed to address the emergency WASH needs through rapid response (RRT)  and  contribute to improve health,  nutrition, education , Livelihood and food security  and protection  outcomes through NRC static WASH response. The proposed interventions are  to reduce prevalence of malnutrition, contribute to reducing WASH-related morbidity and mortality, provide access to basic WASH services in underserved and hard to reach  locations affected by disaster, disability inclusion and mitigating GBV at WASH facility and durable access to WASH amongst 200, 000 IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities in in South Sudan.
The proposed WASH interventions will be implemented in close coordination with NRC’s Shelter, Education, Livelihood and Food security, ICLA and protection programming and teams, applying an integrated approach to uplift people’s lives and contributing to South Sudan HRP and WASH Cluster objectives and the 2022/2023 Humanitarian Response. Recognizing WASH services to be key drivers of health and malnutrition outcomes and women and girls to be the primary users of WASH services, the project aims to reduce GBV risk by ensuring adequate and needs based provision of WASH services that address key protection concerns. NRC’s integrated approach will further address high levels of malnutrition in targeted locations.
NRC will consult and engage communities in preliminary assessments and design process to ensure all NRC’s interventions are tailored to local context and to establish appropriated water and sanitation facilities at community, institutions and household level. To enhance and ensure sustainability and proper usage of the facilities comprehensive training will be provided to female and male members of Water User Committees (WUCs) , Schools and other institutional staff. Solid waste management training will also be provided to solid waste/hygiene committees to implement community-driven solid waste collection and disposal campaigns. 
To ensure durable and continues access to safe water ; NRC will establish / rehabilitate small scale solar powered water supply schemes , new boreholes through cost effective manual Borehole drilling. The proposed water supply interventions will increase the safe water access to schools, health, nutrition and protection centres, disability inclusion and mitigating GBV at WAH facilities and route to WASH facilities. NRC will construct own driven household / family shared latrines to ensure that immediate and long-term sanitation needs are adequately met and facilities are gender and culturally appropriate. The approach will enhance the ownership and sustainability of the facilities. NRC  will also promote good hygiene practices and  awareness through training of community hygiene promoters who then will be conducting hygiene promotion at their own communities , community hygiene campaigns, hygiene promotion campaigns and sessions at intuitional levels. NRC will also provide hygiene kits, WASH-NFIs and soaps to the vulnerable communities specially in hard to reach areas

project_text:
Protection and Assistance for Refugees, Returnees and Asylum Seekers in South Sudan As of January 2022, there are some 335,000 refugees and asylum seekers from neighbouring countries sheltering in South Sudan. Despite enormous socio-economic, security and political challenges, compounded by the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, South Sudan has maintained its open-door policy for people seeking international protection, the majority of whom are women and children, primarily from Sudan, the Democratic Republic of Congo and the Central African Republic.
At the same time, against a backdrop of fragile peace and cautious optimism for longer term stability, hundreds of thousands of South Sudanese refugees have spontaneously returned to the country since the signing of the 2018 Revitalized Peace Agreement. While UNHCR is not promoting or facilitating return to South Sudan, this spontaneous movement has prompted the development of an area-based approach, to support refugees, returnees and host communities, through enhanced engagement with development actors, to support greater access to services where possible.
Refugees largely reside in conflict-affected regions, challenged by an unpredictable security environment as well as at times fragile relations with host communities. Displaced communities will continue to rely on life-saving humanitarian assistance provided by UNHCR and its partners as a result of enduring economic hardship, weak rule of law, limited development support and a lack of social services and infrastructure in refugee-hosting areas as well as in areas of origin. A reduction in basic assistance, especially during a global pandemic, will immediately lead to the deterioration of the humanitarian situation to emergency levels, due to the absence of a safety net, including social services, community support networks and limited access to livelihoods in displacements sites hosting refugees and South Sudanese refugee returnees.
Under the refugee response, all refugees and asylum seekers registered with UNHCR will benefit from various forms of protection interventions, including individual registration and documentation, and multi-sector assistance. Specific protection services, such as SGBV response and child protection will focus on the identified at-risk groups. While water, health, nutrition and education services will continue to maintain indicators within global standards for refugees living in camps, provision of other assistance, including shelter, non-food items and livelihoods support, will be undertaken in a targeted manner, focusing on persons with specific protection needs and vulnerabilities. This will primarily be achieved through participatory assessments, surveys as well as verification exercise to identify vulnerable refugees and their needs. Impact monitoring will be used to gauge the efficiency of projects implemented and for the purposes of course-correction in terms of better targeting of assistance. The needs of persons with disabilities and the elderly will be further mainstreamed in various multi-sector response services. Vulnerable refugees in urban settings will also continue to benefit from targeted protection interventions and facilitation of their access to national services.

project_text:
provision of emergency lifesaving and resilience WASH, ES/NFI, Education FSL and child protection integrated services for IDPS, returnees and venerable host community of Sudan in CD, WD, BN, Aj Jazirah, Khartoum and SK state. Starting on 15 April 2023, fighting between the SAF and the RSF, the number of people in need (PiN) of humanitarian assistance has increased from 15.8 million, estimated in November 2022, to 24.7 million in May 2023, representing a 57 per cent increase. 
The primary objective of this project is to safe live through supporting the newly displaced individuals who are the most vulnerable and marginalized people at risk through multi-sectoral lifesaving intervention. This project will prioritize activities that ensure life-saving assistance and protection to people affected by recent crisis primely and also people at risk of epidemics and floods, and other vulnerable residents - in order to reduce mortality and morbidity in the targeted areas. The proposed action will address 350000 (IDPs-175000(F-85750, M-89250), Returnees- 105,000(F-51450, M-53550), Vulnerable community-70,000(F-34300, M-35700)) crisis affected peoples. The WASH component will respond to the most urgent needs through Operationalization of water treatment plants in Khartoum, Water trucking in areas where supply is disrupted including health facilities and the establishment of distribution points, including in gathering and transit points; Essential WASH supplies and NFI emergency sanitation and handwashing facilities will be provided in hotspot locations; Hygiene promotion and household water treatment practices will be promoted as an immediate alternative, especially for those reliant on surface/river water. project_text:
Strengthening Child Protection interventions for girls and boys most at risk of violence, abuse, neglect and exploitation across whole of Syria In line with the CP Area of Responsibility (AOR) Strategy and the “No Lost Generation” framework, UNICEF will enhance equitable access to quality CP services with a resilience focus, including for Survivors of abuse, violence, neglect and exploitation as well as children with disabilities, targeting 117 high severity sub-districts (3 to 5) and 38 low severity ones.

UNICEF’s CP Strategy in 2022-2023 includes:
• Addressing behavioural, social, cultural and economic determinants of CP violations as a prevention approach.  
• Improving the reach and quality of specialized CP services
• Capacity development of CP responders
•  Monitoring, evidence generation and advocacy 

UNICEF will support the delivery of integrated programming that will encourage social transformation, prioritizing:
• Structured and sustained CP MHPSS and EORE programmes
• Specialized integrated CP services including case management for survivors of violence, exploitation, neglect and abuse (child labour, CAFAAG, child survivors of GBV, child marriages, justice for children, birth registration and unaccompanied or separated children amongst others) 
• Parenting programmes to promote positive child rearing skills and experience for caregivers
• Elimination of violence against children, including GBV prevention and empowerment for girls, boys and women, prevention of violence in schools, homes and communities.
• Awareness-raising on CP risks
• Capacity development of CP responders and social workers

UNICEF will generate evidence to inform the humanitarian response and advocacy including setting up an information management system for case management. UNICEF will embrace new delivery modalities and implement cash transfers aimed at child protection outcomes for vulnerable families. UNICEF will also continue to support the Monitoring and Reporting Mechanism on grave violations against children.

CP services will be delivered by partners based on minimum standards and IASC guidelines. 7,200 CP and social workers will be trained on case management, MHPSS, EORE, advocacy, evidence generation and coordination across sectors for a comprehensive CP response.
 
UNICEF will support MHPSS for 364,000 children to benefit from improved mental health and social wellbeing. UNICEF will equip 61,500 parents and caregivers with skills to provide a stimulating and safe environment at home, including reduced violence.  

Violence prevention is a key priority. Family violence prevalence is high for girls 12-17 years (47%), boys 12-17 years (44%), boys below 12 (45%) and girls below 12 (44%) (UNICEF 2018). UNICEF will work to protect children from violence and abuse through prevention activities in schools, homes and communities and providing survivors of violence with child-friendly and gender sensitive services. Support will be provided for PSEA mechanisms to protect beneficiaries and build the capacity of humanitarian actors. PSEA programming will be implemented with the Protection Sector AORs.

Based on HNO 2021, one in three communities in Syria is reportedly contaminated by explosive ordnance. One in four victims is a child (Joint MA & CP Analysis, 2020). EORE messages will be provided to 1,460,000 children and adults through humanitarian actors and public service providers using static facilities and mobile teams. UNICEF will build the capacity of partners to provide quality EORE that is age, gender and disability appropriate and to provide child victims with assistance.
 
UNICEF will strengthen the justice system to ensure that children in contact with the law victims, offenders or witnesses are protected through child-friendly, gender-sensitive services, that are community-based and family focused.

As Lead Agency for the CP AOR, UNICEF will ensure coordination needs at Hub and WOS levels. Two UN-led and one INGO-led coordination hubs in Damascus, Gaziantep and NES, as well as a WOS overall coordination system, to ensure coherence across the CP response.

project_text:
Prestación de servicios integrales de salud primaria, salud mental y apoyo psicosocial a poblaciones afectadas por el conflicto armado y la crisis fronteriza con Venezuela en Colombia. Esta acción cubrirá algunas de las necesidades básicas insatisfechas de las personas afectadas por el conflicto armado en Colombia, por la crisis económica y política en Venezuela y/o por desastres climáticos (entre otros relacionados al Fenómeno del Niño). Premiere Urgence Internationale (PUI) continuará con los esfuerzos para proporcionar salud primaria de calidad, incluyendo servicios médicos básicos (con entrega de medicamentos), salud sexual y reproductiva, diagnóstico de malnutrición, atención en salud mental y apoyo psicosocial en zonas donde estos servicios son escasos. Se prioriza una atención integral combinando estos servicios con acciones de promoción de salud, intervención de WASH in Health y remisiones en articulación con actores previamente identificados en cada territorio. Las colaboraciones directas con actores especializados en Protección se concretarán a través de consorcios o convenios específicos.
Además, para ajustar la intervención a los contextos priorizados, se combinan modalidades de atención en punto fijos  y atención extramural. Esta última, con el ánimo de alcanzar zonas que carecen de acceso efectivo a la salud.
Las actividades de WASH se contemplan como integradas a la salud, a través de sesiones grupales de promoción a la higiene, entrega de filtros de agua a hogares seleccionados, y posibles rehabilitaciones de puestos de salud. Se articularan estas intervenciones con los actores presentes en cada zona.

project_text: Assistance humanitaire en abri et en Biens non-alimentaires (BNA) pour les sinistrés d'inondation au Niger Dans le cadre de HRP 2023 au travers de ce projet, l'OIM vise à apporter un appui au gouvernement du Niger dans le cadre de la réponse d'urgence aux personnes sinistrées des inondations. Ce projet propose de répondre aux besoins des ménages sinistrés à travers les requêtes qui seront exprimées par le Gouvernement au travers du Ministère de l’Action Humanitaire et de la Gestion des Catastrophes (MAH/GC). Cette réponse s’adressera uniquement aux ménages vulnérables victimes d’inondations dont les abris ou cases auront été effondrées et/ou ceux dont les Biens non-alimentaires (BNA) auront été emportés par les eaux. Le présent projet poursuit comme objectif d’atteindre 10 000 ménages soit 70 000 personnes à travers tout le Niger prioritairement dans les régions de Zinder, Diffa, Maradi et Tahoua. En coordination avec le MAH/GC et la Direction Générale de la Protection Civile (DGPC), l’OIM mettra à disposition 10 000 kits abris et 10 000 kits Biens non-alimentaires qui seront distribués aux ménages sinistrés. En plus des kits, l’OIM couvrira les coûts liés à la logistique et à la distribution des kits. Ce projet ne couvrira pas une zone ou région donnée mais permettra d’intervenir là où les besoins se présentent et aussi de pouvoir compléter les activités des autres acteurs en cas de besoin en tant que prestataire de dernier recours pour la réponse humanitaire en abri d'urgence et BNA. L’OIM en tant que Co-Lead du Groupe de Travail Abri et Bien non-alimentaire (GTABNA) avec le MAH/GC s'assurera que les activités sont menées en étroite coordination avec les autres partenaires humanitaires membres du GTABNA pour la réponse en abri et Biens non-alimentaires pour les ménages sinistrés des inondations au Niger. Conformément à la logique de la stratégie du Secteur abris/BNA et en fonction de la faisabilité, les interventions pourront se faire en transferts monétaires conditionnels. Cela réduirait considérablement les coûts logistiques qui sont très élevés en période hivernale à cause du mauvais état des routes mais aussi et permettrait aussi de résoudre en partie le problème d’accès lié à l'insécurité qui souvent retarde les interventions. Enfin, la mise en œuvre du présent projet fera l’objet d’un suivi régulier de la qualité des interventions réalisées mais aussi de l’implication des bénéficiaires et autorités locales. Pour cela, les feedbacks de la communauté cible seront collectés à travers des évaluations post-distribution et des séances de discussion de groupe séparées par genre et âge avant et après l'assistance. Aussi, en tant qu’acteur humanitaire, l'OIM et ses partenaires de mise en œuvre s’assureront que ses actions n’induisent aucune tension ou problème dans la zone et n’exposent pas les bénéficiaires. A cet effet la phase d'évaluation de besoins sera réalisée de commun accord avec les populations dans les communes ciblées, les sessions d'information sur le projet seront organisées à l'attention de communauté bénéficiaires, le mecanisme de ciblage de bénéficiaires sera réalisé en étroite collabation avec les autorités au niveau local (do no harm). Une collaboration étroite faite avec les acteurs de protection pour un suivi de près de toutes questions de protection et de LTB. Le cout total du projet sera de 6.090.000 USD.

Ce projet propose de répondre aux besoins des ménages sinistrés à travers les requêtes qui seront exprimées par le Gouvernement au travers du Ministère de l’Action Humanitaire et de la Gestion des Catastrophes (MAH/GC). En coordination avec le MAH/GC et la Direction Générale de la Protection Civile (DGPC), l’OIM mettra à disposition 10 000 kits abris et 10 000 kits Biens non-alimentaires qui seront distribués aux ménages sinistrés. project_text:
Programa de seguridad alimentaria basado en la escuela Con el objetivo de contribuir a la seguridad alimentaria de la población con mayores necesidades, el Programa Mundial de Alimentos de Naciones Unidas (WFP, por sus siglas en inglés) en Venezuela desarrolla un programa de asistencia humanitaria basado en la escuela para garantizar el acceso de los más vulnerables a una alimentación adecuada y nutritiva en el entorno escolar, familiar y comunitario. 
Este programa inició en 2021 con comidas escolares en emergencias priorizando escuelas iniciales y de educación especial.

WFP proporciona comidas escolares acompañado de un paquete integrado de intervenciones para mejorar el acceso a alimentos nutritivos y diversificados a través de las escuelas, contribuyendo al mismo tiempo a mejorar la salud y la nutrición de los niños en edad escolar, los estudiantes con discapacidad y el personal escolar, y apoyando a las comunidades a reducir la dependencia en estrategias de afrontamiento. De manera gradual, el WFP está realizando compras locales de alimentos, e incluyendo acciones para apoyar los mercados locales con compras a pequeños productores y apoyo técnico para acceso a mercados.

En este sentido, el programa de comidas escolares en emergencias tiene los siguientes componentes, para asegurar un enfoque integral que apoye al estudiante en el entorno escolar y familiar:

1. Entrega de comidas escolares nutritivas para estudiantes y personal escolar, promoviendo las compras locales y a pequeños productores.
2. Apoyo a la seguridad alimentaria del hogar.
3. Rehabilitación de cocinas escolares para garantizar condiciones adecuadas de preparación de alimentos.
4. Comunicación para sensibilizar acerca de los principios humanitarios, la adecuada preparación de alimentos, nutrición, higiene y mantenimiento de cocinas escolares.
5. Fortalecimiento de capacidades de socios implementadores y personal escolar.
6. Acciones sensibles a la nutrición, que incluyen, tamizaje en las escuelas, educación nutricional, referencia a servicios especializados y entrega de alimento complementario fortificado (Super Cereal Plus).

project_text:
IMPROVING SKILLS AND ECONOMIC OPPORTUNITIES FOR THE BANGLADESHI COMMUNITY AND ROHINGYA WOMEN & YOUTHS IN COX'S BAZAR 							 """"""""IOM will undertake wide variety of activities to create an enabling environment for the Rohingya refugees towards eventual sustainable voluntary return and reintegration in Myanmar in the future when conditions may permit. Such activities will help Rohingya beneficiaries increase self-reliance skills. The livelihoods activities will also focus on the host communities affected by the influx by integrating income-generating livelihoods through support to agricultue and other sectors.
IOM will implement skills development projects to promote the economic resilience of Rohingya refugees in the camps. This training will enhance their capacity and help them utilize their skills in the camps in Bangladesh as self-reliance opportunities and can be used as transferrable skills by them upon return to Myanmar. Rohingya beneficiaries will receive skills training related and applicable to the humanitarian sector (e.g. health, wash, sanitation, site development-construction, etc.) to enable them earning income in the camps. After the end of the training IOM will facilitate in-kind asset support materials to  Rohingya beneficiaries working outside the agricultural sector who are willing to gain basic skills or competencies but lack the physical assets to do so.
IOM will provide host communities with transferable and life skills training (e.g., computer skills, communication, negotiation, psychosocial) and vocational skills training including skills related to green businesses and green financing such as plumbing, ac repair, secretary, patient administration, catering to disaster resilient off-farming tools and methods, waste recycling, electronic refurbishment, financial literacy related to resilient investments and planning, etc. The trades will be identified by thorough skills and needs assessment exercises. This training will give scope to beneficiaries in the host community for income generation. Productive asset support will be given to women beneficiaries who have technical skills but lack inputs/opportunities/assets but are willing to earn a modest income. IOM will provide small business grants through Entrepreneurship Program to the existing Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) to help beneficiaries expand and strengthen their businesses. Support will be given for the establishment of women's cooperatives (such as livestock, handicrafts, etc.,). Cash for work activities will also be included as an income-generation activity in the host community.
To enhance the private sector engagement and promote market linkages, wage subsidy opportunities for beneficiaries will be implemented. To ensure sustainable income generation, emphasis will be given to activities like product fairs for/by the beneficiaries in the host community to sell and promote their products to individuals and wholesalers.  A labour market assessment will be conducted to identify the needs of the beneficiaries based on which suitable activities will be selected. All these activities in both host, as well as refugee community, will be carried out by either implementing partners or implemented directly by IOM. IOM will ensure integration of various cross-cutting issues in the project design by identifying and including the most vulnerable beneficiaries through gender and disability-sensitive beneficiary selection criteria. The selection criteria of vulnerable women will be based on eligibility criteria such as  female-headed households, income below the poverty line, widow, etc.  IOM will also focus on disability throughout the beneficiary selection criteria and assist livelihoods and self-reliance opportunities. Women empowerment, leadership, and decision-making will be promoted by incorporating income opportunities and entrepreneurship opportunities, business development training, financial literacy, etc., for women in the Host Community and self-reliance opportunities for women in the camps to ensure sustainable development and integration into the society.

project_text:
Support the affected people in Aleppo and Idleb Governorates with a comprehensive WASH services Over 2023, the intervention plan will focus on supporting WASH facilities and systems (water supply systems, sanitation systems, wastewater treatment, and solid waste management) in addition to immediate emergency life-saving WASH interventions. Moreover, the intervention will enhance WASH service in schools and healthcare facilities. The intervention will focus on maintaining emergency WASH services in locations targeted by Shafak, in addition, to extend the intervention to the new locations needed in terms of cholera outbreaks or flood responses. as well as Shafak will ensure the upgrade and enhance the water and snaitation systems to promote the access to sustainable access to basic services and improve the quality of the environmental health. The intervention plan will strengthen the community resilience to adapt to living conditions in light of climate changes (drought) and apidamic situation (cholera and COVID-19 outbreak). Shafak, through this intervention, will provide emergency WASH services for 320,000 individuals living in camps and communities.  The intervention will comprise the following components:

a) Rehabilitation/upgrade of 10 water pumping stations benefiting 95,000 Individuals, Shafak will maintain supporting the water pumping stations that were targeted in 2022 adding new locations. Shafak will ensure installing chlorination units in the supported pumping stations and provide the regular maintenance for the damaged electrical and mechanical equipment and installing hybrid (solar powered systems) systems to reduce the operation costs and the emission of CO2. In addition, support Water Association Units (WAUs) by providing monthly running costs for the stations (electricity subscription, fuel, chlorine, engine oil, and incentives for workers) and promote a cost recovery system. As well as train the local communities and apply water safety plans.

b) Provision of WASH emergency services for 150,000 individuals living in camps including water trucking and water quality monitoring, water containers, construction/ repair of emergency latrines, providing cleaning materials for latrines and latrine cleaning, desludging of septic tanks, and solid waste management.

c) Rehabilitation of sewage networks to connect the remote sites, camps, public facilities (schools and health centers) in addition to replacing the damaged sewer lines benefiting 115,000 Individuals in addition to construct wastewater treatment plant for irrigation.Provide desludging services where no sewage network.

d) Rehabilitation of water networks to connect the remote sites, camps, and public facilities (schools and health centers) in addition to replacing the broken water lines benefiting 30,000 Individuals.

e) Supporting municipalities to continue the garbage collection and disposal of waste from 10 communities (around 95,000 individuals), schools, health centers, and surrounding IDP sites. This support will cover operation costs. Also, the rehabilitation of 3 dumpsites and construction 2 solid waste treatment plants equipped with incinerators and medical waste treatment. 

f) Conducting hygiene promotion sessions about the improvement of hygiene practices and behaviors for 60,000 individuals.

g) 60,000 hygiene kits (approx. 360,000 individuals) will be distributed to the IDPs and host communities who don’t have the capacity to secure hygiene materials.

h) provision of WASH services to 5 education centers and 5 health facilities. 

Shafak will ensure support the innovative solutions as possible in its proposed interventions for dealing with water drought issues through supporting solar-powered systems, wastewater treatment. In addition to applying environmental improvement projects through developing solid waste management treatment and elevating the bad impacts of neglecting SWM support.

As for 2024, according to Shafak's strategy and fund availability, it is expected to implement the same activities with the same size and budget.

reportDetails_organization: European Commission's Humanitarian Aid and Civil Protection Department; World Food Programme
project_text:
Food assistance to address increasing levels of severe food insecurity in South Sudan Meet the lifesaving food requirements of people in South Sudan who are facing food security crises, including those living in (ex)-POCs and IDP and those otherwise affected by conflict, natural disaster and/or seasonal food insecurity. WFP will provide general food distributions (GFD) to the most food insecure people in South Sudan. At the field level, food assistance will be overseen by the WFP Field Offices and implemented by NGO partners or provided through the Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM). WFP provides food assistance and common services through a comprehensive and collaborative humanitarian intervention by deploying mobile teams, supported by cooperating partners to reach populations facing the most urgent needs in the most inaccessible areas of the South Sudan, subject to the availability of resources.
Complementary to food distributions, WFP will seek to offer value-added solutions (light resilience- building activities, peace/conflict resolution training also called GFD+), in response to needs and priorities identified by the community. Through GFD+, WFP together with its cooperating partners and other stakeholders will provide unconditional opportunities, identified through a community-based, people-centric participatory approach to targeted beneficiaries. GFD+ adds value to emergency food assistance with a focus on solutions that address the root causes of food and nutrition insecurity and better equip beneficiaries to fight hunger. The GFD+ activity type, duration, frequency, and participation will be catered to specific local sites and may range from COVID-19 awareness, training, or sensitisation on peaceful resolution of conflicts, mitigation measures to nutrition education, dyke rehabilitation and communal asset management, income-generating activities which lead to women's economic empowerment and have positive impact on household food security, or other solutions. WFP will also implement resilience building activities including Food Assistance for Assets (FFA) to support communities to improve their food security, restore their livelihoods, strengthen their resilience to shocks and build self-reliance, while contributing to peace. 
Mitigation measures to reduce and prevent the potential the spread of COVID-19, including new variants, and other potential viral outbreaks have been incorporated into standard operating procedures for all interactions with beneficiaries, including training of partners and stakeholders, increasing general awareness among partners and beneficiaries, enforcing social distancing, promoting handwashing, disinfecting sites, reducing the frequency of distribution cycles, and mandating the utilization of personal protective equipment (PPE). These measures are mainstreamed into all WFP activities.

project_text:
Food Security and Livelihoods Support to disaster affected populations in Northern Bahr el Ghazal, Unity, Western Bahr Warrap, Central Equatoria and Jonglei States of South Sudan The project will utilize the humanitarian pipeline for crops, vegetables and fisheries kits from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO). Where markets are functional, market-based interventions such as direct purchases and or local seed and tool fairs will be sought as informed by respective market assessments. These activities will be complimented by capacity building/training modules in the specific livelihoods so as to improve the targeted farmer production, productivity capacities and improve yields and returns. The fisheries training will enable target beneficiaries utilize their kits in the proper way and also improve their knowledge and skills in fish processing, preservation and marketing. The crops and vegetable production training will be based on the crop production seasonal calendar which includes land preparation, planting weeding, pest and disease management, harvesting, post-harvest management and marketing. Using the Training of Trainers (ToT) approach, the project will target 7,500 crop/vegetable farmers and 4,500 fisher folks with assorted livelihoods inputs support as well as training and engaging community-based extension workers to provide the technical support to these farmers while they replicate the training to the other beneficiaries. The proposed interventions will also train targeted households with trainings on approved agronomic practices, pests and disease control, post-harvest handling and value addition and linkages to markets and other value chain actors in addition, 1,500 HHs will be supported through unconditional/conditional cash transfer programming especially in flood and conflicted affected areas. The action will also target 1,250 HHs with small ruminant (goat/sheep) or poultry restocking through livestock voucher modality, 750 women, youth and men will be engaged in VSLAs/IGAs while 450 HHs will be engaged in natural resource management and climate adaptation activities. The project will support develop youth employable skills through TVET training for 1,000 youths in trades such as welding, bakery, tailoring brick laying and masonry and carpentry, motor mechanics among others for self-sustenance.
To ensure integration, the intervention will target nutrition & health centers, schools and mother garden’s locations conveniently with/without access and proximity of a water source. Additional community gardens will be promoted at locations such as schools, health facilities where they will be jointly tended by students and community volunteers. The FSL interventions will be designed taking into consideration and incorporating mainstreaming of protection, safety, GBV prevention, Prevention of Sexual Abuse & Exploitation and conflict sensitivity analysis.  The project teams will work closely with local authorities to identify persons with disabilities both men and women so that they are supported. This number is not expected to exceed 5% of the 10,500 HH targeted. This ensures participants are selected based on needs alone, a rigorous community-based targeting process with participation and inclusion of vulnerable groups such as female and child headed households, disabled and the elderly.  The proposed project will also take into consideration cross-cutting issues like environmental protection, HIV/AIDS, community-based participatory planning, gender, nutrition will be considered during project implementation.
All agricultural and fisheries activities will be implemented in collaboration with the State Ministry of Agriculture in order to ensure that government extension workers benefit from and also contribute to the technical components that will be offered by the project by so doing building capacities that will continue to be utilized after project closure. Community based extension workers such as lead farmers will be trained to continue supporting other farmers during and after project closure. Skilling component will be done in liaison with the vocational training institutions.

-- agriculture & food Food Security and Livelihoods Support to disaster affected populations in Northern Bahr el Ghazal, Unity, Western Bahr Warrap, Central Equatoria and Jonglei States of South Sudan The project will utilize the humanitarian pipeline for crops, vegetables and fisheries kits from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO). Where markets are functional, market-based interventions such as direct purchases and or local seed and tool fairs will be sought as informed by respective market assessments. These activities will be complimented by capacity building/training modules in the specific livelihoods so as to improve the targeted farmer production, productivity capacities and improve yields and returns. The fisheries training will enable target beneficiaries utilize their kits in the proper way and also improve their knowledge and skills in fish processing, preservation and marketing. The proposed interventions will also train targeted households with trainings on approved agronomic practices, pests and disease control, post-harvest handling and value addition and linkages to markets and other value chain actors in addition, 1,500 HHs will be supported through unconditional/conditional cash transfer programming especially in flood and conflicted affected areas. Skilling component will be done in liaison with the vocational training institutions.

project_text:
WASH static and emergency response for vulnerable IDPs, host communities and returnees in South Sudan. NRC’s planned and proposed Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) intervention for 2023 is continuation of 2022 and   is designed to address the emergency WASH needs through rapid response (RRT)  and  contribute to improve health,  nutrition, education , Livelihood and food security  and protection  outcomes through NRC static WASH response. The proposed interventions are  to reduce prevalence of malnutrition, contribute to reducing WASH-related morbidity and mortality, provide access to basic WASH services in underserved and hard to reach  locations affected by disaster, disability inclusion and mitigating GBV at WASH facility and durable access to WASH amongst 200, 000 IDPs, returnees and vulnerable host communities in in South Sudan.
The proposed WASH interventions will be implemented in close coordination with NRC’s Shelter, Education, Livelihood and Food security, ICLA and protection programming and teams, applying an integrated approach to uplift people’s lives and contributing to South Sudan HRP and WASH Cluster objectives and the 2022/2023 Humanitarian Response. Recognizing WASH services to be key drivers of health and malnutrition outcomes and women and girls to be the primary users of WASH services, the project aims to reduce GBV risk by ensuring adequate and needs based provision of WASH services that address key protection concerns. NRC’s integrated approach will further address high levels of malnutrition in targeted locations.
NRC will consult and engage communities in preliminary assessments and design process to ensure all NRC’s interventions are tailored to local context and to establish appropriated water and sanitation facilities at community, institutions and household level. To enhance and ensure sustainability and proper usage of the facilities comprehensive training will be provided to female and male members of Water User Committees (WUCs) , Schools and other institutional staff. Solid waste management training will also be provided to solid waste/hygiene committees to implement community-driven solid waste collection and disposal campaigns. 
To ensure durable and continues access to safe water ; NRC will establish / rehabilitate small scale solar powered water supply schemes , new boreholes through cost effective manual Borehole drilling. The proposed water supply interventions will increase the safe water access to schools, health, nutrition and protection centres, disability inclusion and mitigating GBV at WAH facilities and route to WASH facilities. NRC will construct own driven household / family shared latrines to ensure that immediate and long-term sanitation needs are adequately met and facilities are gender and culturally appropriate. The approach will enhance the ownership and sustainability of the facilities. NRC  will also promote good hygiene practices and  awareness through training of community hygiene promoters who then will be conducting hygiene promotion at their own communities , community hygiene campaigns, hygiene promotion campaigns and sessions at intuitional levels. NRC will also provide hygiene kits, WASH-NFIs and soaps to the vulnerable communities specially in hard to reach areas
