project_text:
Contribute to reducing WASH-related morbidity and mortality through WASH integrated programming with Health and Nutrition in Fangak, Pibor, Duk, Aweil center, Aweil East, Gogrial West and Twic counties of Jonglei, Northern Bahr el Ghazal and Warrap states. Action Against Hunger has been operational in what is now South Sudan since 1985, responding to both chronic and acute humanitarian needs. AAH strategy is to addresses the immediate and underlying causes of malnutrition in children U5 by linking nutrition with WASH and FSL interventions to foster a meaningful impact upon communities’ resilience as well as prevent childhood morbidity and mortality. Currently Action Against Hunger is implementing a WASH program under SIDA, GFFO, GAC, and ECHO activities in Northern Bahr El Ghazal, Warrap, and Jonglei states with established field offices in Malual-kon, Alek, Old Fangak, and Paguir Payam. In 2023, WASH projects will be implemented to ensure that host communities, IDPs and returnees have safe access to clean water and sanitation facilities with improved hygiene behavior. The proposed activities will improve the nutritional status of children U5 and pregnant and lactating women through an integrated WASH and Nutrition response aimed at breaking diarrhea – malnutrition vicious cycle. This proposed project will ensure the effectiveness of addressing malnutrition in the proposed target area by reducing disease burden in communities as well as availing safe, potable water for use in appetite tests at nutrition sites including monthly Water quality tests which will be carried out by our WASH team in both locations using our established laboratories. 
To achieve the overall project objective and objectives of the HRP-2022/3, we will provide critical services to 41,320 individuals with gender segregation of 21,478 males, 19, 842 females. among them 16,471 under 5 children at both Nutrition/Health facilities and   at the village level with 4 main activities which include: 
1) Contribute to reducing WASH-related morbidity and mortality in priority counties through WASH integrated programming with Nutrition.
2) Integrate Provide access to basic WASH services in emergencies and/or WSC 4 and 5 counties).
3) Community member’s exposure to environmental hazards is reduced through the construction of disaster-resistant structures and infrastructure.
4) Increasing knowledge of appropriate hygiene and sanitation practices among vulnerable and affected populations to prevent and mitigate WASH-related diseases. ACF will implement the above in the catchment areas of its nutrition facilities in Northern Bahr El Ghazal, Warrap and Jonglei states. Baseline KAP surveys will be conducted in all target areas to identify the WASH-related knowledge, attitude, and practices of the communities. 
Detailed needs assessments will be conducted to assess community access to safe water sources and sanitation facilities. The implementation strategy will align with the needs identified in assessments and KAP surveys at the project start. Additionally, the ACF multi-sector emergency response throughout the country will include a WASH component to complement its nutrition work. 
The proposed program strategy takes into account specific gender-related needs during surveys and activity implementation to ensure the equitable participation of all gender and age groups in the locations mentioned above.

project_text:
Protection and Assistance for Refugees, Returnees and Asylum Seekers in South Sudan As of January 2022, there are some 335,000 refugees and asylum seekers from neighbouring countries sheltering in South Sudan. Despite enormous socio-economic, security and political challenges, compounded by the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, South Sudan has maintained its open-door policy for people seeking international protection, the majority of whom are women and children, primarily from Sudan, the Democratic Republic of Congo and the Central African Republic.
At the same time, against a backdrop of fragile peace and cautious optimism for longer term stability, hundreds of thousands of South Sudanese refugees have spontaneously returned to the country since the signing of the 2018 Revitalized Peace Agreement. While UNHCR is not promoting or facilitating return to South Sudan, this spontaneous movement has prompted the development of an area-based approach, to support refugees, returnees and host communities, through enhanced engagement with development actors, to support greater access to services where possible.
Refugees largely reside in conflict-affected regions, challenged by an unpredictable security environment as well as at times fragile relations with host communities. Displaced communities will continue to rely on life-saving humanitarian assistance provided by UNHCR and its partners as a result of enduring economic hardship, weak rule of law, limited development support and a lack of social services and infrastructure in refugee-hosting areas as well as in areas of origin. A reduction in basic assistance, especially during a global pandemic, will immediately lead to the deterioration of the humanitarian situation to emergency levels, due to the absence of a safety net, including social services, community support networks and limited access to livelihoods in displacements sites hosting refugees and South Sudanese refugee returnees.
Under the refugee response, all refugees and asylum seekers registered with UNHCR will benefit from various forms of protection interventions, including individual registration and documentation, and multi-sector assistance. Specific protection services, such as SGBV response and child protection will focus on the identified at-risk groups. While water, health, nutrition and education services will continue to maintain indicators within global standards for refugees living in camps, provision of other assistance, including shelter, non-food items and livelihoods support, will be undertaken in a targeted manner, focusing on persons with specific protection needs and vulnerabilities. This will primarily be achieved through participatory assessments, surveys as well as verification exercise to identify vulnerable refugees and their needs. Impact monitoring will be used to gauge the efficiency of projects implemented and for the purposes of course-correction in terms of better targeting of assistance. The needs of persons with disabilities and the elderly will be further mainstreamed in various multi-sector response services. Vulnerable refugees in urban settings will also continue to benefit from targeted protection interventions and facilitation of their access to national services.

Despite enormous socio-economic, security and political challenges, compounded by the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic, South Sudan has maintained its open-door policy for people seeking international protection, the majority of whom are women and children, primarily from Sudan, the Democratic Republic of Congo and the Central African Republic.
At the same time, against a backdrop of fragile peace and cautious optimism for longer term stability, hundreds of thousands of South Sudanese refugees have spontaneously returned to the country since the signing of the 2018 Revitalized Peace Agreement. While UNHCR is not promoting or facilitating return to South Sudan, this spontaneous movement has prompted the development of an area-based approach, to support refugees, returnees and host communities, through enhanced engagement with development actors, to support greater access to services where possible.
Refugees largely reside in conflict-affected regions, challenged by an unpredictable security environment as well as at times fragile relations with host communities. Displaced communities will continue to rely on life-saving humanitarian assistance provided by UNHCR and its partners as a result of enduring economic hardship, weak rule of law, limited development support and a lack of social services and infrastructure in refugee-hosting areas as well as in areas of origin. A reduction in basic assistance, especially during a global pandemic, will immediately lead to the deterioration of the humanitarian situation to emergency levels, due to the absence of a safety net, including social services, community support networks and limited access to livelihoods in displacements sites hosting refugees and South Sudanese refugee returnees.
Under the refugee response, all refugees and asylum seekers registered with UNHCR will benefit from various forms of protection interventions, including individual registration and documentation, and multi-sector assistance. Specific protection services, such as SGBV response and child protection will focus on the identified at-risk groups. While water, health, nutrition and education services will continue to maintain indicators within global standards for refugees living in camps, provision of other assistance, including shelter, non-food items and livelihoods support, will be undertaken in a targeted manner, focusing on persons with specific protection needs and vulnerabilities. This will primarily be achieved through participatory assessments, surveys as well as verification exercise to identify vulnerable refugees and their needs. Impact monitoring will be used to gauge the efficiency of projects implemented and for the purposes of course-correction in terms of better targeting of assistance. The needs of persons with disabilities and the elderly will be further mainstreamed in various multi-sector response services. Vulnerable refugees in urban settings will also continue to benefit from targeted protection interventions and facilitation of their access to national services.

project_text:
Promoting Gender Equality and Inclusion by ending Sexual and Gender Based Violence in South Sudan Gender inequality gaps in South Sudan continue to widen as Gender Based Violence cases increase. According to Protection Analysis Update, Jan-Mar 2022, It notes that the situation of women and girls in South Sudan is daunting: conflict-related sexual violence is widespread and systematic and it is seen as a form to disrupt the fabric of communities, lack of accountability is exacerbated by conflict with poor socio-economic conditions of women and girls contributing to harmful social and gender norms practices.
This project will work to tackle the unequal power relations and harmful social and gender norms that contribute to GBV using Plan's gender transformative approach.
These will be done  through our gender transformative programming and influencing and Community engagement approach that addresses the root cause of power imbalance. Plan mainstreams GBV, safeguarding and PSEA in all its programs by mitigating risk to the people that we work with and ensuring that they feel safe while working with us. Interventions shall be tailored to have the involvement and participation of men, women, girls and boys in diversity including persons with disabilities.

The project will involve key actors in GBV response and prevention through taking leadership of the Protection Cluster or GBV sub Cluster at the state and county level. Currently, Plan International leads the protection Cluster in Nimule and Co-chair the protection Cluster in Yei. Also, in the rest of the states Plan International has been an active member in the cluster meetings and activities as a member. Plan will build on this to support the initiative of the cluster in coordinating GBV prevention and response interventions. 

Plan International will create, engage and maintain linkages/ relationships with  the key stakeholders and partners, such as Government including Ministry of Gender, police, judiciary including the ABC Court (A- the grassroots traditional court system at the Boma level headed by the Boma Chief;  B- middle traditional court headed by the Payam Head chief; and C- Last Traditional Court system headed by the Paramount chief at County level), religious institutions, cultural and community leaders, etc.

While building on the projects like Action Research on Violence against Women and Girls; Youth Voices in Eastern Equatoria, Integrated response to conflict-affected at-risk boys, girls, women and men in Central Equatoria State, South Sudan, Improving the quality and access in provision of life-saving integrated Health, Protection, Education and Nutrition services for vulnerable children and targeted communities in Pibor county, Jonglei State and Humanitarian protection measure for children and young people affected by South Sudan Crisis(GFFO) in Lakes state, among other Protection/ GBV projects that Plan International implements.

The project will be implemented in collaboration with the State Ministry of Gender, GBV cluster/partners, community leaders and women and youth groups at different levels. Plan International will ensure that these life-saving interventions eg PSS and referrals are provided to critically needed GBV survivors including vulnerable groups and other special cases such as Persons with disabilities. Cases with compounding medical conditions will be supported through CVA and referred for clinical management.
The project will mobilize communities to form drama groups that will will be trained and supported to conduct awareness raising on GBV in communities through radio, community mobilization and sensitization, participating in advocacy events such as 16 days of activism, etc. Youth will be mobilized into groups/ clubs as Champions of Change(CoC) plays a pivotal role in peer to peer mobilization of young people to challenge negative and discriminatory social norms that contribute to GBV. 
COVID-19 mitigation measures will especially those affecting public gatherings will be strengthened with COVID SOPs and items to effect COVID.

project_text:
Emergency WASH Response in South Sudan UNICEF will provide women, men, girls, and boys affected by multiple shocks and hazards
in South Sudan with critical water, sanitation, and hygiene services, items, and facilities.
The objective of this project is to provide lifesaving emergency water supply, sanitation
and hygiene promotion services for con􀂧ict affected people, vulnerable host communities
and people in disease prone (high GAM famine and outbreak related) areas including
protection related actions to mitigate GBV, strengthening of communities’ resilience to
cope with the impact of emergencies and recurrent shocks. This emergency WASH project
will comprise of situation assessments, preparedness, transitional programs, frontline
emergency WASH response, strengthening of partners’ capacity, and cluster coordination
including sector information management. UNICEF will deliver emergency lifesaving
support by providing access to WASH services as per Sphere and WASH Cluster
standards.
The project will focus on addressing the following:
- Effective Cluster coordination mechanism in the country
- Provide timely equitable access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene for IDPs/host
communities and returnees, including transitional programming
- WASH in Nutrition for famine prevention with a minimum package of interventions.
- WASH in Health for outbreak control at wider community level (i.e. Ebola, Cholera, etc.)
- While implementing projects a special attention will be given to mitigate WASH-related
GBV.
The project will also support expansion of partnerships with local and international NGOs
and CBOs in highly affected areas to ensure basic services are provided and long-term
capacity built. The activities will be implemented in complementarity with other sectors
such as Health, Nutrition, Protection and where possible Education projects including
disaster risk reduction (DRR) focusing on strengthening community coping mechanisms.

project_text: Respuesta integral en seguridad alimentaria y nutricional de emergencia para la población más vulnerable afectada por la crisis en Venezuela. Acción Contra el Hambre (ACH) en Venezuela atiende las necesidades humanitarias de los grupos más vulnerables en riesgo de desnutrición aguda: < de 5 años, 5 – 14 años, mujeres embarazadas y lactantes (MEL), personas con discapacidades o con problemas de salud, en particular adultos mayores. Son agravantes las situaciones de pobreza y necesidades básicas no satisfechas como la falta de acceso a: alimentos, condiciones higiénico-sanitarias adecuadas, servicios de salud, y medios de vida. La desnutrición y el deterioro de la salud repercuten en una mayor exposición a factores agravantes como la violencia de género, embarazos adolescentes y criminalidad. A través del HRP, ACH brindará una respuesta humanitaria para la reducción del sufrimiento y ayudar a salvar vidas, identificando casos de desnutrición aguda y severa en las familias más a riesgo. Se trabajará a nivel comunitario y se coordinará con instituciones locales, en particular con escuelas y centros de salud. ACH trabaja con un enfoque de programa país y dentro de una estrategia regional, con intervenciones complementarias e integrales en: 1) Nutrición: sensibilización y consejerías; detección, tratamiento de la desnutrición aguda, y derivación de los casos con complicaciones médicas; capacitación en el manejo preventivo de la desnutrición aguda; 2) Salud: atención primaria, equipos, insumos, medicamentos, métodos anticonceptivos; 3) Seguridad Alimentaria y medios de vida: distribución de alimentos y apoyo para la producción de alimentos; 4) ASH: acceso a servicios de agua, saneamiento, e higiene, en escuelas y centros comunitarios; distribución de kits de higiene, y rehabilitación/reparación de sistemas de abastecimiento de agua y de saneamiento en comunidades. El sector de Protección y género, de manera transversal, trabajará en prevención de VBG, nuevas masculinidades y DSSR; establecimiento y/o fortalecimiento de espacios seguros para mujeres y niñas; atención psico-social, distribución de kits de higiene menstrual y protección para mujeres en riesgo. La respuesta actual de ACH se concentra en Caracas DC, Guárico, Carabobo, Miranda, Zulia, Bolívar, y próximamente en Falcón, Amazonas y Sucre.

project_text:
Programa Nutrifamilias FUNDANA FUNDANA desde hace 30 años, a través de su entidad de atención, ha brindado un hogar protector a más de 32.000 niños, niñas y adolescentes (NNA) víctimas de maltrato, abuso o negligencia. Producto de la crisis social y económica, en nuestra organización hemos evidenciado un aumento significativo de niños y niñas con desnutrición infantil, motivado a una situación económica precaria, impactando negativamente en su alimentación y salud.

En respuesta a esta problemática en 2017 se decide inaugurar el Programa de Atención y Recuperación Nutricional ¨Nutrifamilias¨, que tiene como objetivo promover la recuperación nutricional de los niños, niñas con riesgo o desnutrición aguda sin complicaciones, mujeres embarazadas y en periodo de lactancia (MEL), que además se encuentren en situación de vulnerabilidad social, facilitando su rehabilitación y posterior reinserción a la comunidad.

Para el 2023 el Programa espera atender 6.200 NN menores de 5 años y 2054 Mujeres embarazadas y lactantes a través de tamizaje nutricional, 7500 NNA de 2 a 14 años desparasitados, 375 NN y 375 NN de 6 a 59 meses reciben tratamiento para la desnutrición aguda y suplementos para la vulnerabilidad nutricional respectivamente. Asimismo, 8.254 personas reciben consejería en prácticas claves en temas de Nutrición, WASH y Protección NNA. También, 1.875 personas acceden a productos de higiene y tienen acceso a agua segura. Además, 50 profesionales de salud de la red ambulatoria aliada se ven fortalecidos a través de la capacitación en temas de nutrición y WASH. Finalmente, 120 familias donde uno de sus miembros cursa con desnutrición aguda y tiene una alta vulnerabilidad psicosocial reciben acompañamiento por promotores de convivencia familiar. 

Por otra parte, el Programa contempla la conformación de grupos estables de padres y cuidadora para sensibilizaciones en temas relacionados a la alimentación del lactante y niño pequeño ALNP-E, a fin de fomentar el desarrollo de capacidades y promover estrategias EDC. 
El programa Nutrifamilias se ejecuta en 6 Centros de Protección ubicados en los estados Miranda; municipio Sucre y Baruta  y Distrito Capital; municipio Libertador. Asimismo, se establecerán alianzas con 5 Centros de Salud en comunidades periféricas a los Centros de Protección de FUNDANA a fin de acortar las brechas de acceso a los servicios de nutrición, WASH y Protección. 

Adicionalmente, la estrategia intersectorial de Nutrición, WASH y Protección es una respuesta integral que busca centrar los servicios en el individuo, por medio de una visión integradora y respaldada que responda a sus distintas necesidades y enfocada en la sostenibilidad y la resiliencia.

Finalmente, la participación de los beneficiarios durante todas las fases del proyecto permite medir necesidades sentidas, tener retroalimentación de las acciones y mejorar los servicios constantemente. Para ello, todos los datos estarán desagregados por género, edad, discapacidad y  diversidad, a fin de tener in enfoque inclusivo y adaptado al contexto.

Producto de la crisis social y económica, en nuestra organización hemos evidenciado un aumento significativo de niños y niñas con desnutrición infantil, motivado a una situación económica precaria, impactando negativamente en su alimentación y salud.

En respuesta a esta problemática en 2017 se decide inaugurar el Programa de Atención y Recuperación Nutricional ¨Nutrifamilias¨, que tiene como objetivo promover la recuperación nutricional de los niños, niñas con riesgo o desnutrición aguda sin complicaciones, mujeres embarazadas y en periodo de lactancia (MEL), que además se encuentren en situación de vulnerabilidad social, facilitando su rehabilitación y posterior reinserción a la comunidad.

Para el 2023 el Programa espera atender 6.200 NN menores de 5 años y 2054 Mujeres embarazadas y lactantes a través de tamizaje nutricional, 7500 NNA de 2 a 14 años desparasitados, 375 NN y 375 NN de 6 a 59 meses reciben tratamiento para la desnutrición aguda y suplementos para la vulnerabilidad nutricional respectivamente. Asimismo, 8.254 personas reciben consejería en prácticas claves en temas de Nutrición, WASH y Protección NNA. También, 1.875 personas acceden a productos de higiene y tienen acceso a agua segura. Además, 50 profesionales de salud de la red ambulatoria aliada se ven fortalecidos a través de la capacitación en temas de nutrición y WASH. Finalmente, 120 familias donde uno de sus miembros cursa con desnutrición aguda y tiene una alta vulnerabilidad psicosocial reciben acompañamiento por promotores de convivencia familiar. 

Por otra parte, el Programa contempla la conformación de grupos estables de padres y cuidadora para sensibilizaciones en temas relacionados a la alimentación del lactante y niño pequeño ALNP-E, a fin de fomentar el desarrollo de capacidades y promover estrategias EDC. 
El programa Nutrifamilias se ejecuta en 6 Centros de Protección ubicados en los estados Miranda; municipio Sucre y Baruta  y Distrito Capital; municipio Libertador. Asimismo, se establecerán alianzas con 5 Centros de Salud en comunidades periféricas a los Centros de Protección de FUNDANA a fin de acortar las brechas de acceso a los servicios de nutrición, WASH y Protección. 

Adicionalmente, la estrategia intersectorial de Nutrición, WASH y Protección es una respuesta integral que busca centrar los servicios en el individuo, por medio de una visión integradora y respaldada que responda a sus distintas necesidades y enfocada en la sostenibilidad y la resiliencia.

Finalmente, la participación de los beneficiarios durante todas las fases del proyecto permite medir necesidades sentidas, tener retroalimentación de las acciones y mejorar los servicios constantemente. Para ello, todos los datos estarán desagregados por género, edad, discapacidad y  diversidad, a fin de tener in enfoque inclusivo y adaptado al contexto.

project_text:
Protección de Niños, Niñas y Adolescentes en riesgo, y fortalecimiento de las capacidades de cuidado de sus familias  El proyecto tiene como objetivo promover la protección integral y el ejercicio de derechos de los Niños, Niñas y Adolescentes (NNA) con riesgos de protección y en mayor vulnerabilidad, así como, atender a sus familias para la sostenibilidad de la protección y el alcance del bienestar. Incorpora un componente de desarrollo de medios de vida de las familias de las que hacen parte los NNA, así como, del fortalecimiento de su capacidad de crianza positiva, cuidado adecuado a la edad de los NNA y de la prevención de violencia y otros importantes que pueden impactar a las familias, particularmente a los NNA. 

El proyecto está dirigido principal y prioritariamente a NNA en movilidad, NNA separados de sus progenitores y al cuidado de familiares o terceros, NNA de comunidades indígenas y afrodescendientes, NNA de madres adolescentes y adultas jóvenes, NNA víctimas o en riesgo de violencia, reclutamiento a actividades delictivas, violentas o de explotación, NNA en riesgo de protección y que no ejercen o acceden a sus derechos por no poseer documentos de identidad (acta de nacimiento, cédula, otros), al estar fuera de la escuela, no acceder a la nutrición/alimentación adecuada, no recibir la asistencia en salud que requiere, entre otros, que los exponen a riesgos y deterioran el adecuado desarrollo. 
Desde un enfoque de protección integral, se identificarán los NNA con riesgos de protección en y con las comunidades, se evaluará su situación y necesidades, se proveerán servicios psicosociales, en protección legal y social, así como serán refridos y acompañados para acceder a serviciso complementarios brindados por el sistema de protección público y por otros actores no gubernamentales.  Se establecerán las vías de derivación seguras a través del trabajo articulado con organismos competentes como el CPNNA, CMDNNA, Ministerio Público, DdP entre otras.
 Adicionalmente, la intervención incluye procesos de prevención, formación psicosociales y vinculación con los NNA en las comunidades, que incluirá el entrenamiento en habilidades para la vida, sociales, importancia de la diversidad, la protección personal,  y primeros auxilios psicológicos y cooperación, para que aprendan a identificar situaciones en sí mismos y cuándo un amigo o compañero experimenta estrés, angustia o sentimientos de tristeza, cómo expresar sus emocionas y cómo brindar apoyo. Estos procesos apuntan a fortalecer la experiencia colectiva propiedad de la edad de los NNA, a fortalecer capacidades afectivas, cognitiva y sociales personales que le permitan mitigar y retardar el acercamiento a riesgos del contexto, y a estar en mejores condiciones para enfrentarlos. 

El componente de desarrollo de los medios de vida y fortalecimiento de la capacidad de cuidado y protección de los NNA de las familias se llevará a cabo: 
(i)Actividades de información, orientación y psicoeducación de las personas cuidadoras de los NNA: madres, abuelos u otras familias en condición de vulnerabilidad cabezas de hogar, hombres solos cabeza de hogar y con NNA de los perfiles descritos antes. Las actividades coadyuvarán a su resiliencia, estabilidad emocional y fortalecimiento de capacidades de crianza positiva y para la protección y cuidado de los NNA ante un contexto retador de violencia, separación, movilidad, entre otras. Esto se desplegará mediante la aplicación de metodologías escalables.
(ii)Formación, orientación, acompañamiento y entrega de asistencia en especie y mediante servicios para el desarrollo o fortalecimiento de medios de vida o de generación de ingreso que le permitan a las familias mitigar la difícil situación económica que atraviesan y responder a necesidades básicas, de modo que puedan facilitarse acciones de protección y cuidados de los NNA que las integran.  
El proyecto plantea una mirada multisectorial y promueve el nexo entre lo humanitario con respuesta a necesidades y el desarrollo, trabajando en fortalecimiento de las familias y la protección de NNA en las comunidades

Incorpora un componente de desarrollo de medios de vida de las familias de las que hacen parte los NNA, así como, del fortalecimiento de su capacidad de crianza positiva, cuidado adecuado a la edad de los NNA y de la prevención de violencia y otros importantes que pueden impactar a las familias, particularmente a los NNA. 

El proyecto está dirigido principal y prioritariamente a NNA en movilidad, NNA separados de sus progenitores y al cuidado de familiares o terceros, NNA de comunidades indígenas y afrodescendientes, NNA de madres adolescentes y adultas jóvenes, NNA víctimas o en riesgo de violencia, reclutamiento a actividades delictivas, violentas o de explotación, NNA en riesgo de protección y que no ejercen o acceden a sus derechos por no poseer documentos de identidad (acta de nacimiento, cédula, otros), al estar fuera de la escuela, no acceder a la nutrición/alimentación adecuada, no recibir la asistencia en salud que requiere, entre otros, que los exponen a riesgos y deterioran el adecuado desarrollo. 
Desde un enfoque de protección integral, se identificarán los NNA con riesgos de protección en y con las comunidades, se evaluará su situación y necesidades, se proveerán servicios psicosociales, en protección legal y social, así como serán refridos y acompañados para acceder a serviciso complementarios brindados por el sistema de protección público y por otros actores no gubernamentales.  Se establecerán las vías de derivación seguras a través del trabajo articulado con organismos competentes como el CPNNA, CMDNNA, Ministerio Público, DdP entre otras.
 Adicionalmente, la intervención incluye procesos de prevención, formación psicosociales y vinculación con los NNA en las comunidades, que incluirá el entrenamiento en habilidades para la vida, sociales, importancia de la diversidad, la protección personal,  y primeros auxilios psicológicos y cooperación, para que aprendan a identificar situaciones en sí mismos y cuándo un amigo o compañero experimenta estrés, angustia o sentimientos de tristeza, cómo expresar sus emocionas y cómo brindar apoyo. Estos procesos apuntan a fortalecer la experiencia colectiva propiedad de la edad de los NNA, a fortalecer capacidades afectivas, cognitiva y sociales personales que le permitan mitigar y retardar el acercamiento a riesgos del contexto, y a estar en mejores condiciones para enfrentarlos. 

El componente de desarrollo de los medios de vida y fortalecimiento de la capacidad de cuidado y protección de los NNA de las familias se llevará a cabo: 
(i)Actividades de información, orientación y psicoeducación de las personas cuidadoras de los NNA: madres, abuelos u otras familias en condición de vulnerabilidad cabezas de hogar, hombres solos cabeza de hogar y con NNA de los perfiles descritos antes. Las actividades coadyuvarán a su resiliencia, estabilidad emocional y fortalecimiento de capacidades de crianza positiva y para la protección y cuidado de los NNA ante un contexto retador de violencia, separación, movilidad, entre otras. Esto se desplegará mediante la aplicación de metodologías escalables.
(ii)Formación, orientación, acompañamiento y entrega de asistencia en especie y mediante servicios para el desarrollo o fortalecimiento de medios de vida o de generación de ingreso que le permitan a las familias mitigar la difícil situación económica que atraviesan y responder a necesidades básicas, de modo que puedan facilitarse acciones de protección y cuidados de los NNA que las integran.  
El proyecto plantea una mirada multisectorial y promueve el nexo entre lo humanitario con respuesta a necesidades y el desarrollo, trabajando en fortalecimiento de las familias y la protección de NNA en las comunidades

project_text:
Provision of Inclusive, Protective & Effective Education Services to Conflict-affected Children & Youth in Jonglei & Upper Nile States. This CMD’s Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) for 2022 seeks to provide inclusive, protective and effective education services to accelerate learning recovery and make schools more equitable, efficient and resilient for 7, 339 (3, 302 girls) school-aged children, 250 (50 female) teachers, 275 (82 female) PTA members and 60 (10 female) local education officials in 6 Counties of Jonglei & Upper Nile States by building on investments made during the Pandemic and previous years of EiE programming in South Sudan.

The expected results are equalised participation and improved learning outcomes across gender and disability for 7, 339 (45% female) children and youth through provision of essential school facilities and supplies, psychosocial support, gender-sensitive delivery of curriculum, classroom management, teacher conduct and schoolyard dynamics in 25 target schools (5 ECD centers, 15 primary schools, and 5 secondary schools) in Ayod, Uror & Duk Counties of Jonglei State and Ulang, Nasir and Longechuk Counties of Upper Nile State respectively. These 7, 339 children (5-17) and 250 teachers will be provided with teaching and learning materials in the form of 10 ECD learner kits, 250 learner kits for primary and 10 learner kits for secondary schools. 250 recreational kits will be provided to enhance learning and play and psychosocial wellbeing during schooling.

For their protective and safe school environment, 30 temporary learning spaces will be established in line with Inter-INEE's Minimum Standards for Education in Emergencies and Standards in Education Cluster Strategy 2019; and 30 gender segregated latrines and 30 water points in line with INEE and sphere standards. (unit of measurement: 1:60 for boys, 1:30 for girls). CMD will distribute 95 (500-litre) plastic water tanks with taps, 95 (50-litre) hand-washing tanks with taps and on their metal stands; 285 (1-litre) liquid sanitisers, 190 cartons of toilet soap, 95 bags (20 kgs) of detergent/powder soap, 95, 000 face masks, and 375 pairs of gumboots to provide sanitation and PPE for students and teachers. 2, 000 adolescent girls will receive dignity kits and undergo MHM sessions to better enhance their self-esteem and school attendance.

The plan targets 2, 339 (935 girls & 1, 404 boys) children in Ayod; 1, 000 (400 girls & 600 boys) in Uror; 1, 000 (400 girls & 600 boys) in Duk; 1, 000(400 girls & 600 boys) in Ulang; 1, 000 (400 girls & 600 boys) in Nasir; and 1, 000 (400 girls & 600 boys) in Longechuk. 50 (10 female) teachers in Ayod; 40 (10 female) in Uror; 40 (10 female) in Duk; 40 (10 female) in Ulang; 40 (5 female) in Nasir; and 40 (5 female) in Longechuk will benefit from active EiE pedagogy that is centered on children and adolescents and their full development, and that responds to school needs and favours the equitable achievement of learning goals. These teachers will Improve the quality of gender and disability-inclusive education services and teachers' capacity to protect the wellbeing of all children and prevent the negative impact of the emergencies on learning environments.

Equally important, 75 (27 female) PTA members in Ayod; 40 (11 female) in Uror; 40 (11 female) in Duk; 40(11female) in Ulang; 40(11 female) in Nasir; and 40 (11 female) in Longechuk and 10 (1 female) education officials in Ayod, 10 (1) in Uror; 10 (1) in Duk; 10(1) in Ulang; 10(1) in Nassir; and 10 (1 female) in Longechuk will be trained in School Management, Psychosocial Support (PSS) and Disaster Risk Reduction in Education (DRR).

CMD will also conduct 12 Back to Learning (BTL) campaigns through public information campaigns intended for the entire affected population and/or awareness raising activities aimed at specific segments of the out-of-schoolchildren (OOSC) as well as current learners identified as most at-risk.

project_text: Provision of life-saving interventions to displaced communities in POC, Camps and Camp-like settings through CCCM interventions in South Sudan. The objective of the intended project is to contribute and improve the living conditions in the targeted IDP camps through strengthening the predictability and effectiveness of service provision and protection for displaced communities with the aim to reach durable solutions through strengthening community-self management and in addition to that the project will strengthen coordination and information sharing among all stakeholders. Through this proposed project activities, DRC will ensure that all the displaced communities are enabled to partake meaningfully in the governance structures and management of the sites. This project will also encourage camp residents to participate community led care and maintenance activities aimed at improving safety and hygiene in sites, reducing protection and health risks. DRC will work with the camp management committees to facilitate site maintenance through cash-for-work while utilising members of the IDP community by enabling them to earn temporary income. Through this project, DRC will establish or strengthen an inclusive community governance structures and thematic committees at each site level, the engagement of these structures in CCCM coordination mechanisms alongside active humanitarian partners in the respective sites and representatives of relevant local authorities, as well as through continued support for capacity building, mainly through the delivery of trainings adapted to each type of participation (thematic IDP committee members, site governance members, local authority representatives). The proposed project will enhance Complain, Response and feedback mechanisms.

project_text:
Multi-sectoral life-saving assistance, including life-saving GBV prevention and response services, to conflict-affected population in Pulka, Monguno and Maiduguri, Borno State, Nigeria This project’s objective is to contribute to the reduction of mortality and morbidity of the most vulnerable, IDPs and host community, including children under 5, pregnant and lactating women, adolescent girls and women of reproductive age, the elderly, and people with disabilities, in the hard-to-reach areas of Pulka and Monguno (respectively Gwoza and Monguno LGA), and in Maiduguri Metropolitan Council (MMC). To meet the most vulnerable populations’ urgent and complex needs, and ensure a long-lasting impact, integrated multi-sectoral activities in health, nutrition, protection, psychosocial support (PSS), food security, and livelihoods, will be implemented. The response will also be based on a robust community-based approach, with community activities planned for all sectors to ensure beneficiaries' and communities' ownership of the project. This comprehensive approach and the proposed activities align with all the sectors’ and HRP's priorities, including targeting hard-to-reach areas in Northeast Nigeria’s Borno State, the state most affected by the large-scale humanitarian crisis.
Premiere Urgence Internationale will continue to provide free quality life-saving healthcare services to IDPs and host community in the 9 facilities the organization already supports in Maiduguri MC, Monguno, and Pulka. These services include free outpatient consultations to all age groups and comprehensive sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRH) services. SRH activities comprise ante/postnatal care, 24 hours skilled birth delivery services, including Basic Emergency Obstetric Care (BEmONC), and Gender-based Violence (GBV) treatment with CMR (Clinical Management of Rape). 
PUI will continue to provide life-saving treatment to children under 5 suffering from Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) by supporting 4 OTPS across all three locations (one in Maiduguri’s Bollori II, two in Monguno, and one in Pulka), for treatment of SAM without medical complications, and three Stabilization Centres (SCs), one in every three locations, to provide treatment to SAM with medical complications. In case further emergencies arise, PUI plans to increase its SCs' bed capacities in Monguno and Pulka, and to establish three more OTPs. The nutrition response will include systemic identification and referrals of children suffering from SAM to PUI-supported OTPs and SCs, and awareness-raising sessions and sensitization implemented at community level.
PUI will continue to implement a range of activities to contribute to strengthening targeted protection services to address the needs and vulnerability of persons at heightened risks of violence and exploitation, with tailored responses for GBV survivors, through internal/external referrals whenever needed (i.e legal assistance). To prevent GBV and violence, awareness sessions for women and girls on their rights, as well as for community members, boys, men will be conducted. Community knowledge on protection will be strengthened, with key community stakeholders receiving training on protection issues, including GBV, mental health, PSS, to in turn support identification of cases and concerns, and ensure referrals. PUI will continue to ensure protection monitoring in the intervention areas, to ensure risk identification, referrals, concerted and tailored interventions, as well as advocacies with partners at all levels.
To promote the targeted beneficiaries' self-reliance, and reduce their dependency on humanitarian assistance, PUI will provide food assistance to 5,390 vulnerable individual beneficiaries on a monthly basis for 12 months, as food e-vouchers or e-cash. PUI will identify 700 individuals among beneficiaries of PUI Nutrition services and survivors of GBV or persons exposed to Protection risks due to their economic vulnerability. These persons will receive a training on the management of small business, and a start capital to launch an Income Generating Activity (IGA) of their choice.

project_text:
Improved food security and livelihoods of IDPs, Returnees and Vulnerable host communities in South Sudan The purpose of the project is to improve food consumption, food security, dietary diversity and coping strategies and enhance emergency food production of vulnerable populations in the targeted counties. This will be achieved through provision of Cash-Based Transfers (CBT) to address food needs of vulnerable communities during the lean season and provision of timely and appropriate complementary vegetable and crop livelihood inputs and fishing kits coupled with training in improved agronomic and fishing practices.
In line with the South Sudan FSL cluster HRP objectives and priorities, NPA will support vulnerable populations in IPC 4 and 5 locations as well as some IPC 3 locations. Specifically, NPA will target Canal/Pigi, Fangak, Pochalla and Bor South Counties of Jonglei State, Rumbek East, Rumbek Centre, Cueibet, Yirol East, Yirol West and Awerial Counties of Lakes State, Terekeka County of Central Equatoria State and Kapoeta North County of Eastern Equatoria State.

NPA seeks to support 86,200 HHs (517,200 individuals) through provision of complementary vegetable and crop livelihood inputs and fishing kits across the target counties. Some of the kits will be provided by FAO (core pipeline) while the rest will be procured and distributed directly by NPA to enhance food production.  NPA will build the capacity of the HHs supported with the kits through training on improved agronomic and fishing practices, marketing and group dynamics. A Training of Trainers (ToT) approach will be utilized whereby lead farmers and fisher folk will be trained by NPA. They will then train/share the knowledge and skills with other farmers and fisher folk in their communities. The kits provided through this project and the knowledge gained from the trainings is expected to improve the agricultural and fishing practices of the target HHs thus enhancing and sustaining food production. CBT interventions will target 1,000 HHs (6,000 individuals ) in Rumbek East, Rumbek Centre and Cuiebet Counties in Lakes State to improve their access to food, diversify and improve their food consumption and dietary diversity scores and promote the adoption of positive coping strategies. The planned interventions are aligned to the FSL cluster objectives 1 and 2 and will provide emergency assistance and livelihoods support to save lives and avert total collapse of livelihoods in the target counties.

NPA will integrate development-oriented and conflict-sensitivity activities in this project to enhance the resilience of  vulnerable HHs in line with the Triple Nexus. Therefore, 1,200 vulnerable HHs will be supported with small-scale cash grants to establish IGAs. The target HHs will be mobilized and sensitized to transition to and establish VSLA’s to ease access to financial services and encourage the spirit of saving among the VSLA group members. The IGAs will contribute to increasing and diversifying income and building the resilience of the target HHs at the same time improving functionality of local markets and boosting the local value chains.

NPA will employ a community-based beneficiary selection approach which will entail establishing Project Management Committees (PMCs) to lead the selection of eligible beneficiaries based on the beneficiary selection criteria. Vulnerable HHs with severe food insecurity including female, child, disabled/chronically ill headed HHs; persons living with or at risk of HIV/AIDS and the elderly will be targeted in this project. 
NPA will ensure meaningful engagement of the target communities throughout the project life-cycle through holding regular meetings with the PMCs and community members and Post Distribution Monitoring (PDM) to get their feedback on the project. NPA will ensure that the feedback is incorporated in the implementation of this project and design of future projects. Further, NPA will use a community-based complaints and feedback mechanism to provide a platform for beneficiaries to voice any issues or concerns.

project_text:
Provision of emergency nutrition services and support optimum early childhood development to crisis affected pregnant and lactating women and children aged below 5 years among vulnerable Lebanese and migrants in Lebanon. With Growing triple burden of malnutrition (undernutrition, both stunting and wasting; deficiencies in vitamins and other micronutrients; and overweight and obesity) among women, children and adolescents which affects health, growth and development. 
70% of young children are not exclusively breastfed; 90% of children aged 6-23 months lack dietary diversity and meal frequency; over 40% of all women and children, including Lebanese, are affected by anaemia. In October 2021, 53% of children skipped a meal due to insufficient food in the house, up from 37% just 6 months before. 453,000 Lebanese women and children need urgent nutritional support.
Nutrition and child development should be prioritized as part of the emergency response plan, hence UNICEF will be working under the ERP appeal through a multi-system approach from food, health, social protection, education and water and sanitation systems to protect and promote adequate diets, practices and services to prevent all forms of malnutrition among children and women and support optimum early childhood development. In 2021, the percentage of childcare service providers encountering families with payment difficulties has doubled, reaching 41%.  Additionally, due to the local currency devaluation and the significant increase in fuel prices, the monthly fees per child are no longer sufficient to cover the operational expenses of childcare providers. Therefore, to remain affordable, childcare providers are often constrained to compromise on quality which can negatively affect the healthy development of children, while children in rural areas, camps or informal settlements have little access to ECD.
Building on this momentum of a strengthened enabling environment for nutrition and child development, UNICEF will work with the government and partners to reach the most vulnerable children and women with an essential service package for prevention, early detection, referral, and management of all forms of malnutrition and development delays. Maternal and child nutrition during the first 1,000 days coupled with a nurturing care framework – from conception to age 2 years – remains core to the response.
This will be done by strengthening national capacity across multiple sectors and systems through better evidence, policies, and facility and community-based solutions and programmes.

project_text:
Renforcement de la coordination et du plaidoyer humanitaire au Tchad Le projet vise à renforcer le rôle de OCHA dans la mise en œuvre de son mandat et son rôle auprès des partenaires humanitaires et gouvernementaux au niveau des fonctions coordination, gestion de l’information et plaidoyer. Le bureau national d’OCHA à N’Djaména et ses trois sous-bureaux régionaux à l’Est (Abéché) au Sud (Goré) et la province du Lac (Baga Sola) mettent l’accent sur l’opérationnalisation de ses fonctions y compris en assurant un lien entre les activités humanitaires et de développement (nexus) en vue de promouvoir une solution durable visant à ne pas perpétuer une situation de dépendance humanitaire. Dans le cadre de cette nouvelle façon de travailler outre l’opérationnalisation du nexus, le lien avec les objectifs commun des programmes développement, paix et sécurité sera mis en avant. L’accent est aussi mis sur le renforcement de la coordination civilo-militaire afin de faciliter l’accès et la protection des civils.
Le projet a pour but de renforcer la coordination d’une réponse humanitaire rapide et efficace afin de sauver des vies et protéger les personnes affectées par les situations de crises au Tchad. Une coordination humanitaire rapide et correctement évaluée au niveau des besoins de la population affectée permettra aux acteurs humanitaires de mieux identifier et répondre aux besoins humanitaires, de renforcer la préparation de réponse aux urgences à travers le renforcement des mécanismes de coordination et plus spécifiquement l‘Equipe humanitaire pays, la coordination inter-clusters, la coordination civilo-militaire, les clusters, des groupes de travail et les mécanismes de coordination au niveau de terrain.
Le projet vise aussi à assurer le plaidoyer humanitaire à travers l’analyse des besoins faites par l’ensemble de la communauté humanitaire et ses partenaires en vue une compréhension commune des problématiques auxquels fait face le Tchad, ses causes profondes, l’impact sur les populations. OCHA jouera un rôle clé dans la création d'espaces de collection et d'analyse et gestion d’informations, pour assurer une stratégie de réponse coordonnée menant à des actions humanitaires répondant aux besoins les plus aigus et être mieux préparé face aux urgences soudaines. Le projet permettra également d’assurer conjointement avec la communauté humanitaire le plaidoyer en faveur du respect des principes humanitaires, de la protection des civils, de l'accès humanitaire et pour la mobilisation et l'allocation efficace de ressources humanitaires.
Un accent a été mis sur la mise en œuvre des plans d’action de la redevabilité envers les populations affectées (AAP), la PSEA et la préparation aux urgences en plus d'intégrer une attention au genre et de renforcer la centralité de la protection.
Un plaidoyer pour plus de visibilité des résultats tangibles au niveau de la réponse facilitant la mobilisation de ressources pour les différentes crises au Tchad (mouvement de population – crise du Bassin du Lac Tchad, insécurité alimentaire et malnutrition, urgences sanitaires, catastrophes naturelles) est aussi défini comme une priorité dans ce projet.
OCHA continuera de jouer également un rôle moteur dans le renforcement du lien entre les acteurs humanitaires et de développement et la transformation de la réponse humanitaire, en lien avec les engagements pris au Sommet humanitaire mondial de 2016 et ceci à travers la nouvelle façon de travailler (NWOW) et le renforcement de l’utilisation de la modalité de transfert monétaire.

project_text:
Mejora de los servicios esenciales de Agua, Saneamiento e Higiene de las personas en situación de desplazamiento afectadas directa o indirectamente por la situación humanitaria  NRC Venezuela tiene como objetivo reducir riesgos de salud pública y la prevención de enfermedades relacionadas con el agua y el saneamiento inadecuados, garantizando el acceso al derecho al agua y al saneamiento, reduciendo los riesgos de protección ligados a la situación humanitaria en Venezuela. El programa ASH propone modalidades de (a) respuesta de emergencia, (b) respuesta con soluciones duraderas basada en un enfoque comunitario, y (c) una respuesta Integrada con otros programas de NRC tales como: Educación e ICLA. 

 

La respuesta ASH de NRC continuará incluyendo la provisión de un mínimo de servicios ASH durante la Respuesta de Emergencia (COVID-19 y crisis humanitaria venezolana). Por otro lado, durante la Respuesta con Soluciones Duraderas se pretende mejorar la resiliencia en comunidades meta, fomentando la participación de comunidades en el diseño e implementación del programa, desarrollando sus capacidades locales, y asegurando la sostenibilidad del programa. 

 

La componente de AGUA incluirá: (a) Provisión de agua segura (a nivel del hogar) a través de kits de tratamiento de agua para el hogar y/o kits de manejo de agua) y rehabilitación y sistema de tratamiento de agua a nivel comunitario; (b) Provisión de capacitación y sensibilización (tratamiento, calidad del agua y uso seguro). 

 

La componente de SANEAMIENTO incluirá: (a) Provisión de baterías de baños y duchas culturalmente apropiadas, desagregados por género y estaciones de lavado de manos. Las instalaciones se ubicarán en áreas públicas o institucionales en zonas clave de flujo migratorio; (b) Provisión de kits NFIs de saneamiento (mantenimiento / limpieza); (c)Provisión de contenedores de basura para gestión de residuos sólidos. 

 

La componente de HIGIENE incluirá: (a) Provisión de kits de dignidad e higiene, junto con sensibilizaciones sobre su uso apropiados; (b)Provisión de campañas de sensibilización sobre higiene personal, prevención de enfermedades, higiene menstrual y protección; (c) Creación, capacitación y sensibilización de comités ASH en colegios y comunidades que servirán como apoyo a la promoción de higiene. La respuesta ASH de NRC pretenden ser Integradas a otros programas como el de Educación que apunta a una mejora de la calidad de la educación, inclusivas e integradas con el programa ASH centrándose en la mejora de la infraestructura ASH, para garantizar las instalaciones satisfagan las necesidades de todos los grupos de NNAs, profesores y personas con discapacidad.

project_text:
Programa de seguridad alimentaria basado en la escuela Con el objetivo de contribuir a la seguridad alimentaria de la población con mayores necesidades, el Programa Mundial de Alimentos de Naciones Unidas (WFP, por sus siglas en inglés) en Venezuela desarrolla un programa de asistencia humanitaria basado en la escuela para garantizar el acceso de los más vulnerables a una alimentación adecuada y nutritiva en el entorno escolar, familiar y comunitario. 
Este programa inició en 2021 con comidas escolares en emergencias priorizando escuelas iniciales y de educación especial.

WFP proporciona comidas escolares acompañado de un paquete integrado de intervenciones para mejorar el acceso a alimentos nutritivos y diversificados a través de las escuelas, contribuyendo al mismo tiempo a mejorar la salud y la nutrición de los niños en edad escolar, los estudiantes con discapacidad y el personal escolar, y apoyando a las comunidades a reducir la dependencia en estrategias de afrontamiento. De manera gradual, el WFP está realizando compras locales de alimentos, e incluyendo acciones para apoyar los mercados locales con compras a pequeños productores y apoyo técnico para acceso a mercados.

En este sentido, el programa de comidas escolares en emergencias tiene los siguientes componentes, para asegurar un enfoque integral que apoye al estudiante en el entorno escolar y familiar:

1. Entrega de comidas escolares nutritivas para estudiantes y personal escolar, promoviendo las compras locales y a pequeños productores.
2. Apoyo a la seguridad alimentaria del hogar.
3. Rehabilitación de cocinas escolares para garantizar condiciones adecuadas de preparación de alimentos.
4. Comunicación para sensibilizar acerca de los principios humanitarios, la adecuada preparación de alimentos, nutrición, higiene y mantenimiento de cocinas escolares.
5. Fortalecimiento de capacidades de socios implementadores y personal escolar.
6. Acciones sensibles a la nutrición, que incluyen, tamizaje en las escuelas, educación nutricional, referencia a servicios especializados y entrega de alimento complementario fortificado (Super Cereal Plus).

project_text:
Renforcement de la coordination et du plaidoyer humanitaire au Tchad Le projet vise à renforcer le rôle de OCHA dans la mise en œuvre de son mandat et son rôle auprès des partenaires humanitaires et gouvernementaux au niveau des fonctions coordination, gestion de l’information et plaidoyer. Le bureau national d’OCHA à N’Djaména et ses trois sous-bureaux régionaux à l’Est (Abéché) au Sud (Goré) et la province du Lac (Baga Sola) mettent l’accent sur l’opérationnalisation de ses fonctions y compris en assurant un lien entre les activités humanitaires et de développement (nexus) en vue de promouvoir une solution durable visant à ne pas perpétuer une situation de dépendance humanitaire. Dans le cadre de cette nouvelle façon de travailler outre l’opérationnalisation du nexus, le lien avec les objectifs commun des programmes développement, paix et sécurité sera mis en avant. L’accent est aussi mis sur le renforcement de la coordination civilo-militaire afin de faciliter l’accès et la protection des civils.
Le projet a pour but de renforcer la coordination d’une réponse humanitaire rapide et efficace afin de sauver des vies et protéger les personnes affectées par les situations de crises au Tchad. Une coordination humanitaire rapide et correctement évaluée au niveau des besoins de la population affectée permettra aux acteurs humanitaires de mieux identifier et répondre aux besoins humanitaires, de renforcer la préparation de réponse aux urgences à travers le renforcement des mécanismes de coordination et plus spécifiquement l‘Equipe humanitaire pays, la coordination inter-clusters, la coordination civilo-militaire, les clusters, des groupes de travail et les mécanismes de coordination au niveau de terrain.
Le projet vise aussi à assurer le plaidoyer humanitaire à travers l’analyse des besoins faites par l’ensemble de la communauté humanitaire et ses partenaires en vue une compréhension commune des problématiques auxquels fait face le Tchad, ses causes profondes, l’impact sur les populations. OCHA jouera un rôle clé dans la création d'espaces de collection et d'analyse et gestion d’informations, pour assurer une stratégie de réponse coordonnée menant à des actions humanitaires répondant aux besoins les plus aigus et être mieux préparé face aux urgences soudaines. Le projet permettra également d’assurer conjointement avec la communauté humanitaire le plaidoyer en faveur du respect des principes humanitaires, de la protection des civils, de l'accès humanitaire et pour la mobilisation et l'allocation efficace de ressources humanitaires.
Un accent a été mis sur la mise en œuvre des plans d’action de la redevabilité envers les populations affectées (AAP), la PSEA et la préparation aux urgences en plus d'intégrer une attention au genre et de renforcer la centralité de la protection.
Un plaidoyer pour plus de visibilité des résultats tangibles au niveau de la réponse facilitant la mobilisation de ressources pour les différentes crises au Tchad (mouvement de population – crise du Bassin du Lac Tchad, insécurité alimentaire et malnutrition, urgences sanitaires, catastrophes naturelles) est aussi défini comme une priorité dans ce projet.
OCHA continuera de jouer également un rôle moteur dans le renforcement du lien entre les acteurs humanitaires et de développement et la transformation de la réponse humanitaire, en lien avec les engagements pris au Sommet humanitaire mondial de 2016 et ceci à travers la nouvelle façon de travailler (NWOW) et le renforcement de l’utilisation de la modalité de transfert monétaire.

project_text:
Emergency WASH Response in South Sudan UNICEF will provide women, men, girls, and boys affected by multiple shocks and hazards
in South Sudan with critical water, sanitation, and hygiene services, items, and facilities.
The objective of this project is to provide lifesaving emergency water supply, sanitation
and hygiene promotion services for con􀂧ict affected people, vulnerable host communities
and people in disease prone (high GAM famine and outbreak related) areas including
protection related actions to mitigate GBV, strengthening of communities’ resilience to
cope with the impact of emergencies and recurrent shocks. This emergency WASH project
will comprise of situation assessments, preparedness, transitional programs, frontline
emergency WASH response, strengthening of partners’ capacity, and cluster coordination
including sector information management. UNICEF will deliver emergency lifesaving
support by providing access to WASH services as per Sphere and WASH Cluster
standards.
The project will focus on addressing the following:
- Effective Cluster coordination mechanism in the country
- Provide timely equitable access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene for IDPs/host
communities and returnees, including transitional programming
- WASH in Nutrition for famine prevention with a minimum package of interventions.
- WASH in Health for outbreak control at wider community level (i.e. Ebola, Cholera, etc.)
- While implementing projects a special attention will be given to mitigate WASH-related
GBV.
The project will also support expansion of partnerships with local and international NGOs
and CBOs in highly affected areas to ensure basic services are provided and long-term
capacity built. The activities will be implemented in complementarity with other sectors
such as Health, Nutrition, Protection and where possible Education projects including
disaster risk reduction (DRR) focusing on strengthening community coping mechanisms.

project_text:
Strengthening Child Protection interventions for girls and boys most at risk of violence, abuse, neglect and exploitation across whole of Syria In line with the CP Area of Responsibility (AOR) Strategy and the “No Lost Generation” framework, UNICEF will enhance equitable access to quality CP services with a resilience focus, including for Survivors of abuse, violence, neglect and exploitation as well as children with disabilities, targeting 117 high severity sub-districts (3 to 5) and 38 low severity ones.

UNICEF’s CP Strategy in 2022-2023 includes:
• Addressing behavioural, social, cultural and economic determinants of CP violations as a prevention approach.  
• Improving the reach and quality of specialized CP services
• Capacity development of CP responders
•  Monitoring, evidence generation and advocacy 

UNICEF will support the delivery of integrated programming that will encourage social transformation, prioritizing:
• Structured and sustained CP MHPSS and EORE programmes
• Specialized integrated CP services including case management for survivors of violence, exploitation, neglect and abuse (child labour, CAFAAG, child survivors of GBV, child marriages, justice for children, birth registration and unaccompanied or separated children amongst others) 
• Parenting programmes to promote positive child rearing skills and experience for caregivers
• Elimination of violence against children, including GBV prevention and empowerment for girls, boys and women, prevention of violence in schools, homes and communities.
• Awareness-raising on CP risks
• Capacity development of CP responders and social workers

UNICEF will generate evidence to inform the humanitarian response and advocacy including setting up an information management system for case management. UNICEF will embrace new delivery modalities and implement cash transfers aimed at child protection outcomes for vulnerable families. UNICEF will also continue to support the Monitoring and Reporting Mechanism on grave violations against children.

CP services will be delivered by partners based on minimum standards and IASC guidelines. 7,200 CP and social workers will be trained on case management, MHPSS, EORE, advocacy, evidence generation and coordination across sectors for a comprehensive CP response.
 
UNICEF will support MHPSS for 364,000 children to benefit from improved mental health and social wellbeing. UNICEF will equip 61,500 parents and caregivers with skills to provide a stimulating and safe environment at home, including reduced violence.  

Violence prevention is a key priority. Family violence prevalence is high for girls 12-17 years (47%), boys 12-17 years (44%), boys below 12 (45%) and girls below 12 (44%) (UNICEF 2018). UNICEF will work to protect children from violence and abuse through prevention activities in schools, homes and communities and providing survivors of violence with child-friendly and gender sensitive services. Support will be provided for PSEA mechanisms to protect beneficiaries and build the capacity of humanitarian actors. PSEA programming will be implemented with the Protection Sector AORs.

Based on HNO 2021, one in three communities in Syria is reportedly contaminated by explosive ordnance. One in four victims is a child (Joint MA & CP Analysis, 2020). EORE messages will be provided to 1,460,000 children and adults through humanitarian actors and public service providers using static facilities and mobile teams. UNICEF will build the capacity of partners to provide quality EORE that is age, gender and disability appropriate and to provide child victims with assistance.
 
UNICEF will strengthen the justice system to ensure that children in contact with the law victims, offenders or witnesses are protected through child-friendly, gender-sensitive services, that are community-based and family focused.

As Lead Agency for the CP AOR, UNICEF will ensure coordination needs at Hub and WOS levels. Two UN-led and one INGO-led coordination hubs in Damascus, Gaziantep and NES, as well as a WOS overall coordination system, to ensure coherence across the CP response.

project_text:
Fostering Resilience through Early Recovery response for the most Crisis impacted Communities in Syria The Integrated Response for Resilience Programme aims at providing a comprehensive response through Early Recovery support in 80 communities impacted by the crisis. Communities, particularly  those most dramatically affected – and under additional stress because of IDPs returns and other displacements - need  assistance in reinforcing their resilience to address these shocks as well as the consequences of the protracted crisis, and to address their needs on seriously depleted infrastructures and service capacities.
The essence of the Programme is about providing Syrian communities with – still limited - support to regain  control  over their basic needs (livelihoods, access to essential services) and reduce their dependency on humanitarian assistance. Prioritization of locations, is the outcome of a context analysis and needs assessment conducted on more than  5,000
Syrian communities, based on the following three criteria:
1) Hard to Reach  Areas
2) Areas of major IDPs presence and IDPs returns
3) Highest scoring in the Severity Scale
The integrated response consists of the following components: strengthening of social services-related capacities (access and coverage), livelihoods creation and rural recovery, PWDs support, social cohesion/community safety, reducing gender inequality  and youth marginality, women empowerment, tensions reduction and rehabilitation of basic infrastructure and public services.
The program is built in a modular manner both in terms of geographical and sectoral/thematic interventions and foresees the allotment of average 1 Million US$ per community. Hence, donors willing to support this approach will be able to pre-select certain location(s) and/or area(s) of intervention of their preference, within the 200 prioritized  communities.
The programme relates directly to the sector objectives:
1. Living conditions
2. Livelihoods
3. Access to social services
4. Access to productive and market infrastructure
5.social protection
6. Strengthening of local public services delivery capacity
7. Reinforcing  opportunities and capacities for civic engagement

Fostering Resilience through Early Recovery response for the most Crisis impacted Communities in Syria The Integrated Response for Resilience Programme aims at providing a comprehensive response through Early Recovery support in 80 communities impacted by the crisis. Communities, particularly  those most dramatically affected – and under additional stress because of IDPs returns and other displacements - need  assistance in reinforcing their resilience to address these shocks as well as the consequences of the protracted crisis, and to address their needs on seriously depleted infrastructures and service capacities.
The essence of the Programme is about providing Syrian communities with – still limited - support to regain  control  over their basic needs (livelihoods, access to essential services) and reduce their dependency on humanitarian assistance. Prioritization of locations, is the outcome of a context analysis and needs assessment conducted on more than  5,000
Syrian communities, based on the following three criteria:
1) Hard to Reach  Areas
2) Areas of major IDPs presence and IDPs returns
3) Highest scoring in the Severity Scale
The integrated response consists of the following components: strengthening of social services-related capacities (access and coverage), livelihoods creation and rural recovery, PWDs support, social cohesion/community safety, reducing gender inequality  and youth marginality, women empowerment, tensions reduction and rehabilitation of basic infrastructure and public services.
The program is built in a modular manner both in terms of geographical and sectoral/thematic interventions and foresees the allotment of average 1 Million US$ per community. Hence, donors willing to support this approach will be able to pre-select certain location(s) and/or area(s) of intervention of their preference, within the 200 prioritized  communities.
The programme relates directly to the sector objectives:
1. Living conditions
2. Livelihoods
3. Access to social services
4. Access to productive and market infrastructure
5.social protection
6. Strengthening of local public services delivery capacity
7. Reinforcing  opportunities and capacities for civic engagement

project_text:
Strengthening Child Protection interventions for girls and boys most at risk of violence, abuse, neglect and exploitation across whole of Syria In line with the CP Area of Responsibility (AOR) Strategy and the “No Lost Generation” framework, UNICEF will enhance equitable access to quality CP services with a resilience focus, including for Survivors of abuse, violence, neglect and exploitation as well as children with disabilities, targeting 117 high severity sub-districts (3 to 5) and 38 low severity ones.

UNICEF’s CP Strategy in 2022-2023 includes:
• Addressing behavioural, social, cultural and economic determinants of CP violations as a prevention approach.  
• Improving the reach and quality of specialized CP services
• Capacity development of CP responders
•  Monitoring, evidence generation and advocacy 

UNICEF will support the delivery of integrated programming that will encourage social transformation, prioritizing:
• Structured and sustained CP MHPSS and EORE programmes
• Specialized integrated CP services including case management for survivors of violence, exploitation, neglect and abuse (child labour, CAFAAG, child survivors of GBV, child marriages, justice for children, birth registration and unaccompanied or separated children amongst others) 
• Parenting programmes to promote positive child rearing skills and experience for caregivers
• Elimination of violence against children, including GBV prevention and empowerment for girls, boys and women, prevention of violence in schools, homes and communities.
• Awareness-raising on CP risks
• Capacity development of CP responders and social workers

UNICEF will generate evidence to inform the humanitarian response and advocacy including setting up an information management system for case management. UNICEF will embrace new delivery modalities and implement cash transfers aimed at child protection outcomes for vulnerable families. UNICEF will also continue to support the Monitoring and Reporting Mechanism on grave violations against children.

CP services will be delivered by partners based on minimum standards and IASC guidelines. 7,200 CP and social workers will be trained on case management, MHPSS, EORE, advocacy, evidence generation and coordination across sectors for a comprehensive CP response.
 
UNICEF will support MHPSS for 364,000 children to benefit from improved mental health and social wellbeing. UNICEF will equip 61,500 parents and caregivers with skills to provide a stimulating and safe environment at home, including reduced violence.  

Violence prevention is a key priority. Family violence prevalence is high for girls 12-17 years (47%), boys 12-17 years (44%), boys below 12 (45%) and girls below 12 (44%) (UNICEF 2018). UNICEF will work to protect children from violence and abuse through prevention activities in schools, homes and communities and providing survivors of violence with child-friendly and gender sensitive services. Support will be provided for PSEA mechanisms to protect beneficiaries and build the capacity of humanitarian actors. PSEA programming will be implemented with the Protection Sector AORs.

Based on HNO 2021, one in three communities in Syria is reportedly contaminated by explosive ordnance. One in four victims is a child (Joint MA & CP Analysis, 2020). EORE messages will be provided to 1,460,000 children and adults through humanitarian actors and public service providers using static facilities and mobile teams. UNICEF will build the capacity of partners to provide quality EORE that is age, gender and disability appropriate and to provide child victims with assistance.
 
UNICEF will strengthen the justice system to ensure that children in contact with the law victims, offenders or witnesses are protected through child-friendly, gender-sensitive services, that are community-based and family focused.

As Lead Agency for the CP AOR, UNICEF will ensure coordination needs at Hub and WOS levels. Two UN-led and one INGO-led coordination hubs in Damascus, Gaziantep and NES, as well as a WOS overall coordination system, to ensure coherence across the CP response.

project_text:
Assurer l’offre des soins de santé d’urgence aux populations vulnérables dans les zones enclavées. Le résultat ultime sera d’améliorer la santé des populations, des femmes, des enfants, des jeunes, des hommes, à travers une augmentation de la couverture des services des soins de santé primaires incluant la santé sexuelle et reproductive dans les 6 régions les plus touchées par la crise humanitaire. Ce projet entre en ligne droite avec le plan du cluster santé de 2023 et propose se dérouler sur quatre axes stratégiques : 
•	• Le renforcement de l’offre des soins de santé primaires intégrés d’urgence et de qualité pour les populations déplacées et leurs communautés hôtes qui sera apporté à travers (i) un appui à la réouverture des formations sanitaires par le déploiement de la réserve sanitaire, des médicaments essentiels et matériels médicotechniques, (ii) l’appui en médicaments, matériels médicotechniques et autres intrants aux formations sanitaires fonctionnelles qui assurent l’offre des soins de santé, (iii) la mise en place des postes médicaux avancés dans les zones d’affluence des PDIs, (iv) la mise en place des cliniques mobiles dans les zones d’accès difficiles. Ces dispositifs permettront d’absorber le surplus des besoins en soins de santé primaires des populations dans les 6 régions les plus touchées incluant les personnes handicapées .
•	La facilitation de l’accès aux soins de santé pour les urgences médico-chirurgicales, les soins des survivant-es de violences basées sur le genre par un transfert monétaire dans les six régions d’interventions.
•	Le renforcement du dispositif minimum en situation d’urgence pour l’offre des soins de santé mentale, la santé sexuelle et reproduction et la prise en charge clinique des violences basées sur le genre dans les trois régions d’interventions .
•	Le renforcement des capacités dans la détection et l’alerte précoce, les investigations et la confirmation au laboratoire, l’approvisionnement en intrants et en matériels médicotechniques, l’appui en ressources humaines et le soutien au fonctionnement des équipes de riposte et de coordination des réponses aux épidémies.
•	Le renforcement de la protection du personnel de santé et des agents de santé à base communautaires contre les risques infectieux
